category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep adjacent policy text available at chunk boundaries
prompt: A support team ingests plain-text policies into a new Amazon Bedrock knowledge base data source. Citations often require a short exception statement near the boundary between two chunks. The team needs predictable token limits and wants the neighboring chunks to share some of the text. What configuration best meets these requirements?

choices.text: Choose fixed-size chunking and configure a nonzero overlap percentage with the required token limit.
choices.explanation: This controls chunk size and includes some of the same text in neighboring chunks.

choices.text: Choose no chunking and use the maximum generation token count to split the source documents.
choices.explanation: No chunking keeps each document together. Generation token limits do not control ingestion boundaries.

choices.text: Choose semantic chunking and tune only the response temperature.
choices.explanation: Temperature affects generation. It does not configure ingestion overlap or maximum token size.

choices.text: Create a retrieval filter for the policy date and leave chunking unchanged.
choices.explanation: A retrieval filter selects candidate chunks by metadata. It does not put boundary text in adjacent chunks.

learning.reason: Fixed-size chunking lets the engineer set a maximum token count and an overlap percentage. Overlap carries a portion of adjacent content into each chunk without treating the full document as one unit.
learning.concept: Bedrock Knowledge Bases fixed-size chunk token limit and overlap

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prepare an S3 corpus for metadata-based retrieval
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base ingests manuals from Amazon S3. Different manuals apply to different product lines. The application already passes the approved product line in its retrieval filter. The team needs to attach that filterable product-line value to the existing files without changing the manual text. What should the engineer add?

choices.text: Add an S3 object tag to each manual and assume the retrieval filter receives the tag automatically.
choices.explanation: S3 object tagging alone does not supply the document attributes through this connector's metadata sidecar mechanism.

choices.text: Add a correctly named .metadata.json companion next to each manual with the product line in metadataAttributes, then synchronize the data source.
choices.explanation: The companion supplies document metadata without changing the document body.

choices.text: Put the product line in the system prompt and remove the retrieval filter.
choices.explanation: That can influence the response, but the knowledge base can still retrieve manuals for other product lines.

choices.text: Set the embedding model's batch size separately for each product line.
choices.explanation: Embedding batch size does not attach a product-line metadata key to search results.

learning.reason: The Bedrock S3 data source connector can read a companion metadata JSON object for an ingested document. The document metadata is then available for supported vector-store retrieval filters.
learning.concept: S3 knowledge base metadata sidecar files and retrieval filters

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Choose a parser for manuals with embedded tables and figures
prompt: A RAG application ingests PDF maintenance manuals. Several troubleshooting steps are represented as diagrams and tables, and users need to ask about their contents. A text-only ingestion test omitted this material. The team wants a Bedrock-managed parsing option that can extract information from the embedded visual content. Which configuration should it use?

choices.text: Keep the text-only parser and increase the number of chunks retrieved.
choices.explanation: More chunks cannot restore diagrams or other information that was omitted at ingestion.

choices.text: Keep the text-only parser and increase the response output limit.
choices.explanation: The model may generate a longer answer, but the underlying extracted content is unchanged.

choices.text: Configure Amazon Bedrock Data Automation as the data source parser and ingest the supported PDF documents again.
choices.explanation: The advanced parser can process the visual content that was missing from text-only extraction.

choices.text: Compress the PDFs in Amazon S3 and keep the existing ingestion settings.
choices.explanation: Storage compression changes how files are stored. It does not add visual extraction.

learning.reason: Bedrock Data Automation is an advanced parser suitable for multimodal content within supported documents. Chunking operates on the parsed content and cannot recover information that the parser did not extract.
learning.concept: Bedrock Knowledge Bases advanced parsing for PDF visual content

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reduce embedding dimensionality without mixing incompatible vectors
prompt: A semantic search service uses 1,024-dimensional Titan Text Embeddings V2 vectors. Its engineers evaluate a smaller footprint by switching to a supported 512-dimensional configuration. The vector store requires a fixed dimension per index. What rollout should they use to preserve meaningful comparisons?

choices.text: Change only the query embedding size and keep searching the 1,024-dimensional index.
choices.explanation: The query vector shape will not match the index or the existing document vectors.

choices.text: Mix new 512-dimensional document vectors with the old 1,024-dimensional vectors in the existing index.
choices.explanation: The index expects one dimension, and these embeddings do not have a consistent representation.

choices.text: Keep 1,024-dimensional queries and set a 512-token generation output limit.
choices.explanation: The output limit affects text generation, not embedding dimension.

choices.text: Build a 512-dimensional index, re-embed the corpus at 512 dimensions, and switch queries to use the same setting when the index is ready.
choices.explanation: Corpus and query representations remain aligned with the vector index.

learning.reason: The embedding model can produce different supported output dimensions. Corpus and query vectors must use the same configuration and match the index dimension.
learning.concept: Titan Text Embeddings V2 compatible vector dimensions at ingestion and retrieval

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Join historical features without reading later events
prompt: A dataset contains labeled purchase events with timestamps. A SageMaker Feature Store offline feature group records multiple customer-status updates over time. For each purchase, the training data must contain the most recent status available at the moment of that purchase. The team wants a dataset-level join that does not expose later updates. How should it join the two datasets?

choices.text: Use purchase events as the base and perform a point-in-time accurate join to the offline status group on the customer identifier.
choices.explanation: The join accounts for the time of each purchase and selects the applicable historical feature values.

choices.text: Join purchases to the current online status on customer identifier only.
choices.explanation: The online value may include updates that had not happened at the time of the historical purchase.

choices.text: Choose the first recorded status for every customer and reuse it for all purchases.
choices.explanation: This may avoid later events, but ignores updates already available before each purchase.

choices.text: Join on customer identifier and keep whichever update has the smallest absolute time difference to the purchase.
choices.explanation: An update shortly after a purchase can be closer than the previous status, introducing leakage.

learning.reason: A point-in-time accurate join uses the base record as a time reference and selects eligible features from no later than the base event. Joining only on customer identity can leak future information.
learning.concept: SageMaker Feature Store point-in-time accurate joins

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Store vector metadata according to how queries use it
prompt: An Amazon S3 vector index contains vectors for support documents. Search requests must filter on a small region code. The application also returns a longer excerpt from each matching document, but the excerpt is never used in a filter. The team wants to keep both values in metadata without consuming the filterable metadata budget for the excerpt. What should it specify at index creation?

choices.text: Declare the region key as non-filterable and keep the excerpt key filterable.
choices.explanation: This prevents the query from using the region constraint while exposing an unnecessary field for filtering.

choices.text: Declare the excerpt key as non-filterable and keep the region key filterable.
choices.explanation: The search can filter by region and return the stored excerpt without making the excerpt filterable.

choices.text: Mark both keys as non-filterable and use the vector distance metric to enforce the region.
choices.explanation: A distance metric measures vector similarity. It does not enforce a region metadata condition.

choices.text: Make both keys filterable and reduce the number of matches returned per search.
choices.explanation: The result count does not change which metadata fields use the filterable metadata budget.

learning.reason: S3 Vectors supports declaring metadata keys as non-filterable when creating an index. Those values can still be returned, while filterable keys are usable in query constraints.
learning.concept: S3 Vectors non-filterable metadata configuration

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Create a redacted training corpus without changing the raw archive
prompt: A team stores historical support transcripts in a restricted S3 bucket. Before the records can be made available to the training pipeline, the team must mask customer contact information in a separate copy. It needs the transformed text files, not just the locations or labels of detected entities. Which approach meets the requirement with a managed batch job?

choices.text: Run PII identification in offsets mode and train on the original S3 prefix.
choices.explanation: The job reports where the identifiers are, but the training text would still contain them.

choices.text: Apply Amazon S3 default encryption to the originals and allow the training role to decrypt them.
choices.explanation: Encryption protects the stored originals from unauthorized access but does not mask text for an authorized consumer.

choices.text: Run an asynchronous Amazon Comprehend PII job in redaction mode and point the training pipeline to its designated S3 output.
choices.explanation: The job creates the masked copy without giving training consumers access to the raw transcripts.

choices.text: Enable redaction for responses from the deployed model without changing the training input.
choices.explanation: This acts after inference. The training pipeline would still ingest the underlying identifiers.

learning.reason: An Amazon Comprehend asynchronous PII job can run in redaction mode and write the masked text to a configured S3 output location. A job that only reports PII offsets does not produce the required sanitized corpus.
learning.concept: Amazon Comprehend asynchronous PII redaction mode and separate S3 output

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Detect a growing backlog in feature ingestion
prompt: An AWS Glue streaming job consumes click events to update features. The duration of each Spark micro-batch remains stable, but the feature data is arriving later and later. The team has enabled source-record timestamp and consumer-lag metrics. Which metric directly measures the age of the oldest source record in the processed batch relative to ingestion by Glue?

choices.text: The batch processing time metric (`streaming.batchProcessingTimeInMs`).
choices.explanation: It measures how long Glue takes to process a batch after it reaches the job, not the age of the source record.

choices.text: The number of records processed in a window (`streaming.numRecords`).
choices.explanation: It measures throughput, which can stay stable while the arrival age of records increases.

choices.text: The S3 output object's last-modified time by itself.
choices.explanation: It shows when an output was written, not the age of the oldest source event in that batch.

choices.text: The maximum consumer lag metric (`streaming.maxConsumerLagInMs`).
choices.explanation: It tracks the lag of the oldest record in the batch and can expose a source backlog.

learning.reason: The consumer lag metric is based on the age of a record before reaching Glue, so it can increase even when Spark batch execution duration is stable.
learning.concept: AWS Glue streaming maximum consumer lag versus batch processing time

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Extract a dated relational snapshot without reading the live instance
prompt: A feature engineering team needs several tables as of last night's Amazon RDS backup. Amazon Athena will query the exported data in Parquet. The source database cannot take any training-query load, and the team wants to avoid running a second database instance. What should the team do?

choices.text: Start an RDS snapshot export to S3 from the existing snapshot and select the needed tables.
choices.explanation: The managed export supplies the backup-time data in Parquet without operating another instance.

choices.text: Connect AWS Glue directly to the live database and extract the tables at a lower query concurrency.
choices.explanation: This still queries the source instance and does not use the required backup-time state.

choices.text: Restore the snapshot to a separate RDS instance and use Athena federated queries against it.
choices.explanation: This reads the right time point, but it requires a second running database and does not itself produce the Parquet export.

choices.text: Copy the RDS snapshot to another Region and point an Athena external table at the copied snapshot ARN.
choices.explanation: An RDS snapshot copy is still a database snapshot. It does not expose Parquet objects for Athena.

learning.reason: Snapshot export reads the backup rather than the running database and writes compressed Parquet objects to S3. It can export selected tables where supported.
learning.concept: RDS snapshot export to S3 Parquet

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep clickstream readers from competing for shard read capacity
prompt: An Amazon Kinesis data stream feeds a feature materialization job and two independent reporting jobs. All three currently read with shared throughput. The feature job falls behind during overlapping reads, even though producer utilization is below its limits. Which change gives the feature job up to 2 MB/s per shard independently of the reporting reads?

choices.text: Fetch records more frequently with the existing shared-throughput consumer.
choices.explanation: Polling more often does not reserve throughput and can add competition or throttling.

choices.text: Register the feature job as an enhanced fan-out consumer and configure it to subscribe to the shards.
choices.explanation: This gives the feature consumer dedicated read throughput without requiring the reporting jobs to stop.

choices.text: Switch the producer from PutRecords to PutRecord.
choices.explanation: The producer API does not change the capacity that the three consumers share.

choices.text: Raise the feature job's worker concurrency while keeping shared throughput.
choices.explanation: Additional workers do not establish dedicated throughput on a shard.

learning.reason: Shared-throughput readers compete for the same shard read capacity. Enhanced fan-out registers a consumer with independent read throughput per shard.
learning.concept: Kinesis enhanced fan-out for independent consumers

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reduce scans when queries read a few columns from wide training data
prompt: The preprocessing team stores daily training records as wide CSV files in S3. Athena typically reads only six columns out of several hundred. The team will migrate old partitions and update future writes, and wants to reduce bytes scanned while preserving all columns for occasional use. Which storage change should it make?

choices.text: Compress the existing CSV files and keep the CSV table definition.
choices.explanation: Compression may shrink files, but the row-based representation is still not optimized for reading a small subset of columns.

choices.text: Convert every row to JSON and retain every property in each object.
choices.explanation: This preserves fields but does not introduce columnar column pruning.

choices.text: Rewrite the records in Parquet and configure the external table for Parquet.
choices.explanation: Athena can skip the data blocks for most columns that are not referenced.

choices.text: Use a view to hide most columns and keep the raw CSV storage.
choices.explanation: The SQL projection is useful for callers, but it does not turn the CSV files into columnar storage.

learning.reason: Parquet stores column chunks separately, allowing Athena to read the projected columns. Compressing a row-based file can reduce its total size but does not provide equivalent column pruning.
learning.concept: Athena column pruning with Parquet

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Flatten nested training records without losing child items
prompt: A forecasting dataset has one JSON record per order, with a variable number of line items and a nested array of adjustments under each item. The team uses AWS Glue DynamicFrames and must preserve all adjustments and their relationship to the correct item and order. Which transformation should it use?

choices.text: Project the first line item and first adjustment as columns on the order.
choices.explanation: This drops additional elements from any multi-element array.

choices.text: Rename the arrays with apply_mapping and write them to one flat table without further transformation.
choices.explanation: Field mapping does not create the related tables or generate the required join keys.

choices.text: Aggregate all adjustments across the order before flattening the data.
choices.explanation: Aggregation removes individual adjustment-to-item relationships.

choices.text: Apply relationalize and retain the join keys in the resulting DynamicFrames.
choices.explanation: The separate outputs preserve variable-length entries and links back to the originating records.

learning.reason: Relationalize unnests nested attributes and moves arrays into related DynamicFrames with generated join keys. Keeping parent-child keys makes it possible to rebuild the associations after writing the records as separate tables.
learning.concept: Glue DynamicFrame relationalize and array-generated join keys

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Transcribe calls that switch languages within the same recording
prompt: A training-data pipeline transcribes archived support calls from S3. Callers often switch between English and Spanish in a single recording. The team wants one Amazon Transcribe batch job to recognize both languages in each file, without splitting the file at language boundaries. Which option should the job use?

choices.text: Enable IdentifyMultipleLanguages and supply the supported English and Spanish language options.
choices.explanation: The batch job can recognize and transcribe more than one language in an individual recording.

choices.text: Enable IdentifyLanguage and assume it transcribes all languages that appear in the recording.
choices.explanation: This mode selects the dominant language of the input rather than explicitly recognizing multiple languages.

choices.text: Run the full recording with LanguageCode set to English only.
choices.explanation: A fixed English language setting will not transcribe both languages as requested.

choices.text: Enable speaker labels and map language codes to individual speaker labels.
choices.explanation: Speaker diarization identifies speakers rather than languages and does not determine when a speaker switches languages.

learning.reason: Amazon Transcribe provides separate modes for identifying one dominant language and identifying multiple languages in a recording. The multiple-language mode can select from the supplied supported language options.
learning.concept: Amazon Transcribe batch IdentifyMultipleLanguages

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Backfill historical features without affecting online serving
prompt: A SageMaker Feature Store feature group has an online and an offline store. The team must load historical corrections for model retraining. Production scoring must keep using the same current online values, and point-in-time training joins must still use when each historic event occurred. Which two changes should the backfill writer make? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Set TargetStores to OfflineStore for the backfill records.
choices.explanation: The write updates the historical store without updating the online store.

choices.text: Omit TargetStores so writes use all configured stores.
choices.explanation: Allowing both configured stores does not meet the requirement to avoid changing serving state.

choices.text: Use each historical observation's original event time in the designated event-time feature.
choices.explanation: This preserves the temporal meaning used by point-in-time joins.

choices.text: Replace every event time with the timestamp when the backfill starts.
choices.explanation: Upload time does not represent when the original features were valid.

choices.text: Write the corrected records to OnlineStore only.
choices.explanation: This uses the serving store rather than the historical training store.

learning.reason: PutRecord can target the offline store independently. The event time represents when the features apply and should reflect the historical event rather than the upload time if training joins depend on it.
learning.concept: Feature Store PutRecord TargetStores and historical EventTime

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Rebuild a bounded feature interval without moving the normal checkpoint
prompt: An AWS Glue batch job uses job bookmarks and has already processed several successful runs. The team corrected a feature transformation and needs to reprocess data covered by two recorded bookmark run IDs. It wants the production checkpoint to stay in place and the backfilled outputs written to an isolated prefix. What should it do?

choices.text: Reset the job bookmark and run with the normal destination.
choices.explanation: Resetting changes the saved state and can re-read a broader set of input.

choices.text: Use bookmark pause with the intended from/to run IDs and configure an isolated destination.
choices.explanation: The job can replay the selected input interval without advancing its saved bookmark.

choices.text: Leave bookmarks enabled in ordinary mode and re-run the job from its current checkpoint.
choices.explanation: Normal mode processes new input after the checkpoint, not the previously processed interval.

choices.text: Disable bookmarks and let the job reprocess all historical inputs.
choices.explanation: This does not use the saved run boundaries to limit the replay.

learning.reason: Bookmark pause mode can process a range between run IDs without updating saved checkpoint state. Glue tracks sources rather than cleaning target data, so an isolated output prevents accidental mixing.
learning.concept: AWS Glue bookmark pause and bounded replay

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Increase feature-cache read bandwidth without expanding storage
prompt: The data preparation host uses a gp3 EBS volume as a local cache. The cache fits on the current volume and IOPS are adequate. Monitoring shows that sequential reads are limited by the volume's provisioned throughput. The instance supports higher EBS bandwidth. What is the most direct change?

choices.text: Increase the gp3 volume's capacity only.
choices.explanation: gp3 does not provide more throughput merely because capacity increases.

choices.text: Change to a larger S3 object size in the upstream bucket only.
choices.explanation: This may affect data ingestion efficiency but does not alter provisioned throughput of the cache volume.

choices.text: Increase the gp3 volume's provisioned throughput while retaining the required capacity and IOPS.
choices.explanation: This addresses the measured bottleneck without paying for unused storage.

choices.text: Increase provisioned IOPS only and leave the configured throughput unchanged.
choices.explanation: The provisioned bandwidth limit remains the same even though more operations may be allowed.

learning.reason: For gp3, provisioned throughput can be configured independently of capacity and, within service ratios and limits, without changing provisioned IOPS.
learning.concept: gp3 throughput provisioning independent of volume size

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Retry a Kinesis batch from its earliest failed record
prompt: A Lambda transform receives ordered Kinesis records with sequence numbers represented as s1 through s6. It processes all records and records failures at s3 and s5. The event source mapping has ReportBatchItemFailures enabled and batch bisection disabled. The transform is idempotent. Which response makes the retry begin at s3?

choices.text: Return only the sequence number for s5 because it is the last failed record.
choices.explanation: The retry would start at s5 and bypass the earlier failed s3 record.

choices.text: Throw an exception after writing both failures to the function log.
choices.explanation: The log is not a partial batch response. The function invocation is treated as failed.

choices.text: Return an empty batchItemFailures array and rely on the recorded error logs for the retry.
choices.explanation: An empty list reports success and does not tell the event source to replay the failures.

choices.text: Return batchItemFailures listing the actual sequence numbers corresponding to s3 and s5.
choices.explanation: Lambda uses the lowest reported sequence number and retries from s3.

learning.reason: Lambda treats the lowest sequence number in a valid partial batch response as the checkpoint for retry. It can replay later records in the batch, which is why idempotency matters.
learning.concept: Lambda partial batch responses for Kinesis and lowest-sequence checkpoint

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reject feature records that reference unknown product codes
prompt: A Glue feature pipeline joins transaction records to an approved product table. The product code repeats across transactions, and new transaction batches must be rejected if any non-null code is absent from the reference table. The pipeline already handles missing codes separately. Which Glue Data Quality check should it use?

choices.text: Apply ReferentialIntegrity to the non-null transaction codes against the product table's code column and require a match ratio of 1.
choices.explanation: This validates membership in the approved reference while allowing repeated transaction codes.

choices.text: Require IsUnique on the transaction product code.
choices.explanation: This rejects valid repeated codes and does not check whether a code appears in the reference.

choices.text: Require IsComplete on the transaction product code.
choices.explanation: Non-nullness does not establish reference membership.

choices.text: Compare the distinct code count in the two datasets and check whether the counts match.
choices.explanation: Sets can have equal counts without containing the same codes.

learning.reason: ReferentialIntegrity measures whether values in one dataset exist in the corresponding column or columns of a reference dataset. Its expression can require all included values to match.
learning.concept: Glue Data Quality ReferentialIntegrity across two datasets

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Interpret apparent identifier duplication in a profiling report
prompt: An AWS Glue DataBrew profile reports 1,200 non-null rows, a distinctValuesCount of 1,000, and a uniqueValuesCount of 900 for an event identifier. The team is assessing whether the field can serve as a unique key. What does the report show?

choices.text: There are 1,000 rows with nonrepeated identifiers. The remaining 200 rows must have missing identifiers.
choices.explanation: The premise has no nulls. Distinct count is a count of different values, not singleton rows.

choices.text: There are 1,000 identifier values, of which 900 occur once and 100 occur more than once. The column is not a unique key.
choices.explanation: Subtracting the unique count from the distinct count gives the number of repeated identifier values.

choices.text: There are exactly 100 rows that contain duplicated identifiers across all occurrences.
choices.explanation: The difference counts repeated identifier values, not all rows carrying those values.

choices.text: The column is a valid unique key because its unique count is greater than zero.
choices.explanation: A unique key requires every identifier to be unique, so some singletons are insufficient.

learning.reason: Distinct count is the number of different values present. Unique count is the number of values appearing exactly once. A repeated identifier violates the key requirement even if no value is null.
learning.concept: DataBrew profile distinct values versus values occurring once

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Scale numerical features for a distance-based model
prompt: A nearest-neighbor model uses two approximately symmetric numeric features. One is recorded in milliseconds and the other in small unitless counts. Neither feature should dominate due to units, and the training transformation should center each feature at zero and target unit variance. Which Data Wrangler transform should the team use?

choices.text: Apply min-max scaling to a fixed 0–1 range.
choices.explanation: Min-max scaling aligns ranges but does not target zero means and unit variances.

choices.text: Apply a log transform to the larger feature and leave the other unchanged.
choices.explanation: A log transform can compress large values but does not guarantee the requested center and variance.

choices.text: Apply the Standard scaler, using the parameters fitted on training data consistently in later stages.
choices.explanation: This transforms each feature using its own mean and standard deviation.

choices.text: Apply ordinal encoding to both continuous features.
choices.explanation: Ordinal encoding would replace numeric values with ordered category codes, not standardize their scale.

learning.reason: Standard scaling subtracts the feature mean and divides by its standard deviation. This addresses unit-driven scale differences while keeping the numeric information.
learning.concept: Data Wrangler Standard scaler for centered unit-variance features

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Represent new domain terms from their character patterns
prompt: A search application needs a Word2Vec representation for equipment terms. New model names often share meaningful character sequences with training words but do not appear in the training vocabulary. The team uses a supported single-instance BlazingText Skip-gram configuration. Which change enables vectors for those unseen tokens?

choices.text: Raise the minimum word frequency so the vocabulary contains only the most common words.
choices.explanation: A stricter vocabulary cutoff makes more words unavailable and does not enable composition for unseen terms.

choices.text: Increase the number of epochs without changing the word-only model.
choices.explanation: Extra passes do not cause words absent from all training examples to acquire word vectors.

choices.text: Replace every unseen word with the same fixed token and keep word-only embeddings.
choices.explanation: A single fallback gives all new model names the same representation and loses their character distinctions.

choices.text: Train with subwords enabled so embeddings can be composed from learned character n-grams.
choices.explanation: This uses shared word fragments to represent inputs absent from the word vocabulary.

learning.reason: BlazingText Word2Vec can train embeddings for character subwords. When subwords are enabled, it can construct a vector for a token outside the word vocabulary from its character n-grams.
learning.concept: BlazingText Word2Vec subword embeddings for out-of-vocabulary input

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prepare prompt examples for managed model distillation
prompt: A team wants an Amazon Bedrock student model to reproduce how a compatible teacher handles a specific set of internal drafting requests. It can assemble representative allowed prompts, but it has not collected approved human-written outputs for every request. The team is using Bedrock's prompt-based distillation path. What training input should it prepare?

choices.text: Prepare representative task prompts in the supported JSONL format and let the teacher generate the targets.
choices.explanation: The distillation workflow uses generated responses on representative prompts to adapt the student.

choices.text: Upload unrelated unlabeled documents to continue pretraining the student without using the teacher.
choices.explanation: Additional pretraining does not use the teacher's response behavior as the training signal.

choices.text: Use only the student's current outputs as reference targets and do not invoke the teacher.
choices.explanation: These targets would not transfer knowledge or task behavior from the teacher.

choices.text: Supply only a list of production model IDs, without requests or responses.
choices.explanation: The workflow needs task examples from which to obtain suitable training targets.

learning.reason: Bedrock can use task prompts from a JSONL training input to generate teacher responses. These teacher responses form synthetic training targets for the compatible student model.
learning.concept: Bedrock Model Distillation prompt datasets and generated teacher responses

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Correct existing image annotations without losing the original labels
prompt: An object detection team has completed initial bounding-box labeling in SageMaker Ground Truth. A second team will move the existing boxes where needed and the reviewer must be able to compare the original and adjusted annotations. Which two settings should the engineer use? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use the original output manifest as input to a bounding-box adjustment job.
choices.explanation: The manifest supplies the original boxes that workers need to inspect and edit.

choices.text: Choose verification rather than adjustment, with the expectation that workers will edit the boxes.
choices.explanation: Verification collects judgments about existing annotations and is not the adjustment workflow.

choices.text: Pass a manifest that contains only image URIs, with no original label attributes.
choices.explanation: This removes the annotations workers are supposed to edit.

choices.text: Write adjusted labels under a LabelAttributeName different from that used by the original job.
choices.explanation: The adjustment remains distinct from the original annotations.

choices.text: Reuse the original job's LabelAttributeName for the adjustment API request.
choices.explanation: The adjustment or verification job must use a distinct label attribute name.

learning.reason: An adjustment job must see the original annotations so workers can change them directly. Ground Truth requires a different label attribute name for the adjustment job created with the API.
learning.concept: Ground Truth bounding-box adjustment input and output label attribute

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Measure representation across two groups before training
prompt: An existing SageMaker Clarify customer is auditing a labeled training dataset. The auditor first wants to know whether one of two demographic groups has fewer records overall. The fraction of positive labels within each group will be assessed separately. Which pre-training bias metric answers the first question?

choices.text: Difference in Proportions of Labels (DPL).
choices.explanation: DPL compares within-group fractions of positive observed outcomes, not the number of records belonging to each group.

choices.text: Class Imbalance (CI).
choices.explanation: CI compares representation across the groups without depending on how many of each group's records have positive labels.

choices.text: Accuracy Difference (AD).
choices.explanation: This requires model predictions and compares their accuracy across groups.

choices.text: Counterfactual Fliptest (FT).
choices.explanation: This post-training metric compares predictions for similar observations across groups rather than comparing training sample counts.

learning.reason: Class Imbalance measures group representation in the dataset. Difference in Proportions of Labels compares observed positive outcome rates and can be zero even when the groups have very different sizes.
learning.concept: Clarify pre-training Class Imbalance versus label disparity

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Select a foundation model for one-turn visual reasoning
prompt: A Bedrock application receives a photo of an equipment label and a text question in the same request. It must return a text answer that depends on details in the photo. The team wants a single model invocation with no separate OCR stage. Which two model properties are required? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Support for both IMAGE and TEXT as input modalities.
choices.explanation: The model must read the photo and the accompanying question.

choices.text: Support for IMAGE as an output modality, regardless of the model's inputs.
choices.explanation: Image generation says nothing about whether that model can read the submitted image.

choices.text: Support for an EMBEDDING output modality only.
choices.explanation: A vector output does not provide the required natural-language answer.

choices.text: Support for response streaming with no image input modality.
choices.explanation: Streaming changes how a response is delivered; it does not let the model consume unsupported image inputs.

choices.text: Support for TEXT as an output modality.
choices.explanation: The requested result is a text answer.

learning.reason: A single-model design must accept each modality supplied in the request and generate the requested output modality. An image output capability cannot substitute for an image input capability.
learning.concept: Bedrock foundation model input and output modalities

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Retrieve documents by exact part codes and natural language
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base on Amazon OpenSearch Serverless stores a filterable text field. Users ask both paraphrased questions and queries containing identifiers such as HX-31A. Semantic retrieval works for paraphrases but misses some documents whose strongest signal is the exact identifier. The team must keep semantic matching. What should it change?

choices.text: Keep SEMANTIC search and increase the generation model's temperature.
choices.explanation: Generation randomness is unrelated to locating documents with an exact identifier.

choices.text: Ask the generation model to extract part codes from the contexts that the current retriever returns.
choices.explanation: Post-processing can find a code in a returned chunk but cannot recover a document the retriever omitted.

choices.text: Set the retrieval search type to HYBRID.
choices.explanation: The search can use both the text of the chunks and their vector representation.

choices.text: Reduce retrieval to a single result while leaving the search type as SEMANTIC.
choices.explanation: Returning fewer candidates does not add an exact-text retrieval path.

learning.reason: Hybrid retrieval combines vector similarity with a text search in a compatible vector store. Text search gives exact identifiers another retrieval path without giving up semantic similarity.
learning.concept: Bedrock Knowledge Bases hybrid lexical and semantic retrieval

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Choose an algorithm for multivariate outliers without labels
prompt: A manufacturer collects sensor vectors from machines running many production modes. It has representative historical observations, but too few confirmed failures to build a reliable classifier. The team needs an anomaly score that flags unusual combinations within the current observation, not a forecast of future readings. Which SageMaker built-in algorithm fits?

choices.text: Train a binary classifier with every unconfirmed observation marked as a normal example.
choices.explanation: That treats the absence of investigation as a reliable label and provides no usable confirmed-failure class.

choices.text: Use DeepAR to forecast future sensor values and treat its forecast output as the anomaly score.
choices.explanation: DeepAR generates forecasts. Its output is not directly an anomaly score for an observed vector.

choices.text: Use IP Insights with each sensor value as one input field.
choices.explanation: IP Insights is designed for entity-to-IPv4 usage patterns, not arbitrary multivariate sensor measurements.

choices.text: Train Random Cut Forest on historical sensor vectors and score incoming observations.
choices.explanation: This produces anomaly scores without requiring confirmed-failure labels.

learning.reason: Random Cut Forest is an unsupervised algorithm for scoring the unusualness of observations in a dataset. It can detect deviations across multiple features without labeled anomaly examples.
learning.concept: Random Cut Forest for unlabeled multivariate anomaly scoring

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Balance routine-request cost against quality on complex prompts
prompt: A Bedrock application currently sends both routine and complex requests to its most capable language model. A cheaper model from the same supported model family is adequate for routine prompts. The team wants Bedrock to choose between the models based on expected response quality for each prompt without creating a separate classifier. What should it use?

choices.text: Configure a supported intelligent prompt router for the two Bedrock models and invoke it through its routing identifier.
choices.explanation: Bedrock can choose a candidate for each prompt based on the configured routing behavior.

choices.text: Create an inference profile that sends every request to the same strongest model.
choices.explanation: Region routing or application attribution for one model does not select a cheaper model for easier prompts.

choices.text: Use the cheapest model for every prompt and increase its output token limit.
choices.explanation: The larger output limit does not provide the stronger model on prompts where its quality is needed.

choices.text: Randomly split traffic 50/50 between the models.
choices.explanation: A fixed random split does not consider the relative suitability of the models for each request.

learning.reason: Intelligent prompt routing predicts the relative quality of candidate models and routes a request to an appropriate supported model. It targets cost and quality trade-offs at request time.
learning.concept: Bedrock Intelligent Prompt Routing for compatible model candidates

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Extract invoice totals and line items across different vendor layouts
prompt: An accounts-payable team wants to extract summary fields and itemized charges from single-page invoices with inconsistent layouts. It wants Amazon Textract to provide normalized expense fields and separate line item groups without manually mapping all OCR lines. Which API should it use?

choices.text: Use DetectDocumentText and expect normalized expense field types to be present in its line blocks.
choices.explanation: Text detection returns OCR elements rather than the expense-specific summary and item groups.

choices.text: Use AnalyzeExpense and consume SummaryFields and LineItemGroups.
choices.explanation: The expense-specific response provides these structures for the downstream workflow.

choices.text: Use AnalyzeID and interpret identity document fields as invoice fields.
choices.explanation: AnalyzeID returns normalized information for supported identity documents, not invoices.

choices.text: Use Amazon Comprehend entity recognition on the raw image bytes.
choices.explanation: Comprehend analyzes text. This input and approach do not provide structured invoice line items.

learning.reason: AnalyzeExpense is designed for invoices and receipts. The response separates summary fields from line item groups, unlike plain text detection.
learning.concept: Amazon Textract AnalyzeExpense for summary fields and line items

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Adapt a foundation model without updating all of its weights
prompt: A team has labeled examples for a narrow task and a supported Amazon Nova customization recipe on SageMaker AI. It wants a learned task-specific adaptation rather than per-request prompt examples. The team also wants to train a small set of additional parameters while keeping the original base parameters fixed. What should it choose?

choices.text: Use full-rank supervised fine-tuning.
choices.explanation: It learns from the examples but updates the full parameter set rather than only adapters.

choices.text: Use few-shot examples only in each inference prompt.
choices.explanation: Prompt examples can guide output behavior, but they do not produce a learned adaptation.

choices.text: Use a supervised fine-tuning recipe with low-rank adaptation.
choices.explanation: The task examples train a small set of adapter parameters while the base weights remain fixed.

choices.text: Continue pretraining the entire model on unlabeled text.
choices.explanation: This applies a different learning signal and does not meet the requirement to update only a small adapter.

learning.reason: LoRA is parameter-efficient fine-tuning. It trains compact low-rank updates rather than updating all base model parameters.
learning.concept: SageMaker AI Nova supervised fine-tuning with LoRA adapters

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Choose a tuning strategy that learns from earlier trials
prompt: Each training run for a model takes several hours. The team can run only a modest number of trials and one or two in parallel. It wants validation results from completed trials to inform which hyperparameters to try next. Which SageMaker automatic model tuning strategy should it choose?

choices.text: Use random search and set the same random seed for all trials.
choices.explanation: A seed can make selections reproducible but does not make them dependent on validation feedback.

choices.text: Use grid search over evenly spaced values.
choices.explanation: The grid is defined in advance and does not adapt choices based on results.

choices.text: Run all trials with the current model's hyperparameters and compare finish times.
choices.explanation: Repeating one configuration does not explore the hyperparameter space.

choices.text: Use Bayesian optimization with the available limited parallelism.
choices.explanation: It uses completed trial measurements to guide future parameter choices.

learning.reason: Bayesian optimization uses the results of previously completed trials when proposing new configurations. With limited parallelism, more proposals can make use of that feedback.
learning.concept: SageMaker AMT Bayesian optimization for expensive, low-parallelism trials

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Stop boosting when held-out performance stops improving
prompt: An Amazon SageMaker XGBoost job is allocated up to 1,000 boosting rounds. Training loss continues to improve, but the validation metric has stopped improving for many rounds. The next job should stop adaptively when held-out performance plateaus without requiring the team to guess the exact best round in advance. Which configuration should it use?

choices.text: Provide validation data, select the validation metric, and set early_stopping_rounds.
choices.explanation: The job can stop after the metric fails to improve for the configured number of rounds.

choices.text: Set the learning rate to zero once training loss drops below the previous run's final value.
choices.explanation: This is based on training loss and does not identify a validation plateau.

choices.text: Raise num_round and remove the validation dataset.
choices.explanation: This does not measure the held-out performance required for adaptive stopping.

choices.text: Set a shorter job wall-clock timeout and use the final model from whichever round happened to finish.
choices.explanation: A time boundary does not track improving validation quality.

learning.reason: XGBoost early stopping uses the specified validation metric and a patience expressed in boosting rounds. The upper bound on the number of rounds remains separate from adaptive stopping.
learning.concept: SageMaker XGBoost early_stopping_rounds and a validation channel

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Check and mitigate regression on older tasks during specialization
prompt: A Nova Forge team adapts a model to a specialized support workflow. A pilot improved the new task but degraded performance on established tasks. It can use relevant base-distribution examples in the supported data-mixing workflow and has independent evaluation data. Which two steps best address the regression? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Evaluate only the new support task after every run.
choices.explanation: Improvement on one task alone does not detect older-task regression.

choices.text: Include representative earlier-task examples alongside the new task in the supported training mixture.
choices.explanation: The model continues to see both behaviors during adaptation.

choices.text: Evaluate the candidate and baseline on held-out examples for both established and new tasks.
choices.explanation: This makes measurement of the regression independent of the examples used for weight updates.

choices.text: Copy all held-out older-task prompts into training and reuse them for the final acceptance evaluation.
choices.explanation: That contaminates the acceptance set and can overstate retained generalization.

choices.text: Remove all earlier-task examples and train longer on the specialized prompts.
choices.explanation: More updates on the narrow distribution do not address the demonstrated loss on older tasks.

learning.reason: A task-only training distribution can favor the new behavior at the expense of earlier skills. Combining representative earlier examples with specialization data can help mitigate forgetting. Independent evaluation of both sets of tasks measures the trade-off.
learning.concept: Data mixing during Nova Forge SFT and separate earlier-task evaluation

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Change training logic without rebuilding the framework container
prompt: A SageMaker AI job uses a standard PyTorch training container. The team changes its training script and helper module every experiment but leaves the framework and system dependencies stable. It wants the job to run the latest approved script without building a new Docker image for each change. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Upload the helper only to the input-data channel and run the old command unchanged.
choices.explanation: Training data files alone do not select the new script or load its helper module.

choices.text: Use the approved framework image and configure SourceCode with the script directory and training command.
choices.explanation: The managed job receives the current script and helper code without requiring a new image.

choices.text: Embed each version of the source into a new framework image.
choices.explanation: This works as a packaging method but requires the repeated image rebuild the team wants to avoid.

choices.text: Write the changed script only to the output model archive after each job.
choices.explanation: An output artifact does not change the code that the job executed.

learning.reason: SageMaker script mode packages source code separately from the framework image. ModelTrainer can populate the job from the source directory and execute the supplied training command.
learning.concept: SageMaker AI ModelTrainer script mode and SourceCode

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Preserve the effective batch size as device memory changes
prompt: A SageMaker training run uses one GPU with 16 examples per optimizer update. A longer input sequence now fits only 4 examples per forward/backward pass. The engineer wants an update to still use 16 examples without increasing the peak per-pass batch. Which change provides the intended effective batch size?

choices.text: Use a batch size of 4 and perform an optimizer update after every pass for four times as many steps.
choices.explanation: This changes the number of updates, but each update still uses only 4 examples.

choices.text: Keep a batch size of 16 but increase gradient accumulation to 4.
choices.explanation: Each pass still needs memory for 16 examples, exceeding the stated capacity.

choices.text: Use a per-device batch size of 4 and accumulate gradients for 4 passes before each update.
choices.explanation: Four passes times four examples provide the required effective batch of 16.

choices.text: Use a batch size of 4 and leave accumulation at 1 while scaling up the learning rate.
choices.explanation: The learning rate does not change how many examples contribute to an update.

learning.reason: With one device, the effective batch size equals the number of examples per pass multiplied by the number of gradient accumulation passes before each optimizer update.
learning.concept: Gradient accumulation trades per-pass batch size for more passes per optimizer update

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Make a classification response conform to a required JSON schema
prompt: A Bedrock classifier writes a text response that an application consumes as an object with a fixed set of keys and types. Prompt examples usually work, but the model sometimes returns a prose preface or the wrong structure. The selected model and API support structured outputs. The workflow must not invoke a tool. What should the engineer configure?

choices.text: Add a few more example JSON responses and keep the normal text output mode.
choices.explanation: Examples can help but do not enforce the required schema.

choices.text: Set temperature to zero and leave the response unconstrained.
choices.explanation: Less random decoding does not guarantee field names, types, or the absence of prose.

choices.text: Add an extra metadata filter to the knowledge base.
choices.explanation: A metadata filter selects retrieval results, not the response structure.

choices.text: Request a structured response using the supported JSON schema for the response object.
choices.explanation: The schema constrains the generated structure for downstream parsing.

learning.reason: Bedrock structured outputs can use a supported JSON schema to constrain non-tool model responses. Prompt wording and generation randomness do not enforce schema compliance by themselves.
learning.concept: Bedrock JSON schema structured outputs

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Improve ranking after retrieval without changing the corpus
prompt: A RAG retriever returns 40 candidates, and the right passages are usually in that set. Several are ranked below broad but less useful matches. The generation model can receive only six passages. The team needs a query-aware second-stage score without rebuilding the vector index. What should it add?

choices.text: Pass the query and retrieved candidates to a supported reranker and take the six highest-ranked passages.
choices.explanation: The second stage can promote useful passages that were retrieved but not initially in the top six.

choices.text: Take the first six retrieval results and increase the generation temperature.
choices.explanation: The passages that ranked below the cutoff are still excluded.

choices.text: Change the embedding model for queries only and keep the old corpus vectors.
choices.explanation: Vectors produced under different configurations may not be comparable, and this does not rerank the current candidates.

choices.text: Increase the output token limit without changing the passages given to the model.
choices.explanation: The response can be longer, but the generator still receives the same selected context.

learning.reason: A reranker takes the query and retrieved candidates, estimates each document's relevance, and places stronger matches earlier before selection. It can improve ordering within the candidate set, but cannot include items absent from it.
learning.concept: Bedrock reranking over an existing retrieval candidate set

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Make a reported improvement reproducible for a later reviewer
prompt: Two SageMaker classifiers are trained with different settings. A reviewer needs to determine whether the reported improvement came from the settings or a different split, and then reproduce the training run. The team already uses managed MLflow. What should it record for each run?

choices.text: Log only the highest validation score achieved by either run.
choices.explanation: A score by itself does not show the test conditions, code, or hyperparameters.

choices.text: Log parameters and validation metrics with the same metric definitions, and attach the exact code revision and versioned dataset/split references.
choices.explanation: The reviewer can determine whether runs share a split and recover their inputs and settings.

choices.text: Log the current S3 prefix without recording versions or the split manifest.
choices.explanation: The same prefix can point to different data later, so it does not identify the original experiment.

choices.text: Keep the latest checkpoint without associating it with a run.
choices.explanation: The checkpoint cannot establish the preceding run configuration or evaluation split by itself.

learning.reason: A reproducible MLflow run records the relevant parameters, comparable metrics, and artifacts or stable references to the code and data used. A metric alone cannot show whether inputs changed.
learning.concept: MLflow run provenance with parameters, metrics, and versioned code/data references

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Detect input distribution drift before labels are available
prompt: An existing SageMaker Model Monitor customer captures production inputs. Verified labels arrive a week later. A numeric field retains the correct type and is rarely null, but its value distribution has changed after a data-provider update. The team needs a daily alert for this input change before labels arrive. What should it monitor?

choices.text: Wait for the verified labels and use model quality accuracy as the only daily indicator.
choices.explanation: This cannot deliver the requested same-day detection before the labels arrive.

choices.text: Use only a data-type check on the field.
choices.explanation: A numeric field can remain numeric even when its values follow a different distribution.

choices.text: Use the data quality baseline drift check on captured input and tune the comparison threshold to the allowed distribution distance.
choices.explanation: This identifies the distribution shift even though the field type and completeness have not changed.

choices.text: Compare only the fraction of records whose field is present.
choices.explanation: Completeness may remain stable during a change in numeric values.

learning.reason: A data quality monitor can compare the current feature distribution to an existing approved baseline without ground-truth labels. Delayed labels are needed for evaluating model accuracy rather than this input characteristic.
learning.concept: SageMaker Model Monitor baseline_drift_check for input distributions

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Compare two generated responses with a human preference rating
prompt: An editor wants internal reviewers to compare two Bedrock summarization models on the same requests. They should see the outputs for each prompt side by side and report which version they prefer, with the strength of that preference on a five-point scale. Which setup fits?

choices.text: Run separate thumbs-up/down evaluations on each model without showing paired answers.
choices.explanation: Independent binary ratings do not measure the requested paired strength of preference.

choices.text: Run an automatic exact-match evaluator against one reference summary.
choices.explanation: Exact matching does not collect a human preference between the model outputs.

choices.text: Send the two models different prompt datasets and compare their average response lengths.
choices.explanation: This does not collect paired judgments and introduces different task inputs.

choices.text: Create a human-based evaluation for both models and select the five-point Likert preference rating with an editorial rubric.
choices.explanation: The workforce compares paired outputs for each prompt and records preference strength.

learning.reason: A human-based model evaluation can collect a five-point Likert preference between two responses using reviewer instructions. This differs from independent binary judgment of each response.
learning.concept: Bedrock human model evaluation paired Likert preference

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Explain a single prediction to a model reviewer
prompt: A decision-support classifier has a global feature-importance chart, but an auditor needs to understand why one particular record received a high score. The request is for feature-level contributions to that individual prediction relative to a representative baseline. Which result should the engineer provide?

choices.text: Compute local SHAP values for the selected record and show the direction and size of the feature contributions.
choices.explanation: The attributions apply to this record's output rather than to the dataset on average.

choices.text: Show the dataset-wide mean absolute SHAP ranking without any local results.
choices.explanation: It lists important features overall but loses the direction and magnitude for the selected prediction.

choices.text: Show only the model's overall accuracy on the test set.
choices.explanation: Accuracy measures correctness across records and does not explain the selected result.

choices.text: Show feature correlations from the raw training data and infer that the strongest correlation caused the prediction.
choices.explanation: Input correlations are not model attributions for a specific record.

learning.reason: Local SHAP values explain how features contribute to the selected prediction relative to a baseline. Global summaries describe aggregate behavior and may not match individual explanations.
learning.concept: Local feature attribution with SHAP versus global importance

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Measure ordered word overlap without requiring contiguous wording
prompt: A summarization evaluator must score the wording of each output against a reference. The scoring requirement is to reward the longest matching sequence of words that preserves order while allowing gaps. Which metric implements that requirement?

choices.text: ROUGE-2.
choices.explanation: It measures overlapping contiguous bigrams rather than the longest shared subsequence.

choices.text: ROUGE-L.
choices.explanation: It compares the longest matching word sequence, allowing gaps.

choices.text: BERTScore.
choices.explanation: It compares contextual token embeddings for semantic similarity, not the stated subsequence rule.

choices.text: Exact match.
choices.explanation: It requires the whole answer to match, so it does not reward a shared sequence with gaps.

learning.reason: ROUGE-L is based on a longest common subsequence with the reference. Unlike a contiguous n-gram match, a subsequence can preserve token order even when intervening words differ.
learning.concept: ROUGE-L for longest common subsequence overlap

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Separate poor retrieval from poor response generation
prompt: Two retrieval configurations are being compared on the same knowledge base. A domain expert has prepared questions with reference passages. The team needs to tell whether results are related to the question and whether they contain all the information in the reference passage. It does not want to run a generator for this diagnosis. Which two metrics should the retrieve-only evaluation use? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Faithfulness of the generated answer.
choices.explanation: It compares a generated response to supporting material, and this job has no response generation.

choices.text: Context relevance.
choices.explanation: It measures whether the retrieved passages address the question.

choices.text: Correctness of the generated response.
choices.explanation: It needs an answer to assess, not only the retrieved contexts.

choices.text: Context coverage.
choices.explanation: It measures how much of the information found in the ground-truth text appears in the retrieved passages.

choices.text: Helpfulness of the generated response.
choices.explanation: This is a response-level quality measurement, not a retrieval-only diagnostic.

learning.reason: Context relevance rates whether retrieved passages relate to the question. Context coverage compares retrieved content to the ground-truth passages. Both can be assessed without generating an answer.
learning.concept: Bedrock retrieve-only RAG ContextRelevance and ContextCoverage

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Automate a domain-specific grading rule for model output
prompt: A Bedrock team must evaluate whether a generated policy explanation reports the applicable policy exception and states when it takes effect. Language fluency alone is insufficient. Reviewers already have a written scoring rubric and authoritative examples. How can the team run the same domain-specific rubric at scale and collect consistent structured scores?

choices.text: Use only a generic coherence metric.
choices.explanation: Readable wording does not show whether the exception and date are factually correct.

choices.text: Evaluate by counting the number of tokens in each model response.
choices.explanation: Length cannot determine whether the required policy facts are present and correct.

choices.text: Create a model-as-a-judge job with a custom metric whose rubric scores the exception and effective date, along with the required score schema.
choices.explanation: The evaluator grades the stated business requirement instead of using fluency as a proxy.

choices.text: Increase the generator's temperature and treat diverse responses as higher-scoring outputs.
choices.explanation: Generation diversity does not apply or validate the domain rubric.

learning.reason: A custom model-as-a-judge evaluation can use a defined evaluator prompt, scoring instructions, and an output schema for the specific criterion. The same rubric can be applied across candidates and benchmark items.
learning.concept: Bedrock LLM-as-a-judge evaluation with a custom rubric and score schema

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Select a classifier under a minimum recall constraint
prompt: An alert-triage team uses SageMaker Linear Learner for binary classification. In validation, it must retain at least 95% recall to catch critical incidents. Among operating points that meet this floor, it wants the highest precision to reduce false alarms. Which configuration aligns model selection with that requirement?

choices.text: Select by accuracy and accept the default threshold.
choices.explanation: Accuracy can be high without meeting a recall floor for the positive class.

choices.text: Select by recall_at_target_precision and set the target precision to 0.95.
choices.explanation: This constrains precision and optimizes recall, reversing the operational requirement.

choices.text: Select the highest AUC and declare the recall floor satisfied without checking a threshold.
choices.explanation: AUC aggregates ranking performance across thresholds and does not establish recall at the chosen operating point.

choices.text: Set the selection criterion to precision_at_target_recall and set target_recall to 0.95.
choices.explanation: This asks for higher precision while respecting the required recall target.

learning.reason: Linear Learner can select a binary classifier using precision at a target recall. This uses the business requirement directly rather than optimizing a single aggregate metric over unconstrained behavior.
learning.concept: Linear Learner precision_at_target_recall and target_recall

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Choose synchronous GPU hosting for an image model
prompt: An inspection station sends a small image to a SageMaker endpoint and waits for a defect prediction before advancing the production line. The custom model depends on CUDA and cannot run on a CPU. An already-loaded model returns results within the station's response target. Which deployment target supports this design?

choices.text: Deploy the model on a SageMaker real-time endpoint using a supported GPU instance.
choices.explanation: A GPU-backed real-time endpoint can serve synchronous inference from a loaded container.

choices.text: Use Serverless Inference with provisioned concurrency.
choices.explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps capacity warm but does not make a GPU available for Serverless Inference.

choices.text: Host the model on a GPU-backed SageMaker Asynchronous Inference endpoint.
choices.explanation: The GPU is compatible, but asynchronous inference queues work and returns an output location instead of the prediction in the same response.

choices.text: Deploy to a CPU-only real-time endpoint and scale it out horizontally.
choices.explanation: Increasing CPU capacity does not supply the accelerator required by the model.

learning.reason: An instance-based real-time endpoint can host the model on a supported GPU instance and return the prediction synchronously. Serverless Inference does not provide GPUs.
learning.concept: SageMaker real-time GPU hosting versus Serverless Inference limitations

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Route a request to one model on a shared endpoint
prompt: An application serves hundreds of compatible models through an existing SageMaker multi-model endpoint. All model artifacts are stored under the endpoint's configured model-data prefix. For each request the API has the model artifact's relative path. How should the application choose the requested model without creating a new endpoint?

choices.text: Set TargetVariant to the relative S3 path while leaving TargetModel empty.
choices.explanation: TargetVariant selects a production variant rather than an artifact within a multi-model endpoint.

choices.text: Call InvokeEndpoint on the shared endpoint and set TargetModel to the artifact's relative path.
choices.explanation: The endpoint uses the target path under its configured model-data location.

choices.text: Put the complete S3 bucket URL in the endpoint name.
choices.explanation: EndpointName identifies a hosted endpoint, not its model artifact.

choices.text: Update the endpoint configuration before every request to switch the active model.
choices.explanation: The multi-model endpoint can select a model per invocation without changing the endpoint configuration.

learning.reason: A multi-model endpoint uses the TargetModel parameter to locate and load the requested relative model path. Production variant routing and separate endpoint selection do not select an artifact within the multi-model container.
learning.concept: SageMaker multi-model endpoint TargetModel

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Accept individual requests too large and slow for synchronous processing
prompt: A SageMaker image service receives independent requests throughout the day. An image bundle can be hundreds of MB and take several minutes to process. The API can return an acceptance response and the application can pick up the result asynchronously. Requests should enter the queue as they arrive. Which inference option best fits?

choices.text: Use a standard synchronous real-time invocation and increase only the client timeout.
choices.explanation: A client timeout setting cannot raise the service's payload and processing limits.

choices.text: Run all requests together in one Batch Transform job at the end of each day.
choices.explanation: That delays intake and execution until the batch is assembled, contrary to processing incoming queued requests.

choices.text: Use Asynchronous Inference and submit each request using its S3 input location.
choices.explanation: The endpoint queues and processes individual items and makes the result available independently of the initial API response.

choices.text: Use Serverless Inference with a larger memory tier and return results synchronously.
choices.explanation: More serverless memory does not provide the required combination of large payload, long processing, and queued execution.

learning.reason: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference queues requests, handles larger payloads and longer processing than ordinary real-time inference, and can write results to S3. It does not require collecting the requests into one batch.
learning.concept: SageMaker Asynchronous Inference for queued large individual requests

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Run a large offline prompt dataset through a Bedrock model
prompt: A team must label 80,000 documents with a Bedrock model that supports batch inference. It already assembled compatible inference records in JSONL on S3, and can wait hours for results. The team does not want to manage thousands of client-side requests or continuously running workers. What should it configure?

choices.text: Send each record with ConverseStream and keep every client connection open until all jobs complete.
choices.explanation: This requires operating the many individual online requests the team wants to avoid.

choices.text: Run a model customization job on the unlabeled documents and read the model weights as labels.
choices.explanation: Customization changes the model, not a dataset of per-record inference results.

choices.text: Start a knowledge base ingestion job on the JSONL and treat its ingestion manifest as inference output.
choices.explanation: Ingestion indexes data and reports its status. It does not run the requested classification prompts.

choices.text: Submit a batch model invocation job with the S3 input and output locations and an appropriately scoped job role.
choices.explanation: The managed job handles the prompt records and stores the results without continuously running application workers.

learning.reason: Bedrock batch inference accepts prompt records from S3 in a model invocation job and writes outputs to S3. It is designed for workloads that do not need interactive latency.
learning.concept: Bedrock batch inference job with S3 inputs and outputs

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Deploy a compatible externally trained foundation model on Bedrock
prompt: A research group has already customized an open-weight foundation model outside AWS. The model architecture and exported artifacts are supported by Bedrock Custom Model Import. The team wants to invoke those exact weights through Bedrock without repeating fine-tuning. What should it do?

choices.text: Place the compliant model artifacts at the supported S3 location, create a model import job, and invoke the imported model.
choices.explanation: This imports the trained weights for Bedrock inference without another tuning run.
