choices.text: Select the public base model directly and label the requests with the internal model name.
choices.explanation: Request labels do not change which model weights are loaded.

choices.text: Upload the weights as documents in a knowledge base and synchronize its vector index.
choices.explanation: Knowledge base ingestion prepares retrieval data rather than importing model parameter files.

choices.text: Create an inference profile for the public base model and attach the group's S3 URI as a prompt variable.
choices.explanation: A profile and prompt variable do not import or activate trained parameter weights.

learning.reason: Custom Model Import lets Bedrock bring in a compatible model artifact and register it as an imported model. Choosing a public base model with a similar name would not load the group's weights.
learning.concept: Bedrock Custom Model Import for compatible externally produced model artifacts

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Let an application execute an agent-selected action after its own approval
prompt: A Bedrock agent identifies when it needs a procurement estimate and extracts the inputs for an existing read-only pricing service. The application must review the extracted inputs before it calls the service inside its own trusted environment. It wants the agent to continue the conversation after the application provides the result. What should the action group use?

choices.text: Configure the action group's Lambda to call the service directly before returning a response to the application.
choices.explanation: This starts the service request before the application's required input approval.

choices.text: Configure the action group to return control, let the application validate and execute the request, then send back the result with the invocation identifier.
choices.explanation: This retains the application's approval boundary and gives the agent the result needed for the next turn.

choices.text: Store the service's URL in a prompt and expect the model to call it directly without an action group.
choices.explanation: A prompt string alone does not implement an authorized tool request or result handoff.

choices.text: Create a new agent session after the service call and send only a text copy of the result.
choices.explanation: A new session alone does not complete the prior returned action invocation.

learning.reason: An action group configured to return control sends the selected action and extracted parameters back to the application. The caller can execute its own procedure and return the action result using the invocation identifier.
learning.concept: Bedrock Agents action group Return Control and result handoff

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Preserve an agent conversation without sharing its runtime with another user
prompt: Two users interact with the same AgentCore Runtime deployment. The application needs to continue an existing user's session across multiple calls while keeping a separate execution context for the other user. Which session-handling approach fits?

choices.text: Use the same runtime session ID for every user of the deployment.
choices.explanation: That does not separate the users' execution sessions.

choices.text: Generate a new runtime session ID for every call, including follow-up calls within one conversation.
choices.explanation: This creates new sessions rather than continuing the intended one.

choices.text: Bind a distinct runtime session ID to each authorized conversation and reuse that ID only for that conversation's later requests.
choices.explanation: The runtime can route successive calls to the same isolated session without mixing different sessions.

choices.text: Use the agent runtime ARN as the only conversation identifier.
choices.explanation: The ARN identifies the shared deployment and does not distinguish users' sessions.

learning.reason: AgentCore Runtime identifies an isolated session by its runtime session ID. Reusing the same ID for the intended conversation maintains session continuity, while another conversation needs a different ID.
learning.concept: AgentCore Runtime session identifier and isolation

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Expose an existing API as an agent tool without a custom MCP server
prompt: A team already operates an approved internal API described in OpenAPI and wants multiple agents to discover and call selected operations as MCP tools. It wants one managed gateway that controls access to the API instead of shipping a separate tool server with each agent. What should it configure?

choices.text: Upload the OpenAPI document to a knowledge base without configuring an execution target.
choices.explanation: Retrieval can expose descriptions, but it does not make the operations callable tools.

choices.text: Use AgentCore Memory to store the OpenAPI file and retrieve it as a preference.
choices.explanation: Memory supplies stored information, not an executable API gateway for agents.

choices.text: Give each model the API schema in its prompt and rely on generated text to issue authorized HTTP calls.
choices.explanation: Generating arguments in text does not provide an authenticated execution and discovery mechanism.

choices.text: Configure the API as an AgentCore Gateway target, apply the required authentication, and connect the agents to that gateway's MCP endpoint.
choices.explanation: This makes approved API operations available as shared tools through a managed endpoint.

learning.reason: AgentCore Gateway can turn supported API targets into tools exposed through MCP. Gateway and target authentication govern how an agent discovers or calls the permitted operations.
learning.concept: AgentCore Gateway OpenAPI targets as MCP tools

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Reserve model capacity for steady customer traffic
prompt: A Bedrock application has a predictable sustained demand floor and a business need for a specified amount of model invocation capacity. The selected model and Region support Provisioned Throughput. The workload can commit to capacity, and occasional demand above the floor will be handled separately. Which configuration meets the baseline requirement?

choices.text: Size and purchase Provisioned Throughput for the demand floor, and invoke the resulting provisioned resource.
choices.explanation: This reserves the supported model capacity rather than depending solely on on-demand throughput.

choices.text: Use on-demand invocations alone and increase the client retry count.
choices.explanation: Retries do not dedicate capacity and can add delay during saturation.

choices.text: Set a higher generation token limit for all on-demand requests.
choices.explanation: That changes the request budget and can increase consumption. It does not reserve throughput.

choices.text: Use Bedrock batch inference for all real-time customer traffic.
choices.explanation: Batch jobs do not provide the required interactive serving capacity.

learning.reason: Provisioned Throughput purchases a number of model units to dedicate capacity. On-demand invocations track usage but do not reserve those model units.
learning.concept: Bedrock Provisioned Throughput and capacity in model units

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Pin a tested agent version
prompt: A support application calls an Amazon Bedrock agent. Developers must be able to prepare and test changes during the week while production continues to use the last approved configuration. The application should keep the same alias ID across releases. How should the team deploy the agent?

choices.text: Call the built-in test alias from production and develop changes against the same working draft.
choices.explanation: The test alias follows the working draft. Preparing further draft changes affects the configuration that a caller of this alias sees.

choices.text: Create a production alias that routes to a numbered agent version. Keep using that alias and update its routing after approving a new version.
choices.explanation: The caller's alias ID stays fixed while the deployment chooses which version serves the application.

choices.text: Keep one production alias per release and discover the newest alias at application startup.
choices.explanation: This changes the alias ID across releases and lets alias creation determine production selection instead of explicit approval.

choices.text: Invoke the agent by ID only and provide the approved version in the request session attributes.
choices.explanation: InvokeAgent uses an agent alias ID for routing. Session attributes provide runtime context and do not select the deployed version.

learning.reason: An alias can point applications to a selected immutable agent version, while developers use the working draft and its test alias independently.
learning.concept: Separate an editable agent draft from the version behind the production alias.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Scale long-running inference requests
prompt: A SageMaker AI real-time endpoint hosts multiple inference components. One text-generation component starts missing its latency target when long-running requests overlap. The aggregate endpoint request rate remains steady. The team needs target tracking to add copies of the affected component as its concurrent work rises. Which configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Track SageMakerVariantConcurrentRequestsPerModelHighResolution on the production variant.
choices.explanation: This target describes load at the variant/model level rather than managing the affected inference component's copy count.

choices.text: Track SageMakerVariantInvocationsPerInstance on the production variant.
choices.explanation: Invocation rate per instance can remain flat when requests occupy capacity longer and is aggregated at the wrong level for this objective.

choices.text: Track SageMakerInferenceComponentConcurrentRequestsPerCopyHighResolution on the affected inference component.
choices.explanation: The metric measures concurrent requests per copy and the scaling target can add or remove copies for that component.

choices.text: Set a scheduled scaling action that adds copies before the same daily peak.
choices.explanation: A schedule can anticipate known periods but cannot react to concurrent work at other times.

learning.reason: Concurrent requests per copy reflect in-flight work on the target component and are normalized by active capacity.
learning.concept: Scale inference-component copies using component-level concurrent requests per copy.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Connect both sides of a private endpoint
prompt: An ECS application in a private VPC must call a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint without a public network path. The endpoint's custom container must also fetch reference data from an internal network service in approved subnets. The model is allowed to initiate network calls. Which two changes provide the required paths? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Create a SageMaker AI API interface endpoint with private DNS as the only endpoint.
choices.explanation: SageMaker AI control-plane calls and Runtime inference calls have separate service endpoints.

choices.text: Create a SageMaker AI Runtime interface endpoint with private DNS and permit HTTPS traffic from the ECS application.
choices.explanation: The application can invoke the hosted endpoint through an AWS PrivateLink path.

choices.text: Enable network isolation for the SageMaker model so its container uses the VPC routes to the reference data service.
choices.explanation: Network isolation prevents the container from making the outbound network calls this workload requires.

choices.text: Use the SageMaker AI Runtime endpoint's security group as the sole configuration for the container's outbound path.
choices.explanation: The interface endpoint security group governs connections to its network interfaces. It does not attach the model container to the requested VPC.

choices.text: Supply VpcConfig with the approved subnets and a security group that can reach the internal service when creating the SageMaker model.
choices.explanation: The model's container can reach resources in the selected VPC subnets using the specified security controls.

learning.reason: Client invocation and container-initiated traffic use different paths. Create a Runtime interface endpoint for the first and attach the model to the VPC for the second.
learning.concept: Configure the client-to-Runtime and container-to-private-service paths independently.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Deploy the exact package approved in staging
prompt: An ML platform team approves model packages in SageMaker Model Registry. One package passed staging yesterday. Another was approved today for a different release, and production promotion must still use yesterday's package. The pipeline may run hours after approval. What should the staging pipeline pass to production?

choices.text: Persist the model package group ARN and let production list and select the newest approved version.
choices.explanation: The newest approved package at deploy time may differ from the one that passed staging.

choices.text: Use the staging endpoint name as the sole identifier and describe its currently deployed model at production deploy time.
choices.explanation: A later staging deployment can move the endpoint to another model before production promotion.

choices.text: Persist the training image digest and let production select the newest approved package that uses it.
choices.explanation: Different training runs and package versions can share a container image while containing different learned parameters.

choices.text: Persist the staging-tested model package version ARN in the release manifest and use it when creating the production model.
choices.explanation: This points to the selected registry version even if another package is subsequently approved.

learning.reason: The versioned model package ARN identifies the exact registered model tested during staging.
learning.concept: Pin a versioned model package ARN as a release input.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Avoid a full-fleet inference regression
prompt: A team currently updates a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint in a single step. A flawed update recently raised the model error rate. The next release must expose a small fraction of live requests to the new fleet for a defined observation period and restore the old fleet automatically if a CloudWatch alarm breaches its threshold. Which deployment strategy meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use blue/green canary traffic shifting with a bake interval and configure the model error alarm for automatic rollback.
choices.explanation: SageMaker observes the canary during the interval and can roll back traffic if the associated alarm triggers.

choices.text: Use all-at-once blue/green traffic shifting with automatic rollback on the same alarm.
choices.explanation: The alarm can trigger recovery, but live traffic moves all at once instead of starting with the required small fraction.

choices.text: Use a second production variant with a low initial weight and record the alarm in a team dashboard.
choices.explanation: Variant weights can limit exposure but a dashboard alone does not automatically restore traffic on a breach.

choices.text: Use shadow testing and fail the release if the shadow variant's alarm triggers.
choices.explanation: Shadow testing can measure mirrored requests, but it does not serve responses from the proposed model to a fraction of live callers.

learning.reason: SageMaker deployment guardrails can send a canary percentage to the new fleet and automatically roll back when the configured alarm breaches during deployment.
learning.concept: Shift traffic to a SageMaker canary and bind a rollback alarm to the deployment.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Pause a promotion for human review
prompt: An existing AWS CodePipeline workflow reaches a deploy action after automated model evaluations. A risk team must review the published evaluation report and explicitly approve each run before deployment can proceed. The team wants the fewest new components and the report should be accessible from the approval action. What should the ML engineer add?

choices.text: Publish the report link to SNS from the evaluation action and leave the deploy action as the next step.
choices.explanation: SNS can notify reviewers but does not block CodePipeline while the team decides.

choices.text: Add a manual approval action before deployment and set its external entity link to the evaluation report.
choices.explanation: The pipeline waits for an authorized decision, and the report is available in the approval context.

choices.text: Have CodeBuild wait for an approver to upload a marker file and poll for that file.
choices.explanation: This adds bespoke approval state and polling when the pipeline already has a native approval mechanism.

choices.text: Set the code repository branch to require a pull request review before merging.
choices.explanation: Repository review governs the source revision. It does not approve each later pipeline execution or the resulting model metrics.

learning.reason: A CodePipeline manual approval action pauses progression and can include a review URL so that approval is associated with the pipeline execution.
learning.concept: Gate CodePipeline promotion with a native approval action and review link.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Wait for retraining to finish before evaluating
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow retrains a SageMaker AI model every Monday. Training takes between 20 minutes and 5 hours. The evaluation task must start only after successful training, and a failed training job must take the workflow's existing error path. Which change meets the requirement with the fewest orchestration steps?

choices.text: Call CreateTrainingJob with a request-response task and start evaluation when the task returns the job ARN.
choices.explanation: Returning a job ARN confirms that SageMaker accepted the request, not that training finished.

choices.text: Wait 20 minutes after submitting the job and retry the evaluation task if the model artifact is missing.
choices.explanation: Artifact absence does not distinguish active training from a failed job, and evaluation would be acting as a polling loop.

choices.text: Use the optimized sagemaker:createTrainingJob.sync task with the existing Catch configuration.
choices.explanation: The task waits for the job to finish, so evaluation follows success and errors can route to the workflow's error path.

choices.text: Use a callback task and include the token as a SageMaker job tag without adding any other integration.
choices.explanation: Tagging a job does not cause SageMaker AI to call SendTaskSuccess or SendTaskFailure for an arbitrary callback token.

learning.reason: A Standard workflow can use the SageMaker optimized Run a Job integration to wait for job completion and handle job failures in the training task.
learning.concept: Use the SageMaker optimized .sync integration when downstream work needs a finished job.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Refresh a knowledge base after an editorial batch
prompt: An S3 data source backs a Bedrock knowledge base for an internal product manual. Each night a publishing job adds new files, replaces revised manuals, and removes retired manuals from the configured prefix. The publishing workflow must verify that the knowledge base has processed the batch before marking it available. What should it do?

choices.text: Run Retrieve against the updated file names and repeat the calls until the new results appear.
choices.explanation: Retrieval reads the existing index. Repeating it does not initiate an S3 data source sync.

choices.text: Invoke the embedding model for only the added or modified files and leave the rest of the workflow as it is.
choices.explanation: Producing raw embeddings does not write them into the managed index or remove the entries for deleted files.

choices.text: Create another data source against the same prefix for each night and keep earlier sources attached.
choices.explanation: Previously indexed content can remain attached through the earlier sources, and repeatedly adding sources does not maintain one synchronized view.

choices.text: Start an ingestion job for the existing knowledge base and data source after the writes finish. Wait for completion and check the ingestion statistics for failures.
choices.explanation: The job syncs the existing source and reports its processing results. Marking the batch available can depend on the job outcome.

learning.reason: A data-source sync updates the vector store incrementally for new, modified, and deleted S3 content. The workflow can check the ingestion job status and failed-document statistics before promoting the batch.
learning.concept: Trigger and verify an incremental Bedrock Knowledge Bases ingestion job after a batch of S3 source changes.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Parameterize approved prompt wording
prompt: A claims application uses an approved Bedrock prompt that includes a jurisdiction name and a current claim type. The two values depend on the request, and prompt owners must maintain one central template. The chosen model and generation settings are identical for all requests. How should the engineer pass the dynamic values?

choices.text: Define placeholders in the prompt template, publish a version, and send the two text values as promptVariables when invoking that version with Converse.
choices.explanation: The template stays centralized and each invocation supplies its own values.

choices.text: Use requestMetadata fields on Converse to substitute the two values in the template.
choices.explanation: Request metadata can annotate invocation logging. It does not substitute variables in the prompt body.

choices.text: Create a separate foundation model invocation profile for each jurisdiction and put the jurisdiction and claim type in the profile name.
choices.explanation: Inference profiles can select supported routing or cost attribution, but their names do not interpolate into prompt text.

choices.text: Mirror the approved template into each client application and substitute the values locally before invoking the base model directly.
choices.explanation: Local substitution is possible, but each client would maintain a separate copy of the approved prompt.

learning.reason: Store the two changing values as named placeholders in Prompt management. Converse can use the managed prompt version ARN and fill those placeholders from promptVariables.
learning.concept: Pass dynamic values to a managed Bedrock prompt using Converse promptVariables.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Report custom model readiness correctly
prompt: A team migrates an internal prediction service to a SageMaker AI real-time endpoint. Its image currently exposes /ready and /predict. The application process can start before its model artifact is loaded, and traffic must wait until the model is genuinely ready. Which two changes satisfy the SageMaker serving contract and readiness requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Retain /ready and rely on a Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK to change the route SageMaker probes.
choices.explanation: The image's health check does not change the hosted endpoint's request path for health checks.

choices.text: Return HTTP 200 from /ping as soon as the process starts and rely on 503 responses from prediction requests until the artifact is loaded.
choices.explanation: SageMaker sees the successful health probe as readiness and can route inference before the model is available.

choices.text: Have the web server listen on port 8080 and accept prediction payloads at POST /invocations.
choices.explanation: That is the standard inference request path for the custom HTTP container on the endpoint.

choices.text: Implement GET /ping and return success only when the model is loaded and the service can make a prediction.
choices.explanation: SageMaker uses the status of the probe to determine whether the container can accept inference requests.

choices.text: Use POST /ping as the only health route and keep predictions on /predict.
choices.explanation: The service sends periodic GET /ping probes and normally routes inference to /invocations.

learning.reason: SageMaker sends health checks to GET /ping and prediction requests to POST /invocations. A health response should reflect readiness, not just process liveness.
learning.concept: Implement the SageMaker hosting HTTP contract and base health on model readiness.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Gate registration on the same run's result
prompt: A SageMaker pipeline trains a model and runs a ProcessingStep that emits evaluation.json containing the measured recall for that run. Parallel executions are allowed. Registration must proceed only if the measured recall for the current execution is at least 0.90. How should the pipeline implement the gate?

choices.text: Write all evaluation reports to a single S3 key called latest/evaluation.json and evaluate it after the current ProcessingStep completes.
choices.explanation: Another run can overwrite the shared key before the condition reads it.

choices.text: Expose the evaluation report as a PropertyFile on the processing output. Read the recall with JsonGet in a ConditionStep and register only on the passing branch.
choices.explanation: The condition uses the structured output from the current execution and controls whether its model is registered.

choices.text: Use 0.90 as a pipeline parameter and check whether that parameter is at least 0.90 before registering.
choices.explanation: The parameter is the target threshold, not the measured result from processing.

choices.text: Register every model with PendingManualApproval and use the job's success status as the automated recall gate.
choices.explanation: Successful processing only establishes that evaluation ran. It does not establish that the measured recall met the target, and this design has already registered the model.

learning.reason: A PropertyFile identifies the processing output and JsonGet extracts the numeric evaluation result for a ConditionStep within the same execution.
learning.concept: Use an execution-bound processing property file to gate SageMaker Model Registry registration.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Localize a prediction latency increase
prompt: A SageMaker AI real-time endpoint's p95 latency increased after a change to custom request preprocessing in its inference container. Over the same period, the p95 ModelLatency rose while p95 OverheadLatency and request volume remained stable. What should the platform team investigate first?

choices.text: Change the PrivateLink interface endpoint because OverheadLatency measures only how long the model runs.
choices.explanation: OverheadLatency represents SageMaker request and response overhead outside the model container.

choices.text: Change the caller's retry configuration because ModelLatency includes the time spent in the client's retry loop.
choices.explanation: ModelLatency does not include client retry delays. Changing retry behavior does not explain the measured container-side increase.

choices.text: Profile request decoding, preprocessing, and inference inside the model container.
choices.explanation: These operations fall within the container-side elapsed time reflected by ModelLatency.

choices.text: Increase the data capture sample rate because ModelLatency reports how long the capture worker takes to write to S3.
choices.explanation: The metric measures request handling by the model container, not the elapsed time of a data capture upload.

learning.reason: ModelLatency includes processing inside the model container. With stable OverheadLatency, the container-side path is the stronger first lead.
learning.concept: Use ModelLatency and OverheadLatency to separate container-side work from SageMaker request transport.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Compare two models using live outcomes
prompt: A retail team wants to compare a recommender candidate with the current model for one week. The candidate's recommendations must reach around 20% of real requests so that the team can measure user click-through for each model separately. Both models can share one SageMaker endpoint. Which two steps are appropriate? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Deploy the candidate as a shadow variant and count shadow invocations as impressions.
choices.explanation: Shadow inference responses are not returned to the user, so customers cannot click recommendations from the shadow model.

choices.text: Use the endpoint's total invocation count as the per-variant click-through metric.
choices.explanation: Endpoint invocation counts do not measure clicks and a total count does not distinguish the assigned models.

choices.text: Deploy the current model and candidate as production variants with relative weights of 80 and 20.
choices.explanation: The endpoint can distribute eligible requests across both production variants using their relative weights.

choices.text: Set TargetVariant to the current model on every request and let the endpoint weights select the candidate for 20% of requests.
choices.explanation: Specifying TargetVariant overrides the normal routing by variant weights.

choices.text: Record the invoked production variant with each recommendation impression and join click events to the impressions.
choices.explanation: This ties the business outcome to the model that actually produced the displayed recommendation.

learning.reason: Weighted production variants return live responses from the assigned model. Recording the resulting variant with each impression allows later clicks to be attributed correctly.
learning.concept: Use weighted live A/B variants and attach the invoked variant to downstream outcome records.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Match delayed labels to the original predictions
prompt: An existing SageMaker Model Monitor customer monitors a fraud classifier with Data Capture enabled. The caller sends a unique InferenceId that the label service can recover after the fraud investigation. Predictions and final labels arrive hours apart and in different orders. Which change lets the Model Monitor quality job match them reliably?

choices.text: Write a new unique event ID whenever the label is created.
choices.explanation: The new ID is unique but unrelated to the ID of the captured prediction, so it cannot match the records.

choices.text: Sort both feeds by ingestion time and use record position within each hour as the match key.
choices.explanation: Actual labels are delayed and can arrive out of order. Model Monitor also uses identifiers rather than positional matching.

choices.text: Use the model endpoint name as the event ID for every label from that endpoint.
choices.explanation: Many predictions share the same endpoint name, so it cannot uniquely identify a prediction.

choices.text: Write the original InferenceId as eventMetadata.eventId on each ground truth record and configure the quality job to read those S3 files.
choices.explanation: With a captured inferenceId present, Model Monitor matches that value to the ground truth record's eventMetadata.eventId.

learning.reason: When a captured record has an inferenceId, Model Monitor uses it to find the corresponding ground truth event. The ground truth files must store that value in their event metadata.
learning.concept: Join ground truth with captured predictions using the caller's InferenceId when it is present.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep alerting metrics affordable and searchable
prompt: An inference gateway emits latency metrics through CloudWatch Embedded Metric Format. Operators need a latency dashboard per deployed model version and the ability to find the log for a single request. The gateway processed a million requests last week and the custom metric count rose sharply after requestId was added as a dimension. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Retain the model version as a dimension and record requestId only as a structured log field.
choices.explanation: The dashboard stays grouped by model version, and CloudWatch Logs queries still have the individual request identifier.

choices.text: Keep both dimensions but publish metrics at one-minute resolution.
choices.explanation: Resolution does not reduce the number of distinct time series created by unique dimension values.

choices.text: Hash each request ID and use the full digest as the request dimension.
choices.explanation: Hashing does not materially reduce cardinality when the generated digests are still unique.

choices.text: Publish one separate namespace per request and remove requestId from the dimensions.
choices.explanation: Unique namespaces would still create separate metrics and would make dashboard aggregation harder.

learning.reason: EMF creates a distinct custom time series for each unique metric dimension set. A request identifier can remain queryable as a structured log field without becoming a time series dimension.
learning.concept: Use bounded CloudWatch metric dimensions and keep unique identifiers in the log event.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Find a tool timeout hidden by agent retries
prompt: An AgentCore application sometimes returns a fallback answer even though its overall HTTP response succeeds. Each agent run can issue several model calls and tool calls. Operations has enabled agent tracing and needs to find which call timed out within a particular invocation. What should the team inspect?

choices.text: Inspect only the endpoint invocation count for the affected minute.
choices.explanation: The count can show traffic volume but not which step inside one invocation failed.

choices.text: Open the distributed trace for the affected invocation and inspect each tool span's error status, timing, and retry sequence.
choices.explanation: The trace shows the operation-level timeline and can expose timeouts hidden by the fallback path.

choices.text: Use successful HTTP responses to identify invocations where no tool timed out.
choices.explanation: The fallback can produce a successful response despite the underlying tool error.

choices.text: Compare the agent's account-wide memory use before and after the fallback.
choices.explanation: Resource totals do not show the failing call or its place in the individual invocation.

learning.reason: A trace relates the child spans for model and tool operations to a single invocation. Span timing and error details can identify a failing tool even when application code catches the error.
learning.concept: Use per-invocation AgentCore traces to identify errors handled inside a successful top-level request.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Distinguish workflow failures from state throttling
prompt: A Standard Step Functions pipeline performs daily feature preparation. When the team rolls out more parallel branches, the workflow execution time increases but most executions still succeed. The team wants an alarm specifically for throttled state transitions rather than failed executions. Which Step Functions CloudWatch metric should it use?

choices.text: Alarm on ExecutionsFailed for the feature preparation state machine.
choices.explanation: This counts failed executions, so it can miss throttling in runs that complete successfully.

choices.text: Alarm on ExecutionsTimedOut only.
choices.explanation: It reports executions that exceed their timeout, not delayed transitions within completed executions.

choices.text: Alarm on ExecutionThrottled for the feature preparation state machine.
choices.explanation: It exposes throttled state transitions for that state machine even when executions later finish successfully.

choices.text: Use a low threshold on ExecutionsStarted.
choices.explanation: This measures execution starts. Branch parallelism can increase transition traffic without increasing the number of execution starts.

learning.reason: ExecutionThrottled counts throttled state transitions and retries related to the StateTransition limit. Successful executions can still experience this bottleneck.
learning.concept: Use Step Functions ExecutionThrottled to detect pressure on state transitions independently of terminal failure.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Find which agent sessions consume memory
prompt: The CloudWatch dashboard for a Bedrock AgentCore Runtime endpoint shows unusual memory consumption. Several thousand sessions use that endpoint, and a few sessions are suspected of holding large in-memory state. The operations team needs to rank sessions by their measured memory consumption for the affected time window. What should it use?

choices.text: Group the endpoint's CloudWatch MemoryUsed-GBHours metric by the endpoint Name dimension.
choices.explanation: Name distinguishes endpoints, so every session under that name contributes to the same aggregate.

choices.text: Rank sessions by model output token count only.
choices.explanation: Token volume does not measure the lifetime or size of each session's in-memory state.

choices.text: Read the account's billing statement and group the runtime charge by session identifier.
choices.explanation: Billing is authoritative for charges, but the endpoint's per-session operational attribution is provided by resource usage logs.

choices.text: Enable Runtime USAGE_LOGS and aggregate agent.runtime.memory.gb_hours.used by session.id for the affected window.
choices.explanation: The logs carry the session-level memory measurement and can be grouped and ranked by session.

learning.reason: The endpoint-level resource metrics are aggregated. AgentCore Runtime USAGE_LOGS include a session identifier and measured CPU and memory usage, which can be grouped by session.
learning.concept: Use AgentCore Runtime session-level resource usage logs for attribution below the endpoint level.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Choose an inference host using a measured workload
prompt: A team can run its image classifier on several SageMaker real-time CPU and GPU instance families. The service must sustain 300 requests per second under a production-shaped load and meet a p95 latency target. The goal is the lowest cost per successful prediction among compliant configurations. What should the engineer do?

choices.text: Run an Inference Recommender custom load test for the candidate families with the representative requests and latency and throughput requirements. Compare cost per inference for passing configurations.
choices.explanation: Measured latency and throughput establish feasibility, and cost per inference lets the team compare candidates of different capacities.

choices.text: Select the candidate with the lowest price per instance-hour and add replicas until aggregate CPU utilization is low.
choices.explanation: A lower hourly price does not ensure the lowest required fleet cost or guarantee that single-request latency meets the target.

choices.text: Use the fastest hardware from model training and divide its hourly price by the offline training throughput.
choices.explanation: Training throughput does not measure serving latency or request capacity for this model.

choices.text: Choose the family with the lowest median latency from a single request and skip concurrent tests.
choices.explanation: Median latency for a single request does not establish p95 latency and capacity under production load.

learning.reason: A custom Inference Recommender load test can use a sample payload and production traffic pattern. Compare cost per inference only among configurations meeting the throughput and latency requirements.
learning.concept: Benchmark compatible instance configurations against representative inference traffic before choosing on unit cost.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Reduce cost for interruption-tolerant retraining
prompt: A nightly SageMaker AI training job runs a custom framework for three hours and has a flexible completion window. The training script currently writes only a final model. The team wants to use spare capacity and resume from a checkpoint no more than approximately twenty minutes old. Which three changes are required? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Enable Managed Spot Training and configure a maximum wait time greater than the maximum training runtime.
choices.explanation: The job can use spare capacity and the longer wait allows for interruption or capacity delays.

choices.text: Make the script save training checkpoints at least every twenty minutes and load the latest checkpoint from the configured local directory on startup.
choices.explanation: The custom framework must serialize and restore its state, such as weights, optimizer state, and the training step.

choices.text: Configure the final model artifact output location to also serve as the checkpoint store without changing the training script.
choices.explanation: The final artifact output location alone does not make a custom script write interim snapshots or resume from them.

choices.text: Set the maximum wait time shorter than the training runtime to keep the spot job from being interrupted.
choices.explanation: The wait limit does not prevent interruptions, and SageMaker requires it to be greater than the configured maximum runtime.

choices.text: Configure SageMaker to synchronize the script's checkpoint directory to a job-specific S3 path.
choices.explanation: SageMaker can restore the saved files to the local checkpoint directory when the interrupted job resumes on replacement capacity.

learning.reason: Managed Spot Training can lower compute cost for flexible jobs. Persist frequently written checkpoints in S3 and have the training script restore them after an interruption.
learning.concept: Combine Managed Spot Training with checkpoint intervals and restore logic aligned to the allowed progress loss.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Attribute shared model spend to teams
prompt: Three applications in one AWS account invoke the same supported Bedrock foundation model in the same Region under a shared execution role. Finance needs actual AWS billing costs grouped by cost center for future invocations. Application teams can change the model reference they send. What should the engineer implement?

choices.text: Use one system-defined inference profile and put the cost center in the user prompt.
choices.explanation: Text in a prompt is model input, and billing does not interpret it as a cost allocation tag.

choices.text: Create an application inference profile for each cost center, tag each profile, activate the cost allocation tag, and invoke Bedrock through the appropriate profile.
choices.explanation: AWS can attribute the profile's usage to the activated tag for billing analysis.

choices.text: Tag the shared execution role once for each cost center without changing invocation requests.
choices.explanation: One shared role does not distinguish the applications, and competing values cannot represent separate request owners as a single tag.

choices.text: Add the cost center to each request's metadata and expect those values to appear as activated tags in Cost Explorer.
choices.explanation: Per-request metadata can support log analysis but does not become a cost allocation tag in billing reports.

learning.reason: Each application can invoke the model through a separately tagged application inference profile. Activated cost allocation tags enable grouping future profile-associated costs in billing tools.
learning.concept: Attribute future Amazon Bedrock billed usage with tagged application inference profiles.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Cache reusable prompt content
prompt: A Bedrock application sends a long set of identical instructions and policy text on every request, followed by case details that always change. The supported model has prompt caching enabled, the fixed portion meets its token minimum, and repeat requests arrive within the cache lifetime. The team must preserve both portions of the prompt. Where should it place an explicit cache checkpoint?

choices.text: Put the cache checkpoint at the end, after the changing case details.
choices.explanation: Changing case content makes the full prefix before that checkpoint differ across requests.

choices.text: Put the case details first, append the fixed material, and put the checkpoint at the end.
choices.explanation: A fixed suffix does not help if the prefix covered by the checkpoint starts with different content.

choices.text: Put the instructions and policies first, add the cache checkpoint, and append the case details after it.
choices.explanation: The reusable prefix remains identical across calls, and the per-case portion is still sent for inference.

choices.text: Put the checkpoint before the instructions and policies.
choices.explanation: That leaves the repeated tokens outside the cached prefix.

learning.reason: An explicit prefix checkpoint after the stable material can match across requests even when the case details that follow it change.
learning.concept: Place the Bedrock prompt-cache checkpoint after sufficiently long stable content and before request-specific content.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Get early and actual overspend alerts
prompt: A team operates its ML platform in a dedicated AWS account and has several months of stable billing history. Finance wants email if projected month-end costs exceed $8,000 and also wants a separate email when actual monthly costs first exceed $7,000. The alerts must not interrupt workloads. What should the team configure?

choices.text: Create one actual-spend alert at $8,000 and rely on it to predict month-end spend.
choices.explanation: An actual alert only evaluates recorded spend and does not supply the required projection or earlier actual alert.

choices.text: Configure Service Quotas to warn when a deployment's projected spend is $8,000.
choices.explanation: Resource or request quotas do not evaluate actual or forecasted account charges in dollars.

choices.text: Configure a budget action that stops ML compute when the forecast reaches $8,000.
choices.explanation: An action to stop resources conflicts with the requirement to send alerts without interrupting workloads.

choices.text: Create a recurring $8,000 monthly cost budget with a forecasted alert at $8,000 and an actual alert at $7,000, without automated budget actions.
choices.explanation: This monitors the month-end projection and realized spend as separate conditions and leaves workloads running.

learning.reason: A recurring AWS cost budget supports separate forecasted and actual notifications. Configuring alerts without budget actions satisfies the notification requirement.
learning.concept: Set distinct forecasted and actual AWS Budgets alerts against monthly spend.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Identify which feature drives new token costs
prompt: Several features in one application use the same Bedrock model and inference profile through Converse. Finance sees rising usage. Engineering must distinguish input growth from output growth and attribute it to the application feature, but policy forbids storing request or response text in telemetry. What should engineering collect?

choices.text: Publish separate input and output token counts from the response's usage object with a non-sensitive feature dimension.
choices.explanation: This supports feature-level cost diagnosis with minimal telemetry and no payload storage.

choices.text: Record only totalTokens per feature.
choices.explanation: The total hides whether input or output usage caused the increase.

choices.text: Enable text model invocation logging for full request and response records, then query totals grouped by feature.
choices.explanation: Full text logs collect the payloads prohibited by the stated policy.

choices.text: Read billed cost grouped by the existing shared inference profile and derive token direction from the total.
choices.explanation: The profile is shared across features, and an aggregate currency figure does not establish input and output counts for each feature.

learning.reason: Converse returns input and output token counts in usage. The caller already knows the feature and can emit just counters labeled with that feature.
learning.concept: Record separate Converse usage counters by a bounded caller-known feature label without capturing prompt or response bodies.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Allow the pipeline to hand off one execution role
prompt: A CI role has permission to create SageMaker models. Its CreateModel request fails because it cannot pass the approved inference execution role. The approved role already trusts SageMaker and can read its model artifact. Security allows the CI role to nominate only that execution role for model hosting. Which change meets the requirement?

choices.text: Grant iam:PassRole to the approved inference execution role only.
choices.explanation: The failed permission check applies to the CI caller, which is submitting the execution role in CreateModel.

choices.text: Grant iam:PassRole to the CI role with Resource set to the approved inference execution role ARN.
choices.explanation: This permits the CI role to pass the selected role while keeping the role's trust and runtime permissions in place.

choices.text: Add the CI role as a trusted principal on the execution role and leave the CI permissions as they are.
choices.explanation: Permission to assume a role and permission to pass it to a service are separate. A trust change alone does not grant iam:PassRole to the caller.

choices.text: Attach s3:GetObject to the CI role for the model artifact.
choices.explanation: Artifact access does not authorize the CreateModel caller to pass the execution role.

learning.reason: The calling identity needs iam:PassRole on the execution role it supplies. Scoping the caller permission to the approved role avoids granting it the ability to pass other roles.
learning.concept: Grant the calling pipeline scoped iam:PassRole instead of changing the model execution role's artifact access.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Audit serving API calls to one regulated endpoint
prompt: A team already records CloudTrail management events. Auditors also need the calling identity and time for InvokeEndpoint calls made to one designated SageMaker real-time endpoint. Traffic to the remaining endpoints should not be captured by the new selector. What should the team configure?

choices.text: Filter the existing management event selector for CreateEndpoint and UpdateEndpoint.
choices.explanation: Creation and updates are management operations. They do not identify callers that later invoke the model.

choices.text: Use the endpoint's CloudWatch Invocation metric grouped by model variant.
choices.explanation: The metric reports counts. It does not provide the calling identity for each API event.

choices.text: Add an advanced data event selector for AWS::SageMaker::Endpoint and filter to the audited endpoint ARN and InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: The selector records the applicable data-plane calls without enabling them for the other endpoints.

choices.text: Enable S3 object-level CloudTrail events for the bucket containing the model artifact.
choices.explanation: Artifact object access does not represent inference request calls to the endpoint.

learning.reason: SageMaker InvokeEndpoint is a CloudTrail data event. Advanced event selectors can select the endpoint resource type, exact resource ARN, and applicable event name.
learning.concept: Add a narrowly scoped CloudTrail data event selector for audited endpoint invocations.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep the summary while masking detected PII
prompt: A support tool generates plain-text conversation summaries using Bedrock. Approved source text may be processed inside the application, but the final text shown to reviewers must mask detected customer email addresses and phone numbers while keeping the rest of the summary. Which configuration directly supports this policy?

choices.text: Configure the sensitive information output action to block whenever it detects an email or phone number.
choices.explanation: Blocking replaces the affected response with the configured blocked message, losing the rest of the summary.

choices.text: Enable only the sensitive information detection action and use the model response without further processing.
choices.explanation: Detection can report what was found, but it does not alter the response text.

choices.text: Use a contextual grounding check and raise its relevance threshold.
choices.explanation: Relevance checks whether the answer addresses the query. They do not identify and mask email addresses or phone numbers.

choices.text: Apply a guardrail to the model invocation and configure the sensitive information output action to mask email and phone entities.
choices.explanation: Detected entities are replaced with type markers in the response while other text can remain visible.

learning.reason: A Bedrock Guardrails sensitive information filter can apply an anonymization action to the specified entity types in model responses. The application should consume the guarded response.
learning.concept: Configure Bedrock Guardrails output masking for the sensitive entity types the user-facing response must redact.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Wait for the image scan before promoting
prompt: A pipeline pushes a SageMaker inference image to Amazon ECR. Security requires scanning the candidate for vulnerabilities in both operating-system and supported language packages. Each deployment must be blocked while that specific image's first scan is pending or if its findings exceed policy. Deployment should never silently switch to another image pushed under the same tag. What should the team implement?

choices.text: Enable ECR enhanced scanning on the repository. Wait for the initial scan for the pushed digest, inspect its findings against policy, and promote only that digest if it passes.
choices.explanation: This covers both package classes and ties the decision and deployment to the same image.

choices.text: Enable enhanced scanning but pass the gate whenever a findings query is empty immediately after pushing the image.
choices.explanation: No results before an asynchronous scan completes do not establish that the image has no findings.

choices.text: Enable ECR basic scanning on push and approve the image as soon as the scan succeeds.
choices.explanation: ECR basic scanning covers operating-system vulnerabilities, and does not provide the required language-package coverage.

choices.text: Enable enhanced scanning, approve the most recently scanned digest in the repository, and deploy the mutable latest tag.
choices.explanation: The scan results and the image deployed can refer to different image digests.

learning.reason: ECR enhanced scanning, powered by Amazon Inspector, covers supported OS and language packages and signals completion of the initial scan. The approval should refer to the pushed digest and check its findings.
learning.concept: Use ECR enhanced scanning and gate deployment on the completed results for the exact image digest.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Restore read access to a cross-account model artifact
prompt: A SageMaker endpoint in a consuming account cannot load its approved model artifact from a producing account. The execution role and bucket policy already allow GetObject on the exact artifact, and the S3 request uses the expected role. The object uses SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key in the producing account. KMS logs show a denied Decrypt from the model execution role. Which two permissions should the team add? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Allow s3:ListBucket on the artifact bucket for the execution role.
choices.explanation: The request already reaches KMS during object retrieval. Listing the bucket does not authorize decrypting the object.

choices.text: Allow the human deployer to use kms:Decrypt on that key and leave the model execution role unchanged.
choices.explanation: The model execution role, rather than the human deployer, is the identity whose artifact read needs authorization.

choices.text: Allow kms:Encrypt on a new key in the consuming account.
choices.explanation: Encrypt permissions on another key cannot decrypt this object, which is encrypted under the producing account's key.

choices.text: Allow the consuming account's model execution role to use kms:Decrypt in the producing KMS key's key policy.
choices.explanation: The key-owning account must authorize use of the key by the external execution role.

choices.text: Allow kms:Decrypt on that producing KMS key ARN in the consuming model execution role's identity policy.
choices.explanation: Cross-account access also requires the consuming account to allow the caller's action on the key.

learning.reason: Cross-account KMS permissions need both authorization in the producing key policy and matching IAM permission for the consuming role.
learning.concept: Authorize decrypt on the producing KMS key on both sides of a cross-account artifact read.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Report endpoint configurations using unapproved keys
prompt: A security team needs recurring compliance checks for SageMaker endpoint configurations. The team has a list of approved KMS key ARNs. It must flag both configurations without a KMS key and configurations that reference a key outside the list, without writing its own evaluation function. Which solution meets the requirement?

choices.text: Enable the same Config managed rule and omit kmsKeyArns.
choices.explanation: This checks that a key is configured but does not restrict it to the required list.

choices.text: Record SageMaker endpoint configurations in AWS Config and enable SAGEMAKER_ENDPOINT_CONFIGURATION_KMS_KEY_CONFIGURED with the approved key ARNs supplied in kmsKeyArns.
choices.explanation: The periodic managed evaluation checks the appropriate resource type and enforces the supplied key list.

choices.text: Enable automatic rotation for the approved keys and use the rotation status as the endpoint compliance signal.
choices.explanation: An approved key's rotation status does not identify endpoint configurations that omit a key or use a different one.

choices.text: Create a CloudTrail management event trail and treat every successful CreateEndpointConfig call as compliant.
choices.explanation: Successful configuration creation does not enforce the organization's allowed key list or evaluate existing configurations.

learning.reason: The AWS Config managed rule checks the endpoint configuration's KmsKeyId and accepts a list of approved key ARNs as a parameter.
learning.concept: Evaluate SageMaker endpoint configurations against an allowed KMS key list with an AWS Config managed rule.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Call a foundation model from ECS without a stored key
prompt: A long-running ECS service calls a Bedrock model through the AWS SDK. The service must deploy without any static credential secret, automatically renew its credentials, and allow inference only against the designated model. Which authentication setup meets those requirements?

choices.text: Attach the Bedrock inference policy only to the ECS task execution role and leave the task IAM role unset.
choices.explanation: The task execution role is used by the ECS agent for operations such as image pulls. It does not provide the application with task-role permissions.

choices.text: Generate a long-term Bedrock API key, store it in Secrets Manager, and load it when the service starts.
choices.explanation: The arrangement still depends on a stored key and does not supply the automatically renewed task credentials required by the application.

choices.text: Assign the ECS task an IAM role permitting the required Bedrock invocation on the designated model and use the SDK's default credential provider chain.
choices.explanation: The application receives rotating task role credentials and uses the role's limited permissions.

choices.text: Copy a short-term Bedrock API key into each task definition revision and redeploy when it expires.
choices.explanation: The task would depend on credential injection and redeployment for renewal, which the task role avoids.

learning.reason: An ECS task IAM role supplies automatically managed temporary credentials to application code through the container credential provider. Its policy can grant the needed invoke operation for the designated model.
learning.concept: Use the ECS application task role and SDK credential chain for renewable, scoped Bedrock access.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Remove deleted items from a feature lake
prompt: A feature lake mirrors a DynamoDB table every hour. The lake uses a customer-and-day key stored in an item attribute, not the DynamoDB primary key. Downstream processing must remove rows when an item that existed at the start of the interval has been deleted. The source table has point-in-time recovery. The job already has a base snapshot and can use the managed DynamoDB export. What data should it request for each interval?

choices.text: Export changes with NEW_IMAGES and derive the customer-and-day key from the new image of each deleted item.
choices.explanation: A deleted item has no new image. In this mode the export contains its DynamoDB key, which is insufficient for the lake's key.

choices.text: Export only a full table snapshot at the end of the interval and apply its records as upserts.
choices.explanation: Upserts from a current snapshot do not remove lake records absent from that snapshot.

choices.text: Export changes with NEW_IMAGES and use the export timestamp as the day in each deletion key.
choices.explanation: The export timestamp is not the historical customer-and-day key stored on the deleted item.

choices.text: Export changes for the hourly interval with NEW_AND_OLD_IMAGES and derive the deletion target from the old image.
choices.explanation: The old image can identify the destination row for a deleted source item; the absence of a new image indicates the removal case.

learning.reason: For a deleted item, the new-only incremental export contains its DynamoDB key. The new-and-old view also supplies the previous image, where the lake's alternate key was stored.
learning.concept: Use DynamoDB incremental export old images to reconcile removals under a different downstream key.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Mount a shared high-throughput training dataset
prompt: A distributed SageMaker training script makes random POSIX reads of many small image files through multiple epochs. The images are stored in S3. The team wants a managed parallel filesystem with an S3 data repository association and does not want each training job to copy the full dataset to every worker before starting. Which input configuration fits?

choices.text: Associate Amazon FSx for Lustre with the S3 repository and configure a SageMaker filesystem input channel for the training workers.
choices.explanation: The workers get a shared POSIX filesystem with a managed association to the source data.

choices.text: Configure SageMaker Pipe mode directly against S3 and let the training script issue arbitrary seek operations on each named file.
choices.explanation: Pipe mode provides sequential input streams and is not a shared filesystem of named, randomly seekable files.

choices.text: Configure an EBS volume on each worker and use File mode with the full S3 dataset on every worker.
choices.explanation: This stages local copies rather than providing the requested shared parallel filesystem.

choices.text: Mount Amazon EFS and specify the original S3 prefix as an EFS filesystem path without a data import step.
choices.explanation: EFS can be a SageMaker filesystem input, but the files need to exist on EFS first. Merely specifying an S3 prefix does not create an S3 data repository association.

learning.reason: SageMaker can mount an Amazon FSx for Lustre filesystem as a training input. An S3 repository association can expose the training dataset through the shared parallel filesystem.
learning.concept: Present S3-originated training data through an FSx for Lustre data repository association and SageMaker filesystem input.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Correct write throttling from one partition key
prompt: A provisioned Kinesis data stream ingests readings from several hundred sensors. The producer uses factory ID as its partition key, and one busy factory exceeds the per-shard write limit by itself. The stream shows spare write capacity on other shards. Only per-sensor record order matters, and sensor IDs are globally unique with no single sensor exceeding a shard's write capacity. What is the most appropriate producer change?

choices.text: Increase the stream's shard count and continue using the same factory ID for every reading from that factory.
choices.explanation: The hot factory's identical keys continue to map to one shard. Adding aggregate capacity does not make one key span shards.

choices.text: Use sensor ID as the partition key and retain factory ID as a payload field.
choices.explanation: A high-cardinality sensor ID can distribute writes across shards while assigning each sensor to a consistent key.

choices.text: Switch to on-demand capacity and keep the existing partition key distribution.
choices.explanation: A single key can still exceed its shard's write limits in on-demand mode.

choices.text: Generate a random partition key for every reading and discard the source sensor's sequence information.
choices.explanation: This can distribute writes but does not preserve the required per-sensor ordering.

learning.reason: Each partition key hashes to one shard. Replacing the factory-wide key with the sensor ID can distribute that factory's load while keeping one sensor's records on one partition key.
learning.concept: Resolve hot Kinesis write keys by choosing a finer partition key that respects the required ordering boundary.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Close event-time feature windows despite an idle shard
prompt: A Managed Service for Apache Flink job uses Kinesis and groups feature events into five-minute event-time windows. Most source tasks still read recent events, but one assigned source task receives no events overnight. The downstream watermark stalls at the idle task's last watermark. The team must keep event-time windows and cannot generate synthetic events. Which adjustment should it make?

choices.text: Increase the allowed out-of-orderness interval for every input.
choices.explanation: That delays watermarks from live inputs but does not advance or ignore a silent input's old watermark.

choices.text: Replace the event-time windows with processing-time windows.
choices.explanation: Processing-time windows can progress with wall-clock time, but they would change the grouping semantics the team must retain.

choices.text: Configure a suitable withIdleness timeout on the event-time watermark strategy.
choices.explanation: An idle input is excluded from the downstream minimum while active inputs continue to supply watermarks.

choices.text: Increase state checkpoint frequency.
choices.explanation: Checkpoints improve recovery and state durability. They do not change how idle inputs contribute watermarks.

learning.reason: By default the downstream watermark uses the minimum input watermark. An idleness timeout lets Flink ignore the idle input in that calculation while other tasks continue advancing event time.
learning.concept: Exclude idle Flink upstream subtasks from event-time watermark calculation with withIdleness.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Format labeled CSV for a built-in training channel
prompt: A team exports data to train SageMaker's built-in Linear Learner as a binary classifier. The existing CSV has one header row and the label in the final column. The team must keep CSV and must avoid treating labels as numeric features. What change is required?

choices.text: Remove the header, leave the label last, and set the content type to text/csv.
choices.explanation: Removing the header alone does not move the target to the column expected by the algorithm.

choices.text: Put the label in the first column but retain the header so the algorithm can recognize the target name.
choices.explanation: The input format is headerless. It does not read the header to discover label columns.

choices.text: Remove the header and mark the channel as text/csv with label_size=0 while keeping the labeled records.
choices.explanation: The setting describes data without label columns and does not separate the binary target from the features.

choices.text: Write headerless records with the label first and set the training channel content type to text/csv.
choices.explanation: The algorithm can read the first field as the target and interpret the remaining fields as features.

learning.reason: For supported SageMaker built-in algorithms consuming labeled CSV, the training records are headerless and carry the target in the first column.
learning.concept: Write labeled built-in SageMaker training CSV with the target first and no header.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Merge a field that has two valid source types
prompt: A Glue job combines two suppliers' DynamicFrames. After the union, the reference field is a ChoiceType: one source sends a numeric ID and the other sends an alphanumeric string. Downstream normalizers need to see the original typed value in one nested reference field. They cannot discard either type, cast values, or add sibling top-level fields. How should the job resolve the ambiguity?

choices.text: Apply ResolveChoice with make_struct to the reference field.
choices.explanation: The struct preserves the typed alternatives underneath one field.

choices.text: Apply ResolveChoice with make_cols to the reference field.
choices.explanation: This also preserves type alternatives but creates separate top-level columns for them, which the output contract excludes.

choices.text: Apply ResolveChoice with project:string to the reference field.
choices.explanation: Projection retains the string type and can discard values of the numeric type.

choices.text: Apply ResolveChoice with cast:string to the reference field.
choices.explanation: Casting can normalize values to one representation but no longer preserves the original numeric type.

learning.reason: ResolveChoice with make_struct replaces the ambiguous field with a struct containing separate members for the possible types.
learning.concept: Preserve conflicting AWS Glue ChoiceType values within one nested field using make_struct.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Retrieve enough eligible nearest neighbors
prompt: An OpenSearch Service domain uses a Lucene HNSW index for product embeddings. A vector query requests 20 neighbors, and a top-level post_filter keeps only listings from one sales region. It often returns just three listings even though many eligible listings exist. The team wants to keep approximate vector search and avoid choosing a larger fixed candidate count for each region. Which query change meets this objective?

choices.text: Keep the current post_filter and increase only the outer response size.
choices.explanation: A larger response size cannot recover eligible neighbors that were not found in the vector candidate search.

choices.text: Move the region term filter into the k-NN query for the Lucene vector field.
choices.explanation: The filter can participate in search rather than being applied only after selecting the unfiltered neighbors.

choices.text: Replace the filter with a sorting rule that places the target region first after retrieving 20 neighbors.
choices.explanation: Sorting the same candidates cannot retrieve additional eligible vectors or strictly exclude other regions.

choices.text: Replace the approximate query with an exact script-scoring query over all matching documents.
choices.explanation: Exact pre-filtering can return eligible results, but it abandons the requested approximate search approach.

learning.reason: Lucene supports applying a filter within the k-NN search. This lets the search target eligible neighbors instead of discarding ineligible items from an already truncated unfiltered result.
learning.concept: Apply an efficient filter inside the Lucene k-NN query to avoid underfilled results from post-filtering.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Validate multimodal supervised fine-tuning records
prompt: A team prepares a text-and-image supervised fine-tuning dataset for Amazon Nova. It stores one conversation object per line and already checks JSON syntax. An audit finds examples in which the answer was serialized before the user turn and records with inaccessible training image references. Which two additional validations should run before job submission? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Verify that each conversation in messages begins with a user turn and ends with the expected assistant response.
choices.explanation: This ensures the training target is in the assistant turn and follows its user input.

choices.text: Verify that each referenced S3 image exists and is accessible through the Bedrock job's permissions.
choices.explanation: A syntactically valid S3 URI is insufficient if the training job cannot retrieve its referenced image.

choices.text: Sort conversation turns alphabetically by their role field.
choices.explanation: Alphabetical sorting puts assistant before user and can destroy the conversation order.

choices.text: Accept missing assistant responses and assume the supervised job will generate target responses from the images.
choices.explanation: The supervised dataset requires target responses; missing answers are not filled automatically by the job.

choices.text: Validate access only to the JSONL object and infer that image objects are also accessible.
choices.explanation: The referenced images have their own object locations and permissions, which the manifest check does not establish.

learning.reason: The supported message format starts with a user turn and ends with the assistant response. Image URI permissions must also allow Amazon Bedrock to access the actual referenced objects.
learning.concept: Validate prompt-response turn roles and image reference access in Nova multimodal fine-tuning data.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Deliver telemetry into S3 by payload region
prompt: A new Firehose stream receives one JSON sensor event per record. Athena users need S3 objects partitioned by the sales region in each event, even when events from different regions arrive interleaved. The region is an existing top-level field. The team wants Firehose to do the routing without a function or later rewrite. Which two changes to Firehose meet the requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Enable dynamic partitioning and configure an inline jq expression that extracts the region key from each JSON record.
choices.explanation: The partitioning engine receives a region value derived from each record.

choices.text: Enable timestamp expressions in the S3 prefix and use the stream's AWS Region as the sales-region directory.
choices.explanation: The AWS Region identifies infrastructure location. A delivery-time expression does not read the sales-region field.
