choices.text: Include the parsed region key in the S3 destination prefix using partitionKeyFromQuery.
choices.explanation: Firehose uses the extracted key to deliver records under that region's prefix.

choices.text: Configure a random prefix and set Athena table partition projection to the known sales regions.
choices.explanation: Partition projection generates expected paths, but the random prefixes do not place each record under its sales region.

choices.text: Set the sales-region field as the upstream Kinesis partition key without changing Firehose's destination prefix.
choices.explanation: Kinesis sharding does not automatically configure Firehose to use that field in S3 object paths.

learning.reason: Inline jq parsing can extract a partition key from each JSON record. Firehose can use the extracted key in the destination prefix while buffering records by partition.
learning.concept: Partition Firehose S3 delivery by an inline key extracted from each record.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Extract forms and tables from multipage scans
prompt: A training pipeline receives 60-page scanned PDF forms in S3. It needs forms and table relationships, not only line text. Extraction can finish in the background, and the pipeline should fetch results after a success notification instead of polling every few seconds. Which workflow meets these requirements?

choices.text: Call StartDocumentTextDetection with SNS and retrieve the pages with GetDocumentTextDetection.
choices.explanation: This fits the background workflow but detects text rather than returning the requested structured form and table relationships.

choices.text: Use AnalyzeDocument synchronously with the multipage PDF and attach an SNS notification channel to the request.
choices.explanation: The synchronous workflow does not provide this multipage asynchronous notification flow.

choices.text: Call StartDocumentAnalysis for the S3 document with forms and tables enabled and an SNS notification channel. Retrieve the pages with GetDocumentAnalysis after success.
choices.explanation: The asynchronous API accepts the multipage document and returns the requested relationships.

choices.text: Trigger Lambda from the original S3 object's creation and treat that notification as confirmation that Textract results are ready.
choices.explanation: Object creation starts the process. It cannot report completion of the later Textract job.

learning.reason: Textract asynchronous document analysis supports multipage PDF and returns requested structured features. SNS can announce completion, after which the client retrieves the result pages.
learning.concept: Use asynchronous Textract document analysis and fetch results after the completion notification.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Set a shorter lifetime for selected online features
prompt: A SageMaker feature group already records the correct event time and retains its history offline. Most records should expire from online serving after 24 hours, but records marked as provisional should expire after 2 hours. The application must keep one feature group and the same lookup key. Which change implements the two lifetimes?

choices.text: Set only a group TtlDuration of 2 hours and add an ordinary 24-hour retention feature to each permanent record.
choices.explanation: Adding an ordinary feature does not override the expiry configuration. Most records would expire too early.

choices.text: Use different S3 lifecycle rules for provisional and normal records in the offline store.
choices.explanation: This removes historical storage objects and does not enforce the online record's expiry.

choices.text: Keep the 24-hour default and enable ExpirationTimeResponse only for provisional online reads.
choices.explanation: The response option includes expiry information. It does not change the record's configured expiry.

choices.text: Set a feature group TtlDuration of 24 hours and supply a TtlDuration of 2 hours only when putting a provisional record.
choices.explanation: Records without an override inherit 24 hours. The shorter duration applies to the provisional records.

learning.reason: Feature Store supports an online expiration duration at feature-group level and at individual-record level. A provisional record can override the group default without changing its event time or key.
learning.concept: Use a Feature Store group TTL default and override it when writing a provisional record.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reduce time spent listing Glue catalog partitions
prompt: A Glue job reads one day of data from a table with millions of Glue Data Catalog partitions. Its push_down_predicate already prevents unrelated S3 files from being read. The job still starts slowly because its client retrieves the full partition list before applying the predicate. Which change targets that delay?

choices.text: Create a partition index aligned to the partition keys in the date filter and pass a compatible catalogPartitionPredicate.
choices.explanation: The catalog uses the index to restrict the partition listing returned to the Glue job.

choices.text: Use a Spark filter with the same date expression immediately after loading the DynamicFrame.
choices.explanation: The job must first enumerate the catalog partitions and may initiate more input work before a later Spark filter runs.

choices.text: Increase the number of Glue workers and retain only the existing push_down_predicate.
choices.explanation: More workers do not change the full partition enumeration preceding that predicate.

choices.text: Rewrite each partition's input files in larger Parquet blocks.
choices.explanation: Larger files can improve scan efficiency, but the reported delay occurs while enumerating catalog partitions.

learning.reason: Glue catalogPartitionPredicate can perform server-side partition pruning using available partition indexes, reducing full catalog enumeration before S3 file access.
learning.concept: Use a Glue partition index and server-side catalog partition predicate for catalog enumeration overhead.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Handle partial results from a serving feature read
prompt: A prediction service uses BatchGetRecord on an online feature store. Some HTTP 200 responses contain valid records plus UnprocessedIdentifiers. The service must keep completed reads, retry read work the service did not process, and avoid treating those identifiers as missing features immediately. What should it do?

choices.text: Return defaults for every identifier absent from Records whenever the HTTP status is 200.
choices.explanation: The HTTP request can succeed while individual identifiers are still unprocessed.

choices.text: Retain the returned Records and submit a bounded retry for UnprocessedIdentifiers with the original feature projections.
choices.explanation: This completes pending reads without rerunning work that already succeeded.

choices.text: Retry the original full batch and discard all earlier Records.
choices.explanation: That can repeat completed work and lose usable results if the new response is also partial.

choices.text: Retry only identifiers from Records for which ExpiresAt is null.
choices.explanation: A null expiration is unrelated to whether the service processed the record.

learning.reason: The response separates retrieved records, errors, and unprocessed identifiers. The application can retry the unprocessed subset, with backoff and a request deadline.
learning.concept: Treat Feature Store batch reads as potentially partial and retry only UnprocessedIdentifiers.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Preserve adjacency across midnight
prompt: A linear traffic forecast uses the hour of day. Its current numeric hour feature puts 23 and 0 at opposite ends of the scale, even though the station's operating behavior just before and after midnight is similar. The team wants a continuous representation in Data Wrangler. Which transform should it apply?

choices.text: Scale the numeric hour to the interval from zero to one.
choices.explanation: Scaling keeps 23 and 0 at opposite ends of the interval.

choices.text: Use the raw hour as an ordinal integer and standardize it.
choices.explanation: A monotonic affine transform changes scale and offset but does not remove the discontinuity.

choices.text: Featurize the datetime with cyclic encoding for the hour-of-day component.
choices.explanation: Hours next to each other across midnight remain close in the continuous representation.

choices.text: One-hot encode the hour into separate columns with no additional features.
choices.explanation: Separate indicators avoid the large scalar gap but do not encode continuity between adjacent hours.

learning.reason: A cyclic encoding represents periodic time components around a circle rather than as a monotonically increasing scalar.
learning.concept: Use cyclic datetime encoding when nearby values wrap around the end of a time period.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Match text queries against product photos
prompt: A search feature indexes product photos with no captions. A buyer must be able to search those pictures using a text description and receive nearest-neighbor results. The existing system uses unrelated text and image encoders that happen to return vectors of the same length, but distance scores are poor. Which change addresses the representation problem?

choices.text: Keep the unrelated encoders and pad each output with the same number of zeros.
choices.explanation: Padding changes vector lengths but does not realign their learned coordinates.

choices.text: Embed the file names with the existing text encoder and discard all image vectors.
choices.explanation: The requirement is to find visual content and the files have no descriptive text.

choices.text: Keep separate encoders and replace cosine similarity with Euclidean distance.
choices.explanation: Changing the distance calculation does not make independently learned representations comparable.

choices.text: Re-embed photos and encode text queries with the same Titan Multimodal Embeddings model and consistent output settings.
choices.explanation: The vectors represent both modalities in the same learned space.

learning.reason: Comparable dimensions do not align independently trained embedding spaces. Titan Multimodal Embeddings can encode image-only and text-only inputs into a compatible representation for cross-modal similarity.
learning.concept: Use a shared multimodal embedding space for a text query and an image corpus.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Search small passages and return larger context
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base contains long equipment manuals in OpenSearch. Search must locate a precise troubleshooting passage, but the generation input should include the higher-level section metadata and neighboring steps even when the match comes from a short paragraph. Using a single large embedding per section harmed the retrieval ranking. Which chunking approach addresses both needs?

choices.text: Configure hierarchical chunking with a smaller child chunk and a larger parent chunk.
choices.explanation: The knowledge base can select relevant children and return broader parent context.

choices.text: Use one large fixed-size chunk per section and leave retrieval unchanged.
choices.explanation: That would still embed and search the large sections whose ranking the team found too coarse.

choices.text: Use no chunking and treat each complete manual as a single unit.
choices.explanation: This makes the indexed portion even larger than a section and does not provide a fine search unit.

choices.text: Use only tiny standalone chunks and lower the number of results.
choices.explanation: The resulting context would be less likely to include relevant neighboring steps belonging to the same section.

learning.reason: Hierarchical chunking searches child chunks and can replace the matches with their broader parent chunks, giving precise matching and larger returned context.
learning.concept: Use hierarchical retrieval when the search unit should be smaller than context supplied for generation.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Generate translated examples without changing model codes
prompt: An ML team is augmenting HTML support articles with translations. Product codes inside some spans must survive exactly as written, including punctuation, while the surrounding explanations should be translated. The articles are sent through an Amazon Translate operation that accepts HTML. Which source preparation meets this policy?

choices.text: Submit the entire HTML document as plain text with a formality preference.
choices.explanation: Formality affects tone and does not mark specific input spans as immutable.

choices.text: Mark each code span with translate="no" and submit the input as HTML.
choices.explanation: Translate preserves the text inside the marked elements and processes surrounding text normally.

choices.text: Add identical source and target values to custom terminology and treat that as an exact preservation guarantee for every occurrence.
choices.explanation: Custom terminology influences contextual translation, but AWS does not guarantee that it is used in every match.

choices.text: Apply profanity masking and rely on it to skip alphanumeric tokens.
choices.explanation: Profanity masking is a separate output control and does not explicitly exempt designated codes from translation.

learning.reason: Amazon Translate honors do-not-translate markers in supported HTML inputs. Marking just the spans containing codes preserves the original content while allowing surrounding prose to be translated.
learning.concept: Protect fixed tokens with HTML do-not-translate tags in a translation augmentation pipeline.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep cross-table joins with protected identifiers
prompt: Two DataBrew recipes process datasets that share a normalized loyalty ID. Analysts may join the datasets using a protected ID but may not view the originals. A separate authorized audit process must be able to recover an original ID from its protected representation. Which approach meets both requirements?

choices.text: Use probabilistic encryption with a fresh random value for every occurrence of an ID.
choices.explanation: It preserves reversibility for authorized callers but repeated values generally encrypt to different ciphertexts.

choices.text: Replace both ID columns with an identical one-way hash of each input.
choices.explanation: An identical hash can preserve equality, but it does not support authorized decryption to recover the input.

choices.text: Use the same deterministic encryption configuration and key for both ID columns, reserving decryption access for the audit process.
choices.explanation: Equal normalized input IDs produce equal ciphertext under the same setup, and an authorized holder can decrypt it.

choices.text: Replace IDs with random values generated separately by each recipe without maintaining a mapping.
choices.explanation: The replacements do not reliably preserve cross-table equality and cannot be reversed.

learning.reason: Using consistent deterministic encryption for both fields produces equal ciphertext for equal inputs. Authorized decryption remains possible under the scheme's key controls.
learning.concept: Use deterministic encryption for protected equality joins with controlled reversibility.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep variants of each source case in one split
prompt: A team fine-tunes a Bedrock model on approved technical support cases. Each case yields several paraphrased prompt-and-response records. A random split across records put paraphrases from the same case in both datasets and the reported validation loss looked unexpectedly low. How should it prepare the next job's inputs?

choices.text: Hash each final prompt independently to assign its split and reject only identical hashes.
choices.explanation: Paraphrases produce different hashes and can still cross the split.

choices.text: Train on every original case and use paraphrased versions of all cases for validation.
choices.explanation: The validation wording changes, but the model can still have learned the same source cases and answers.

choices.text: Refresh the random split across final records every epoch so leakage averages out.
choices.explanation: Repeated reassignments do not enforce case-level independence and can expose holdout cases to training.

choices.text: Assign each original case to one split before expanding it into paraphrases, then export training and validation files in the selected model's format.
choices.explanation: The holdout measures performance on different cases rather than variants of training records.

learning.reason: Partitioning at the source-case level separates related examples while still providing model-specific training and validation datasets.
learning.concept: Avoid near-duplicate leakage by assigning a source case and its augmentations to one fine-tuning split.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Catch partial deliveries in Glue Data Quality
prompt: An AWS Glue ETL job refreshes a dataset whose normal size grows each week. Once enough history exists, operations wants the job's Data Quality rule to accept the current run only when its row count is at least 85% of the mean of the previous seven runs in the same evaluation context. No fixed record-count threshold should be maintained. Which rule meets the requirement?

choices.text: RowCount >= avg(last(7)) * 0.85
choices.explanation: The rule compares the current count with exactly the specified fraction of the recent mean.

choices.text: RowCount >= last(7) * 0.85
choices.explanation: The right-hand side would contain multiple values. A numeric comparison requires a scalar.

choices.text: RowCount >= avg(last(7)) * 1.15
choices.explanation: This demands 115% of the mean and rejects normal runs that meet the lower bound.

choices.text: RowCount >= last(1) * 0.85
choices.explanation: The immediately preceding count is a different baseline from the mean of seven runs.

learning.reason: A DQDL dynamic rule uses last(7) for recent history and avg to turn the list into a scalar baseline.
learning.concept: Compare Glue Data Quality RowCount with an aggregate of recent results.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Direct labeling effort toward uncertain images
prompt: An existing Ground Truth labeling workflow handles a large image classification dataset. Human labels are available for a seed sample, and the project can accept supported automated labeling for confident records. It must continue sending uncertain images to the human workforce rather than automatically accepting every model prediction. What should it enable?

choices.text: Run Batch Transform once and retain every highest-probability class as an approved label.
choices.explanation: A top predicted class can still have low confidence. This design never sends it for review.

choices.text: Enable automated data labeling for the supported image classification job and use the human workforce in the active-learning loop.
choices.explanation: Ground Truth can auto-label confident examples and ask workers about uncertain examples.

choices.text: Use only label consolidation across multiple workers on every image.
choices.explanation: Consolidation can improve human-label agreement, but it does not automatically label confident examples.

choices.text: Enable automatic labeling for all low-confidence images and route only high-confidence cases to workers.
choices.explanation: This spends expert work on the least uncertain cases and admits the candidates that need review.

learning.reason: Ground Truth automated data labeling can train from human labels, use a validated confidence threshold for auto-labeling, and send uncertain records back to people.
learning.concept: Use Ground Truth active learning to route low-confidence labeling candidates to people.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Find selection bias introduced by requiring complete pairs
prompt: A product inspection model trains only on records that contain both a photo and a written inspection report. Before the inner join, two supplier groups have similar approval rates. Completion counts suggest that rejected items from one supplier group are much less likely to include photos. The team needs to determine whether filtering to complete pairs distorts the training population and fix sampling without inventing labels. Which two actions should it take? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Compare record retention by supplier group and observed outcome, and check positive-label proportions before and after filtering to complete pairs.
choices.explanation: This tests whether the completeness filter changes the training population differently across groups.

choices.text: Balance the total number of joined records for the two suppliers without checking labels.
choices.explanation: Equal supplier counts can still conceal selective loss of rejected items within one of the groups.

choices.text: Calculate the overall approval rate on the joined records and discard the supplier group labels.
choices.explanation: The aggregate cannot isolate a group-specific change in which examples survive the completeness filter.

choices.text: Collect or recover verified photo-report pairs for the underrepresented group-and-outcome slice, keeping the original verified labels.
choices.explanation: This addresses the missing examples without creating false pairings or changing their labels.

choices.text: Copy missing photos from other items with the same approval label until each group has equal counts.
choices.explanation: This introduces photo-report pairs that do not describe the same item and undermines the training data's validity.

learning.reason: A modality-completeness filter can change the outcome distribution differently across groups. Comparing retention and observed label rates by group localizes selection bias before targeted data collection.
learning.concept: Audit class-conditional retention before and after multimodal joins and recover underrepresented verified pairs.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Balance rare positives without changing holdout prevalence
prompt: A SageMaker XGBoost training set contains 24,000 negatives and 600 positives. The team wants a starting weight that gives the two classes roughly equal total weight in training. Its holdout must retain the production class prevalence. Which setting should it try first?

choices.text: Set scale_pos_weight to 0.025 for training and keep the holdout unchanged.
choices.explanation: The inverse ratio would reduce the influence of the already rare positive class.

choices.text: Keep scale_pos_weight at 1 and duplicate positives only in the holdout until both classes are balanced.
choices.explanation: This does not change training and changes the prevalence the holdout must preserve.

choices.text: Set scale_pos_weight to 40 for training and keep the holdout unchanged.
choices.explanation: Weighting the 600 positives by 40 gives their class a total weight comparable with the 24,000 negatives.

choices.text: Set max_depth to 40 and retain default class weighting.
choices.explanation: Tree depth does not independently increase the contribution of the positive class to the objective.

learning.reason: XGBoost scale_pos_weight can raise the importance of positive examples. A training-set ratio of 24,000 divided by 600 is 40.
learning.concept: Set XGBoost positive class weight from training prevalence and leave the evaluation split unweighted.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Impute skewed readings without deleting rows
prompt: A Data Wrangler preparation flow handles a numeric equipment reading. The distribution has a long right tail. Some missing readings must be filled to retain all labeled rows. The owner asks for a replacement based on observed values in the training partition that is less sensitive to unusually large readings. Existing non-missing values must stay unchanged. Which transform is most appropriate?

choices.text: Use Impute missing with the mean strategy fitted on the training partition.
choices.explanation: It keeps rows but gives unusually large readings more influence over the replacement.

choices.text: Remove rows with missing readings and clip the largest observed readings.
choices.explanation: This drops labeled rows and modifies existing values.

choices.text: Fill all missing readings with zero without computing a statistic.
choices.explanation: Zero is a constant rather than the requested replacement computed from observed values.

choices.text: Use Impute missing with the median strategy fitted on the training partition.
choices.explanation: This uses the center of observed training readings and avoids pulling the replacement toward a few large values.

learning.reason: Median imputation uses a measure of central tendency that is more resistant to large outliers than a mean. It fills missing entries while leaving observed entries in the output.
learning.concept: Use median imputation when missing numeric values need an outlier-resistant replacement.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Screen candidate models for long requests
prompt: Two Bedrock models meet a legal summarizer's quality target on short samples. They have different tokenizers and documented context limits. Long requests include system instructions and retrieved text, and the application needs room to generate up to 2,000 tokens. The candidates support CountTokens. How should the engineer determine which model can accommodate representative long requests before benchmarking generation?

choices.text: Count tokens for each candidate using the complete request payload, and compare the counts and 2,000-token output allowance with that model's limits.
choices.explanation: This captures model-specific tokenization and the space consumed by all prompt components.

choices.text: Count the retrieved words with a shared tokenizer and compare only those counts with each model's context limit.
choices.explanation: This omits instructions and ignores differences in model tokenization and output requirements.

choices.text: Send the same long prompt with a ten-token output limit and accept any model that succeeds.
choices.explanation: A successful short response does not show that 2,000 output tokens can fit for those inputs.

choices.text: Select the model with the largest context limit using only the published limit, without measuring either candidate's requests.
choices.explanation: The largest published window may not imply that the team's actual request distribution fits the desired completion budget.

learning.reason: CountTokens evaluates the inference-shaped input with the specified model's tokenizer. The candidate must satisfy both its input limits and the context budget needed for the requested output.
learning.concept: Evaluate model-specific input token usage and reserve the required completion budget.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Train toward a verifiable calculation objective
prompt: A team uses a supported Nova model to produce billing calculations. It has representative prompts and a deterministic validator that can check the numeric result from input facts. It lacks a high-quality target reasoning trace for each prompt, but can automatically score multiple different correct response styles. The team wants to improve the model itself against that objective. Which strategy fits the available data?

choices.text: Supervise on the unmodified model's responses and make every original response its own ground-truth answer.
choices.explanation: Training on the current responses without validating them can reinforce the calculation errors being targeted.

choices.text: Run reinforcement fine-tuning with a Lambda reward function that checks the candidate result against the validator.
choices.explanation: The grader can reward any valid output of the calculation, and the training uses those rewards to update the model.

choices.text: Enable a JSON output schema for the amount field and expect that to teach the model to calculate correctly.
choices.explanation: A schema can validate structure or type. It does not score arithmetical correctness or change model weights.

choices.text: Use the validator once to remove difficult prompts and continue invoking the unchanged model directly.
choices.explanation: Filtering requests this way does not improve the model's ability to solve them.

learning.reason: Bedrock reinforcement fine-tuning samples model responses and learns from reward scores. A deterministic Lambda grader can use the existing validator without declaring one canonical reasoning trace.
learning.concept: Use objective reward grading in Bedrock reinforcement fine-tuning when valid outputs can be verified programmatically.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Forecast distributions for related inventory series
prompt: A retailer has daily unit sales for thousands of products. It wants a model that can learn from related historical product series and provide both a median forecast and a higher quantile for stocking decisions. It can provide product categories and known future promotion features. Which SageMaker algorithm fits?

choices.text: Train one binary classifier to predict whether tomorrow's sales exceed today's sales.
choices.explanation: A binary direction prediction does not provide a distribution of units sold.

choices.text: Train a separate Random Cut Forest for each product and interpret anomaly scores as sales quantiles.
choices.explanation: Anomaly scores do not represent multi-step demand forecasts or forecast quantiles.

choices.text: Train DeepAR across product series with relevant category and future promotion features, and request the required forecast quantiles.
choices.explanation: One model can learn from the related series and return quantiles for decisions with different stockout tolerances.

choices.text: Create a K-Means cluster for each product category and treat its centroid as a full forecast distribution.
choices.explanation: A cluster centroid is neither a model of future temporal behavior nor a distribution of outcomes.

learning.reason: DeepAR learns a probabilistic forecast across multiple related univariate time series and supports quantiles and optional covariates.
learning.concept: Select DeepAR for cross-series probabilistic forecasts with categorical and known future inputs.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Inspect generated SQL before running it
prompt: A company wants a Bedrock chat application to answer questions about current order totals stored in Redshift. Questions require exact aggregation over the latest rows. Company policy requires the application to inspect the generated SQL before it executes, and the team wants to avoid updating a vector index for every order. Which design fits?

choices.text: Use RetrieveAndGenerate directly with the structured Knowledge Base and inspect the SQL only after displaying its answer.
choices.explanation: The operation can execute retrieval before the application has performed its required SQL inspection.

choices.text: Serialize every order as a paragraph and use vector similarity over a nightly indexed snapshot to compute totals.
choices.explanation: Top matching rows do not reliably include all rows needed for an exact current aggregation.

choices.text: Place a daily summary of Redshift outputs in the prompt and let the model estimate totals for future requests.
choices.explanation: A stale summary cannot answer arbitrary exact queries on the latest committed rows.

choices.text: Connect a structured Knowledge Base to the data and call GenerateQuery. Validate the returned SQL in the application and execute only approved queries with read-only access.
choices.explanation: This supports live data and inserts inspection between generation and execution.

learning.reason: A Knowledge Base for structured data can use GenerateQuery to produce SQL without executing it. The application can review and run the approved query against the current database.
learning.concept: Separate SQL generation from execution with GenerateQuery and a structured Bedrock knowledge base.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Choose a training configuration that meets a deadline
prompt: A benchmark measured four SageMaker training configurations that reach the same required validation score. The deadline is three hours. Assume only billed training instance time is relevant, rates are per instance-hour, and each listed instance is billed for the full job runtime. Which compliant configuration costs the least?

choices.text: Two instances at $4 each per hour, taking 2.5 hours.
choices.explanation: The training finishes by the deadline and costs $20, the lowest among the compliant options.

choices.text: One instance at $4 per hour, taking 4 hours.
choices.explanation: This costs $16 but misses the three-hour deadline.

choices.text: Four instances at $4 each per hour, taking 1.5 hours.
choices.explanation: This meets the deadline but costs $24 because each instance is billed.

choices.text: One larger instance at $9 per hour, taking 2.5 hours.
choices.explanation: This meets the deadline but costs $22.50.

learning.reason: Compare job wall time against the deadline, then multiply it by instance count and the per-instance rate. Two instances for 2.5 hours at $4 per hour cost $20.
learning.concept: Compare training deadline and total instance-hour cost using measured runtimes.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Benchmark an optimized inference option correctly
prompt: A team compares standard and latency-optimized inference for the same supported Bedrock model and configuration. During a high-volume run, some requests sent with the optimized setting can be served in standard mode when optimized capacity is unavailable. The team needs reliable latency percentiles and billed-mode comparisons. What should it record?

choices.text: Treat all requests sent with latency optimized as having been served in optimized mode.
choices.explanation: This can mix fallback observations into optimized-mode results and misstate the cost comparison.

choices.text: Record the performance configuration in each response and report per-mode latency and the frequency of fallback in the requested optimized group.
choices.explanation: The response identifies the serving mode, and the fallback rate quantifies production behavior under the tested load.

choices.text: Classify all successful requests below the median latency as optimized.
choices.explanation: Naturally fast standard requests and slow optimized requests can be misclassified using latency alone.

choices.text: Assume a successful optimized request guarantees that later requests with the same prompt use optimized mode.
choices.explanation: Capacity can vary between calls, so an earlier request does not establish how later requests were served.

learning.reason: Bedrock can fall back to standard latency. The served configuration is visible in the API response and distinguishes actual standard service from optimized service.
learning.concept: Classify latency benchmarks by the served Bedrock performance mode rather than the requested mode alone.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Measure sentiment toward each item in the same review
prompt: An English product review often praises one device while criticizing its companion accessory. A team needs a managed API that returns sentiment for each mentioned entity so it can aggregate device and accessory feedback separately. It does not have a labeled training corpus. Which Comprehend capability meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use document sentiment and copy its dominant label to every product name found in the review.
choices.explanation: Document-level polarity cannot distinguish the praise and criticism attached to separate products.

choices.text: Use entity detection alone and interpret each entity detection confidence as its sentiment.
choices.explanation: Detection confidence measures whether a mention was detected, not whether the user praised it.

choices.text: Use targeted sentiment and associate the returned mention sentiments with their corresponding product entities.
choices.explanation: This supplies separate polarity for different entities in one review.

choices.text: Use key phrase extraction and treat the number of phrases containing each product as polarity.
choices.explanation: Frequency of mention is unrelated to whether the opinion is positive or negative.

learning.reason: Targeted sentiment returns entity mentions and the sentiment associated with each mention, allowing opposite opinions in the same review to be separated.
learning.concept: Use Amazon Comprehend targeted sentiment when opinion polarity is needed at entity level.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Model sparse click interactions without enumerating feature crosses
prompt: An advertising team trains on sparse one-hot features for ad category, page category, and device type. It needs a supervised click predictor that can learn pairwise feature interactions without manually materializing every combination. It prefers a built-in SageMaker algorithm. Which approach should it use?

choices.text: Train a built-in Linear Learner on the same raw one-hot columns and do not add interaction terms.
choices.explanation: An additive linear model on unchanged columns does not learn pair-specific effects.

choices.text: Use PCA to reduce the sparse features and directly treat a principal component as a click probability.
choices.explanation: PCA is unsupervised and a component value is not a calibrated supervised prediction.

choices.text: Train an unsupervised Random Cut Forest on the sparse features and interpret its anomaly score as click likelihood.
choices.explanation: Anomaly detection does not learn the relationship to the click labels.

choices.text: Train a built-in Factorization Machines binary classifier on the sparse features and click labels.
choices.explanation: The model can learn feature-pair interactions without a separate explicit feature for each combination.

learning.reason: The built-in Factorization Machines algorithm represents pairwise interactions with factors, allowing efficient supervised learning on high-dimensional sparse features.
learning.concept: Use SageMaker Factorization Machines for supervised pairwise interactions in sparse input.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Reuse tuning history after a dataset refresh
prompt: A SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning job found promising ranges for a classifier. New examples have since been added to the training and validation datasets. The algorithm and objective remain compatible with the parent job. The team wants to use the parent's tuning observations to inform the new search while testing candidate configurations on the refreshed data. Which configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Create a warm-start tuning job with TRANSFER_LEARNING and reference the earlier job as a parent.
choices.explanation: This allows refreshed data and reuses observations to help choose new candidates.

choices.text: Create an IDENTICAL_DATA_AND_ALGORITHM warm-start job while replacing the training and validation data.
choices.explanation: That warm-start type requires the same input data as the parent.

choices.text: Start a new random search with the same ranges and omit the parent reference.
choices.explanation: The reused range limits are not the parent's actual tuning observations.

choices.text: Deploy the parent's best model package directly, then use its old validation score to rank current candidates.
choices.explanation: This neither runs a new search nor measures the candidates on the refreshed dataset.

learning.reason: TRANSFER_LEARNING warm start allows a new tuning job to use different input data while making use of previous tuning results.
learning.concept: Choose the AMT warm-start type that permits new data while inheriting relevant tuning history.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Remove a straggler caused by uneven S3 files
prompt: A custom distributed SageMaker training job has eight workers and a training channel using ShardedByS3Key. Input consists of a few very large objects and many tiny ones. The job synchronizes training steps across hosts, and metrics show one host spends much longer decoding its input while the others wait. The framework already reads only the files assigned to each host. Which action targets the bottleneck?

choices.text: Add more workers while keeping the same few large objects.
choices.explanation: One large object still belongs to a single input shard assignment, so new workers do not break it up.

choices.text: Rewrite the training dataset as many comparably sized objects and keep ShardedByS3Key.
choices.explanation: The input distribution can assign multiple balanced objects to each worker rather than putting a giant object on one host.

choices.text: Increase the learning rate on hosts that finish decoding first.
choices.explanation: The learning rate does not change input decoding time or relieve the collective synchronization wait.

choices.text: Switch to FullyReplicated without changing the framework's data reading logic.
choices.explanation: Each worker would receive the full input instead of a separate assignment, causing duplicate work and changing data coverage.

learning.reason: ShardedByS3Key distributes objects rather than byte ranges within an object. Repartitioning into numerous similarly sized training objects reduces uneven per-worker input.
learning.concept: Balance distributed SageMaker input by making S3 object shards comparable in processing size.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Reduce an XGBoost generalization gap
prompt: An XGBoost model has nearly perfect training predictions but much lower validation performance across multiple independent folds. A split audit confirms no leakage and similar train and validation distributions. Most final tree leaves contain very few effective training examples. Which two changes directly constrain this complexity? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Reduce max_depth.
choices.explanation: Shallower trees reduce the model's ability to fit very specific combinations of features.

choices.text: Increase max_depth without changing any other parameter.
choices.explanation: More splitting capacity can increase the observed overfitting.

choices.text: Decrease min_child_weight.
choices.explanation: The model would permit even smaller children, aggravating the stated mechanism.

choices.text: Recompute training metrics on the validation records and keep the original model unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing the reporting boundary does not constrain tree complexity or improve generalization.

choices.text: Increase min_child_weight.
choices.explanation: Higher minimum child weight prevents splitting to create children with too little effective training data.

learning.reason: Shallower trees cap the number of successive splits. A higher min_child_weight discourages leaves with very little effective training weight.
learning.concept: Constrain XGBoost tree depth and minimum child weight when small leaves overfit.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Prevent leakage when stacking base models
prompt: A team combines two classifiers in a stacking ensemble. Its current meta-model trains on predictions from base models fitted on the very rows they predict. The meta-model performs well on its training inputs but fails on new data. The team must keep learned stacking weights. How should it construct the meta-model's training inputs?

choices.text: Fit base models once on all development rows, then shuffle those predictions before fitting the meta-model.
choices.explanation: Shuffling changes row order but does not remove in-sample optimism or leakage.

choices.text: Use holdout test labels as an input to the meta-model and refit against the base predictions.
choices.explanation: Outcome labels would be unavailable as inference features and would invalidate the held-out assessment.

choices.text: Split development data into folds, fit each base model on the other folds, and build meta-training rows using predictions on each held-out fold.
choices.explanation: Each meta-training row uses base predictions made without exposing its label to the generating base models.

choices.text: Average the outputs equally at inference and discard the meta-model.
choices.explanation: This eliminates the learned stacking weights rather than correcting their training data.

learning.reason: Out-of-fold predictions come from a base model that did not train on the record it predicts. These outputs provide realistic training features for the stacking layer.
learning.concept: Train the stacking layer on out-of-fold predictions to avoid in-sample base-model leakage.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Teach a prompt the boundary between similar labels
prompt: A Bedrock model classifies support tickets using short label definitions. It often confuses a question about cancelling renewal with a report of a completed cancellation. The team has a few approved labeled examples that demonstrate the difference. It needs a quick change to inference behavior while keeping the same model weights. Which prompt change is most suitable?

choices.text: Raise the temperature to make the model more willing to choose a different label.
choices.explanation: More sampling variance does not teach the model how the two cases should be classified.

choices.text: Add examples for only the common class and omit the examples of completed cancellations.
choices.explanation: That leaves the ambiguous boundary unrepresented on one side and can accentuate label bias.

choices.text: Set an output schema containing the permitted label names but leave the input examples absent.
choices.explanation: A schema can limit valid output names without explaining when each name applies.

choices.text: Add both types of labeled boundary examples as clearly delimited demonstrations before the unlabeled ticket.
choices.explanation: The model can infer the distinction from explicit input-label pairs while classifying the new ticket.

learning.reason: Few-shot input-output examples show how the labels apply to representative boundary cases, which short definitions alone may not convey.
learning.concept: Use representative few-shot demonstrations to disambiguate a classification boundary without retraining.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Recover recall after vector quantization
prompt: An OpenSearch Service vector index uses disk-based Faiss search and retains full-precision vectors for rescoring. A new compression level reduced memory use but sorting quantized candidates loses some exact top matches. The team can tolerate extra query work and wants to rescore a larger set per query without rebuilding the index or returning more final results. Which change should it test?

choices.text: Increase the query's rescore oversample_factor and keep k fixed.
choices.explanation: More initial candidates can be reconsidered with their original vector values before truncation to k.

choices.text: Keep the rescoring configuration fixed and raise the final k above the application's required response count.
choices.explanation: That changes the requested neighbor count rather than explicitly expanding just the rescoring candidate pool.

choices.text: Increase vector compression further while leaving the rescoring candidate pool unchanged.
choices.explanation: More compression increases representation loss and does not add any candidates eligible for rescoring.

choices.text: Change the graph construction ef_construction parameter in the running query.
choices.explanation: That parameter controls graph building, not the number of full-precision candidates re-ranked for the current query.

learning.reason: The rescore oversample_factor controls how many approximate candidates are loaded and re-ranked with full-precision vectors before results are reduced to k.
learning.concept: Increase retrieval oversampling for full-precision rescoring while keeping the requested result count fixed.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Stabilize the first updates without lowering the eventual rate
prompt: A supported Bedrock Nova customization job is unstable during the first few updates when it starts immediately at the selected learning rate. A previous experiment showed stable training once the model reached that rate gradually. The team wants the same target learning rate and enough subsequent updates at the intended schedule. Which hyperparameter should it adjust?

choices.text: Reduce the target learning rate and leave the warmup at zero.
choices.explanation: This changes the eventual step size instead of creating the requested initial ramp.

choices.text: Increase learningRateWarmupSteps within the job budget and keep the target learning rate unchanged.
choices.explanation: The initial updates use a smaller learning rate before approaching the selected target.

choices.text: Increase epochs while keeping the same zero-warmup configuration.
choices.explanation: More passes do not change the first updates that caused the instability.

choices.text: Reduce learningRateWarmupSteps while keeping the target rate.
choices.explanation: The model would reach the target even sooner, the opposite of the observed stabilizing change.

learning.reason: Learning-rate warmup steps control how many initial updates are used to increase the rate to its configured value. A modest warmup preserves subsequent useful training steps.
learning.concept: Increase learning-rate warmup for gradual initial updates while preserving the target rate.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Compare shadow error rates when the traffic counts differ
prompt: A SageMaker shadow test mirrors a representative 10% of production requests to a candidate. The original variant saw 10,000 invocations and 100 model errors. The shadow saw 1,000 invocations and 30 model errors over the same period. Its p95 ModelLatency was lower. The release gate requires that the candidate's per-request model error rate not increase. What should the engineer conclude?

choices.text: The shadow passes because 30 errors are fewer than 100 errors.
choices.explanation: The raw counts use different denominators and are not comparable as rates.

choices.text: The shadow passes because its rate is 0.3% when calculated using all 10,000 production invocations.
choices.explanation: Most production requests were never sent to the shadow. Its own 1,000 invocations are the denominator.

choices.text: The shadow fails the error-rate gate because its rate is 3% versus the production rate of 1%.
choices.explanation: Lower latency does not compensate for a separate required error-rate gate.

choices.text: The shadow fails because every request sent to both variants must have identical latency.
choices.explanation: The quality gate concerns error rates, and the latency result is a separate metric.

learning.reason: Compare per-variant error rates using the number of invocations received by each variant. The rates are 1% for production and 3% for shadow.
learning.concept: Normalize shadow and production model errors by each variant's own invocation count.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Catch non-finite gradient values during training
prompt: An existing SageMaker Debugger customer runs a supported PyTorch job. Loss sporadically becomes NaN, and the engineers suspect that an individual gradient first becomes infinite. Tensor collection for gradients is enabled. Which built-in rule should they configure to catch either NaN or infinity in the recorded gradients?

choices.text: Use VanishingGradient and set its threshold near zero.
choices.explanation: That rule detects gradients with very small mean magnitude. It does not test for the requested non-finite values.

choices.text: Use LossNotDecreasing to detect a plateau in the training loss.
choices.explanation: A plateau rule cannot directly identify a non-finite gradient tensor.

choices.text: Use AllZero on the gradient collection.
choices.explanation: A tensor whose values are all zero is finite and is a different failure condition.

choices.text: Use ExplodingTensor on the gradient collection and set only_nan to false.
choices.explanation: The rule can flag either infinity or NaN among the recorded gradients.

learning.reason: ExplodingTensor detects non-finite tensors. Restricting it to collected gradient tensors and leaving only_nan false lets it report both cases.
learning.concept: Use SageMaker Debugger ExplodingTensor to detect NaN and infinity in monitored tensors.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Compare rare-event ranking across operating thresholds
prompt: Two SageMaker classifiers return continuous scores for a fault that occurs in 0.5% of real examples. The same representative holdout is available for both candidates. The decision threshold has not been chosen, and operations wants a summary of the tradeoff between the precision of alerts and the share of faults detected across thresholds. Which measure should the team compare?

choices.text: Area under the precision-recall curve for each candidate on the same holdout.
choices.explanation: It summarizes precision and recall across thresholds for the target positive class.

choices.text: Overall accuracy at a fixed 0.5 threshold.
choices.explanation: One operating point cannot summarize the tradeoff. Accuracy can also be dominated by the many negatives.

choices.text: Area under the ROC curve as the direct summary of alert precision.
choices.explanation: ROC relates true positive rate to false positive rate, not precision to recall.

choices.text: The fraction of fault examples above each model's median score, without considering wrong alerts.
choices.explanation: This describes sensitivity at a particular threshold and excludes precision.

learning.reason: The precision-recall curve measures precision and recall as the threshold changes. Its area summarizes the tradeoff on a holdout with the intended positive prevalence.
learning.concept: Use AUPRC to compare precision-recall tradeoffs for rare positives on the same population.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Interpret asymmetric semantic coverage scores
prompt: A model condenses technical notices. Reviewers see that short responses use only correct concepts, but omit several concepts the reference notices contain. BERTScore precision is high and BERTScore recall is low. What is the most consistent explanation?

choices.text: Most reference tokens have close matches in the candidate, but many candidate tokens have no close match in the reference.
choices.explanation: That pattern would favor recall over precision and is more consistent with a verbose answer adding unrelated content.

choices.text: Most candidate tokens have close matches in the reference, but more reference tokens lack close matches in the candidate.
choices.explanation: This describes a short response that stays on topic but omits reference content.

choices.text: Precision measures exact word order, so a short candidate can score high only when it preserves all reference phrases.
choices.explanation: BERTScore uses contextual token similarities and does not require every reference phrase or exact word order for high precision.

choices.text: The difference proves the response contradicts the reference even though it covers all concepts.
choices.explanation: The scores describe semantic alignment and coverage. They do not prove logical contradiction.

learning.reason: Precision averages semantic token matches from the candidate perspective. Recall averages them from the reference perspective. A short, relevant answer can match most of its own tokens while covering only part of the reference.
learning.concept: Interpret BERTScore precision and recall using the direction of candidate-reference token coverage.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Compare toxic output risk on matched prompts
prompt: An evaluation team compares a production and a candidate Bedrock model before rollout. It needs a quantitative toxicity comparison on the same held-out set of realistic customer prompts. Factual accuracy is already covered by a separate evaluation. Which two choices isolate the requested behavior? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use a separate prompt set for each model selected from the requests each one already handled successfully.
choices.explanation: The differences could come from prompt mix and selection bias rather than from the models.

choices.text: Run both models on the same held-out prompts and hold other compatible generation settings fixed.
choices.explanation: Using the same input population reduces variation due to prompts and settings.

choices.text: Score toxicity in the generated text for each model and compare the results.
choices.explanation: The comparison measures the specific output behavior of interest.

choices.text: Score only the content of the original prompts for toxicity without generating responses.
choices.explanation: This measures input properties and does not show how either model behaves.

choices.text: Use exact-match accuracy on an unrelated factual question-answering dataset to infer the safer model.
choices.explanation: Factual accuracy on another task does not measure toxicity of the tested outputs.

learning.reason: An automatic model evaluation can use a toxicity metric with matching prompts. Keeping prompts and generation settings controlled improves comparability between the models.
learning.concept: Compare model-output toxicity on a fixed held-out prompt set using a dedicated metric.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Find unsupported claims when the evidence was retrieved
prompt: A Bedrock RAG assistant retrieves all the needed policy passages, but generated responses sometimes add extra fees that are absent from those passages. The team wants a built-in metric on a retrieve-and-generate evaluation that directly checks whether the response is supported by the retrieved context. Which metric should it select?

choices.text: Builtin.ContextCoverage in a retrieve-only evaluation.
choices.explanation: Coverage can be high because the correct passage was retrieved, even if the generated response later adds unsupported details.

choices.text: Builtin.Completeness.
choices.explanation: Completeness asks whether the response covers expected content, which does not directly test every added claim against the source.

choices.text: Builtin.Faithfulness.
choices.explanation: This metric targets whether the response adds claims absent from the supplied context.

choices.text: Builtin.Refusal.
choices.explanation: This measures whether the model declined to answer, unrelated to whether an answered claim is supported.

learning.reason: Faithfulness checks whether statements in a generated response are supported by the available context. Retrieval coverage measures a different component.
learning.concept: Measure Bedrock RAG faithfulness when generation introduces claims beyond retrieved evidence.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Warm a serverless endpoint before requests arrive
prompt: A CPU-only SageMaker Serverless Inference endpoint serves almost all queries during a scheduled morning reporting window. The first requests often violate the response target because of cold starts. The team wants to keep the serverless endpoint, pre-warm enough capacity before the window, and reduce reserved capacity afterward. Which approach meets the requirement?

choices.text: Set a high MaxConcurrency and continue using only on-demand serverless capacity.
choices.explanation: MaxConcurrency limits concurrent invocations but does not pre-warm that many execution slots.

choices.text: Set up only target tracking on current concurrency utilization and leave the pre-window capacity unchanged.
choices.explanation: Reactive scaling does not raise capacity before the known arrival of requests.

choices.text: Send all early reports to an asynchronous endpoint and return its result location instead of the answer.
choices.explanation: This changes the synchronous contract and does not improve the existing serverless endpoint's readiness.

choices.text: Register the variant's DesiredProvisionedConcurrency scaling target and schedule a scale-out before reporting and a scale-in afterward.
choices.explanation: Warm provisioned capacity can be established before the first requests, with less reserved capacity outside the window.

learning.reason: Application Auto Scaling can schedule adjustments to serverless Provisioned Concurrency before predictable traffic and reduce it after the window.
learning.concept: Schedule SageMaker Serverless Provisioned Concurrency for known traffic windows.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Keep three inference stages under one managed endpoint
prompt: The team has separate containers for feature normalization, prediction, and formatting a business response. A synchronous prediction request must pass through all three in that order. The caller should make only one request, and the team wants SageMaker to run the stages together on each endpoint instance. Which hosting configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Deploy the three containers in a SageMaker serial inference pipeline in the required execution order.
choices.explanation: The endpoint sends each container's output to the next container for the same request.

choices.text: Use direct invocation mode and set TargetContainerHostname to the preprocessing container.
choices.explanation: Direct mode targets one container. This does not automatically call the prediction and formatting stages.

choices.text: Deploy each container as a separate production variant and set all three weights equally.
choices.explanation: Variant weighting selects which variant serves a request, rather than composing a request across every variant.

choices.text: Deploy the containers as a multi-model endpoint and rely on the model artifact name to chain the stages.
choices.explanation: Multi-model routing loads the requested model. It does not define an ordered three-stage chain.

learning.reason: A SageMaker serial inference pipeline executes containers in order and forwards each intermediate response to the next container on the same instance.
learning.concept: Deploy ordered preprocessing, prediction, and postprocessing containers as a serial SageMaker inference pipeline.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Keep record IDs out of model input while retaining them in results
prompt: A SageMaker Batch Transform job reads JSON Lines records that contain transaction_id and features. The container accepts only features. Downstream processing needs transaction_id and the prediction in each result record without a second job to join files. Which three settings together meet the requirement? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Set InputFilter to select features only.
choices.explanation: This sends the model exactly the field it accepts.

choices.text: Set InputFilter to include transaction_id with the features.
choices.explanation: This passes an unsupported field to the container.

choices.text: Set JoinSource to Input.
choices.explanation: SageMaker retains original input fields alongside the prediction.

choices.text: Set OutputFilter to select transaction_id and SageMakerOutput from the joined record.
choices.explanation: The final file contains the required association without keeping unused feature content.

choices.text: Set JoinSource to None and expect OutputFilter to recover transaction_id from the source file.
choices.explanation: The separate source record is not available to OutputFilter when its contents were not joined.

learning.reason: InputFilter chooses what is sent to the model, JoinSource can append the prediction to the original record, and OutputFilter keeps the necessary IDs and responses.
learning.concept: Use SageMaker Batch Transform input and output filters with JoinSource set to Input.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Call an already-deployed Marketplace model through Bedrock
prompt: A team deployed a compatible Bedrock Marketplace foundation model into its account and has the ARN of the resulting SageMaker endpoint. The application already standardizes on the Bedrock Runtime InvokeModel API. Which model identifier should it pass when invoking this deployment?

choices.text: Use the SageMaker public hub content ARN from the catalog as the modelId.
choices.explanation: The hub identifier describes the source model, not the caller's deployed instance.

choices.text: Use the full deployed SageMaker endpoint ARN as InvokeModel's modelId.
choices.explanation: This routes the Bedrock invocation to the model deployed on that endpoint.

choices.text: Use the ARN of the deployment's SageMaker execution role as the modelId.
choices.explanation: The execution role authorizes hosting operations and does not identify an inference target.

choices.text: Use only the endpoint's unqualified name, as in the SageMaker InvokeEndpoint API.
choices.explanation: For this Marketplace flow, Bedrock Runtime expects the endpoint ARN rather than the SageMaker endpoint name.

learning.reason: Bedrock Runtime can invoke the deployed Marketplace model using the ARN of the SageMaker endpoint associated with the marketplace deployment.
learning.concept: Invoke a deployed Marketplace model using its SageMaker endpoint ARN as the Bedrock model identifier.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Combine results across two specialist agents
prompt: An existing Amazon Bedrock Agents deployment has a pricing specialist and a contract specialist. A request can ask how a proposed price changes obligations under an existing contract. The final response must combine findings from both specialists, with one agent accountable for the synthesis. Which collaboration setup fits?

choices.text: Use SUPERVISOR_ROUTER only to choose one specialist to return the final response for all requests.
choices.explanation: Single-destination routing does not ensure both specialists' findings are synthesized.

choices.text: Disable collaboration and create one alias with routing instructions to the two specialists.
choices.explanation: An alias selects a version of one agent and does not coordinate separate agents.

choices.text: Associate both prepared specialists as collaborators and use SUPERVISOR so the supervisor coordinates their results and answers.
choices.explanation: The supervisor can use both specialists and produce one synthesized response.

choices.text: Invoke each specialist independently and forward whichever response returns first.
choices.explanation: This drops part of the required pricing and contract context.

learning.reason: The SUPERVISOR configuration lets the supervisor orchestrate collaborators and produce a final response from their contributions.
learning.concept: Choose Bedrock Agents supervisor orchestration when a response requires synthesis across collaborators.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Enable compliant cross-Region model capacity
prompt: An application runs successfully with in-Region Bedrock inference. The organization is considering cross-Region capacity but permits inference only in selected Regions. The candidate geographic profile includes a destination prohibited by the organization's SCP, and profile calls fail. Which rollout decision preserves the residency policy?

choices.text: Keep the profile and rely on Bedrock to skip the disallowed destination automatically.
choices.explanation: A blocked destination can make the call fail; Bedrock does not limit the profile to only the allowed subset.

choices.text: Switch to a global inference profile while granting access only to the local source Region.
choices.explanation: The source Region does not bound a global profile's routing destinations.

choices.text: Use an application inference profile based on the current geographic profile and add tags for each approved Region.
choices.explanation: Tags can support attribution but do not narrow the underlying destination set.

choices.text: Select an eligible profile and source Region whose complete destination set is permitted, and confirm required IAM and SCP access. Retain in-Region inference if no eligible profile exists.
choices.explanation: This preserves the residency boundary and avoids depending on a profile with a blocked destination.

learning.reason: A cross-Region profile can route to any destination it defines. If an SCP blocks a destination, invoking that profile can fail even if other destinations are available.
learning.concept: Validate all Bedrock inference-profile destinations against residency and SCP requirements.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Retrieve evidence for both sides of a comparison
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base answers single-product warranty questions correctly. When a user compares coverage for two different products, retrieval often finds evidence for only one product. The team wants a managed adjustment that can run separate searches for components of a compound question before composing one answer. Which setting should it enable?

choices.text: Set the RetrieveAndGenerate query transformation type to QUERY_DECOMPOSITION.
choices.explanation: Bedrock can run separate retrieval queries for the components of the comparison.

choices.text: Increase the model's maximum response tokens and leave retrieval unchanged.
choices.explanation: A longer answer budget does not make the retrieval stage search for the other product.

choices.text: Append the entire prompt again to the vector query so the longer input has more weight.
choices.explanation: Repetition does not isolate or separately search for each product.

choices.text: Lower the number of returned retrieval results to one so both policies can be inferred from the best result.
choices.explanation: One result can omit an entire side of the comparison. The system would have less evidence.

learning.reason: Query decomposition can split a complex prompt into separate focused searches and use their evidence to generate one response.
learning.concept: Enable Bedrock Knowledge Bases query decomposition for multi-part evidence collection.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Migrate two stacks that share a network export
prompt: A networking CloudFormation stack exports the private subnet ID used by two SageMaker deployment stacks. The old subnet must stay usable until each deployment stack has moved to a new subnet. Both stacks use Fn::ImportValue. Which sequence respects CloudFormation's dependencies and supports a staged migration?

choices.text: Replace the subnet ID in the existing export before changing either consumer.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation prevents changing an exported value while it is imported.

choices.text: Publish the new subnet ID under a separate export name. Update each consumer to import it, then remove the old export after no stack imports it.
choices.explanation: The existing consumers remain valid during the transition, and the protected export is removed only after its imports are gone.

choices.text: Delete the exporting stack first and leave both deployment stacks unchanged.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation blocks deletion while the exports are in use, and those consumers still need the subnet.

choices.text: Use the old and new subnet IDs as simultaneous values for the same export name.
choices.explanation: An export name must be unique within the account and Region. It cannot represent two separate values simultaneously.

learning.reason: An imported export cannot be modified or removed until its consumers are updated. A separate export lets both subnet IDs remain available during migration.
learning.concept: Introduce a new CloudFormation export and migrate imports before removing the old export.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Publish only the inference artifact from a training image
prompt: A custom SageMaker training container writes a final model and a diagnostic report. Training succeeds, but the deployment cannot find the final model artifact. The script currently saves both files under its working directory in the image. Which layout lets SageMaker publish the finished model separately from the diagnostic output?

choices.text: Write both files under /opt/ml/output/data and configure the endpoint to read the training image's working directory.
choices.explanation: The working directory does not carry files generated by the separate training job into hosting.

choices.text: Write both files under /opt/ml/model and rely on SageMaker to recognize the report by its extension.
choices.explanation: The model directory is packaged as a unit. Its content is not split by a diagnostic file extension.

choices.text: Write the trained model under /opt/ml/model and the diagnostic report under /opt/ml/output/data.
choices.explanation: SageMaker packages the required model from its defined model path and uploads auxiliary output separately.

choices.text: Put the trained model under /opt/ml/input/data and write the report to the model directory.
choices.explanation: The input channel path does not define the final model artifact. The model folder would instead contain the report.

learning.reason: SageMaker packages files written to /opt/ml/model as model artifacts. Other training output belongs under /opt/ml/output/data.
learning.concept: Write the deployable artifact and auxiliary training output to the distinct SageMaker container paths.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Replace an endpoint configuration while keeping its invoke name
prompt: An automation job has already created a new SageMaker Model for an existing prediction service. It must point the running endpoint at that model and new instance settings without asking clients to change their endpoint name. The old configuration must remain available for recovery. Which API sequence fits?

choices.text: Call CreateEndpoint again using the existing endpoint name and the replacement configuration.
choices.explanation: CreateEndpoint is for a new endpoint and cannot update a named resource already in use.

choices.text: Change the previous ModelName in the original deployment manifest and take no endpoint action.
choices.explanation: Editing a manifest alone does not change the configuration used by an existing endpoint.

choices.text: Use UpdateEndpointWeightsAndCapacities to replace the model resource bound to a production variant.
choices.explanation: That API changes variant weight or capacity settings and does not replace the referenced SageMaker Model.

choices.text: Create a new endpoint configuration referencing the new model and settings. Call UpdateEndpoint with the existing endpoint name and new configuration name.
choices.explanation: The endpoint name stays stable while the hosting configuration is replaced.

learning.reason: UpdateEndpoint takes the existing endpoint name and a new endpoint configuration. The old configuration can remain available for a future update.
learning.concept: Apply a new SageMaker endpoint configuration to an existing endpoint using UpdateEndpoint.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Wake asynchronous capacity on a single queued request
prompt: An asynchronous SageMaker endpoint scales down to zero when idle. Its regular target-tracking policy responds when the queue is sufficiently large, but a single new request can remain queued below the target. The team wants to retain scale-to-zero and trigger capacity when any request is waiting with no instances. What should it add?

choices.text: Add a step-scaling policy that scales up when HasBacklogWithoutCapacity indicates queued work with zero instances.
