choices.explanation: The endpoint can start capacity for even one queued request while preserving the idle scale-to-zero behavior.

choices.text: Set the minimum instance count to one and keep the same target tracking.
choices.explanation: This avoids the empty endpoint but prevents the required scale-to-zero behavior.

choices.text: Scale on CPU utilization of the current instances when a new request arrives.
choices.explanation: With zero instances there is no current compute utilization to trigger this response.

choices.text: Increase the regular queue target so the endpoint scales sooner.
choices.explanation: A larger threshold can allow a small backlog to wait even longer before it triggers scaling.

learning.reason: HasBacklogWithoutCapacity explicitly indicates queued work while the instance count is zero. A step-scaling policy can use that signal to start one instance.
learning.concept: Use the async backlog-without-capacity signal to bootstrap scale-out from zero.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Connect a private vector collection to a knowledge base
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base uses a custom service role to access a private OpenSearch Serverless collection. The role already has the required IAM permissions, but the collection's network and data access policies do not mention Bedrock or the role. Public access must remain disabled. Which two changes are needed? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Allow only access from a developer desktop's OpenSearch Serverless VPC endpoint.
choices.explanation: That does not authorize the AWS service as a private source and does not grant data permissions to its role.

choices.text: Add Bedrock as an allowed AWS source service in the collection's private network policy.
choices.explanation: This permits the Bedrock service to reach the collection privately.

choices.text: Make collection network access public and leave the data policy unchanged.
choices.explanation: This violates the private-access requirement and still leaves the role absent from the data access policy.

choices.text: Grant the knowledge base role the required collection and index operations in a data access policy.
choices.explanation: The specific service role is then authorized to read or write the relevant index as required.

choices.text: Change only the trust relationship on the role so Bedrock can assume it a second time.
choices.explanation: The missing controls are the collection's network and data access policies. Role trust alone does not satisfy either one.

learning.reason: OpenSearch Serverless checks both the network policy and the data access policy. The network policy can allow Bedrock private service access and the data policy can grant the exact knowledge base role access to its target index.
learning.concept: Grant both Bedrock private network access and role-scoped vector collection data access.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Match citations to individual generated statements
prompt: A documentation assistant already invokes Bedrock RetrieveAndGenerate. Its interface currently displays all sources at the bottom. The team wants to put each source marker beside the exact part of the generated response it supports, without parsing the response for guessed document names. Which response fields should it use?

choices.text: Sort all retrieved references by document title and assign them to generated sentences in the same order.
choices.explanation: Document title order has no relationship to which claims a reference supports.

choices.text: Use each citation's generatedResponsePart.textResponsePart.span to locate answer text and its retrievedReferences to display the associated sources.
choices.explanation: The service returns the span and its matching evidence together.

choices.text: Split the response into equal-length text segments based on the number of retrieved references.
choices.explanation: Reference counts do not establish the positions or lengths of cited claims.

choices.text: Use the response sessionId to compute the page position of each citation.
choices.explanation: The session ID maintains conversational context and does not identify text spans or source pages.

learning.reason: Each citation associates generated text and its span with one or more retrieved references. The app can use those fields to map source locations to the answer.
learning.concept: Map a RetrieveAndGenerate citation's generated text span to that citation's retrieved references.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Remember user preferences across independent conversations
prompt: A support agent starts a new conversation each time a user opens its interface. It should recall a user's preferred communication format across conversations while ensuring its preference lookups are scoped to the authenticated user. The team uses managed AgentCore Memory. How should it organize the long-term preferences?

choices.text: Scope all preference records to the current conversation's session ID and require an exact match on subsequent requests.
choices.explanation: A new conversation has a different session ID, so it would not retrieve prior preferences under that key.

choices.text: Store preferences in one shared namespace and rely on natural-language ranking to infer which user owns a result.
choices.explanation: Similarity ranking is not an ownership check and cannot guarantee separation of users' preferences.

choices.text: Use the user preference memory strategy with an actor-level namespace, resolving the actor ID from the caller's authenticated identity.
choices.explanation: The strategy can consolidate that user's preferences and use their namespace in later conversations.

choices.text: Write preferences into ephemeral process memory for each conversation and use the default runtime endpoint across users.
choices.explanation: A shared endpoint does not make temporary state durable or enforce ownership for long-term retrieval.

learning.reason: A user preference strategy extracts persistent preferences. The actor-level namespace scopes them to the same verified actor across sessions.
learning.concept: Store AgentCore long-term user preferences at the authenticated actor level across sessions.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Calculate how many model copies fit on each host
prompt: A SageMaker endpoint instance has 4 allocatable accelerators, 12 allocatable CPU cores, and 48 GiB of allocatable RAM after fixed overhead. Before deployment, measurements show one inference-component copy requires 1 accelerator, 5 CPU cores, and 18 GiB of RAM. The copies must meet all three reservations. What is the maximum number of these copies that can fit on one instance?

choices.text: Three copies.
choices.explanation: Three would require 15 cores and 54 GiB RAM, above the available resources.

choices.text: Four copies.
choices.explanation: There are four accelerators, but that alone does not determine valid placement.

choices.text: One copy.
choices.explanation: Two can fit concurrently within all three stated resource limits.

choices.text: Two copies.
choices.explanation: They require 2 accelerators, 10 cores, and 36 GiB RAM. A third copy would exceed CPU and RAM.

learning.reason: Each copy needs all resource types. Accelerator capacity permits four copies, but both CPU and RAM permit only two.
learning.concept: Size SageMaker inference component placement by the tightest per-copy compute reservation.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Test an authorization policy against real request patterns
prompt: An AgentCore Gateway already serves agent tools. A team wrote a narrower policy engine configuration and wants to review which tool calls it would deny before changing live authorization behavior. It will enforce the policy after unexpected denials are resolved. Which sequence meets the requirement?

choices.text: Associate the policy engine in LOG_ONLY, review decision telemetry, then change to ENFORCE after validating the policy.
choices.explanation: This exposes would-be decisions while preserving current behavior during observation.

choices.text: Associate the policy engine in ENFORCE immediately and use production failures to find denied actions.
choices.explanation: ENFORCE can block real requests during the observation period.

choices.text: Skip the policy engine and infer its decisions from tool invocation counts.
choices.explanation: Invocation counts cannot show what the proposed policy would have allowed or denied.

choices.text: Update the agent prompt to describe the new rules and review the model's explanation of each decision.
choices.explanation: Prompt instructions do not evaluate the deployed authorization policy against actual calls.

learning.reason: LOG_ONLY evaluates and records what the policy would decide without enforcing it. ENFORCE is the mode that applies the decisions after validation.
learning.concept: Validate AgentCore Gateway policy decisions in LOG_ONLY before enabling enforcement.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Start a release workflow when a model package is approved
prompt: A SageMaker registry group receives candidate versions marked PendingManualApproval. A separate deployment workflow should start when a version in this group becomes Approved. The event source may deliver an event again, and unrelated registry events must not promote a model. Which orchestration fits?

choices.text: Trigger the workflow on every successful CreateTrainingJob event for the account.
choices.explanation: Training completion does not establish that a model package was registered or approved.

choices.text: Match SageMaker Model Package State Change events for the target group and Approved status. In the target, confirm the package is still approved and deduplicate by its version ARN.
choices.explanation: The event selects the desired state, current-state validation avoids stale approval, and retries do not promote the version twice.

choices.text: Match all registry events and always promote the package group ARN's newest version.
choices.explanation: This can promote an unrelated or still-pending version because the operation disregards the approved version in the event.

choices.text: Start promotions when an event reports PendingManualApproval and wait until the deployment finishes to check approval.
choices.explanation: This makes a deployment happen before the required approval decision.

learning.reason: EventBridge receives Model Package State Change events containing approval details. A scoped target can verify the current package state and use the version ARN for idempotency.
learning.concept: Trigger promotion from scoped model-package approval events with version-level deduplication.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Invalidate pipeline cache when training data changes
prompt: A preprocessing step in SageMaker Pipelines enables caching. A CI workflow overwrites training.csv at the same S3 URI and executes the pipeline again. Its step inputs, options, and cache window remain unchanged, so the step can reuse yesterday's prepared output. The team wants unchanged inputs to remain cacheable while new dataset content triggers new preprocessing. What should it change?

choices.text: Extend the cache expiry and continue overwriting the input object at the same URI.
choices.explanation: A longer reuse window can keep serving the stale processing output for longer.

choices.text: Change the output object's S3 retention rule while leaving the processing input identical.
choices.explanation: Output retention does not make changed training content visible to the cached step inputs.

choices.text: Publish changed content to a new immutable dataset URI and pass that URI as the processing input.
choices.explanation: Changing the versioned input attribute invalidates cached work for changed data while repeat requests for the same URI can still reuse results.

choices.text: Keep the mutable input URI and turn off caching for the entire pipeline permanently.
choices.explanation: That can avoid stale results but also removes the required cache reuse for unchanged inputs.

learning.reason: Step caching compares selected step attributes rather than independently validating all object contents behind an unchanged S3 URI. A new immutable URI in the processing input provides a changed attribute.
learning.concept: Represent changing S3 content with immutable input locations used in SageMaker pipeline cache keys.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Catch prompt regressions hidden by a higher average score
prompt: A candidate Bedrock prompt raises average summary quality on held-out tickets. Release policy separately requires every safety escalation summary to include its escalation deadline. Those tickets represent only 2% of the holdout. The current pipeline checks only the overall mean quality score. What should the team change in the prompt release test?

choices.text: Raise the overall quality threshold but use the same traffic-weighted mean as the only gate.
choices.explanation: A higher mean can still mask failures on a small slice whose requirement is mandatory.

choices.text: Score deadline preservation only in the prompt examples used while writing the candidate.
choices.explanation: Those examples can show that the prompt works on seen cases without checking the required behavior on held-out cases.

choices.text: Report the escalation-slice score but allow the overall average to override a failed deadline check.
choices.explanation: That observes the failure but does not enforce the stated release policy.

choices.text: Add a representative held-out escalation slice and independently require its deadline-preservation check to pass before promoting the prompt variant.
choices.explanation: A failed deadline check can block release even if average quality improves elsewhere.

learning.reason: A mean quality score weights rare escalation cases lightly. A separate release gate on representative escalation examples directly verifies the mandatory behavior.
learning.concept: Add a slice-specific mandatory behavior gate to prevent rare prompt regressions being hidden by an aggregate score.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Recover the lineage of a custom model version
prompt: An incident review needs the base-model ARN and exact customization-job ARN for a specific Bedrock model used the previous week. The on-call engineer has the model ARN captured in the deployment record. Multiple customization jobs have display names with the same prefix. What should the engineer use?

choices.text: Call GetCustomModel using the captured ARN and read baseModelArn and jobArn from that response.
choices.explanation: The returned metadata is tied to the specific model version in the deployment record.

choices.text: Choose the newest customization job whose name starts with the same prefix.
choices.explanation: A newer job with a similar name may have produced a different model.

choices.text: Describe the model's current inference profile and assume the profile creation time identifies the customization job.
choices.explanation: Inference routing information does not uniquely identify the artifact's training job.

choices.text: Use the public foundation-model catalog to infer the customization job.
choices.explanation: The catalog describes available base models and does not store this account's custom-model job lineage.

learning.reason: GetCustomModel accepts the custom model identifier and returns its baseModelArn and jobArn. These link the selected artifact to the exact job even when names are similar.
learning.concept: Read exact Bedrock custom-model provenance from its model resource rather than guessing from job names.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Identify the failed pipeline step in the notification
prompt: A SageMaker pipeline has several processing and evaluation steps. When a step fails, the operations team needs a notification containing the step name, pipeline execution ARN, and failure reason. It wants the alert at the step transition, without periodic Describe calls. Which event should it subscribe to?

choices.text: Match only whole-pipeline execution status events and read stepName directly from them.
choices.explanation: Whole-pipeline events describe execution state and do not provide the same step-specific detail.

choices.text: Match SageMaker Model Building Pipeline Execution Step Status Change events with currentStepStatus equal to Failed.
choices.explanation: The event carries the identifiers and reason needed to route the alert directly to the responsible team.

choices.text: Match every CreateProcessingJob API event and interpret a successful creation as a step failure.
choices.explanation: Accepting a job request happens before its eventual outcome and does not provide a step failure reason.

choices.text: Use a CloudWatch alarm on the count of pipeline executions and include its metric name as the failed step.
choices.explanation: The count cannot identify a particular execution step or explain its failure.

learning.reason: The pipeline execution step status change event includes the step name and execution ARN, plus failureReason when the step fails.
learning.concept: Use SageMaker pipeline step status events for targeted failure diagnostics.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Recognize a changed feature-to-outcome relationship
prompt: A deployed churn classifier receives the same type and distribution of features as it did during validation. New verified labels show that, for comparable customer profiles, churn is now more frequent after a change in the renewal policy. The schema is unchanged. Which finding should direct the team's next monitoring change?

choices.text: Monitor only feature histograms because the evidence demonstrates covariate drift.
choices.explanation: Stable input histograms do not detect the change in outcome probabilities for similar feature records.

choices.text: Treat the issue as schema drift and add another field-type check.
choices.explanation: The schema is unchanged. A type check does not assess the feature-to-label relationship.

choices.text: Monitor performance and conditional outcome changes using recent labels because the evidence indicates concept drift.
choices.explanation: The relationship between features and the outcome changed even though input distributions appear stable.

choices.text: Measure only endpoint latency to detect changes in churn behavior.
choices.explanation: Latency measures serving performance, not the predictive relationship with the target.

learning.reason: Concept drift concerns changed outcomes conditional on the inputs. Marginal input checks can stay stable while the relationship learned by the model stops holding.
learning.concept: Detect concept drift with current labeled outcomes when input distributions are stable.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Isolate interventions on generated content after a guardrail update
prompt: An application calls Bedrock ApplyGuardrail separately for prompts and generated answers. It is the only guardrail workload in a dedicated AWS account and Region and uses exactly one version at a time. Following an output policy update, total interventions grew. Which CloudWatch time series distinguish the stage where the increase occurred?

choices.text: Inspect only the total InvocationsIntervened for the new guardrail version, without separating content sources.
choices.explanation: The version total shows the overall change but does not indicate which stage caused it.

choices.text: Compare InvocationClientErrors by content source.
choices.explanation: An intervention can be a successful guardrail action. It is not necessarily a client error.

choices.text: Compare TextUnitCount by version and treat any increase as a corresponding number of interventions.
choices.explanation: Text units measure the amount of processed content, not how often the policy intervened.

choices.text: Compare the Input and Output series for InvocationsIntervened using the GuardrailContentSource dimension.
choices.explanation: The two series distinguish decisions about user prompts from decisions about generated answers.

learning.reason: GuardrailContentSource distinguishes Input from Output for InvocationsIntervened. Compare these series around the known time of the policy rollout.
learning.concept: Separate guardrail intervention telemetry by the evaluated content source.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Give operations one dashboard across workload accounts
prompt: Three AWS accounts publish SageMaker endpoint metrics in the same Region. Operators in a dedicated monitoring account need one CloudWatch dashboard using the original account metrics. Policy prohibits copying raw inference payloads or writing separate custom metrics for this dashboard. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Link each workload account as an observability source to the monitoring account, share metrics, and build widgets using source-account metrics.
choices.explanation: The monitoring account can display the existing SageMaker metrics without copying inference data or publishing duplicates.

choices.text: Republish prediction payloads from all accounts into the monitoring account and build new metrics from the payloads.
choices.explanation: This transfers data the policy prohibits and duplicates telemetry already available.

choices.text: Add all endpoint names as dimensions on a monitoring-account-only metrics query and do not configure cross-account sharing.
choices.explanation: Matching dimension values do not grant access to metrics stored in another account.

choices.text: Create a separate dashboard in each source account and use the monitoring dashboard only for links.
choices.explanation: This leaves the operators without the requested combined view of the metrics.

learning.reason: Cross-account observability can share selected telemetry from linked source accounts, enabling dashboard widgets to reference the original metrics from the monitoring account.
learning.concept: Build one CloudWatch dashboard with linked source-account metrics through cross-account observability.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Avoid coupling unrelated workloads through an SDK rate limiter
prompt: A gateway uses one AWS SDK client for inference calls for multiple business units. A burst from one unit receives throttling errors. The gateway needs bounded automatic retries with jitter but must avoid a client-side rate limiter that delays initial requests for the unaffected units because the client is shared. Which retry choice fits?

choices.text: Use adaptive mode on the same shared client for all traffic and rely on it to isolate each unit automatically.
choices.explanation: Adaptive mode's limiter is per client, so one unit's throttles can delay requests from other units sharing it.

choices.text: Use standard retry mode with a configured maximum attempt count and keep the application request deadline.
choices.explanation: This allows bounded, randomized retries without Adaptive mode delaying first attempts through a shared rate limiter.

choices.text: Retry every throttled call immediately with the same interval forever.
choices.explanation: Unbounded, synchronized retries increase load and violate the deadline and retry limits.

choices.text: Disable SDK retries entirely and return the first throttling error.
choices.explanation: That avoids extra attempts but does not provide the requested automatic retry behavior.

learning.reason: Standard retry mode provides jittered backoff and a retry quota without Adaptive mode's client-wide first-attempt rate limiter.
learning.concept: Use AWS SDK standard retry mode when a shared client must retry but cannot throttle unrelated initial calls.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Find unusual model spend below the monthly budget
prompt: A mature AWS account has normal weekly peaks in its ML-service spend. Finance wants notice when a service charge departs significantly from its own historical pattern even if the overall monthly budget is still under its limit. It also needs the main cost contributors ranked by dollar impact. Which service feature fits?

choices.text: Use only a forecasted AWS Budgets alert at the monthly limit.
choices.explanation: A forecast below the limit can coexist with a material departure from a particular service's usual pattern.

choices.text: Alarm on Bedrock InvocationLatency as a direct measure of unexpected charges.
choices.explanation: Request latency does not establish billed cost or identify its financial contributors.

choices.text: Set up AWS Cost Anomaly Detection for the relevant spend and subscribe to anomaly notifications.
choices.explanation: It considers recurring spend patterns and provides ranked cost contributors for investigation.

choices.text: Increase Service Quotas for training instances so that cost alerts are emitted sooner.
choices.explanation: Quotas govern resource availability and cannot analyze historical charge patterns.

learning.reason: AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses learned spend patterns and provides root-cause dimensions such as service, account, Region, and usage type.
learning.concept: Use learned-billing anomaly detection to flag abnormal spend independently of a fixed monthly budget.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Commit to a predictable usage baseline across instance families
prompt: A team has a dependable baseline of eligible SageMaker AI training and inference usage. It cannot tolerate interruptions and expects to shift the baseline among supported instance sizes, families, and Regions. Finance can commit to a consistent hourly dollar amount but wants that commitment to follow eligible usage. Which option fits?

choices.text: Use Managed Spot Training for all baseline training and inference traffic.
choices.explanation: Spot Training can be interrupted and does not provide the stated benefit for steady hosted inference usage.

choices.text: Buy an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for one family and Region and assume that it automatically covers all SageMaker components.
choices.explanation: That is a separate plan type and does not give the requested SageMaker coverage and flexibility.

choices.text: Commit to keeping one fixed instance type in the original Region and rely on the commitment applying if the jobs move.
choices.explanation: A commitment tied to a fixed configuration does not satisfy the requirement to follow eligible usage through the stated changes.

choices.text: Purchase a SageMaker AI Savings Plan sized for the predictable eligible baseline.
choices.explanation: It follows eligible SageMaker usage across the expected resource changes without selecting interruptible capacity.

learning.reason: SageMaker AI Savings Plans apply discounted pricing to eligible SageMaker instance usage across components, families, sizes, and Regions in exchange for an hourly spend commitment.
learning.concept: Apply a SageMaker AI Savings Plan to steady eligible usage that moves across configurations.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Release resources between independent agent visits
prompt: Most AgentCore Runtime sessions complete a task and then remain idle for 15 minutes. Session telemetry shows resource use accumulating during the idle period. Users rarely return within five minutes, durable state is stored outside the microVM, and approved long-running active tasks must keep their current maximum lifetime. Which change addresses idle resource use?

choices.text: Reduce idleRuntimeSessionTimeout to a tested lower value and retain maxLifetime.
choices.explanation: Idle compute can end earlier without tightening the maximum lifetime for active work.

choices.text: Reduce maxLifetime to five minutes while keeping the default idle timeout.
choices.explanation: The hard lifetime could terminate approved active tasks that run beyond five minutes.

choices.text: Reduce the foundation model's output token limit but keep lifecycle settings the same.
choices.explanation: This may change model usage but does not shorten how long a completed session remains idle.

choices.text: Generate a new session ID after each response and leave the idle timeout unchanged.
choices.explanation: Previous sessions still remain idle until their current lifecycle rule releases the compute.

learning.reason: Idle timeout terminates the compute only after a period without activity. Maximum lifetime is a separate limit that can affect active work.
learning.concept: Reduce AgentCore idle runtime timeout independently of maximum active compute lifetime.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Bound the cost of overly verbose outputs
prompt: A Bedrock assistant generates three-bullet summaries. Input size is stable, but some requests produce far more output tokens than needed. The selected model must stay the same, and typical valid answers fit comfortably within 250 output tokens. The team wants a per-request output ceiling while preserving the complete input. What should it do?

choices.text: Trim every input to the first 250 tokens but leave model output settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: This removes source content and does not enforce an output ceiling.

choices.text: Set inferenceConfig.maxTokens to a tested output ceiling and verify that summaries finish before reaching it.
choices.explanation: This caps generation while allowing the full input and exposes truncation during validation.

choices.text: Lower temperature without setting a maximum token count.
choices.explanation: Temperature changes sampling behavior and cannot enforce a fixed maximum response length.

choices.text: Enable prompt caching on the fixed instructions and assume the generated answer is capped automatically.
choices.explanation: Caching reusable input can improve input processing efficiency but does not limit new output length.

learning.reason: Converse inferenceConfig.maxTokens constrains generated tokens. An evaluated cap beyond the usual response length reduces long-tail work without discarding the input.
learning.concept: Cap generated tokens independently of input length with Bedrock Converse maxTokens.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Avoid recomputing identical embeddings in bulk refreshes
prompt: A custom indexing job calls a Bedrock text embedding model on every document chunk, every night. The team pays to embed unchanged text repeatedly, although only a small fraction of chunks change. It needs to keep the per-document metadata, and must never reuse an embedding computed with a different model configuration. Which design is appropriate?

choices.text: Cache by document filename alone and reuse the first vector for every future revision.
choices.explanation: The same filename can contain new text, so this can keep stale embeddings after an edit.

choices.text: Cache by hash of the text only and reuse cached vectors when changing the output dimensions or model version.
choices.explanation: Text equality does not make outputs from different embedding configurations compatible.

choices.text: Cache vectors by a content hash combined with model version and embedding configuration. Attach each reused vector to its own document metadata and re-embed on cache misses.
choices.explanation: This reuses unchanged computation without mixing incompatible embeddings or document-specific metadata.

choices.text: Cache one vector per document category and share it across all chunks with that category label.
choices.explanation: A category label does not make different chunk text represent the same meaning.

learning.reason: Embeddings are generated for the text input and configured model output. Cache by the exact embedding input, model version, and output settings so only changed inputs or settings need fresh calls.
learning.concept: Reuse embedding results for identical model version, embedding settings, and exact text while storing document metadata independently.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Scan repository material before the container exists
prompt: An ML platform already scans its final ECR image. It now needs managed static checks on first-party inference API source, third-party dependencies, and infrastructure-as-code changes in a connected repository before a build is promoted. Which addition directly covers that earlier stage?

choices.text: Increase the frequency of the existing ECR image scan.
choices.explanation: Scanning the same artifact more often does not evaluate unbuilt source or infrastructure files in the repository.

choices.text: Use CloudTrail to list every commit author and treat an approved identity as proof of secure code.
choices.explanation: Identity auditing does not check the contents for security issues.

choices.text: Rely only on an endpoint health check after deployment.
choices.explanation: A readiness check neither scans the repository nor identifies findings before promotion.

choices.text: Configure Amazon Inspector Code Security for the supported repository and use its findings in the pre-promotion review.
choices.explanation: The scan evaluates the source, dependencies, and infrastructure definitions without waiting for a built image.

learning.reason: Amazon Inspector Code Security can scan supported connected repositories for findings in source code, dependencies, and IaC. ECR image scanning covers a distinct artifact stage.
learning.concept: Use Inspector Code Security repository scans alongside artifact scanning for earlier CI/CD findings.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Restrict training reads to the approved columns and rows
prompt: A SageMaker preparation job uses Athena engine version 3 to query a Lake Formation managed table. Approval covers only a fixed set of feature columns and rows whose consent flag is true. Other principals still need full access to the table. The training role has no direct S3 bypass and should receive no broader SELECT grants. How should access be granted?

choices.text: Create a Lake Formation data filter with the approved columns and consent predicate, then grant the training role SELECT on that filter.
choices.explanation: The restriction applies through the integrated Athena query regardless of the SQL the training role submits.

choices.text: Grant full SELECT to the training role and include the predicate only in one team-owned Athena query.
choices.explanation: The role could submit a different query and read rows or columns outside the approved subset.

choices.text: Make the entire dataset available to the role in S3 and remove unapproved fields after download.
choices.explanation: That gives the training role access to data it is not permitted to read.

choices.text: Grant SELECT with column filtering only and assume the correct consent rows will be selected by Athena.
choices.explanation: A column filter alone does not enforce the required row predicate.

learning.reason: A Lake Formation data filter can combine column restrictions with a row filter. Granting SELECT on that filter to the training role limits its authorized query results.
learning.concept: Use a Lake Formation cell-level data filter for the training role's approved columns and rows.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Bind a knowledge base role to its approved resource
prompt: A dedicated service role provides document access to one Bedrock knowledge base. It currently trusts the Bedrock service principal without source conditions. The security standard requires both an explicit owning-account check and a check for the specific approved knowledge base. Which two changes belong in the trust statement? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Restrict only the role's S3 actions and leave the assumption trust unchanged.
choices.explanation: Data permissions do not restrict which source knowledge bases cause the role to be assumed.

choices.text: Set aws:SourceAccount to the account that owns the approved knowledge base.
choices.explanation: This checks the expected account for the service-to-service request.

choices.text: Use the source document bucket ARN as the permitted aws:SourceArn for role assumption.
choices.explanation: The caller context identifies the invoking Bedrock resource. The document bucket is not that resource.

choices.text: Replace the Bedrock service principal with the application developer's IAM user.
choices.explanation: That removes the service trust needed by the knowledge base and does not implement delegated service assumption.

choices.text: Restrict aws:SourceArn to the exact ARN of the approved Bedrock knowledge base.
choices.explanation: This binds assumption to that resource rather than any knowledge base in the account.

learning.reason: The service principal can remain Bedrock while source conditions constrain the account and exact knowledge base resource for which Bedrock may assume the role.
learning.concept: Restrict AWS service role assumption by both source account and exact Bedrock knowledge base ARN.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Retain approved inference inputs and outputs for review
prompt: A dedicated account runs a Bedrock model via InvokeModel and has approval to retain selected application text for a controlled audit. The security team must review the exact request and response content, with access limited to its encrypted audit destinations. Existing API audit events give it caller information but no bodies. What should the ML team configure?

choices.text: Record only CloudWatch input and output token count metrics.
choices.explanation: Token counts describe size and do not contain the text under review.

choices.text: Enable Bedrock model invocation logging for text and configure authorized encrypted destinations and retention for the collected records.
choices.explanation: The configured logging captures text bodies for review and the destination controls restrict access.

choices.text: Add more CloudTrail API events and use them as a substitute for documenting request and response text.
choices.explanation: API audit telemetry does not provide the complete InvokeModel text bodies required here.

choices.text: Turn on payload logging only in application clients and leave all clients able to read the central log store.
choices.explanation: That fails the stated destination access policy and can leave gaps if clients do not log a request.

learning.reason: Bedrock model invocation logging can capture invocation payloads and send them to approved CloudWatch Logs and S3 destinations. API audit records serve a different purpose.
learning.concept: Enable Bedrock model invocation logging for authorized payload review with restricted destinations.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Find the configuration blocking a private call
prompt: An internal EC2 application times out when connecting to the private SageMaker Runtime interface endpoint on TCP port 443. Private DNS resolves to the expected endpoint address. The two resources are in the same VPC, and the team wants to identify which routing or filtering component blocks the configured path without sending test packets. What should it use?

choices.text: Examine only aggregate SageMaker ModelLatency for the endpoint.
choices.explanation: The request may never reach model execution, so model processing latency cannot locate the network blockage.

choices.text: Review only the application's IAM policy simulator output for InvokeEndpoint.
choices.explanation: IAM authorization does not diagnose a TCP connection that times out before the request reaches the service.

choices.text: Run Reachability Analyzer for the source network interface and destination interface endpoint on TCP 443.
choices.explanation: It checks whether the configured path is reachable and can report the blocking components.

choices.text: Use VPC Flow Logs alone to identify the exact rule responsible for a rejected flow.
choices.explanation: Flow logs can show traffic metadata and rejection, but do not directly identify the blocking rule in every case.

learning.reason: Reachability Analyzer models the network path and reports blocking configuration components such as security groups or network ACLs without sending traffic.
learning.concept: Use static VPC path analysis to localize a private endpoint's network configuration failure.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Isolate the training container while staging approved artifacts
prompt: A SageMaker training job runs a vendor-supplied container. Compliance requires that the container make no outbound network calls, including to S3, and receive no AWS credentials. SageMaker must still download the configured training input and upload the trained model to the approved S3 locations. Which two changes meet the requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Attach the container to private subnets with an S3 endpoint and allow its network access only to S3.
choices.explanation: The runtime could still call S3 directly, which the policy prohibits.

choices.text: Place AWS credentials for the input bucket in the image and disable external internet access.
choices.explanation: Even without internet access, providing embedded credentials violates the isolation requirement.

choices.text: Enable network isolation on the SageMaker training job.
choices.explanation: The runtime receives no AWS credentials and cannot make outbound service calls.

choices.text: Configure the job's training input and model output paths and give its execution role access only to those approved resources.
choices.explanation: The SageMaker service can stage local files and publish the model with its execution role.

choices.text: Omit SageMaker's execution role and let the isolated training script obtain temporary credentials when it starts.
choices.explanation: Isolation prevents the requested outbound call and the environment must not expose credentials to the script.

learning.reason: With network isolation, SageMaker can stage approved inputs and outputs itself using the execution role while the container cannot call external services or access AWS credentials.
learning.concept: Use SageMaker network isolation with service-managed S3 transfer and a scoped execution role.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Detect sensitive data in a staging prefix
prompt: New training files land in an S3 staging prefix each week. Compliance wants recurring object-level findings if supported file contents contain regulated identifiers. The workflow needs a managed inspection step and should preserve the original files for a separate approval process. Which control should it configure?

choices.text: Enable S3 server access logging and infer sensitive content from which principals put each object.
choices.explanation: Access logs record object operations, not the sensitive data types in the object body.

choices.text: Enable encryption at rest and treat every encrypted object as having passed sensitive content review.
choices.explanation: Encryption keeps stored data protected but does not classify its contents.

choices.text: Use an S3 lifecycle rule that moves older files to a different storage class and reports those transitions.
choices.explanation: Storage class transitions neither inspect for regulated identifiers nor produce the requested findings.

choices.text: Configure a recurring Macie discovery job scoped to the staging prefix and select the applicable managed data identifiers.
choices.explanation: Macie can report sensitive content on individual objects without rewriting the training files.

learning.reason: Amazon Macie discovery jobs analyze the contents of supported S3 objects, can run on a schedule, and can use prefix scope and managed identifiers to report findings.
learning.concept: Use scoped, scheduled Amazon Macie discovery for sensitive content in staged S3 training files.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Require the approved guardrail at the API boundary
prompt: An organization has approved a particular numbered Bedrock guardrail version. Multiple teams already have permission to invoke foundation models through Converse and InvokeModel. A forgotten application setting must not allow calls without the required guardrail version. How should security enforce it?

choices.text: Apply a policy that explicitly denies covered model invocation actions when bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier differs from the approved versioned ARN, and allow the authorized guardrail application.
choices.explanation: This makes the approved guardrail an authorization requirement regardless of other model invocation allows.

choices.text: Attach a conditional Allow for the guardrail to a new policy but leave all existing unconditional invocation Allows as the only controls for other cases.
choices.explanation: Conditional Allow alone does not override another valid unconditional Allow.

choices.text: Put a reminder to invoke the guardrail in every system prompt and trust the model to apply it.
choices.explanation: Prompt content cannot enforce API authorization or insert a missing guardrail configuration.

choices.text: Add the approved guardrail as a cost-allocation tag on each model inference profile.
choices.explanation: Tags do not require that inference requests include a guardrail or a particular version.

learning.reason: The bedrock:GuardrailIdentifier condition key can enforce the approved version in supported inference APIs. An explicit deny on an omitted or different identifier applies even when another policy allows invocation.
learning.concept: Enforce the approved numbered Bedrock guardrail via an IAM explicit deny for mismatched or missing identifiers.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Evaluate a lower-cost host with an artifact compiled for it
prompt: An inference service currently runs an image classifier compiled with SageMaker Neo for its GPU family. The team identified a supported CPU instance family that could meet the latency target at lower cost. The original model artifact and framework are compatible with Neo on the new target. How should the team compare this option before migration?

choices.text: Copy the existing GPU-compiled artifact unchanged to any supported CPU instance and test only whether the endpoint starts.
choices.explanation: A GPU-targeted compilation is not guaranteed to run on the CPU target, and startup does not establish serving performance.

choices.text: Compile the original artifact for the candidate CPU target, deploy it to a matching test instance, and measure latency and cost at the required load.
choices.explanation: The artifact matches the hardware and the results can support a fair operating-cost decision.

choices.text: Compile again for the existing GPU target but change only the SageMaker endpoint's instance family to CPU.
choices.explanation: Changing the host does not change the compiled artifact's target.

choices.text: Infer model latency by scaling the GPU benchmark result in proportion to the CPU instance's hourly price.
choices.explanation: Instance price does not predict how this model executes on different hardware.

learning.reason: Neo compilation is target-specific. Compile the original artifact for the candidate CPU target and benchmark the resulting model on that target.
learning.concept: Recompile for a supported SageMaker Neo target family before measuring performance on it.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Diagnose wrong tool choice in selected agent runs
prompt: An AgentCore support agent sometimes chooses the order-tracking tool when the user asked to check inventory. Both tools work when called, and the final response can sound helpful even after the wrong choice. For an incident review the team has recorded session spans and wants to score the observed tool-selection decisions on the exact affected spans. Which evaluation meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use a final-answer helpfulness score on a newly sampled set of live sessions.
choices.explanation: That evaluates a different property on different sessions and can miss the historical wrong tool choice.

choices.text: Alarm on the agents' overall HTTP error count.
choices.explanation: A valid response with the wrong tool can still succeed at the transport level.

choices.text: Send the recorded session spans to on-demand evaluation with Builtin.ToolSelectionAccuracy and specify the affected span IDs.
choices.explanation: The evaluator examines tool choice at the selected span scope.

choices.text: Score only whether the selected tool received syntactically valid parameters.
choices.explanation: Well-formed parameters can be passed to an inappropriate tool; parameter validity does not evaluate selection.

learning.reason: AgentCore on-demand evaluation can target supplied span IDs. Builtin.ToolSelectionAccuracy assesses whether the selected tool was appropriate.
learning.concept: Use an on-demand tool selection evaluator on specific historical AgentCore spans.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Export an Athena training snapshot without a new table
prompt: A SageMaker workflow needs the result of an existing Athena SELECT as Parquet files. It cannot create intermediate catalog tables. Each successful export should have its own prefix, and downstream code must identify which objects belong to that export. Which approach meets the requirements?

choices.text: Run a normal SELECT and set the query result output location to a path ending in .parquet.
choices.explanation: The extension does not change the ordinary SELECT result format.

choices.text: Use CTAS with Parquet and assume that setting an external location prevents catalog table creation.
choices.explanation: CTAS still creates a table.

choices.text: Use UNLOAD to the same previously populated unpartitioned prefix and assume it replaces earlier files.
choices.explanation: UNLOAD checks that an unpartitioned output destination is empty and does not replace those files.

choices.text: Use UNLOAD with format PARQUET to a new empty prefix, and consume the successful query's output manifest.
choices.explanation: The query exports Parquet without a new catalog table and the manifest identifies its written files.

learning.reason: UNLOAD writes supported formats without creating a table and emits a data manifest. Using an empty prefix isolates each unpartitioned export.
learning.concept: Use Athena UNLOAD and its manifest for a catalog-free collection of exported query objects.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Preserve the exact version used to train a regulated model
prompt: An audit requires an ML team to preserve the exact version of a training manifest for seven years. Even administrators in the active account must be unable to remove that protected version or shorten its retention. New manifest versions may be written for later runs. Which storage control fits?

choices.text: Use an Object Lock enabled, versioned S3 bucket and set compliance retention on the model's manifest version.
choices.explanation: The protected version remains available for the retention period, while newer versions can still be added.

choices.text: Use S3 Versioning alone and retain the version ID in the model record.
choices.explanation: Versioning identifies revisions but does not prevent a sufficiently privileged user from deleting an earlier version.

choices.text: Use an Object Lock governance retention that administrators can bypass.
choices.explanation: Governance permits operation by specially authorized callers, which is too weak for the stated requirement.

choices.text: Apply only a legal hold that administrators can lift on request without a timed retention period.
choices.explanation: A removable legal hold does not give the required irreversible retention date.

learning.reason: S3 Object Lock compliance retention protects an individual version until a specified date and prevents users from shortening the lock.
learning.concept: Use compliance-mode S3 Object Lock for immutable retention of a specific version.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reduce KMS traffic from new encrypted objects
prompt: A pipeline writes millions of small training objects with SSE-KMS. Storage requests succeed, but KMS request volume has become a bottleneck. The team must keep SSE-KMS with the same key and can use a key policy compatible with the bucket-level encryption context. Existing objects can stay as written. What should it change for new writes?

choices.text: Increase the S3 object's multipart upload part size and leave the encryption configuration alone.
choices.explanation: The stated bottleneck is the large count of separately encrypted objects, not the part size of individual uploads.

choices.text: Enable S3 Bucket Keys on the bucket's SSE-KMS configuration.
choices.explanation: New eligible objects use a bucket-level key instead of needing the original pattern of KMS calls for each object.

choices.text: Switch the bucket default to SSE-S3.
choices.explanation: This stops using the required KMS key.

choices.text: Turn on S3 Versioning so every upload gets a version ID.
choices.explanation: Version IDs improve history management and do not reduce how often encryption needs KMS.

learning.reason: S3 Bucket Keys let S3 reuse a bucket-level key for multiple objects under the same KMS key, reducing calls to KMS.
learning.concept: Enable S3 Bucket Keys for new SSE-KMS writes when per-object KMS traffic is the bottleneck.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Resume a streaming ingest after a planned restart
prompt: A Glue streaming ETL job reads Kafka telemetry. During maintenance the team needs to restart the same compatible application without intentionally replaying retained events or skipping unread ones. The source data is retained and the existing sink already handles retry safely. Which state must be carried forward?

choices.text: Start with a new checkpoint and use the latest starting position.
choices.explanation: Unread events that arrived before the restart may be skipped.

choices.text: Start with a new checkpoint and use the earliest retained offset.
choices.explanation: This can replay already processed retained records.

choices.text: Restart with the same persistent checkpoint location.
choices.explanation: The job can resume using the streaming progress recorded there.

choices.text: Enable Glue job bookmarks and discard the streaming checkpoint.
choices.explanation: Glue streaming jobs use checkpoints rather than batch job bookmarks.

learning.reason: Glue streaming ETL uses its checkpoint to track successfully read source data. Keeping the existing checkpoint lets a compatible restarted job continue from its saved progress.
learning.concept: Preserve the Glue streaming checkpoint to resume source offsets after restarting.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Apply hourly corrections to an Iceberg feature table
prompt: A pipeline prepares one change row per customer key per hourly batch. It must update changed features, insert new customers, and remove deleted customers in one transaction against an existing Apache Iceberg table. Readers should not see separate partial updates. Which Athena operation is suitable?

choices.text: Use one INSERT INTO statement to append every operation as a new row.
choices.explanation: An append does not remove or update earlier rows in the table.

choices.text: Run separate DELETE, UPDATE, and INSERT statements and expose the table immediately after each one.
choices.explanation: Consumers can see intermediate states between statement commits.

choices.text: Export the current target to CSV and update its files while leaving the Iceberg table metadata unchanged.
choices.explanation: Iceberg readers use table metadata to determine committed contents, so rewriting an unrelated CSV output is insufficient.

choices.text: Use an Athena engine version 3 MERGE INTO keyed by customer, with clauses for deletion, update, and insertion.
choices.explanation: One statement applies the distinct actions to the managed Iceberg table transactionally.

learning.reason: Athena engine version 3 supports transactional MERGE INTO for Iceberg. A statement can combine matched and unmatched update, delete, and insert actions.
learning.concept: Apply normalized change records atomically to an Iceberg feature table with Athena MERGE INTO.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Join a large event table to a small reference dataset
prompt: An AWS Glue Spark job enriches 4 TB of event data with a 20 MB product lookup table. After projection, the complete lookup fits comfortably in every executor's memory. Measurements show the event-side sort-merge shuffle dominates runtime. The event data cannot be reduced before enrichment. Which change targets the bottleneck?

choices.text: Use a broadcast join for the projected product lookup.
choices.explanation: Executors can join the local event partitions against the small copied lookup.

choices.text: Broadcast the 4 TB event table and keep the lookup partitioned.
choices.explanation: The event table cannot fit in executor memory and would create very large data transfers.

choices.text: Coalesce all event rows into one partition before the join.
choices.explanation: This would concentrate the large dataset instead of letting executors process its existing partitions in parallel.

choices.text: Increase the number of shuffle partitions without changing the join strategy.
choices.explanation: This can change shuffle partition sizes, but the large-side shuffle would still exist.

learning.reason: A broadcast hash join distributes the small lookup to executors and allows them to join locally against event partitions, avoiding the large-side shuffle.
learning.concept: Broadcast a small reference dataset when large-side join shuffle dominates Glue job cost.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Match an Aurora vector index to the query's distance operator
prompt: An Aurora PostgreSQL product search must rank non-unit-normalized embeddings by cosine distance. Its query orders by the pgvector cosine operator and limits results, but the existing HNSW index was built for L2 distance and the planner does not use it. Which change preserves the required ranking and gives the planner a compatible index?

choices.text: Keep the L2 index and rewrite the query to use Euclidean distance.
choices.explanation: That could match the existing index but changes the ranking, especially with unequal vector magnitudes.

choices.text: Create an HNSW index with vector_cosine_ops and retain the cosine distance operator in the query.
choices.explanation: The index and query use the same distance definition.

choices.text: Use vector_ip_ops and negative inner product without normalizing the vectors.
choices.explanation: Without unit normalization, inner product can rank higher-magnitude vectors differently from cosine.

choices.text: Increase the existing L2 index's ef_search and retain the cosine query.
choices.explanation: Search breadth cannot make an index built for another distance operator compatible with the query.

learning.reason: A pgvector HNSW index needs the operator class that matches the query operator. Cosine ordering requires vector_cosine_ops.
learning.concept: Match the pgvector cosine distance operator with the HNSW cosine operator class.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Create timestamped shot features from stored video
prompt: A model will learn from edits in stored training videos. For each video the team needs frame-accurate shot start and end timestamps, independent of which objects appear or what anyone says. Which Amazon Rekognition analysis should it request?

choices.text: Request only TECHNICAL_CUE segments and treat every cue as a cut.
choices.explanation: Technical cues are events such as credits or black frames and do not enumerate normal shot transitions.

choices.text: Use video label detection and treat each first appearance of a label as a cut.
choices.explanation: Objects can enter or leave during a shot, and a cut can keep the same visible objects.

choices.text: Request SHOT segments with StartSegmentDetection and use GetSegmentDetection to read the boundaries.
choices.explanation: Shot detections identify intervals between cuts without relying on object labels.

choices.text: Use text detection and take every detected subtitle timestamp as a shot boundary.
choices.explanation: Text appearance does not identify edit transitions.

learning.reason: StartSegmentDetection with SHOT identifies shot boundaries, and GetSegmentDetection returns their timestamps and durations.
learning.concept: Use the Rekognition Video Segment API shot detector to extract edit boundaries.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Write a sparse feature correction without erasing other values
prompt: A feature group uses a Standard_V2 online store. A live record already exists for the customer. A correction service knows the customer ID and one revised value, but must retain every other feature and avoid a read-modify-write of the whole record. Which API operation should it use?

choices.text: Call PutRecord with only the customer identifier and corrected value.
choices.explanation: PutRecord overwrites the record rather than updating only those fields.

choices.text: Call UpdateFeatureGroup with a new feature definition for the customer.
choices.explanation: That changes which features the group can contain, not the values in a particular record.

choices.text: Call GetRecord with a FeatureNames selection containing the corrected field.
choices.explanation: GetRecord reads projected fields and does not write the correction.

choices.text: Call UpdateRecord with the customer record identifier and only the corrected feature.
choices.explanation: The existing record is updated without overwriting other values.

learning.reason: UpdateRecord can change specified values on an existing record in a supported online store while preserving omitted features.
learning.concept: Use an authorized partial feature update for an existing record on a supported Feature Store online store.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Preserve invalid rows and their parsing details for review
prompt: A Glue DynamicFrame pipeline reads vendor JSON. Some malformed records are recorded as parsing errors. Valid records should keep flowing, while the team needs the error details and the individual malformed records under a separate quarantine prefix. The error threshold is already configured to allow this batch to continue. Which transform directly exposes what quarantine needs?

choices.text: Call errorsAsDynamicFrame on the relevant DynamicFrame and write that output separately.
choices.explanation: This provides the row-level errors while allowing successful data to follow its own output path.

choices.text: Store only errorsCount alongside the successful dataset.
choices.explanation: The count does not preserve the malformed records or their error descriptions.

choices.text: Use stageErrorsCount as the source of the quarantine files.
choices.explanation: This reports a number for the current stage, not the row payloads and context.

choices.text: Call assertErrorThreshold and persist only its status.
choices.explanation: A threshold result can signal job failure, but it is not the requested row-level error dataset.

learning.reason: errorsAsDynamicFrame exposes the nested error records from a DynamicFrame, including parsing context for individual malformed inputs.
learning.concept: Write Glue DynamicFrame error records to quarantine using errorsAsDynamicFrame.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Roll out an additional feature without replacing the group
prompt: A team needs an additional numeric feature in an existing SageMaker feature group. The same group and identifier must remain available to old clients. The ingestion service must not write the new value until the schema update is ready. Which two actions implement the additive rollout? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Write the new field first with PutRecord and rely on automatic schema inference.
choices.explanation: A record write does not register a new group feature definition.

choices.text: Delete the group and create a replacement that reuses its identifier feature name.
choices.explanation: This does not preserve the existing group or automatically retain its records.

choices.text: Submit UpdateFeatureGroup with the new feature definition in FeatureAdditions.
choices.explanation: The new definition augments the current schema without replacing the group.

choices.text: Add the new feature by setting a value in OnlineStoreConfig.
choices.explanation: Online store configuration controls serving settings rather than the feature schema.

choices.text: Wait for the feature group update to succeed before enabling new writes.
choices.explanation: An HTTP 200 for the update request indicates it was accepted, not that the new schema is ready.

learning.reason: FeatureAdditions extends an existing feature group. The API update is asynchronous, so the write rollout should follow completion of the group update.
learning.concept: Apply an additive Feature Store schema change and await its asynchronous completion before ingesting new values.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Work through a stream backlog without changing per-key order
prompt: A Lambda stream transform has increasing Kinesis IteratorAge, although the stream has available read throughput. CPU work in each invocation limits processing to one batch at a time per shard. The stream has many station keys per shard, sends unaggregated records, and the team needs per-station ordering rather than order across all stations. What can improve compute concurrency within each shard?

choices.text: Raise only the function's reserved concurrency but leave a parallelization factor of one.
choices.explanation: This may remove a function quota bottleneck, but the mapping would still schedule only one batch at a time per shard.

choices.text: Raise ParallelizationFactor on the existing event source mapping and confirm sufficient Lambda concurrency.
choices.explanation: Lambda can work on multiple batches per shard without abandoning the applicable per-key ordering.

choices.text: Change all records on each shard to one fixed partition key.
choices.explanation: This would eliminate independent keys Lambda could process concurrently while preserving order.

choices.text: Set a larger batching window to run more simultaneous batches for the same shard.
choices.explanation: The batching window controls how long records can accumulate, not the mapping's per-shard parallel batch count.

learning.reason: ParallelizationFactor allows multiple Lambda batches from a shard while maintaining ordering at partition-key level for the stated stream.
learning.concept: Increase Lambda parallel batches per Kinesis shard when only partition-key order is required.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Choose an explicit indicator for unseen categories
prompt: A linear model uses one-hot input for a vendor attribute with a stable training vocabulary. New vendor codes can arrive in production. The vector width must remain fixed, and the model needs an explicit indicator for unknown values instead of dropping rows or encoding them as an all-zero vector. Which Data Wrangler options meet the requirement?

choices.text: Use One-hot encode with Keep and turn on Drop last category.
choices.explanation: The missing category is last. Dropping that entry makes unknown values use an all-zero vector.

choices.text: Use One-hot encode with Skip and leave Drop last category disabled.
choices.explanation: Skip can remove the affected rows instead of assigning an unknown indicator.

choices.text: Use One-hot encode with the Keep invalid handling strategy and leave Drop last category disabled.
choices.explanation: The last category has an explicit entry, and new values outside the fitted vocabulary use it.

choices.text: Refit the encoder every time production sees a new vendor code.
choices.explanation: Refitting can change the input width or mapping expected by the existing model.

learning.reason: The Keep strategy treats missing or unseen values as the last category. Leaving Drop last category disabled preserves that category's vector entry.
learning.concept: Keep a fixed one-hot vocabulary with an explicit unknown-category slot.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Honor a domain-specific boundary when indexing manuals
prompt: A team's plain-text manuals include approved section markers. A Bedrock knowledge base must split exactly on those markers using existing preprocessing logic. Stock fixed and semantic chunking cannot implement this convention. The team wants the custom transformation to run inside the managed ingestion flow. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Use semantic chunking alone with a high breakpoint percentile.
choices.explanation: A semantic score threshold cannot guarantee boundaries at specific source markers.

choices.text: Use fixed-size chunking and change its overlap value until all section markers line up.
choices.explanation: Token overlaps do not make different documents split at domain-specific delimiters.

choices.text: Implement the splitter only after RetrieveAndGenerate has returned its answer.
choices.explanation: Postprocessing the answer cannot change the chunks originally embedded and retrieved.

choices.text: Select no built-in chunking and configure the custom transformation Lambda with the intermediate S3 location.
choices.explanation: The Lambda can apply the approved rules and return the chunk files for further ingestion.

learning.reason: Bedrock supports a custom transformation Lambda to create chunks. Selecting no built-in chunking lets the Lambda determine the boundaries without first receiving fixed chunks.
learning.concept: Use Bedrock custom ingestion transformation and no native chunking for domain-specific split logic.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Mask designated entities without changing other clinical text
prompt: A team processes approved short English clinical notes inside its controlled environment. Its prepared training copy should replace only detected entities of approved PHI categories and retain the rest of each note. The service must report candidate locations and scores for the team's review policy, and should not alter the source notes itself. What should the team do?

choices.text: Call DetectPHI and use the returned categories, offsets, and scores to replace approved spans in a derived text copy.
choices.explanation: The caller controls which reported spans are masked and preserves source notes separately.

choices.text: Use InferICD10CM and replace all diagnosis codes it returns.
choices.explanation: Diagnosis coding serves a different purpose and does not identify the necessary PHI spans.

choices.text: Replace the entire note whenever PII is suspected.
choices.explanation: This would lose unrelated text that the prepared dataset must retain.

choices.text: Use document sentiment and mask sentences labeled negative.
choices.explanation: Sentiment is unrelated to whether a span contains a designated protected identifier.

learning.reason: DetectPHI returns candidate entity categories, locations, and confidence scores. An owned preprocessing step can transform selected spans on a separate copy.
learning.concept: Use Comprehend Medical entity offsets and confidence to drive a controlled PHI masking step.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep the grading key separate from the reinforcement prompt
prompt: A Nova reinforcement fine-tuning dataset has prompts and verified reference outputs. The grader must see the reference output, but the model should generate an answer without receiving the key as prompt context. Each training example is one JSONL record. Where should the team store the two inputs?

choices.text: Put both the task and the reference in the system message.
choices.explanation: This exposes the answer to the model while it is supposed to solve the task.

choices.text: Put the input prompt in messages and the verified output in reference_answer.
choices.explanation: The grader can use the reference while the model receives the intended input messages.

choices.text: Put the reference only in the document filename instead of the JSONL record.
choices.explanation: The documented grading input is a record field. The filename does not supply per-example targets.

choices.text: Put the verified answer in messages as the final assistant turn and omit reference_answer.
choices.explanation: That makes the verified answer part of the supplied message context and does not provide a separate grading reference.

learning.reason: Nova RFT uses messages for the model's prompt and reference_answer for expected outputs or criteria supplied for grading.
learning.concept: Keep the Nova RFT grading reference separate from the model's input messages.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Choose embedding purposes for document retrieval
prompt: An application uses Nova Multimodal Embeddings to index maintenance PDFs. Operators will search the index with text queries. The team already uses identical vector dimensions. Which two embedding-purpose choices match the two roles in this application? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use TEXT_RETRIEVAL for the text query solely because it contains text.
choices.explanation: Retrieval purpose is selected by the expected target content, not just the query's form.

choices.text: Use CLASSIFICATION for all source and query embeddings.
choices.explanation: Classification is a separate application objective and does not select the retrieval settings.

choices.text: Use DOCUMENT_RETRIEVAL for stored source representations and GENERIC_INDEX for search input.
choices.explanation: That reverses the roles of indexed content and the retrieval query.

choices.text: Use GENERIC_INDEX for embeddings written from the source PDFs.
choices.explanation: This optimizes the content representations for indexing regardless of the indexed modality.

choices.text: Use DOCUMENT_RETRIEVAL when embedding a query meant to retrieve the PDFs.
choices.explanation: The query optimization targets documents even though the query itself is text.

learning.reason: The database content uses GENERIC_INDEX. The query purpose depends on the modality being retrieved, so a text query targeting PDFs uses DOCUMENT_RETRIEVAL.
learning.concept: Set retrieval embedding purpose by target modality rather than the query modality.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prepare an entity lexicon for unannotated reports
prompt: An ML team needs Amazon Comprehend to recognize proprietary component codes in English plain-text service reports. It has a curated dictionary of codes and a large unannotated report corpus. No one has annotated offsets, but the exact known examples appear repeatedly in the reports. What should the team provide to train a contextual custom recognizer using the available assets?

choices.text: Supply only the dictionary without any document corpus.
choices.explanation: The entity-list approach also requires example documents where the entries appear.

choices.text: Define each code as a document-level sentiment label and provide the existing reports.
choices.explanation: Sentiment categories do not identify which text spans contain proprietary components.

choices.text: Supply the Text and Type entity-list CSV together with unannotated documents containing those code occurrences.
choices.explanation: The recognizer uses the entity examples and their context in the corpus.

choices.text: Use the annotation format and omit all entity spans from the annotation file.
choices.explanation: That does not provide the labeled spans required by the annotation-based approach.
