learning.reason: Comprehend can train a custom recognizer from an entity list and plaintext documents where entities appear, using matching occurrences in document context.
learning.concept: Train Comprehend custom entities from both an entity list and representative unannotated plain text.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Verify a mapped feature value against a reference
prompt: A migrated Glue dataset contains one unique, non-null device_id per row. A reference dataset contains the corresponding unique sensor_key. The verification must flag cases where a row's migrated temperature differs from the matching reference value. Other columns are allowed to differ. Which DQDL rule configuration meets this need?

choices.text: Use ReferentialIntegrity on device_id and sensor_key alone.
choices.explanation: That confirms key membership without comparing the temperature values.

choices.text: Use RowCountMatch with identical counts for the two datasets.
choices.explanation: Datasets can have equal row counts while the corresponding values are wrong.

choices.text: Use AggregateMatch on average temperature only.
choices.explanation: Opposite differences in individual rows can cancel in the aggregate.

choices.text: Use DatasetMatch with device_id mapped to sensor_key and map only the temperature columns, requiring all primary rows to match.
choices.explanation: This checks individual matched temperature values while excluding unrelated columns.

learning.reason: DatasetMatch joins on mapped unique keys and can compare selected non-key columns, allowing focused validation rather than a total or key-presence check.
learning.concept: Compare selected field values on paired rows using a Glue DatasetMatch key and column mapping.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Label object identities across frames
prompt: An existing Ground Truth customer needs bounding boxes in video frames for several visually similar boxes moving on a conveyor. Training must learn the trajectory of each distinct box, even when two boxes of the same class exchange positions. Which annotation approach fits?

choices.text: Use video frame object tracking and keep one instance ID per physical box across the frames in which it appears.
choices.explanation: The trainer can associate the sequence of coordinates with the same object.

choices.text: Use independent frame classification and label every frame that contains a box.
choices.explanation: This provides no object coordinates or cross-frame identity.

choices.text: Use independent detection boxes labeled only with the object class and no track identifiers.
choices.explanation: Those labels can train a detector, but two same-class boxes are not linked consistently across frames.

choices.text: Assign a new unique identifier to every bounding box in every frame.
choices.explanation: That breaks continuity because the same physical object appears under multiple identities.

learning.reason: Video frame object tracking associates each annotation with an instance ID that continues across frames for the same object.
learning.concept: Use stable object instance IDs in Ground Truth video frame object tracking labels.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Audit group disparity within comparable groups
prompt: An existing Clarify customer audits observed approval labels before model training. Group proportions differ across application categories with very different approval rates. The team needs a metric that conditions the disparity on those category strata rather than relying on a pooled group rate. Which pre-training measure fits?

choices.text: Use Class Imbalance (CI) on the entire dataset.
choices.explanation: It compares group sample sizes and ignores observed approval outcomes.

choices.text: Use Conditional Demographic Disparity (CDD) with application category as the grouping variable.
choices.explanation: It accounts for disparity within the designated strata when using observed labels.

choices.text: Use a pooled Difference in Proportions of Labels without grouping.
choices.explanation: This can miss or conflate differences associated with unequal category mix.

choices.text: Use Conditional Demographic Disparity in Predicted Labels before any model produces predictions.
choices.explanation: That is the post-training counterpart. The available target here is the observed label.

learning.reason: Conditional Demographic Disparity evaluates group disparity across defined subgroups on the observed labels rather than collapsing the category structure.
learning.concept: Condition a pre-training disparity audit on relevant subgroup strata using Clarify CDD.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Increase varied minority examples while keeping holdout realistic
prompt: A binary classifier's training partition has few positive rows. All predictors are scalar numeric measurements for which interpolation among nearby positive examples is acceptable. The team must retain all majority rows and wants new positive feature combinations rather than copies. The holdout must remain untouched. Which two actions satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use Data Wrangler SMOTE to generate synthetic observations from the minority class.
choices.explanation: It can add varied synthetic feature combinations without requiring removal of majority rows.

choices.text: Apply the balancing transform only to the training partition.
choices.explanation: The holdout retains authentic class frequency and stays free of samples derived from its own rows.

choices.text: Use random undersampling to discard most majority observations.
choices.explanation: This violates the requirement to keep all majority training rows.

choices.text: Use random oversampling that only duplicates existing positive rows.
choices.explanation: It increases positive count but does not create new feature combinations.

choices.text: Apply the synthetic balancing before splitting the whole dataset into training and holdout.
choices.explanation: Related real and synthetic observations could cross the split and evaluation prevalence would change.

learning.reason: Data Wrangler's SMOTE synthesizes examples by interpolating between neighboring minority samples. Applying it only after partitioning preserves evaluation prevalence.
learning.concept: Use train-only SMOTE when interpolation is appropriate and majority data must remain.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Screen existing examples without running generation
prompt: Before using a corpus of existing prompt and expected-response pairs for training, a team must screen both fields under its approved Bedrock content policy. The organization uses separate thresholds for input and output and requires flags before training. It cannot send the corpus through a foundation model for generation. How should the pipeline screen the two fields?

choices.text: Submit only the prompt to a foundation model and score its new response under the output policy.
choices.explanation: The new response would not screen the actual expected-response text stored in the training corpus.

choices.text: Send both fields as INPUT and assume output thresholds will also be enforced.
choices.explanation: Setting the source to INPUT does not select the separate output policy.

choices.text: Call ApplyGuardrail for prompt records as INPUT and for expected responses as OUTPUT, then quarantine according to the evaluation results.
choices.explanation: This applies the two policy directions to the existing text without generating new responses.

choices.text: Validate that each row is JSON and assume policy compliance when it parses.
choices.explanation: Syntax validation cannot identify content that violates the specified policy.

learning.reason: ApplyGuardrail evaluates supplied text directly. The source field lets the team apply the relevant prompt or response policy to each existing text field.
learning.concept: Screen existing prompt-response fields independently using ApplyGuardrail source-specific policies.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep the newest reading per asset efficiently
prompt: An Athena preparation query needs one calibration result per machine before model training. Several calibration results are revisions. Each machine's revision times are unique, input order is not guaranteed, and large row-number windows exceeded memory limits. Which aggregation preserves the calibration result belonging to the latest revision?

choices.text: Group by machine_id and select max(calibration_result) independently of max(revised_at).
choices.explanation: The maximum calibration result may belong to a different record than the newest revision.

choices.text: Select DISTINCT machine_id, calibration_result, and revised_at.
choices.explanation: Rows with different timestamps remain distinct rather than collapsing to one per sensor.

choices.text: Group by machine_id and choose arbitrary(calibration_result).
choices.explanation: An arbitrary value has no guarantee of coming from the latest reading.

choices.text: Group by machine_id and select max_by(calibration_result, revised_at).
choices.explanation: This retains the value from the latest revision timestamp for each machine.

learning.reason: max_by returns the first expression from the record with the maximum second expression within a group. This can replace a large ordered deduplication window.
learning.concept: Use max_by with a timestamp to keep the corresponding latest field value per entity.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Select a successor before a model retires
prompt: The Bedrock model that powers an internal summarizer now reports LEGACY in its model lifecycle status. The application still works. Its replacement must meet existing summary quality and latency thresholds in the same Region. What is the appropriate selection process?

choices.text: Check the model's end-of-life date in Bedrock, benchmark active models available in the required Region on representative requests, and migrate to a passing one before retirement.
choices.explanation: This manages availability while checking actual workload compatibility.

choices.text: Wait until calls fail and rely on Bedrock to map the old model ID automatically to its successor.
choices.explanation: The configured model ID is not automatically migrated at end of life.

choices.text: Choose the newest model name and move immediately without region or quality checks.
choices.explanation: Recency does not prove availability, latency, or suitability.

choices.text: Keep the model ID permanently because one request succeeded after Legacy status appeared.
choices.explanation: Successful calls during the legacy period do not establish availability beyond retirement.

learning.reason: A legacy model has a retirement timeline and Bedrock does not automatically migrate calls. Select an active, supported candidate and measure it before switching.
learning.concept: Use Bedrock lifecycle status and measured application requirements when selecting a successor.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Align response style using comparative feedback
prompt: Editors have ranked pairs of replies to the same customer questions. Each pair has a preferred and rejected answer, but exact wording varies and there is no reliable numerical rule for judging tone. The team wants to update a supported Nova model using these choices. Which SageMaker customization approach best uses its data?

choices.text: Fine-tune with the rejected replies as the only supervised targets.
choices.explanation: That trains toward the responses the editors preferred less.

choices.text: Use a Direct Preference Optimization recipe with prompt-aligned preferred and rejected examples.
choices.explanation: The objective can move the model toward the response qualities favored by editors.

choices.text: Apply continued pre-training to all replies and remove their preference labels.
choices.explanation: Unlabeled text exposure does not explicitly learn the editor rankings.

choices.text: Use a reward that checks exact word-for-word equality against one chosen answer for every prompt.
choices.explanation: That treats valid stylistic alternatives as wrong and does not use the comparative judgments as intended.

learning.reason: Direct Preference Optimization learns from paired chosen and rejected responses. It uses comparative judgments directly without a separate programmatic reward function.
learning.concept: Use DPO to train on preferred and rejected responses to the same prompt.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Learn relationships between two kinds of objects
prompt: A search team has pairs consisting of a help article and a short customer issue, each with a graded relevance label. It wants a built-in SageMaker model that learns representations from both inputs and scores a new article–issue pair. It does not want an unsupervised grouping of articles alone. Which model fits?

choices.text: Train K-Means on the articles alone and use the cluster label as the pair's graded relevance.
choices.explanation: Unsupervised articles-only clusters do not learn how an issue relates to an article from labels.

choices.text: Train a Random Cut Forest on issue lengths and use anomaly scores as relevance.
choices.explanation: Input unusualness is unrelated to the observed relevance of a specific pair.

choices.text: Train Object2Vec on labeled issue–article pairs and use it to score new pairs.
choices.explanation: Pairwise supervision matches the relevance objective.

choices.text: Forecast article usage with DeepAR and rank pairs by the resulting demand quantile.
choices.explanation: Time-series demand forecasts do not score the contents of an issue–article pair.

learning.reason: Object2Vec learns from labeled object pairs and can produce a similarity score or relationship prediction for heterogeneous input objects.
learning.concept: Use Object2Vec when supervision describes the relationship between two objects.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Detect defect types using a managed custom vision service
prompt: A plant needs bounding boxes for two visual defects specific to its products. Generic labels detect the product but do not distinguish the defects. The team has annotated images for both defect classes and prefers managed training over maintaining a vision architecture. What should it select?

choices.text: Increase the confidence threshold for generic DetectLabels results and reuse them as defect labels.
choices.explanation: A threshold cannot introduce categories the generic model does not distinguish.

choices.text: Train with only one image-level defect label per image and assume the label locates each defect.
choices.explanation: Image-level labels alone do not provide the box supervision in the requirement.

choices.text: Use DetectText on every image and treat the found character positions as defects.
choices.explanation: Text positions do not identify these visual defect classes.

choices.text: Train a Rekognition Custom Labels model using images with bounding-box annotations for the defect classes.
choices.explanation: The trained model can detect the custom classes and report their locations.

learning.reason: Rekognition Custom Labels can train a managed vision model from annotations for domain-specific labels and object locations.
learning.concept: Select Rekognition Custom Labels for managed training on proprietary visual categories and locations.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Retrieve evidence through relationships between entities
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base answers isolated questions from equipment documents. A new task asks which products are affected when a supplier changes a component that appears in multiple assemblies. The relevant facts span standards and parts manuals, and some supporting chunks do not contain the supplier name. The team wants managed retrieval that can follow connections between entities after the initial match. Which architecture fits?

choices.text: Use a Bedrock knowledge base backed by Neptune Analytics GraphRAG to retrieve linked supporting chunks.
choices.explanation: Graph traversal can expand the initial result to connected component and assembly evidence.

choices.text: Use exact string matching for the supplier name as the only retrieval rule.
choices.explanation: Supporting chunks that refer only to a linked assembly or component can be missed.

choices.text: Send only the supplier name to a base language model without internal documents.
choices.explanation: The model does not receive the specific assembly relationships maintained in the manuals.

choices.text: Sort all independently matched document chunks by timestamp and return the newest single match.
choices.explanation: Recency cannot traverse the relationships required to connect the facts.

learning.reason: Managed GraphRAG combines vector search with Neptune Analytics relationships and expands from the initial nodes to linked content.
learning.concept: Use Bedrock GraphRAG when document retrieval depends on relationships across related entities.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Fit a model that is too large for one training device
prompt: A training job cannot load one full replica of its model and required state onto a single supported GPU, even with one example per device. The architecture and precision must be preserved, and the available multi-GPU host has enough aggregate memory. Which distribution strategy addresses the constraint?

choices.text: Use replicated data parallelism and send fewer samples to each GPU.
choices.explanation: Each GPU would still need a full replica, which already exceeds its memory.

choices.text: Use a supported model-parallel strategy to partition model state across the GPUs.
choices.explanation: Individual devices hold only part of the model state while cooperating during training.

choices.text: Keep one GPU and reduce the per-device batch size below one.
choices.explanation: There must be at least one example, and the model state itself remains too large.

choices.text: Start several independent training jobs with the same one-GPU configuration.
choices.explanation: Separate processes do not combine memory to fit one replica.

learning.reason: Model parallelism partitions the model across devices. Ordinary replicated data parallelism still requires a complete model per device.
learning.concept: Partition a model across accelerators when the full replica cannot fit on one device.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Lower cost for requests that can finish more slowly
prompt: A team generates overnight review snippets through synchronous Bedrock runtime calls. It cannot change its request/response interface or commit to reserved capacity. The selected model supports all Bedrock service tiers. Higher latency is acceptable and the team wants the discounted tier for such requests. Which option fits?

choices.text: Select Priority to minimize inference latency.
choices.explanation: The priority mode delivers faster service at a price premium, not the requested discount.

choices.text: Purchase Reserved capacity for the notebook workflow.
choices.explanation: Reservation violates the no-commitment requirement.

choices.text: Select the Flex service tier for these inference requests.
choices.explanation: It is designed for less time-sensitive tasks at a discount.

choices.text: Move all work to an asynchronous batch invocation job.
choices.explanation: That changes the current synchronous request/response contract.

learning.reason: Flex supports lower-priced inference for workloads that tolerate longer processing time, without reserving dedicated capacity.
learning.concept: Use the Bedrock Flex service tier for latency-tolerant requests that must keep the runtime API flow.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Improve domain transcription using contextual evidence
prompt: A team transcribes long recordings from water-treatment facilities. Many errors are real-word substitutions between homophones, and the intended terms depend on nearby technical phrases. The team has a large corpus of accurate domain transcripts and is not mainly trying to change spelling or display forms. What should it use?

choices.text: Use only a custom vocabulary with preferred DisplayAs spellings.
choices.explanation: Vocabulary can boost or format terms but does not learn context from the available transcripts.

choices.text: Enable speaker diarization and assume that separate speaker labels fix term substitutions.
choices.explanation: Diarization identifies speakers, not how technical words are used in context.

choices.text: Run language identification and accept the default model once the language is recognized.
choices.explanation: Knowing the language does not resolve systematic within-language homophones.

choices.text: Train and use a custom language model with the representative domain transcripts.
choices.explanation: It learns contextual language patterns that help distinguish the intended terms.

learning.reason: A Transcribe custom language model learns how domain terms appear in context, making it suitable for systematic context-dependent recognition errors.
learning.concept: Use a Transcribe custom language model when neighboring domain language resolves recognition choices.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Score an unusual account and IPv4 pairing
prompt: A security team has historical account-and-IPv4 pairs but very few confirmed abuse labels. An IPv4 address can be normal for one account and unusual for another. The team needs a built-in SageMaker algorithm that understands that association and returns an anomaly score for each new pair. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Train IP Insights on known historical account and IPv4 pairs and score new pairs.
choices.explanation: The score reflects whether an address is anomalous for that entity.

choices.text: Count occurrences by IPv4 address alone and use one global rarity threshold.
choices.explanation: Global rarity loses which accounts normally use an address.

choices.text: Train a supervised binary classifier and treat every unlabeled event as confirmed abuse.
choices.explanation: That creates unsupported positive labels and does not fit the unlabeled learning requirement.

choices.text: Train a regression model to predict the integer value of the next address from time of day.
choices.explanation: Prediction error on integer-valued IPv4 does not inherently measure the entity-address association.

learning.reason: IP Insights learns associations between entities and IPv4 addresses without target labels and scores the novelty of a new pair.
learning.concept: Use SageMaker IP Insights for unsupervised entity-specific IPv4 association anomalies.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Expose a custom validation metric from an unchanged script
prompt: A framework training script prints a line containing val_f1=0.82 at each evaluation. The SageMaker job must make that changing value visible as a named training metric without adding CloudWatch client code to the script. Which job configuration supports this?

choices.text: Add an application tag named val_f1 and change its value after training finishes.
choices.explanation: Tags are resource metadata and do not publish the logged time series.

choices.text: Add a MetricDefinitions entry for the metric name with a regex that captures the number following val_f1=.
choices.explanation: SageMaker can parse the logged value and publish it as the configured metric.

choices.text: Set only the desired metric name in the tuner and provide no extraction definition for the custom image.
choices.explanation: Naming the objective is insufficient if the training data pipeline never exposes the values to SageMaker.

choices.text: Read GPU utilization and rename that metric val_f1.
choices.explanation: Resource utilization is a different measurement from validation performance.

learning.reason: SageMaker extracts custom metrics from training logs when given a metric name and regular expression with the numeric value captured.
learning.concept: Emit a custom SageMaker training metric by matching existing log output through MetricDefinitions.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Allocate epoch budget among many tuning candidates
prompt: An iterative classifier publishes validation scores after every epoch. The team can run many trials in parallel and wants a tuning strategy that starts candidates with small budgets, stops weak ones early, and increases resources for promising configurations within the same search. Which strategy fits?

choices.text: Use grid search and run every configuration for the full number of epochs.
choices.explanation: A full-budget grid does not reallocate resources based on intermediate results.

choices.text: Use random search with a fixed full epoch budget for every job.
choices.explanation: It chooses candidates randomly but does not enforce the requested promotion mechanism.

choices.text: Use Hyperband and configure the iterative training resource bounds.
choices.explanation: It performs the multi-fidelity budget allocation across candidates.

choices.text: Use a warm-start setting without selecting a multi-fidelity strategy.
choices.explanation: Warm start can use prior tuning observations; it is not the described epoch-budget policy.

learning.reason: Hyperband uses intermediate metrics at different resource levels to stop underperforming configurations and promote stronger ones to more epochs.
learning.concept: Use Hyperband for model tuning with comparable intermediate results and adjustable compute budgets.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Keep half-precision speed without losing small gradient values
prompt: A supported GPU training configuration is faster with FP16 mixed precision, but some small FP16 gradients round to zero. The team wants to retain mixed precision while protecting gradient magnitude during backpropagation. Which change addresses the immediate numerical issue?

choices.text: Round small gradients to zero explicitly before backpropagation.
choices.explanation: That removes the learning signal the team needs to preserve.

choices.text: Raise the optimizer learning rate without changing gradient computations.
choices.explanation: The learning rate acts on the computed gradients and cannot restore values already rounded to zero.

choices.text: Convert model weights to FP16 after the completed training job and leave the training run unchanged.
choices.explanation: A post-training conversion cannot correct gradient underflow that occurred during training.

choices.text: Use dynamic loss scaling and unscale gradients before applying optimizer updates.
choices.explanation: Scaling gives small gradients a better chance of being represented in FP16 and preserves the intended update scale after unscaling.

learning.reason: Loss scaling increases gradient magnitudes during reduced-precision computation and unscales them before the optimizer update.
learning.concept: Use dynamic loss scaling where FP16 training loses small gradient values.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Address high error on both training and validation data
prompt: A delivery-time regressor has high training and validation error. Its optimization has converged, the labels are reliable, and diagnostics show most errors arise when the training inputs omit which delivery zone applies. Those zones have different handling rules. Which experiment directly addresses the observed underfitting mechanism?

choices.text: Add the delivery-zone feature, applying the same transformation in training and validation, then reassess errors by zone.
choices.explanation: The model can now learn systematic distinctions that were absent from the original input.

choices.text: Increase regularization until the model is even less sensitive to inputs.
choices.explanation: A stronger penalty cannot introduce the missing zone information.

choices.text: Stop training earlier to reduce the gap between the two error values.
choices.explanation: The issue is high error on both partitions, not divergence between them after successful fitting.

choices.text: Track only the validation metric and leave the model inputs unchanged.
choices.explanation: Changing what is reported does not change the information available to the model.

learning.reason: A model cannot learn differences driven by information absent from every example. Adding a predictive feature can reduce systematic bias in both partitions.
learning.concept: Add missing predictive information when train and validation both show systematic underfitting.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Run an expensive specialist only when the first model needs help
prompt: A small image classifier handles most inspections correctly. A larger specialist is more accurate on difficult examples but is too expensive to run on every input. The base classifier's confidence is calibrated on representative validation data, and the team can evaluate a range of confidence thresholds. Which design meets the cost and quality goals?

choices.text: Run both models for every case and average their outputs equally.
choices.explanation: This can combine predictions but pays the specialist cost for every input.

choices.text: Run the small classifier first and invoke the specialist only below a validated confidence threshold.
choices.explanation: Routine cases avoid specialist cost while difficult examples can get the more accurate model.

choices.text: Choose the small classifier in advance for a fixed random fraction of cases.
choices.explanation: Random assignment is unrelated to where the specialist improves quality.

choices.text: Call the specialist only when the smaller classifier is most confident.
choices.explanation: This directs extra costs to cases that are less likely to need help.

learning.reason: A prediction cascade first runs the low-cost model, then sends only uncertain cases to the larger one. Tune the threshold against held-out quality and usage goals.
learning.concept: Use a measured post-inference confidence gate to cascade from a cheap model to an expensive specialist.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Adapt a short prompt for a successor model
prompt: An application migrated to a supported Bedrock model. Its short English prompt now produces inconsistent results. The team wants a managed heuristic rewrite specifically for the new model, with the ability to review the candidate before changing production. It has no evaluation dataset for optimization yet. What should it do?

choices.text: Request optimization for the old model and deploy that output without checking the new model.
choices.explanation: The optimization is model-specific, and the requested target is the successor.

choices.text: Change only the prompt resource's display name to the successor model name.
choices.explanation: A display name does not rewrite the prompt or improve instruction following.

choices.text: Submit the existing text to OptimizePrompt with the new targetModelId and review the returned rewrite before publishing it.
choices.explanation: The optimization produces a candidate for the selected model without directly changing the live prompt.

choices.text: Run a model customization job without prompt examples and assume that it automatically edits the prompt text.
choices.explanation: Model customization changes model behavior and is not the requested prompt rewrite.

learning.reason: Simple Bedrock prompt optimization can rewrite a short prompt for a specified model without needing an evaluation dataset. The result can be evaluated before deployment.
learning.concept: Generate a target-specific Bedrock prompt candidate using simple prompt optimization.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Tune when retrieval should abstain
prompt: A Bedrock assistant must abstain when a retrieval result gives insufficient evidence. The retrieval service returns relevance scores, and the team has labeled questions with and without useful retrieved evidence. A minimum evidence-recall requirement must be met while reducing unsupported answers. How should the engineer select a score cutoff?

choices.text: Use 0.9 because a score of 0.9 always means exactly a 90% chance that the evidence is sufficient.
choices.explanation: A relevance score is not established as a calibrated probability.

choices.text: Use the lowest score observed in one known good query as a fixed cutoff for every embedding model.
choices.explanation: One query cannot establish operating characteristics, and score distributions can change with the model.

choices.text: Always return the top result without checking the score or evidence.
choices.explanation: A top-ranked chunk can still give insufficient evidence if none of the retrieved chunks is useful.

choices.text: Sweep score thresholds on labeled examples, select one that meets the evidence-recall requirement, and validate it on held-out queries for this retriever.
choices.explanation: The cutoff follows empirical tradeoffs for the deployed scoring system.

learning.reason: Bedrock provides a retrieval score for ranking. The application can use labeled query evidence to measure operating tradeoffs instead of treating the raw score as a calibrated probability.
learning.concept: Tune a retrieval acceptance threshold on labeled evidence outcomes and validate after scorer changes.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Compare candidate responses without exposing them to callers
prompt: A SageMaker shadow test is already mirroring live requests to a candidate. The production variant must continue returning every response. Reviewers want to compare actual model predictions from both variants on the mirrored requests, not just endpoint latency and errors. Approved capture storage is available. What should they enable?

choices.text: Enable shadow-test data capture to the approved S3 destination and compare variant responses for the mirrored inputs offline.
choices.explanation: This preserves the user-facing production responses while saving the content comparison needs.

choices.text: Use only the side-by-side endpoint latency dashboard.
choices.explanation: Operational metrics do not contain model predictions.

choices.text: Promote the model immediately and compare replies reported by customers afterward.
choices.explanation: That exposes candidate results before the required offline review.

choices.text: Send live callers to the candidate through production variant weights.
choices.explanation: Weighted production traffic would return candidate predictions to some users, violating the constraint.

learning.reason: A shadow test can log requests and responses for the two variants to S3. The candidate's responses remain outside the user response path.
learning.concept: Capture predictions from both SageMaker variants for content-level offline comparison of mirrored traffic.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Rank features by typical contribution magnitude
prompt: An existing SageMaker Clarify customer explains a binary classifier using local SHAP values. Feature A contributes strongly in opposite directions for different observations, so its signed average is near zero. The team needs a global importance ranking that preserves magnitude regardless of direction. Which aggregation should it use?

choices.text: Take the absolute value of the signed mean after averaging.
choices.explanation: Positive and negative contributions can cancel before the absolute value is taken.

choices.text: Use mean_abs across the evaluation observations.
choices.explanation: It captures the typical magnitude of the feature's contribution.

choices.text: Rank using only the largest positive contribution from one instance.
choices.explanation: A single extreme contribution does not represent typical magnitude across the evaluation set.

choices.text: Rank features by the correlation of each feature's raw values with row number.
choices.explanation: That measures an ordering artifact instead of how the model used the feature.

learning.reason: The mean_abs aggregation averages the absolute local SHAP values. Opposing signs do not cancel before computing global importance.
learning.concept: Use mean absolute local SHAP for direction-independent global feature importance.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Evaluate whether reported risk probabilities are trustworthy
prompt: A classifier that ranks equipment failure risk has good discrimination. An operations scheduler consumes its probabilities directly to size spare capacity. For a holdout bin with mean prediction 0.80, only 55% of items fail. What should the model evaluation report conclude?

choices.text: The probability is appropriate because discrimination is already good.
choices.explanation: A model can rank outcomes well while systematically overestimating risk.

choices.text: The classifier is underconfident because the observed event rate is numerically smaller than the model score.
choices.explanation: An estimate higher than the observed proportion indicates overconfidence for the positive event.

choices.text: The classifier is overconfident in that bin. Evaluate a calibration correction on independent data before treating its scores as probabilities.
choices.explanation: The predicted 80% materially exceeds the observed 55%, despite good ranking.

choices.text: Set a fixed classification threshold of 0.55 and conclude that this makes the original probabilities reliable.
choices.explanation: A classification threshold maps scores to decisions and does not recalibrate the scores themselves.

learning.reason: A reliable predicted probability should agree with observed outcome frequency across similarly scored cases. Good ranking does not imply calibrated probability levels.
learning.concept: Use reliability curves to compare average predicted probability against empirical event rates.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Explain a score reduction for partial translations
prompt: A translation model began stopping early. Its generated fragments still contain many matching n-grams, and modified n-gram precision is close to the previous run. The team observes that the fragments are collectively shorter than the reference translations and that corpus BLEU fell. What part of BLEU helps explain the decrease?

choices.text: The score uses only the longest common subsequence and ignores n-gram precision.
choices.explanation: That describes a different family of metrics and does not account for BLEU's length adjustment.

choices.text: The score subtracts a fixed amount for each repeated source-domain word, regardless of length.
choices.explanation: BLEU does not define that source-word penalty.

choices.text: The score automatically gives a bonus when a translation ends earlier than its reference.
choices.explanation: The length effect is a penalty for insufficient output, not a short-output bonus.

choices.text: The brevity penalty reduces scores when the candidate corpus is shorter than its effective reference length.
choices.explanation: It discourages very short partial translations that would otherwise keep high precision.

learning.reason: Corpus BLEU multiplies its precision-based score by a brevity penalty when total candidate length falls below effective reference length.
learning.concept: Account for BLEU's brevity penalty even when retained output has strong n-gram precision.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Measure how early the first useful passage arrives
prompt: A Bedrock RAG service evaluates a ranked top-five retrieval list for each of three queries. Human labels place the first relevant passage at ranks 1 and 4 for the first two queries. No passage is relevant for the third. The report defines reciprocal rank as one divided by the first relevant rank, with zero if none is found. What value should it report for mean reciprocal rank?

choices.text: Approximately 0.417.
choices.explanation: The missed query stays in the denominator and contributes zero.
This averages only over the two successful queries, overstating retrieval quality.

choices.text: Approximately 0.667.
choices.explanation: This is the fraction of queries with a relevant hit, not the average reciprocal rank.
This uses just the second query's reciprocal rank and ignores the other two.

learning.reason: Average the contribution of all three queries, including the failed retrieval. The value is (1 + 1/4 + 0) / 3.
learning.concept: Include missed queries as zero when averaging the first relevant retrieval rank.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Render partial results as the hosted model produces them
prompt: A web application uses a SageMaker real-time endpoint whose container supports response streaming. It sends one request and should display the response in parts on the same connection. It does not need the client to send new messages midstream. Which Runtime operation fits?

choices.text: Use ordinary InvokeEndpoint and assume the fully buffered response exposes the same payload-part events.
choices.explanation: The standard operation does not provide the response-streaming event contract.

choices.text: Use InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream and handle the payload parts as the response arrives.
choices.explanation: The synchronous request can receive multiple payload parts over the response stream.

choices.text: Use InvokeEndpointAsync and wait for the S3 output location to contain a completed object.
choices.explanation: Asynchronous object delivery does not stream parts over the same connection.

choices.text: Run a Batch Transform job and display each S3 object as a token stream.
choices.explanation: Batch jobs do not provide the required per-request response connection.

learning.reason: InvokeEndpointWithResponseStream returns the response incrementally for a compatible hosted container without a bidirectional request stream.
learning.concept: Use the SageMaker response-streaming invocation for one input and incremental outputs.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Handle successful and failed asynchronous predictions
prompt: A workflow already invokes a SageMaker asynchronous endpoint. The InvokeEndpointAsync response returns an inference identifier and output location as soon as work is queued. The workflow must consume results once ready and branch automatically on failures without periodically probing S3. Which setup is appropriate?

choices.text: Mark the inference successful as soon as InvokeEndpointAsync returns HTTP success.
choices.explanation: Acceptance indicates queuing, not a completed inference result.

choices.text: Listen only for an object creation notification on the original input prefix.
choices.explanation: That object appears before the inference finishes and does not indicate its outcome.

choices.text: Configure SNS success and error topics in the asynchronous output configuration and consume their notifications for the invocation.
choices.explanation: Downstream processing can distinguish completion from failure without polling for object existence.

choices.text: Treat the absence of an SNS message immediately after submission as a permanent failure.
choices.explanation: The asynchronous request can legitimately still be queued or processing.

learning.reason: SageMaker async inference can send SNS notifications when an invocation succeeds or errors, allowing a consumer to handle the specific completed request.
learning.concept: Use asynchronous inference success and error notifications to resume downstream processing.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Reuse custom weights across independent on-demand deployments
prompt: A supported Bedrock customization job produced one model. Staging and production should invoke the same trained weights while keeping independent deployment resources and tags. Staging deployment changes must not require retraining or editing production. On-demand inference is available in the chosen Region. What should the team deploy?

choices.text: Run the customization job again for staging and rely on matching names to guarantee identical weights.
choices.explanation: A second training job is unnecessary and its output is a different trained model artifact.

choices.text: Use one shared deployment ARN with a stage label inside each prompt.
choices.explanation: A prompt label does not separate deployment resources or their lifecycle settings.

choices.text: Send all requests to the base foundation model and provide the custom model's name in the text.
choices.explanation: Text does not select the trained custom weights.

choices.text: Create separately named and tagged on-demand custom model deployments pointing to the one trained model, and configure each app with its own deployment ARN.
choices.explanation: The applications share weights but use distinct deployment resources.

learning.reason: A Bedrock custom model deployment references the underlying custom model and is independently named and tagged. Applications invoke the environment's deployment ARN.
learning.concept: Create distinct Bedrock on-demand deployment resources for one trained model when environments need separate lifecycles.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Ensure a specific branch wins when conditions overlap
prompt: A Bedrock Flow has a condition node for work orders. Both the urgent-maintenance rule and the general-maintenance rule match an urgent maintenance request. Those requests currently go to the general branch because it appears first. All other maintenance requests must still take the general branch, with unrelated requests going to a default handler. What should the engineer change?

choices.text: Order the urgent-maintenance condition before the general-maintenance condition and keep the default for unmatched input.
choices.explanation: This sends overlapping cases to the specific branch while retaining general and default routes.

choices.text: Keep the order and expect the more specific expression to override the earlier true condition automatically.
choices.explanation: Bedrock evaluates configured order, not expression specificity.

choices.text: Remove the urgent rule and rely on the default branch to catch urgent maintenance.
choices.explanation: The general rule would match first, so these requests would not reach the default.

choices.text: Make both conditions identical and redirect from whichever downstream node finishes first.
choices.explanation: One matching condition is selected by order; completion timing does not choose the branch.

learning.reason: A Bedrock Flow condition node evaluates its conditions in order. The first satisfied condition determines the downstream path.
learning.concept: Put the more specific Bedrock Flow condition ahead of a broader matching rule.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Build a container that can start on the agent runtime
prompt: A team uses the AgentCore Runtime container deployment path documented for ARM64. It pushed an image from an x86 CI worker. The agent works on that worker, but runtime startup fails because the binary dependencies were packaged for x86-64. Which change fixes the deployment artifact?

choices.text: Retag the existing x86 image with a name ending in arm64.
choices.explanation: An image tag changes its label, not the architecture of its layers.

choices.text: Build and test a linux/arm64 image with ARM64-compatible base and dependencies, then deploy that artifact.
choices.explanation: The binary architecture now matches the managed execution environment.

choices.text: Increase the runtime memory setting and keep the x86 libraries.
choices.explanation: Memory size does not translate an incompatible instruction architecture.

choices.text: Change only the ECR repository's region while retaining the same image.
choices.explanation: Copying the artifact to a Region does not rebuild its incompatible binaries.

learning.reason: The deployed image and its native dependencies must run on the required ARM64 runtime. The build can target linux/arm64 even when the builder is another architecture.
learning.concept: Build an AgentCore container and native libraries for the runtime's supported ARM64 platform.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Switch run inputs without redeploying a pipeline definition
prompt: A SageMaker pipeline already declares a dataset URI and an evaluation threshold as parameters. An approved backfill needs different values for just one run. The scheduled production pipeline must keep its existing defaults and definition. How should the caller start the backfill?

choices.text: Update the shared pipeline definition with the new defaults and leave them in place.
choices.explanation: Scheduled executions could then inherit the backfill values.

choices.text: Write different default values as resource tags on the pipeline.
choices.explanation: Tags are metadata and do not provide parameter override values to pipeline steps.

choices.text: Pass the alternate dataset URI and threshold as parameters when starting the backfill execution.
choices.explanation: The override is scoped to that execution rather than changing the stored defaults.

choices.text: Set the caller's local environment variables but start the managed pipeline without any parameter values.
choices.explanation: The remote job does not use the caller's local environment as pipeline parameters.

learning.reason: Build-time defaults apply unless the caller overrides declared parameters when it starts a particular execution.
learning.concept: Override declared SageMaker pipeline parameters on one execution to preserve shared defaults.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Prevent successive scale-ins without slowing recovery
prompt: A SageMaker real-time endpoint already scales out quickly enough under its target-tracking policy. After a traffic drop it removes instances repeatedly in close succession, leaving little room for a rebound. The team wants to slow successive scale-in actions while keeping the current scale-out behavior. Which policy setting should it adjust in testing?

choices.text: Increase only ScaleOutCooldown.
choices.explanation: This changes the pace of additions instead of directly spacing out removals.

choices.text: Set the maximum instance count to the current minimum.
choices.explanation: This removes the capacity headroom needed to recover when traffic rebounds.

choices.text: Reduce ScaleInCooldown.
choices.explanation: This permits repeated removals sooner, worsening the observed behavior.

choices.text: Increase ScaleInCooldown while retaining the existing ScaleOutCooldown.
choices.explanation: This makes consecutive removals more conservative and does not prohibit a needed scale-out.

learning.reason: Scale-in cooldown blocks additional scale-in during the configured period. Target tracking can still initiate scale-out when demand warrants it.
learning.concept: Increase only scale-in cooldown when scale-in actions occur too close together.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Turn natural-language search preferences into metadata constraints
prompt: A custom Bedrock knowledge base already indexes publication year and product segment as metadata. Users specify combinations in free text such as asking for recent consumer guides. Relevance filters are optional search preferences, while authorization is enforced separately. Which configuration lets Bedrock derive a filter at query time without a custom parser?

choices.text: Configure implicitFilterConfiguration with descriptions and types for the searchable metadata attributes and a model ARN.
choices.explanation: The model can infer a metadata filter from the user's question using the specified attributes.

choices.text: Add the same explicit filter constant to every request regardless of the query.
choices.explanation: A fixed filter cannot reflect a different year or segment from each question.

choices.text: Put the publication year in the system prompt for generation after retrieval and assume it limits the vector query.
choices.explanation: Generation-time text does not construct a query-time metadata filter.

choices.text: Remove all metadata from the index and rely on implicit filtering to regenerate stored attributes.
choices.explanation: Implicit filtering generates a predicate; it does not restore the stored attribute values to match.

learning.reason: Implicit filtering uses a specified model to derive a retrieval filter from the prompt and the declared eligible metadata schema.
learning.concept: Provide a metadata schema and a filter-generation model for Bedrock implicit filtering.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Order deployment after the service role policy is attached
prompt: A CloudFormation template creates a service role, a separate AWS::IAM::Policy attached to it, and a deployment resource that assumes the role to read model artifacts. The deployment resource references the role, but creation sometimes starts before the policy is attached. How should the template prevent that ordering problem?

choices.text: In the IAM policy resource, set DependsOn to the deployment resource.
choices.explanation: This makes policy attachment happen later, increasing the risk of deployment failure.

choices.text: In the deployment resource, set DependsOn to the separate IAM policy resource.
choices.explanation: CloudFormation creates the policy before attempting the resource that needs it.

choices.text: Move the policy's YAML block to the top of the template.
choices.explanation: Declaration order does not establish a CloudFormation dependency.

choices.text: Add another attribute reference to the IAM role without referencing the policy resource.
choices.explanation: The role dependency still does not require the separate policy to finish first.

learning.reason: A reference to the IAM role establishes a role dependency but not automatically one on a separate policy resource. DependsOn can make the deployment wait for the policy.
learning.concept: Declare a CloudFormation dependency on an external service-role policy required during deployment.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Connect Bedrock to a prepared Aurora vector database
prompt: A team prepared a supported Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, enabled pgvector, and created a table and least-privilege database user for a Bedrock knowledge base. The managed integration now needs its API connection and database credentials. No custom connector is allowed. Which two prerequisites must the team configure? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Enable RDS Data API on the Aurora cluster.
choices.explanation: The supported Bedrock integration uses the Data API to access the cluster.

choices.text: Make the database publicly reachable and supply only its hostname.
choices.explanation: Public network reachability does not replace the managed Data API and credential requirements.

choices.text: Store the designated database user's credentials in Secrets Manager and authorize the knowledge base role to use the secret.
choices.explanation: The integration retrieves that credential for database access.

choices.text: Put the database password into the generation prompt.
choices.explanation: Prompt text is not a connection credential configuration.

choices.text: Replace the database user with only an S3 bucket policy.
choices.explanation: An S3 policy does not authenticate database queries.

learning.reason: The Bedrock Aurora integration requires RDS Data API and a secret containing the database credentials. The service role needs permissions for the scoped resources.
learning.concept: Configure RDS Data API and an authorized Secrets Manager database credential for Bedrock.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Answer about a one-off document without maintaining a knowledge base
prompt: A support application receives a single temporary PDF and must answer a question about that document. A supported Bedrock model is available. Policy forbids adding these one-off uploads to a shared persistent knowledge base. Which managed retrieval approach works without setting up a data source and indexing job?

choices.text: Attach the PDF to a shared S3 data source and run a knowledge base ingestion job.
choices.explanation: That copies the one-off document into the persistent retrieval corpus forbidden by policy.

choices.text: Run GenerateQuery against the PDF using a structured Redshift data source.
choices.explanation: GenerateQuery translates natural language to SQL for structured data, not a one-off PDF.

choices.text: Use RetrieveAndGenerate with an EXTERNAL_SOURCES configuration for the allowed document object.
choices.explanation: The application can query the individual document without maintaining an index for it.

choices.text: Send only the PDF title to a hosted model and assume it can access the private object.
choices.explanation: A title does not provide the document contents to the model.

learning.reason: RetrieveAndGenerate supports an external document source. The request can identify the document without creating a shared knowledge base.
learning.concept: Use Bedrock external-source retrieval for a supported single-document request.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Keep an agent's workspace when a microVM stops
prompt: A microVM-based AgentCore job writes a local project workspace that must survive a graceful stop and later resume for the same session. Different sessions must not see each other's files. The project can use managed session storage, and the runtime version remains fixed. Which setup meets the requirement?

choices.text: Write files only to the runtime's ordinary temporary directory and reuse the same ID afterward.
choices.explanation: Reusing the session ID alone does not persist files from ordinary ephemeral storage.

choices.text: Mount the same shared read-write path for all sessions without any isolation boundary.
choices.explanation: That can make one session's private workspace accessible to another.

choices.text: Store only a conversation summary and reconstruct the exact workspace from it.
choices.explanation: A summary is not a durable copy of the files and cannot guarantee their recovery.

choices.text: Store workspace files on the managed session storage mount and resume with the same runtime session ID after the stop completes.
choices.explanation: The next microVM mounts the persisted files belonging to that session.

learning.reason: Managed session storage gives each session an isolated mounted directory and restores it across stop and resume on the same session ID.
learning.concept: Use an isolated AgentCore managed session storage mount for file persistence across compute replacement.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Share accelerator memory across task-specific adapters
prompt: A platform serves many task variants of the same large base model. Each task has a compatible LoRA adapter artifact. Keeping one full base model replica per task is exhausting GPU memory, and different requests must still use different adapters. Which SageMaker design addresses the problem?

choices.text: Deploy a base inference component and create separate adapter inference components that reference it.
choices.explanation: Tasks can use their own adapters while sharing the base model's serving resources.

choices.text: Fuse each adapter into a separate full model and reserve equivalent GPU capacity for each one.
choices.explanation: This would continue to duplicate the base model per task.

choices.text: Average all adapter weights before deployment and use one result for every task.
choices.explanation: That removes independent adapter selection and can change the behavior expected for each task.

choices.text: Deploy only adapter artifacts as standalone full models.
choices.explanation: LoRA weights are deltas and need the compatible base weights during inference.

learning.reason: Adapter inference components reference the same base inference component and use compatible LoRA artifacts. This avoids hosting independent base-model weights for every adapter.
learning.concept: Serve compatible LoRA adapters over a common SageMaker base inference component.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Authenticate a gateway to a private business API without a user prompt
prompt: An AgentCore Gateway receives authenticated internal agent calls. Its target API accepts a scoped OAuth 2.0 token issued for the gateway application, not a token representing an individual user. Calls must run unattended, and the inbound token has a different audience. Which outbound setup meets the requirement?

choices.text: Forward the inbound token unchanged to the target API.
choices.explanation: That token has the wrong audience and does not represent the required downstream application credential.

choices.text: Configure an outbound OAuth provider for the target with the client credentials grant and the approved target scopes.
choices.explanation: The gateway obtains a downstream application token without needing a user to log in.

choices.text: Use an interactive authorization code flow for each invocation.
choices.explanation: This asks for end-user authorization, which is not part of the unattended service flow.

choices.text: Place the client secret in all agent prompts so the model can attach it to requests.
choices.explanation: This unnecessarily exposes a credential and does not replace the managed token flow.

learning.reason: A configured OAuth resource credential provider can obtain a scoped client-credentials token for the downstream target without an interactive user authorization flow.
learning.concept: Use AgentCore outbound client credentials when the downstream tool authorizes the gateway application itself.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Connect CI to a private repository without sharing a developer credential
prompt: A model deployment pipeline needs to fetch source from one private GitHub repository. The organization permits a repository-scoped GitHub App connection and prohibits storing a developer's personal access token in build variables. Which CodePipeline source setup fits?

choices.text: Copy a developer's personal access token into every build action environment.
choices.explanation: That violates the credential rule and spreads a user credential to multiple jobs.

choices.text: Give the pipeline role Amazon S3 read permissions for the GitHub organization name.
choices.explanation: An S3 permission does not authenticate to GitHub.

choices.text: Use GitHub via GitHub App, authorize the AWS connection for the specific repository, and allow the pipeline role to use that connection.
choices.explanation: The managed connection supplies repository access scoped to the approved source.

choices.text: Make the repository public for pipeline fetches and rely on branch protection to preserve its privacy.
choices.explanation: Branch rules govern changes, not who can see a public repository.

learning.reason: A GitHub App connection through AWS CodeConnections can be scoped to selected repositories, and the source action uses that connection rather than a personal token.
learning.concept: Use a scoped CodeConnections source action for approved private GitHub code.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Orchestrate model tasks from a large manifest
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow must run one independent evaluation per row of a large CSV in S3. The manifest is larger than the state input payload limit. The service owner approves hundreds of concurrent evaluations but wants a hard concurrency ceiling. Which two properties identify the appropriate orchestration? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Configure a Distributed Map with the S3 CSV as the input item source.
choices.explanation: The state machine can iterate the manifest without loading it into the parent execution's state input.

choices.text: Parse the entire CSV into the parent state's inline JSON before starting a normal Inline Map.
choices.explanation: The resulting state input is subject to the size limit already exceeded.

choices.text: Create one Parallel branch in the definition for every manifest row.
choices.explanation: The fixed definition does not naturally represent a changing set of runtime rows.

choices.text: Set the Map Run's maximum concurrency based on the downstream service's tested capacity.
choices.explanation: The workflow can run work in parallel while limiting simultaneous child executions.

choices.text: Leave concurrency unlimited and use the S3 object size as a substitute for rate control.
choices.explanation: Manifest size does not enforce the permitted number of running evaluations.

learning.reason: Distributed Map can read CSV directly from S3 and start separate child executions. MaxConcurrency bounds the downstream invocation pressure.
learning.concept: Use Step Functions Distributed Map with an S3 item reader and explicit concurrency cap.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Rerun evaluation and registration from known artifacts
prompt: A SageMaker pipeline successfully prepared data and trained a model, but a temporary software error stopped the evaluation step. The fix affects only evaluation. For the retry, the team must run evaluation and the dependent registration step using the exact model artifact from that failed execution, without rerunning training. Which option fits?

choices.text: Start a full execution with the old pipeline parameters and assume it uses the same artifact.
choices.explanation: A full run can retrain rather than reuse the exact selected model.

choices.text: Query the registry for the newest approved model and evaluate it instead.
choices.explanation: The newest approved version can be unrelated to the model produced by the failed run.

choices.text: Run only the registration step and use the earlier training metrics as a replacement for the failed evaluation.
choices.explanation: The requirement explicitly includes running the corrected evaluation before registration.

choices.text: Start a selective execution for the evaluation and registration steps, referencing the earlier run's execution ARN.
choices.explanation: The selected steps use the required prior outputs without retraining.

learning.reason: Selective execution runs the selected connected steps and can use a reference execution to supply outputs from the skipped training step.
learning.concept: Use selective pipeline execution with the prior execution ARN for known skipped-step artifacts.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Run retraining on a predictable schedule
prompt: A registered SageMaker retraining pipeline should start every Monday at a specified UTC time even when no new S3 object arrives. Operations wants a managed schedule that starts the existing pipeline directly, with a role limited to that workflow. Which setup meets the request?

choices.text: Configure an EventBridge scheduled rule for the UTC time with the pipeline as a target and a role that can start that pipeline.
choices.explanation: The schedule can launch the pipeline without a data event or a supplementary compute job.

choices.text: Start a pipeline from every S3 object creation event only.
choices.explanation: No object event is guaranteed to occur at the required time.

choices.text: Leave a SageMaker Studio notebook running continuously and make a person press Run each Monday.
choices.explanation: The pipeline would depend on a manual action and an unnecessary persistent workspace.

choices.text: Match only SageMaker pipeline completion events and use those to infer the next Monday.
choices.explanation: A completion event does not establish the required wall-clock schedule.

learning.reason: An EventBridge scheduled rule can target the existing pipeline. Its assumable target role can authorize starting only that pipeline.
learning.concept: Schedule an existing SageMaker pipeline through EventBridge using scoped start permissions.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Reproduce a custom model deployment in a second Region
prompt: Disaster recovery requires inference from the same already customized Bedrock model in a different supported Region. The target Region must host its own copy under its approved encryption and access rules. Training again is not acceptable. Which model-management workflow fits?

choices.text: Start a new fine-tuning job in the recovery Region and assume the same hyperparameters guarantee identical weights.
choices.explanation: Retraining is prohibited and does not by itself reproduce the exact existing artifact.

choices.text: Use the supported Bedrock model copy workflow for the approved model and deploy the copy in the target Region after verifying it.
choices.explanation: The target has a regional artifact of the same trained model without a new customization job.

choices.text: Use only a cross-Region inference profile and assume it creates a local copy of the custom model.
choices.explanation: Inference routing is not a model artifact copy operation.

choices.text: Create an application tag named RecoveryRegion on the original custom model.
choices.explanation: A tag records metadata and does not materialize the model in a different Region.

learning.reason: A supported custom model can be copied to another Region. The target deployment references the resulting model copy after the copy job succeeds.
learning.concept: Copy the approved custom Bedrock model to the recovery Region and deploy its local artifact.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Withdraw one retired source while keeping the rest of the knowledge base
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base contains current manuals and a separate obsolete data source. The obsolete source's indexed content must be removed when that source is retired. The vector store and the indexed current manuals must remain. Which operation implements that scope?

choices.text: Set RETAIN on the obsolete source and remove its resource, assuming RETAIN applies only to S3 originals.
choices.explanation: RETAIN preserves its converted data in the vector store, contrary to the stated requirement.

choices.text: Delete the entire shared vector store and keep only the original manuals in S3.
choices.explanation: The remaining knowledge base would lose its indexed current data too.

choices.text: Confirm the obsolete source uses the DELETE data deletion policy, then remove that source and verify its content is gone from retrieval.
choices.explanation: The policy targets the source's indexed data without deleting the vector store itself.

choices.text: Change the generator system prompt to ignore the old manuals while leaving their indexed data in place.
choices.explanation: The indexed material would still exist and could be retrieved, contrary to the retirement requirement.

learning.reason: The data source deletion policy controls what happens to its converted vectors on source deletion. Deleting the source with DELETE removes its data while leaving the vector store resource.
learning.concept: Use the Bedrock data source DELETE policy to retire only the affected source's indexed content.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Monitor the perceived delay before the response starts
prompt: A Bedrock streaming assistant's users report a longer pause before the first displayed word. Once output begins, the text arrives at the usual rate. The team wants a built-in CloudWatch metric focused on the interval from submitting the streaming request until the first token arrives. Which metric should it monitor?

choices.text: InvocationLatency alone.
choices.explanation: Total latency does not isolate the startup interval from later generation.

choices.text: OutputTokenCount.
choices.explanation: This counts generated tokens and does not measure their arrival delay.

choices.text: InvocationThrottles.
choices.explanation: This detects quota-related rejections, not the startup duration of successful streams.

choices.text: TimeToFirstToken for the streaming model traffic.
choices.explanation: It measures the time between sending the request and receiving its first token.

learning.reason: TimeToFirstToken measures startup response for supported streaming operations. End-to-end invocation latency also includes generation after the first token.
learning.concept: Monitor Bedrock TimeToFirstToken for delays before any streamed token is delivered.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Retain diagnostics after asynchronous failures are exhausted
prompt: An asynchronous Lambda enrichment function retries failed ingest events. After its configured attempts are exhausted, the operations team must retain both the original request and details of the final function error in one structured record. Which failure-handling option meets the requirement?

choices.text: Configure an on-failure destination such as an approved SQS queue.
choices.explanation: The destination receives the full invocation record for exhausted failures.

choices.text: Set a Lambda dead-letter queue and expect it to include the same response payload.
choices.explanation: The asynchronous DLQ receives the original event without the function response details.

choices.text: Track the function's Errors metric and derive the original request from the aggregate value.
choices.explanation: A metric count cannot recover an individual payload and error context.

choices.text: Configure only an on-success destination and consume its records for failures.
choices.explanation: The success destination does not receive invocations that exhaust retries.

learning.reason: An asynchronous on-failure destination receives an invocation record with request context, request payload, and response details. A dead-letter queue retains the original event only.
learning.concept: Use a Lambda asynchronous on-failure destination when response diagnostics must accompany the discarded event.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep repeat visitors in their assigned experiment cohorts
prompt: A SageMaker two-variant recommender experiment assigns visitors to a treatment or control cohort before each visitor's first request. All visits by that visitor must use the same variant, even across different clients and sessions. The application can look up the assignment. How should it invoke the shared endpoint?

choices.text: Set endpoint variant weights to the desired enrollment shares and omit TargetVariant.
choices.explanation: Weighted per-request routing does not preserve a visitor's assignment.

choices.text: Resolve the stored cohort and pass its variant in TargetVariant on every eligible request.
choices.explanation: Returning visits continue to use the assigned model.

choices.text: Pass the expected variant as a CloudWatch metric dimension after each invocation.
choices.explanation: Telemetry after the call cannot change which variant served the request.

choices.text: Send only the visitor ID as the model request payload and rely on routing to infer assignment.
choices.explanation: Ordinary weight-based routing does not interpret application cohort IDs within the payload.

learning.reason: The InvokeEndpoint TargetVariant parameter routes directly to an assigned production variant rather than choosing it randomly according to weights.
learning.concept: Use explicit production-variant targeting for persistent experimental cohort assignment.
