category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Detect an incomplete agent response after streaming starts
prompt: A ticket agent uses Bedrock ConverseStream and begins rendering output after the first content events. An incident shows that a 200 response and several content deltas sometimes precede a stream error. The UI currently marks that partial answer as complete. What should completion monitoring use?

choices.text: Mark every HTTP 200 complete before decoding subsequent events.
choices.explanation: Transport success at stream start does not establish the eventual outcome.

choices.text: Treat the first contentBlockDelta as proof the answer finished.
choices.explanation: A delta is an incremental part and more events may follow or fail.

choices.text: Track messageStop and its reason, and classify stream errors or closure before a valid stop as incomplete.
choices.explanation: This distinguishes usable completed output from a stream that ended after only partial data.

choices.text: Mark completion solely after the first token arrives within its latency target.
choices.explanation: Fast startup can coexist with a later error or missing terminal event.

learning.reason: The initial response and content deltas do not guarantee complete generation. The client should require an acceptable terminal message stop and handle stream errors or premature closure as incomplete.
learning.concept: Treat terminal streaming events, rather than the initial HTTP response, as the completion signal.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Avoid treating a possible policy answer as established
prompt: A Bedrock Automated Reasoning check evaluates an assistant's statement about an internal benefit. The result is SATISFIABLE, with one scenario where the statement is true and another where it is false. No other issue was found. Policy requires the application to serve the statement as fact only when it follows from current context and rules. How should it handle this result?

choices.text: Treat SATISFIABLE as equivalent to VALID and serve the answer immediately.
choices.explanation: The two scenarios show that the claim has not been proved under the current context.

choices.text: Assume the policy has an impossible contradiction and discard every rule.
choices.explanation: A satisfiable claim has plausible scenarios. It does not by itself indicate inconsistent premises or rules.

choices.text: Choose the true scenario because it supports the original generated answer.
choices.explanation: That assumes the condition the application has yet to verify.

choices.text: Inspect the alternative scenarios, clarify the missing condition, and validate again before asserting the conclusion.
choices.explanation: The possible-true result alone does not establish that the claim follows from the current inputs.

learning.reason: SATISFIABLE indicates the claim can be true under some assumptions and false under others. An application can inspect missing premises and ask for clarifying information.
learning.concept: Require supporting premises when an Automated Reasoning result is only satisfiable.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Show new model endpoints automatically in a dashboard
prompt: New model endpoints appear weekly and publish the same metric with an EndpointName dimension. The operator wants a graph that automatically shows each active matching time series as new endpoints start publishing, without changing the dashboard or setting up alarms for this feature. What should it use?

choices.text: Use a SEARCH expression scoped to the desired namespace, metric, and endpoint dimensions in the graph.
choices.explanation: The graph can discover newly reporting metrics matching the search.

choices.text: Enter every current EndpointName manually in the widget.
choices.explanation: That fixed list does not automatically add future endpoint values.

choices.text: Build a graph widget with one hard-coded endpoint name and change its visual label to All models.
choices.explanation: A label does not change the query's metric selection.

choices.text: Create a separate fixed metric alarm for each existing endpoint and plot only those alarms.
choices.explanation: Existing alarms do not discover new endpoint metric series for the graph.

learning.reason: CloudWatch graphs can use a SEARCH expression to find matching metric series dynamically, including metrics emitted after the graph was created.
learning.concept: Discover new endpoint metric series through a CloudWatch graph search expression.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Secure accelerator availability for a planned training run
prompt: A training team can schedule a several-day job within a known future window. It needs enough eligible SageMaker accelerator capacity together and wants to reserve it ahead of time. This is a one-off run, so recurring usage discounts alone do not solve the capacity risk. Which option addresses it?

choices.text: Purchase a SageMaker AI Savings Plan and assume it reserves physical accelerator availability.
choices.explanation: Savings Plan discounts do not provide the specific future capacity reservation.

choices.text: Find an eligible Flexible Training Plan for the required host type, count, and duration, and schedule the job for its reserved period.
choices.explanation: The plan addresses capacity availability for the upcoming job rather than only changing its price.

choices.text: Use Managed Spot Training as the sole guarantee that all required hosts are available without interruption.
choices.explanation: Spot capacity is interruptible and does not guarantee the requested window.

choices.text: Increase the account's service quota and assume the requested hardware will always be available at that time.
choices.explanation: A higher quota is a usage allowance, not a reservation of actual capacity.

learning.reason: SageMaker Flexible Training Plans reserve eligible compute capacity for planned periods and can be used by jobs that fit a reservation.
learning.concept: Reserve SageMaker training capacity ahead of a known accelerator window with a Flexible Training Plan.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Calculate the final quota charge for one request
prompt: For a Bedrock runtime model, the documented output-token quota burndown is five to one. A completed request reports 800 uncached input tokens, 100 cache-write input tokens, 300 cache-read tokens, and 120 output tokens. How many tokens does this request consume from its final token quota?

choices.text: 1,800 tokens.
choices.explanation: This also counts the 300 cache-read tokens, which are excluded from the final quota calculation.

choices.text: 1,020 tokens.
choices.explanation: This treats output as one to one instead of applying the specified burndown rate.

choices.text: 1,500 tokens.
choices.explanation: Add 800 uncached and 100 cache-write tokens to 120 output tokens multiplied by five.

choices.text: 1,400 tokens.
choices.explanation: This drops cache-write input, which contributes to quota use.

learning.reason: Final quota usage counts uncached input and cache-write input plus weighted output. Cache-read input does not contribute to this runtime quota total.
learning.concept: Apply the model-specific output burndown to quota usage separately from cache-read billing.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Compare cost using the workload's measured token mix
prompt: Two Bedrock models meet a task's quality and latency requirements. Per request, Model A averages 4,000 input and 1,000 output tokens, with assumed prices of $0.002 and $0.010 per 1,000 tokens, respectively. Model B averages 4,000 input and 500 output tokens at $0.003 and $0.008 per 1,000. Assume no cache use or other charges. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Model A is cheaper because it has the lower input rate.
choices.explanation: Input cost alone omits the longer, more expensive output for Model A.

choices.text: The models cost the same because both have 4,000 input tokens.
choices.explanation: Input rates differ and the output terms are also different.

choices.text: Model B costs $0.036 per request because all tokens use the output rate.
choices.explanation: The 4,000 input tokens use the specified input rate.

choices.text: Model B costs $0.016 per request, below Model A's $0.018.
choices.explanation: Model B's smaller and cheaper output offsets its higher input rate.

learning.reason: Apply the input and output price separately to each model's measured counts. Model A costs $0.018 and Model B costs $0.016 per request.
learning.concept: Estimate serving cost from the measured input and output mix at their separate rates.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep active background work from being treated as idle
prompt: A custom AgentCore Runtime agent acknowledges a request quickly and then continues a background computation. Its ping always returns Healthy. The session can stop at the idle threshold even though computation is ongoing. The maximum lifetime is already sufficient, and genuinely idle sessions should still be reclaimed. What should change?

choices.text: Return HealthyBusy from the ping handler while background work is active and Healthy after it ends.
choices.explanation: Active work is not treated as idle, while completed sessions can still become idle.

choices.text: Report HealthyBusy permanently for all sessions.
choices.explanation: Genuinely idle sessions would be treated as active and consume resources unnecessarily.

choices.text: Set a longer hard maximum lifetime while continuing to report Healthy throughout the computation.
choices.explanation: The idle classification would persist, independently of the maximum lifetime.

choices.text: Shorten the idle timeout without changing the ping response.
choices.explanation: The session could be reclaimed even sooner while the background task is still active.

learning.reason: For a custom runtime, reporting HealthyBusy while background work runs tells AgentCore the session is active. The status can return to Healthy when work finishes.
learning.concept: Report AgentCore Runtime activity accurately instead of lengthening every idle session.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: End generation at an application-defined boundary
prompt: A Bedrock model reliably produces a variable-length category code followed by a unique delimiter. After that delimiter it often continues with explanations the application discards. Complete codes vary in length, so a small fixed maximum could truncate valid values. The selected model supports stop sequences. What change targets the extra generation?

choices.text: Set maxTokens to the length of the shortest observed code.
choices.explanation: This can cut off longer valid codes before reaching their delimiter.

choices.text: Configure the delimiter in stopSequences and keep a separate reasonable maximum as a fallback.
choices.explanation: Generation can end at the expected boundary even when valid code lengths differ.

choices.text: Lower temperature and assume the model will never continue after a delimiter.
choices.explanation: Temperature affects token sampling, not the explicit stopping condition.

choices.text: Keep generation unchanged and trim the returned string after the delimiter.
choices.explanation: This removes extra output from the UI but still generates the discarded tokens.

learning.reason: A supported stop sequence tells the model to stop once it generates the designated delimiter rather than using a fixed token count as the only boundary.
learning.concept: Use a Bedrock stop sequence when the application has a reliable semantic end marker.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep deployed images eligible for new findings
prompt: An ECR repository holds images that remain active in production for several months. The existing control scans just after a new push. Security needs new vulnerability findings for existing eligible images as vulnerability information changes, without republishing the image every day. Which two configuration checks address this? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Configure enhanced continuous scanning for the repository.
choices.explanation: Continuous scanning can revisit eligible repository images after the initial scan.

choices.text: Use scan on push only and reuse the original successful result for all future decisions.
choices.explanation: A successful initial scan cannot report vulnerabilities identified later.

choices.text: Archive images in ECR immediately after deploying them and assume Inspector keeps continuously scanning them.
choices.explanation: Archived images are not eligible for that ongoing scan.

choices.text: Replace image scanning with application-level health metrics.
choices.explanation: Endpoint health does not track new dependency vulnerability findings.

choices.text: Verify the configured re-scan eligibility window covers the intended retention and usage pattern.
choices.explanation: An image that ages out of eligibility will no longer be monitored merely because the repository has continuous scanning enabled.

learning.reason: Enhanced continuous scanning can rescan eligible images after new findings arise. Eligibility duration must cover the team's long-lived image usage.
learning.concept: Enable ongoing Inspector scanning and match image eligibility duration to the deployment lifecycle.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Delegate a private access path to a shared training bucket
prompt: Several apps share an S3 training bucket. A new app should read objects under approved/features/ through an app-specific named access path, only from its VPC. Other apps must keep their existing policies and the new role has no direct bucket access. Which design fits?

choices.text: Give the app the full bucket policy and ask it to call only keys beginning with the approved prefix.
choices.explanation: Application convention is not a permission boundary.

choices.text: Create an internet-origin access point and whitelist all authenticated AWS principals.
choices.explanation: This does not provide either the VPC boundary or the app-specific least-privilege restriction.

choices.text: Create a VPC-origin access point for the bucket. Scope its policy to the app role and approved objects, and permit that path in the underlying bucket policy.
choices.explanation: The app receives a distinct private access point without broader direct bucket access.

choices.text: Put the dataset's VPC name into object metadata and leave authorization unchanged.
choices.explanation: Object metadata does not enforce a VPC origin or grant the scoped access path.

learning.reason: A VPC-origin S3 access point can have a policy for specific object resources and principals. The underlying bucket authorization must permit the access point path.
learning.concept: Use an app-specific VPC-origin S3 access point with a prefix-scoped policy and compatible bucket authorization.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Diagnose an artifact link that expires before its requested time
prompt: An authorized review portal issues an S3 download URL requesting six hours of validity. Its signing role has only 45 minutes remaining on its temporary session. No shorter bucket policy applies and the object stays available. A reviewer's new download request after one hour fails. Why?

choices.text: S3 uses the later of the role session expiration and the URL expiration.
choices.explanation: The credential lifetime bounds the URL at the earlier time.

choices.text: Signing the link automatically extended the role session to six hours.
choices.explanation: Creating a presigned request does not extend the session used to sign it.

choices.text: A presigned URL cannot authorize any request from a user without AWS credentials of their own.
choices.explanation: The URL carries authorization derived from the signing principal; the recipient need not supply separate credentials for this operation.

choices.text: The signing role session expired, so the URL ceased to authorize new downloads before its requested six-hour expiry.
choices.explanation: S3 evaluates the temporary credentials when processing a new signed request.

learning.reason: A presigned URL created with temporary credentials cannot remain valid after those signing credentials expire.
learning.concept: Treat an S3 presigned URL's usable duration as bounded by the signing credential lifetime.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Mask sensitive values while retaining restricted audit access
prompt: A prediction service occasionally includes customer email addresses in log messages. For newly ingested events, operators must see masked values in Logs Insights and through an existing subscription filter. Approved incident auditors must be able to inspect originals during an investigation. Which actions satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Associate a customer managed KMS key with the log group and allow auditors to decrypt with that key.
choices.explanation: Encryption at rest protects the stored data, while normal retrieval can still return decrypted email addresses.

choices.text: Attach a data protection policy with the email address data identifier to the log group.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch Logs masks values matching the configured identifier before they reach the supported egress points.

choices.text: Grant logs:Unmask to the scoped auditor role and keep this permission out of routine operator roles.
choices.explanation: Auditors can request unmasked records through supported operations; regular read permission does not expose the original value.

choices.text: Filter out events that contain email addresses in the subscription pattern.
choices.explanation: Dropping subscription records would not mask any values and would leave Logs Insights visibility unchanged.

choices.text: Replace email addresses in the application logger before sending any records to the log group.
choices.explanation: Permanent redaction at the source would remove the originals that auditors must be able to inspect.

learning.reason: A log-group data protection policy masks matches on egress. Auditors can request unmasked values when authorized, while routine readers and subscriptions receive masked values.
learning.concept: Select log-group masking and independently grant the ability to unmask only to authorized auditors.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Control which model a workload can invoke over a shared interface endpoint
prompt: Multiple workloads already reach a shared Amazon Bedrock Runtime interface endpoint. The application roles have separate AWS identity policies, but the platform team must also enforce a ceiling at the shared endpoint: only approved roles may invoke the designated model through that endpoint. The team must leave those roles' permissions elsewhere and the endpoint's network configuration in place. What should it change?

choices.text: Edit the interface endpoint policy to permit only the approved role principals and relevant invocation action on the designated model resource.
choices.explanation: The policy limits requests at the endpoint itself. The approved requests still require the applicable identity and resource permissions.

choices.text: Use an ingress rule on the endpoint security group to limit each model resource to its approved role ARN.
choices.explanation: Security groups match network attributes. They do not evaluate signed IAM principals, API actions, or model resources.

choices.text: Attach a permissions boundary limiting model access to each approved role.
choices.explanation: A boundary would limit the roles on any access path and would not create the requirement at the endpoint for other roles.

choices.text: Enable private DNS on the endpoint and give the designated model a separate application DNS alias.
choices.explanation: DNS directs clients to a network destination. It does not enforce which credentials and model resources are allowed there.

learning.reason: An endpoint policy is an additional gate for traffic using the endpoint. It can restrict principals, Bedrock actions and supported model resources without replacing identity permissions.
learning.concept: Choose the policy layer that adds a principal, action and resource constraint only to requests that traverse this endpoint.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Detect policy grants that expose model artifacts outside the organization
prompt: An organization stores model artifacts in S3 across several accounts. Security needs findings when a bucket policy permits a principal outside the organization to access those artifacts, even if no object has been downloaded. Approved sharing between accounts in the organization should generate no finding. Which approach meets the requirements?

choices.text: Create a separate IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer for each account, using each account alone as its zone of trust.
choices.explanation: Each analyzer would treat other member accounts as outside its zone and flag approved cross-account sharing.

choices.text: Create an IAM Access Analyzer external access analyzer with the organization as its zone of trust.
choices.explanation: It generates findings for supported resources that grant access outside the organization and treats member accounts in the zone as trusted.

choices.text: Turn on CloudTrail S3 data events and alert when GetObject is called by an external principal.
choices.explanation: This discovers recorded use of permissions, while the requirement covers grants that have never been exercised.

choices.text: Turn on S3 Block Public Access and use its public-access status as the finding.
choices.explanation: A bucket policy granting access to a specific, trusted-by-policy external account is not necessarily public. The required boundary is organization membership.

learning.reason: The organization is the external access analyzer's zone of trust. Potential access granted by a policy to a principal outside that zone is enough to generate a finding; no access event is required.
learning.concept: Set the zone of trust to the whole organization and analyze possible access based on grants.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Authenticate a bearer-only client with temporary Bedrock credentials
prompt: An engineer is testing an Amazon Bedrock model in one Region with a supported client library that accepts bearer tokens but cannot sign requests with AWS Signature Version 4. Policy requires temporary credentials, issued under an identity with only the necessary inference permissions. Which credential should the engineer supply?

choices.text: Generate a long-term Amazon Bedrock API key and rely on the test process terminating to invalidate it.
choices.explanation: Ending the process does not invalidate a long-term key that has already been issued.

choices.text: Send the AWS STS session token from AssumeRole directly in the bearer header.
choices.explanation: The STS session token is part of a temporary AWS credential set used for request signing. It is not a Bedrock bearer token.

choices.text: Generate a short-term Amazon Bedrock API key in the target Region using a least-privilege role session.
choices.explanation: A supported client can present the resulting temporary token as a bearer credential to the Bedrock service in that Region.

choices.text: Send a token from the IAM OIDC identity provider directly in the bearer header.
choices.explanation: In AWS federation, such a token can be exchanged for AWS credentials. It is not the corresponding Bedrock API key for direct model invocation.

learning.reason: A short-term Bedrock API key can be generated using authorized AWS credentials for the Region and sent as a bearer token by compatible clients.
learning.concept: Choose a temporary credential that the library can send directly in its bearer header and that reflects an authorized caller.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Evaluate streamed model output before exposing it to users
prompt: A support application uses InvokeModelWithResponseStream with a supported Amazon Bedrock model and guardrail. The team wants to keep streaming because answers are long, but every returned chunk must be evaluated by the guardrail before it can reach the customer. A modest additional delay per chunk is acceptable. Which setting meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use asynchronous guardrail processing and configure the application to stop displaying text at the first intervention.
choices.explanation: Some content can reach the customer before an asynchronous intervention. Stopping later output does not retract those chunks.

choices.text: Apply the guardrail to the user's prompt first and stream the generated output without output guardrail processing.
choices.explanation: A prompt check does not evaluate content that the model generates.

choices.text: Complete a non-streaming InvokeModel call, then render the final response progressively in the browser.
choices.explanation: The browser can simulate progressive rendering, but the service returns the whole answer together, losing the application's streaming behavior.

choices.text: Use synchronous guardrail processing for the streaming request.
choices.explanation: Bedrock buffers output for evaluation and applies the configured guardrail before returning the corresponding chunks.

learning.reason: In synchronous streaming, the guardrail evaluates buffered output before Bedrock emits it. Asynchronous streaming can return some content before the evaluation runs.
learning.concept: Select the streaming guardrail mode based on evaluation timing and permissible buffering.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Set a default and bounds for idle notebook sessions
prompt: A SageMaker Studio administrator wants newly launched compatible JupyterLab applications in a domain to shut down by default after 90 minutes of idleness. Researchers have different workflows, so they must be allowed to choose an idle timeout within a 60- to 180-minute range. Active sessions should continue running. Which configuration meets those requirements?

choices.text: Enable domain-level JupyterLab idle shutdown, use a 90-minute default, and allow a user-configurable timeout from 60 through 180 minutes.
choices.explanation: These settings express inactivity-based shutdown and the required range of user choice.

choices.text: Enable domain-level JupyterLab idle shutdown and set the default, minimum, and maximum to 90 minutes.
choices.explanation: Setting all three values equal enforces one timeout and prevents researchers from selecting another value.

choices.text: Create an EventBridge schedule to stop each JupyterLab application 90 minutes after it launches.
choices.explanation: A launch-based interval can stop actively used applications and does not implement an idle threshold.

choices.text: Set an EC2 Auto Scaling policy on the domain to scale in after 90 minutes of low average CPU use.
choices.explanation: EC2 group scaling does not configure the SageMaker Studio application lifecycle or allow users to select an application idle timeout.

learning.reason: SageMaker Studio supports native app idle shutdown with a default and configurable customization bounds. A schedule independent of app activity cannot satisfy the active-session requirement.
learning.concept: Translate default and allowed range into domain-level application idle settings.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Keep a feature lake current from a transactional database
prompt: A feature pipeline needs an initial extract of selected Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL tables and subsequent inserts, updates, and deletes in Amazon S3. The source remains writable, and the team wants the change volume to follow database activity instead of repeatedly exporting the whole tables. Logical replication prerequisites have been met. Which ingestion approach meets these requirements?

choices.text: Schedule AWS DMS full-load-only tasks and overwrite the target each hour.
choices.explanation: Repeated reloads duplicate the transfer of unchanged records and do not deliver operation-level change records.

choices.text: Create an AWS DMS task with an S3 target to migrate existing data and replicate ongoing changes.
choices.explanation: The full-load phase initializes the dataset, and PostgreSQL change capture delivers subsequent changes while the source remains in service.

choices.text: Start a CDC-only task at the current log position and use its first output as the historical extract.
choices.explanation: CDC-only can capture changes from its configured position. It does not populate existing rows that never change.

choices.text: Export one RDS snapshot to S3 and configure S3 event notifications for later PostgreSQL row changes.
choices.explanation: A snapshot export captures a point in time. S3 notifications react to changes in S3 and do not observe source database writes.

learning.reason: A DMS full load copies existing records and change data capture writes ongoing source changes to the S3 target. A downstream process can then apply the operation records to its curated feature tables.
learning.concept: Select an ingestion mode that covers both the initial state and the subsequent database change stream.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Replicate a historical training corpus after enabling live replication
prompt: Cross-Region replication now copies new training objects from a versioned S3 bucket. An audit found that objects uploaded before the rule was created are absent from the replica. Their original versions must remain available in the source, and quarantined versions must stay excluded. What should the data engineer do for the one-time backlog?

choices.text: Assign the existing objects the live rule's current priority, then wait for the rule to revisit the prefix.
choices.explanation: Changing rule priority affects rule selection. It does not make live replication scan the old corpus.

choices.text: Run a normal S3 synchronization that copies the latest object for each key.
choices.explanation: A latest-object copy may recover object names but does not replicate the specified historical versions under the replication rule.

choices.text: Run an S3 Batch Replication job with a manifest that lists the eligible historical object versions.
choices.explanation: The job acts on the specified existing objects, preserving source versions and avoiding a rewrite to trigger the live rule.

choices.text: Enable S3 Replication Time Control and use its replication metrics to track the older keys.
choices.explanation: Time control addresses eligible new objects governed by live replication. It does not initiate replication for the historical backlog.

learning.reason: S3 Batch Replication handles eligible historical versions under the replication configuration. A manifest can scope the job to the required object versions.
learning.concept: Choose on-demand replication of selected existing versions while leaving live replication to handle new writes.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Make newly delivered feature partitions queryable without registering them
prompt: A pipeline writes nearly contiguous daily feature partitions into S3 under a deterministic date-and-region path. All consumers use the same Athena table and filter on dates and regions. Registering each new partition delays dataset availability, even when the S3 upload is already complete. The paths and allowed region values can be described in table properties. What should the team change?

choices.text: Create a Glue partition index for the existing registered partitions and leave the ingestion job unchanged.
choices.explanation: The index can improve lookup of catalog entries. Newly written locations still have to be registered.

choices.text: Run MSCK REPAIR TABLE before every query that may span a newly arrived day.
choices.explanation: This still introduces explicit partition discovery and registration before the data is queryable.

choices.text: Enable Athena query result reuse for queries with the same region and date filters.
choices.explanation: Result reuse can return an earlier query result. It does not register or infer newly arrived partitions.

choices.text: Enable Athena partition projection with a date range, the allowed region values, and the existing S3 path template.
choices.explanation: Athena derives locations from table properties and can query a new partition without first fetching its catalog entry.

learning.reason: Athena can calculate expected partition locations from table properties. A custom storage location template fits a predictable existing directory layout.
learning.concept: Replace per-partition catalog registration for an Athena-only dataset with predictable partition rules.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reproduce the exact table state used for a model run
prompt: A model card records the Apache Iceberg snapshot ID used to extract its training data in Athena. The table has received late changes since that run, and an auditor needs the same rows as the original extraction. The recorded snapshot is still retained. The team cannot change the current table state. How should it repeat the query?

choices.text: Run the original query with FOR VERSION AS OF and the recorded snapshot ID on the table reference.
choices.explanation: The version qualifier reads from the exact retained Iceberg snapshot without rolling back the table.

choices.text: Filter the current table for event timestamps on or before the training run's start time.
choices.explanation: Late updates may change rows with older event times. Filtering the current snapshot cannot undo those updates.

choices.text: Use the time the model artifact was uploaded in a FOR TIMESTAMP AS OF query.
choices.explanation: Training and upload can occur after other Iceberg commits; the upload time does not necessarily identify the input snapshot.

choices.text: Read the S3 prefix directly and include every object last modified before model registration.
choices.explanation: Object timestamps alone do not determine which files and delete information the Iceberg snapshot included.

learning.reason: Athena version travel reads the retained data for the recorded Iceberg snapshot while leaving the current table and other readers alone.
learning.concept: Use the stored table snapshot identifier as the read boundary instead of approximating it from business timestamps.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reduce straggler time when joining two large feature datasets
prompt: A Glue 4.0 Spark job performs a shuffle join between two large feature datasets. A few common entity values cause a small number of shuffle partitions to dominate the runtime. Neither dataset can fit in every executor's memory, and both sources must retain their true entity keys. The job template disabled adaptive query execution. Which change addresses the observed bottleneck?

choices.text: Force a broadcast hash join using the smaller of the two input datasets.
choices.explanation: Even the smaller input exceeds the executor memory constraint. A forced broadcast can create memory failures.

choices.text: Enable adaptive query execution and its skewed-join optimization.
choices.explanation: Spark can split oversized shuffle partitions according to runtime statistics so more tasks share the work.

choices.text: Increase the number of static hash partitions while keeping adaptive execution disabled.
choices.explanation: Every occurrence of a hot key still hashes into a single partition. Increasing the count mainly helps keys that distribute across partitions.

choices.text: Coalesce the two outputs into fewer partitions before the join.
choices.explanation: Coalescing reduces task parallelism. It does not break up work for an oversized shuffle partition at the join.

learning.reason: Adaptive skew optimization subdivides disproportionately large shuffle partitions and handles the corresponding join data needed for those subdivisions.
learning.concept: Identify a runtime strategy that redistributes large shuffle partitions without broadcasting the whole data side or changing entity identity.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Improve extraction for recurring fields on specialized forms
prompt: A claims pipeline uses Amazon Textract Queries to produce features from information printed on scanned forms. Extraction is consistently inaccurate on the insurer's specialized form layouts, even after the queries have been made unambiguous. The insurer can annotate representative forms and wants to keep calling the Textract document analysis API. Which actions meet the requirement? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Switch the pipeline to DetectDocumentText and send the original query strings as extraction settings.
choices.explanation: This operation returns text detection results and is not the document analysis API that evaluates Queries.

choices.text: Train an Amazon Textract Custom Queries adapter on representative documents with the desired answer spans annotated.
choices.explanation: The adapter customizes the pretrained extraction behavior for recurring layouts and fields.

choices.text: Add more aliases to each unchanged query and deploy without adapter training.
choices.explanation: Aliases identify answers in the response. They do not supply supervised layout examples to the extractor.

choices.text: Provide the trained adapter ID and version with the queries on a supported document analysis operation.
choices.explanation: The request uses the trained adapter for the specified document or pages.

choices.text: Add the form names to an Amazon Transcribe custom vocabulary and use that vocabulary in Textract.
choices.explanation: A speech vocabulary affects transcription. It is not a Textract document extraction adapter.

learning.reason: A Custom Queries adapter can learn from representative documents. AnalyzeDocument or StartDocumentAnalysis can select a particular trained adapter version and ask the intended queries.
learning.concept: Improve the existing extraction model with an annotated adapter and select the resulting version during document analysis.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Catch a broken relationship between two measurements
prompt: Before retraining a model, a quality gate checks measurements from a reference sensor and a field sensor. Both columns may still have acceptable ranges and completeness after a wiring error, but readings from the two sensors stop moving together linearly. The team wants this gate to evaluate one incoming batch using AWS Glue Data Quality. Which rule best represents the condition?

choices.text: Require that each sensor's StandardDeviation stays near its historical value.
choices.explanation: Both series can have realistic variability even when their row-level pairing has been lost.

choices.text: Require each column to stay within its calibrated numeric range using ColumnValues.
choices.explanation: Valid individual values can still be paired with unrelated measurements.

choices.text: Require the ColumnCorrelation for the reference and field readings to stay above a validated positive threshold.
choices.explanation: The coefficient tests whether the paired readings share the expected positive linear relationship.

choices.text: Require the two columns to have the same Completeness score.
choices.explanation: Completeness compares the presence of values. It does not measure how their values move together.

learning.reason: ColumnCorrelation measures the Pearson relationship across paired numeric values, which matches a check that two measurements still vary together linearly.
learning.concept: Validate the relationship between columns, independently of each column's range and completeness.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prevent future labels from leaking across a time-based holdout
prompt: A model predicts whether a customer will renew in the next 30 days. Each example has features as of its observation date and a label derived from the following 30 days. The validation set simulates scoring at the beginning of May, as though the model had been trained then. What should the team do with late April examples whose labels depend on May events?

choices.text: Put all April observations into training because their feature timestamps predate May.
choices.explanation: The label for a late April observation depends on outcomes not available by the simulated training cutoff.

choices.text: Randomly stratify April and May examples by label before splitting.
choices.explanation: Stratification can balance class proportions but does not enforce which outcomes the model could have observed at the cutoff.

choices.text: Keep the examples but assign every unfinished label window the non-renewal class.
choices.explanation: This avoids looking ahead by mislabeling unresolved examples. It introduces systematic label noise near the cutoff.

choices.text: Exclude from training examples whose 30-day label windows end after the May cutoff.
choices.explanation: This reproduces the labels available to a real model training at that date and keeps future outcomes out of the training set.

learning.reason: The simulated model can train only on examples whose complete target window would already have been observable at the evaluation cutoff. Leave a gap for examples whose target spans cross that cutoff.
learning.concept: Apply the data availability cutoff to the label-window end, as well as the feature time, in a retrospective split.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Build an approximate vector index within the refresh window
prompt: A batch job refreshes an Aurora PostgreSQL embedding table from scratch daily. A pilot found that both a tuned IVFFlat index and an HNSW index meet the same recall and query latency targets, but graph construction does not fit the refresh window. The fully populated table is available before the index must be built. Which change should the team make?

choices.text: Bulk-load the daily vectors, then build the IVFFlat index on the populated table.
choices.explanation: The build can learn meaningful list centers from the current vectors and avoids the cost of constructing the HNSW graph.

choices.text: Create the IVFFlat index on the new empty table, then load vectors without rebuilding the index.
choices.explanation: Building before the vectors arrive prevents the build from learning representative centers from the refreshed corpus.

choices.text: Reduce hnsw.ef_search during daily refresh to speed up HNSW construction.
choices.explanation: This parameter controls work during search. It does not reduce graph construction work.

choices.text: Drop the approximate index and sort the entire table by distance for every request.
choices.explanation: This can return exact neighbors but scans the corpus at query time and does not preserve the required approximate search approach.

learning.reason: IVFFlat typically builds faster and learns its list centers from populated vectors. Existing pilot results establish that it meets this workload's measured retrieval targets.
learning.concept: Choose the validated approximate index with the lower build cost and populate the table before the index learns its data clusters.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Consolidate small Iceberg files without interrupting writers
prompt: A streaming pipeline creates many small Parquet data files in a registered Amazon S3-backed Apache Iceberg table. Athena query startup slows as planning and file-open operations increase. The pipeline must keep writing and readers must see the same committed records. Which low-maintenance change should the team make?

choices.text: Enable snapshot retention optimization and rely on it to merge data files used by the current snapshot.
choices.explanation: Retention manages expired snapshots and associated files. It does not consolidate the live small files.

choices.text: Enable AWS Glue Data Catalog compaction for the Iceberg table and use the binpack strategy.
choices.explanation: Compaction combines smaller data files into larger ones and commits replacement files through the Iceberg table.

choices.text: Enable orphan file deletion so every small file referenced by an active snapshot is removed.
choices.explanation: Files referenced by the table are not orphan files. Deleting live files directly would break reads.

choices.text: Recatalog the current Parquet files as a Hive-style table using partition indexes.
choices.explanation: Cataloging the same objects differently does not reduce their count and discards the existing Iceberg table semantics.

learning.reason: Managed Iceberg compaction can rewrite small files into larger ones and commit the table change through Iceberg, preserving logical rows for readers.
learning.concept: Apply table-aware data-file compaction while keeping the table's writers and file format.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Turn a recurring transformation into managed feature ingestion
prompt: A team recalculates household-level features by applying existing PySpark transformations to a daily dataset in S3. It wants SageMaker Feature Store to load the source and ingest the transformed rows automatically into an existing feature group. Which changes achieve this? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Ingest the source rows directly with PutRecord before applying aggregation in notebooks.
choices.explanation: This stores raw rows rather than automatically producing transformed household features.

choices.text: Decorate the transformation, configuring the S3 data source and the target feature group.
choices.explanation: The processor needs the sources to load and a feature group to receive the completed records.

choices.text: Make the decorated function return only a path and write the feature batch to a local CSV.
choices.explanation: A path to a local file is not the transformed feature DataFrame that the decorator ingests.

choices.text: Replace the transformation with a BatchGetRecord call against the target group.
choices.explanation: This retrieves existing online feature values. It does not compute or ingest updated household-level features.

choices.text: Return the transformed PySpark DataFrame with the feature group's record identifier and event-time fields.
choices.explanation: The output must conform to the target feature schema so the SDK can ingest it.

learning.reason: A Feature Processor definition supplies the input sources and target group with a decorated transformation that returns the feature rows. The SDK handles loading and ingestion around that function.
learning.concept: Provide the processor's input and output mapping and return the transformed features from the decorated function.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Route very late observations into a correction flow
prompt: A Managed Service for Apache Flink DataStream job generates event-time features using five-minute windows. It accepts late updates for two additional minutes. After that window state is removed, observations must be retained for offline corrections without changing the online feature results. Which change preserves both requirements?

choices.text: Extend the allowed lateness until the latest known arrival and continue to use only the main output.
choices.explanation: This would allow old events to update the online result during the extended interval.

choices.text: Switch to processing-time windows so every late event enters the currently active window.
choices.explanation: This can place an observation in the wrong event-time bucket and changes the resulting features.

choices.text: Configure sideOutputLateData for the window and send that side output to a separate correction sink.
choices.explanation: Events too late for the window follow the side output without extending the main aggregation's acceptance period.

choices.text: Reduce the watermark delay so the old window closes faster and keep only the main output.
choices.explanation: The window would still drop events beyond its lateness limit, which would leave the correction process without the records.

learning.reason: A Flink event-time window can send events outside its allowed lateness to a side output. A separate sink retains them after the main window no longer accepts updates.
learning.concept: Route observations beyond the retained window to another sink without extending the online updates.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Read an archived corpus for a one-time model audit
prompt: A required audit will re-run a scoring job against a fixed manifest of S3 Glacier Deep Archive objects. The job must read the objects during a three-day review without creating a permanent working dataset. It can begin once all listed inputs are ready. Which actions should the engineer take? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Start the job on the first successful RestoreObject API response.
choices.explanation: Acceptance of the request does not mean any particular object is ready, much less all entries in the manifest.

choices.text: Modify the S3 Lifecycle archive rule to transition those objects back to S3 Standard immediately.
choices.explanation: Editing the lifecycle rule does not restore already archived objects for a read window.

choices.text: Submit restore requests for the manifest's objects with a duration that covers the review window.
choices.explanation: The restored copies provide temporary read access and the underlying objects remain archived.

choices.text: Confirm that each requested restoration is complete, then start the scoring job using the original keys.
choices.explanation: A successful request only initiates restoration. Once it completes, the same object keys can be read for the requested duration.

choices.text: Copy the archived objects directly into a new permanent Standard bucket before restoring them.
choices.explanation: Archived contents must be restored before copying, and the review calls for temporary availability.

learning.reason: Glacier Deep Archive requires an asynchronous restore of a temporary accessible copy. The job can wait for readiness for every manifest entry and use the original object keys during the restore period.
learning.concept: Arrange a temporary restore window and wait for restored objects to become readable before launching the job.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Collect pixel-level labels for irregular regions in images
prompt: A team is building a model that estimates how much of each aerial image is covered by water, trees, and bare soil. It must learn to assign one class to every pixel, including irregular shapes and boundaries between classes. Which Ground Truth labeling task should the team use?

choices.text: Use object detection with one bounding box around each visible region.
choices.explanation: Boxes include pixels outside irregular regions and do not specify the class at their true boundaries.

choices.text: Use multi-label image classification and attach all classes visible anywhere in each image.
choices.explanation: Image-level labels give no location or coverage information for a class.

choices.text: Use object tracking and keep a stable object identifier across neighboring images.
choices.explanation: Tracking associates instances across frames. Stable IDs do not by themselves provide per-pixel semantic masks.

choices.text: Use semantic segmentation and have annotators draw class masks for the relevant regions, including a background class as needed.
choices.explanation: The class masks specify the pixel-level labels the model must learn.

learning.reason: Semantic segmentation produces a class mask at pixel resolution and supplies the training signal for class coverage and boundaries.
learning.concept: Choose annotation granularity that directly matches the prediction the model will make.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Join sensitive records using consistent pseudonyms
prompt: Two approved preprocessing jobs must join records on a low-entropy customer identifier. Both may read the source IDs, but downstream readers should see only deterministic pseudonyms. Those readers must not be able to try likely IDs against the pseudonyms without the protection key, and the system does not need to decrypt a pseudonym. Which approach meets the requirements?

choices.text: Use the same restricted AWS KMS HMAC key and normalization in both jobs. Store each GenerateMac result in place of the source ID.
choices.explanation: The same key, message and algorithm produce matching tags. Access can be scoped to the preprocessing roles so downstream readers cannot generate corresponding tags.

choices.text: Hash the normalized ID with SHA-256 alone in both jobs and give downstream readers no additional permissions.
choices.explanation: Readers can hash guessed IDs locally without any permission. Low-entropy values are vulnerable to an offline guessing comparison.

choices.text: Encrypt each ID independently with a fresh random nonce and join on the ciphertext.
choices.explanation: Fresh nonces make equal plaintext IDs produce different ciphertext values, which prevents the equality join.

choices.text: Use a different protected HMAC key for each job and join the resulting tags directly.
choices.explanation: The same ID produces different tags under different keys, so the datasets cannot join on their tags alone.

learning.reason: Both preprocessors can generate a keyed HMAC over a canonical ID under the same restricted key. Matching inputs produce matching pseudonyms and a holder of only the pseudonyms cannot recompute candidates offline without the key.
learning.concept: Use a deterministic keyed one-way transform for joinable identifiers and restrict access to the MAC operation.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Deliver streaming JSON as columnar training data
prompt: An existing Amazon Data Firehose stream receives newline-separated JSON telemetry. The data must arrive in S3 as Parquet, preserving typed nested fields for an Athena feature pipeline. The team wants native conversion in the delivery service and can maintain a schema that matches the input. Which configuration should it use?

choices.text: Enable GZIP output compression in Firehose and name the compressed data objects with a .parquet suffix.
choices.explanation: Compression and the file extension do not change the underlying JSON encoding.

choices.text: Enable Firehose record format conversion with a compatible JSON deserializer, a matching Glue schema with nested structures, and a Parquet serializer.
choices.explanation: These settings let Firehose parse the records, map field types, and write Parquet during delivery.

choices.text: Set Parquet as the Athena table's input format while leaving Firehose to write unconverted JSON.
choices.explanation: Table metadata describes how to read files. It does not transcode the records at delivery.

choices.text: Configure dynamic partitioning by two fields and add a Glue schema without enabling format conversion.
choices.explanation: Partition routing determines destination prefixes. It does not serialize objects into Parquet.

learning.reason: Firehose's conversion feature uses a JSON deserializer, a Glue Data Catalog schema, and a Parquet serializer before delivery to S3.
learning.concept: Configure the native format conversion at ingest, including the schema needed to interpret nested input.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Separate online freshness from offline training availability
prompt: An ingestion service successfully sends PutRecord calls to a SageMaker feature group with both stores enabled. The updated feature values are readable online, but an Athena extract launched seconds later does not yet contain some rows. No write errors were returned. What should the training pipeline change?

choices.text: Repeat each PutRecord immediately whenever Athena does not show it after the API returns.
choices.explanation: Submitting more writes does not remove buffering and can add multiple records to offline history.

choices.text: Change the event times to the current processing time whenever an online read succeeds.
choices.explanation: Rewriting timestamps changes the feature history and has no effect on when buffered writes reach S3.

choices.text: Wait until the expected records or batch completeness marker can be verified in the offline store before creating the training extract.
choices.explanation: This handles the documented offline buffering interval and prevents a partial offline dataset from being used.

choices.text: Replace the extract with GetRecord calls against the online store for the same identifiers.
choices.explanation: Online reads return current values and cannot substitute for the required historical training records.

learning.reason: Offline Feature Store writes are buffered and batched to S3. Online visibility does not serve as an offline commit barrier.
learning.concept: Gate a batch extraction on confirmed offline arrival, rather than treating successful online visibility as a signal to start training.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Transform a right-skewed feature that includes valid zeros
prompt: An AWS Glue PySpark job prepares nonnegative transaction counts for a model. Zeros are common and meaningful. The feature has a very long right tail, and the team wants to retain ordering while making large count differences less dominant. Which transform should the job apply?

choices.text: Apply the natural logarithm directly to the count feature.
choices.explanation: The logarithm of zero is undefined, so this does not keep the valid zero values as finite outputs.

choices.text: Z-score the original counts using the training mean and standard deviation.
choices.explanation: An affine rescaling preserves the distribution's skew and does not selectively compress the right tail.

choices.text: Cap all counts above the 95th percentile at that percentile.
choices.explanation: Clipping reduces the effect of high counts but loses ordering among all observations above the cap.

choices.text: Apply log1p to the count feature.
choices.explanation: The transformation maps zero to zero and compresses differences at large counts while remaining increasing.

learning.reason: The natural logarithm of one plus the count is defined at zero, grows more slowly at large counts, and preserves the original ordering.
learning.concept: Apply a monotonic right-tail compression that handles zero without replacing valid observations.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Generate vector fields as newly written documents are indexed
prompt: Writers send a title and a description to an Amazon OpenSearch Serverless collection that supports ML inference pipelines. The team has registered an embedding model. Existing clients must keep sending text only, and each new document must have a stored vector derived from its description before semantic search can retrieve it. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Configure an ingest pipeline with an ml_inference processor, map the description to the embedding model input, and store the model output in the matching vector field.
choices.explanation: Each document flows through inference during ingest and can be indexed with its generated vector.

choices.text: Run only a search pipeline that generates a vector for the user's query.
choices.explanation: The query vector does not create missing embeddings for the documents in the index.

choices.text: Change the description field's mapping directly from text to knn_vector without changing the ingest path.
choices.explanation: A vector mapping expects numeric vector data. It does not embed raw descriptions by itself.

choices.text: Configure a reranker to score text after the vector search completes.
choices.explanation: Reranking can reorder candidates retrieved earlier. It cannot retrieve documents missing vectors in the initial semantic search.

learning.reason: An ingest ML inference processor can map a document's text field into the model request and write the output to an indexed vector field at indexing time.
learning.concept: Determine whether model inference must run at ingestion, with the source field mapped into the model and its output mapped into a stored vector.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Normalize equivalent text without flattening meaningful characters
prompt: A text corpus mixes accented characters typed as a single code point with the same characters represented by a base letter and a combining mark. Duplicate checks and tokenization should treat canonically equivalent spellings consistently. The team must preserve compatibility distinctions, such as circled numbers and ordinary digits, when they carry meaning. Which preprocessing should it apply?

choices.text: Apply Unicode Normalization Form KC before duplicate checks and tokenization.
choices.explanation: Compatibility normalization can map a circled number to an ordinary digit, which would lose a required distinction.

choices.text: Apply Unicode Normalization Form C before duplicate checks and tokenization.
choices.explanation: It unifies equivalent combining sequences and maintains compatibility distinctions such as circled digits.

choices.text: Remove all combining marks from the raw code-point sequence.
choices.explanation: Removing marks can turn accented words into different words and can handle composed and decomposed input inconsistently.

choices.text: Re-encode each source file as UTF-8 without Unicode normalization.
choices.explanation: UTF-8 represents both sequences but does not reconcile their different code-point representations.

learning.reason: NFC maps canonically equivalent sequences to a composed canonical representation where possible and does not apply compatibility mappings.
learning.concept: Choose canonical composition before tokenization and comparison while retaining compatibility distinctions.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Explain why several matched table chunks return as one result
prompt: An Amazon Bedrock knowledge base indexes parsed Markdown with fixed-size chunking. A page contains a short table whose chunks match the query in several places, but Retrieve returns one result with the broader table text. The retrieval limit is larger than one. Which behavior explains the result?

choices.text: The embedding model returns a single vector for this entire data source whenever any table is present.
choices.explanation: Matching chunks can have independent vectors. Consolidation happens when their shared context is returned.

choices.text: The requested retrieval limit sets a minimum, so the vector store must have failed after returning the first chunk.
choices.explanation: The limit is not a guaranteed result count and matching chunks can legitimately collapse into fewer results.

choices.text: Bedrock can replace matching chunks with their shared table context and return that context once.
choices.explanation: The retrieved results can consolidate different matching chunks when they map to the same parsed table or page context.

choices.text: Fixed-size chunking returns parent sections only when a hierarchical parent chunk size is also configured.
choices.explanation: For parsed tables and figures, broader context can be returned even when fixed-size chunking is configured.

learning.reason: For supported parsed content that contains a table or figure, Bedrock can use broader page or table context. Chunks that share the same context are consolidated in the response, even with fixed-size chunking.
learning.concept: Distinguish the text used to match a vector from the broader shared context returned to the caller.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prepare unlabeled domain documents for continued pre-training
prompt: An organization plans continued pre-training on a supported Amazon Nova 1.0 checkpoint. It has rights-cleared manufacturing manuals and reports but no instruction-answer labels. A teammate proposes converting every section into a conversation with an empty assistant reply. Which format and content meet the CPT data requirements?

choices.text: Write JSONL objects with user turns ending in an empty assistant turn.
choices.explanation: That resembles incomplete instruction training data. It does not match the CPT text-only object schema.

choices.text: Write one row for each prompt with a chosen and rejected answer, using empty strings for both.
choices.explanation: Preference pairs provide no useful training signal here and are not the required CPT representation.

choices.text: Write embedding vectors for the passages to JSONL instead of the passage text.
choices.explanation: CPT consumes text to learn domain language. Precomputed vectors do not match the expected examples.

choices.text: Write JSONL objects with a single text field containing cleaned, naturally flowing domain passages.
choices.explanation: This preserves the unlabeled corpus while matching the required schema for Nova 1.0 CPT.

learning.reason: Nova 1.0 CPT accepts one text string per JSONL object for naturally flowing domain content. It does not need labeled responses or chat turns.
learning.concept: Match the data format and absence of labels to continued pre-training rather than supervised instruction tuning.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Measure transcription quality where aggregate performance hides disparities
prompt: A multilingual speech pipeline will create text for a model. Its traffic-weighted word error rate improved, but most validation clips are from one locale. Before expanding the pilot, the team needs to determine whether word-level error exceeds a threshold in each locale, with background noise tracked separately. Which evaluation design meets this goal?

choices.text: Collect a representative held-out audio and verified transcript set across locales and noise conditions. Report WER and sample coverage for each slice.
choices.explanation: Each slice measures its own word errors against reference words, making locale differences and gaps in coverage visible.

choices.text: Report pooled word error rate weighted by current traffic, then infer from any improvement that every locale meets the threshold.
choices.explanation: A large high-traffic locale can dominate the result even when smaller locales miss their thresholds.

choices.text: Compare the average length of generated transcripts per locale without reference transcripts.
choices.explanation: Output length cannot measure the substitutions, insertions, and deletions relative to the true transcript.

choices.text: Use one clean recording per locale and compare the model's confidence score.
choices.explanation: One recording does not cover the noise conditions, and prediction confidence is not a direct measure of errors against reference words.

learning.reason: Transcription quality can differ by locale and audio conditions. A representative evaluation with verified reference transcripts and WER by slice exposes differences that pooled WER can hide.
learning.concept: Collect aligned audio and reference text across relevant slices and report accuracy separately for each slice.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Increase rare examples seen by the trainer without changing validation prevalence
prompt: A PyTorch classifier for sensor faults trains on a large, severely imbalanced set. Minority examples are valid observations, and the team cannot synthesize additional data or change loss weights. The validation set must continue to represent real prevalence. How should the team change its sampler?

choices.text: Use the same weighted sampler for validation and calculate precision from the resulting balanced validation stream.
choices.explanation: Changing the validation prevalence would change the meaning of measured precision for the operational population.

choices.text: Use a WeightedRandomSampler with replacement and inverse-class-frequency weights per training example. Leave validation sampling unchanged.
choices.explanation: Rare training items are drawn more often, while validation still represents the operational class distribution.

choices.text: Oversample the minority rows before making the training and validation split.
choices.explanation: Repeated copies could appear on both sides of the split and alter the original validation prevalence.

choices.text: Randomly shuffle the training examples uniformly before each epoch.
choices.explanation: Shuffling changes the order of examples while preserving the original class proportions.

learning.reason: Weighted random sampling with replacement can repeatedly draw real minority training examples by assigning per-example weights, independently of how validation is sampled.
learning.concept: Modify the distribution of training draws while keeping validation data unchanged and keeping the loss function fixed.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Control reasoning latency without removing depth from difficult requests
prompt: A Bedrock application uses a Claude model that supports an explicit extended-thinking budget. Tests show that multi-constraint scheduling requests benefit from a larger budget, but short factual lookups meet quality targets without extended thinking. Most traffic is factual and latency sensitive. What should the team do?

choices.text: Enable the larger reasoning budget for every request and shorten the prompt's visible answer instructions.
choices.explanation: A shorter requested answer does not independently cap the tokens used for internally generated extended thinking.

choices.text: Disable extended thinking for every request and increase the permitted visible output length.
choices.explanation: More output capacity is not equivalent to the tested thinking budget and does not preserve the measured quality gain.

choices.text: Disable extended thinking for routine lookups and enable the validated larger budget for multi-constraint requests.
choices.explanation: This preserves the demonstrated reasoning gain on complex requests while avoiding it as a default cost for routine traffic.

choices.text: Use the highest thinking budget but set the model's temperature lower to limit latency.
choices.explanation: Lower sampling variability is not a dependable control for the reasoning tokens or latency this application measured.

learning.reason: Extended thinking can increase latency and token use. Request-level controls allow the application to spend more reasoning only on the cases that benefit from it.
learning.concept: Match the request's reasoning budget to measured task complexity and quality needs.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Fit reusable centroids for numerical usage profiles
prompt: A product team has scaled usage vectors and no labels. Analysts want six recurring usage profiles and need to assign each newly observed account to a learned representative center. They plan to use a built-in SageMaker algorithm that fits the centers on a large dataset. Which approach should they take?

choices.text: Fit Random Cut Forest with six trees and use the most active tree as the account's cluster.
choices.explanation: The number of trees controls the ensemble. Anomaly scoring does not assign an account to one learned centroid per requested profile.

choices.text: Fit PCA with six components and use the coordinate with the largest magnitude as the account's cluster.
choices.explanation: Principal components are directions of variance, not six clusters or learned representative account centers.

choices.text: Fit a six-class Linear Learner classifier using the account identifiers in place of class labels.
choices.explanation: Supervised classification requires meaningful training labels; account identifiers do not identify the desired profiles.

choices.text: Fit the SageMaker K-Means algorithm with six clusters and use the nearest learned centroid for new vectors.
choices.explanation: K-Means learns representative centers without labels and supports assignment through distances to those centers.

learning.reason: SageMaker K-Means learns a requested number of centroids from unlabeled numerical data. New vectors can be assigned to the closest learned center.
learning.concept: Select centroid-based clustering when the desired output is a fixed set of recurring profiles and assignments to those profiles.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Keep the training script independent of its input location
prompt: A SageMaker managed training job uses a supported framework container in script mode. The training and validation sets are supplied as separate named input channels, train and validation, using File mode. The script still reads both splits from laptop directories and fails in the container. Which actions fix the issue and preserve the split? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use SM_MODEL_DIR as the input directory for both datasets.
choices.explanation: The model directory is intended for output artifacts, not for train or validation input.

choices.text: Copy the laptop paths into job hyperparameters without relocating or remapping the datasets.
choices.explanation: Parameters change the strings a script receives. The laptop filesystem is not mounted in the training container.

choices.text: Resolve the training data directory from SM_CHANNEL_TRAIN inside the script.
choices.explanation: The managed framework container provides the local directory for the train channel in this variable.

choices.text: Concatenate both channels into a single shuffled table before creating the loaders.
choices.explanation: This loses the explicitly defined validation split and can leak its data into training.

choices.text: Resolve the validation data directory from SM_CHANNEL_VALIDATION and use it only in the validation loader.
choices.explanation: The separately named channel maps to its own path, which preserves separation between fitting and evaluation.

learning.reason: SageMaker framework containers expose input paths through channel-specific SM_CHANNEL names. The script can resolve both directories at runtime and keep their data loaders separate.
learning.concept: Bind application input paths to the framework container's named channels without combining training and validation records.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Explore positive hyperparameters across several orders of magnitude
prompt: A SageMaker Automatic Model Tuning job tests regularization values from 0.00001 to 10. The team has a limited number of trials and wants the search to explore relative changes across this range, so a change from 0.001 to 0.01 deserves comparable attention to a change from 0.1 to 1. Which range setting matches that intent?

choices.text: Define a continuous positive range with Logarithmic scaling.
choices.explanation: The scale distributes attention in log space, where tenfold intervals have equal widths.

choices.text: Define a continuous range with Linear scaling and leave the numeric bounds unchanged.
choices.explanation: Linear search spans absolute differences, so a large fraction of the range lies among higher-magnitude values.

choices.text: Define an integer range from 0 through 10 and keep default scaling.
choices.explanation: The useful fractions are no longer legal candidates in the integer range.

choices.text: Set the minimum to zero and use Logarithmic scaling.
choices.explanation: Zero is outside the domain of a log transform. The minimum must be strictly positive.

learning.reason: A logarithmic distribution gives comparable search coverage to multiplicative intervals across a strictly positive range.
learning.concept: Choose a tuning scale based on relative changes over positive values spanning orders of magnitude.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Classify support notes that have several independent topics
prompt: A support dataset labels each note with all applicable topics, such as delayed delivery and damaged item. New notes can have several labels, and the set of possible combinations changes over time. The team wants one managed Amazon Comprehend classifier whose results can identify the individual topics. What should it configure?
