choices.text: Train a single-label classifier with a separate class for every observed combination of topics.
choices.explanation: This treats each existing combination as one mutually exclusive outcome and does not predict new combinations of individual labels directly.

choices.text: Train a custom classifier in multi-label mode with every applicable topic attached to each training note.
choices.explanation: The classifier can return multiple independent topic labels for a single document.

choices.text: Duplicate each multi-topic note once per label and train one multi-class model on the copies.
choices.explanation: Identical inputs would have conflicting exclusive targets, and multi-class prediction is still limited to one class per note.

choices.text: Train a custom entity recognizer on topic words and treat all recognized strings as document-level topic labels.
choices.explanation: This finds spans, while topic classification can require context even when the literal topic words are absent.

learning.reason: Comprehend multi-label classification learns overlapping categories from individual documents that have been tagged with one or more labels.
learning.concept: Choose labels that remain individually predictable when a single document contains several topics.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Reduce training startup time without rewriting the file reader
prompt: A SageMaker training script uses normal filesystem reads to scan a small number of large objects in S3 sequentially. File mode spends much of each short training job downloading all of the dataset before the entry point starts. The team wants to keep the loader's filesystem interface and start reading without downloading every object first. Which input mode fits?

choices.text: Use Pipe mode and keep the loader that expects ordinary seekable files and directory paths.
choices.explanation: Pipe mode exposes streaming input differently and requires an input reader designed for the pipe.

choices.text: Keep File mode and configure ShardedByS3Key on the existing single-instance job.
choices.explanation: One host still receives the whole assigned dataset, and File mode still stages it before training.

choices.text: Use FastFile mode for the S3 input prefix.
choices.explanation: The script still reads filesystem paths, and the job can begin consuming data without staging the full dataset first.

choices.text: Increase the job's model output volume while leaving File mode unchanged.
choices.explanation: More capacity may help if the job ran out of space, but it does not avoid the pre-training transfer.

learning.reason: FastFile mode makes S3 objects visible through a filesystem interface and streams object data as it is read. Sequential reading of larger files is a suitable access pattern.
learning.concept: Select streaming with file semantics when the existing loader should keep its file interface.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Combine lexical and semantic hits without comparing raw scores
prompt: An OpenSearch hybrid query combines a keyword clause and a vector clause for retrieval. Their scores have different distributions. The team wants documents ranked near the top by both clauses to receive a boost, using only each document's position in each list. The deployment supports OpenSearch score ranker pipelines. Which change meets the requirement?

choices.text: Add each document's raw lexical and vector scores and sort by the sum.
choices.explanation: Raw addition treats different score scales as comparable and can let one retrieval clause dominate the ranking.

choices.text: Choose the larger of each document's two raw scores and discard the smaller score.
choices.explanation: This still compares incompatible score scales and ignores agreement across clauses.

choices.text: Rerank only the top keyword results with a model that scores text similarity.
choices.explanation: Any relevant document retrieved only by the vector clause never reaches the reranker, so this does not fuse both result lists.

choices.text: Configure a score ranker processor that uses reciprocal rank fusion on the hybrid query's clause results.
choices.explanation: It combines reciprocal rank contributions, allowing high positions in several lists to improve a document's combined order.

learning.reason: Reciprocal rank fusion combines contributions based on ranked positions from retrieval clauses, so it does not need the keyword and vector scores to share a scale.
learning.concept: Use rank-based fusion when only relative positions across heterogeneous retrieval clauses should affect the merged ranking.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Honor a monotonic rule while retaining nonlinear predictions
prompt: A SageMaker XGBoost model estimates the risk of a machine breakdown. Engineering requires the predicted risk to stay the same or increase as cumulative run hours increase, with all other input values held constant. The model must still capture nonlinear interactions with other features and may be retrained. Which training change meets the requirement?

choices.text: Set an increasing monotonic constraint on cumulative run hours and leave unrelated features unconstrained.
choices.explanation: The tree learner restricts how predictions can change with that feature while retaining the model's ability to capture nonlinear effects.

choices.text: Sort training records by cumulative run hours before fitting unconstrained trees.
choices.explanation: Row order does not prevent different leaves from assigning lower risk to a higher runtime.

choices.text: Include only high-risk records at higher run-hour values and fit unconstrained trees.
choices.explanation: Changing training samples can bias the data but does not impose an exact monotonic condition at prediction time.

choices.text: Check that global importance for cumulative run hours is high and accept the trained model.
choices.explanation: Importance describes how much a model uses a feature; it does not guarantee the direction of change with other features fixed.

learning.reason: XGBoost supports an increasing monotonic constraint on a selected feature. The same model can still use nonlinear trees and unconstrained behavior for other features.
learning.concept: Encode a per-feature monotonic requirement in training rather than inferring it from average trends.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Resolve entities with auditable exact matching rules
prompt: A feature team wants to unify accounts from two systems. A match must use an approved exact rule, either a shared verified identifier or, for unresolved records, a combination of two normalized identifiers. Reviewers need each resulting match group to record which rule produced it. The team wants a managed matching workflow with no labeled training set. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use the ML-based workflow and allow any pair above a similarity threshold to be matched.
choices.explanation: A learned similarity score does not ensure a match satisfied one of the two approved exact conditions.

choices.text: Use a simple rule-based AWS Entity Resolution workflow with the verified-identifier rule first and the two-field exact rule second.
choices.explanation: The service applies the configured waterfall and records both the resulting match ID and the match rule.

choices.text: Search a vector index and accept the nearest account whenever the top result exceeds a confidence threshold.
choices.explanation: Vector proximity can link records without an exact rule match and does not supply the requested match-rule provenance.

choices.text: Run a simple rule-based workflow with the two-field rule first and use the verified identifier only when a fuzzy match is needed.
choices.explanation: This changes precedence and attempts to use fuzzy matching in a mode restricted to exact matching.

learning.reason: A simple rule-based workflow can apply ordered exact conditions, generate match IDs, and record the match rule. Putting the most specific condition first lets it take precedence.
learning.concept: Choose explicit rule-based identity resolution when deterministic approved matching evidence and provenance are required.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Keep accelerators fed by moving CPU-heavy preprocessing
prompt: A SageMaker GPU training job spends much of its time waiting for CPU-based decompression and augmentation, while GPU memory and compute would be sufficient for the model itself. The training code can distribute work across instance groups. The team needs preprocessing to continue alongside training with a lower cost than adding idle GPU hosts. Which changes are required? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Add more GPU instances of the existing type and replicate the complete preprocessing loop on every GPU worker.
choices.explanation: This pays for more accelerators while maintaining the original CPU work placement.

choices.text: Set the training job to use only CPU instances to make each host specialize in preprocessing.
choices.explanation: That removes the accelerator resources still required for training.

choices.text: Leave the script unchanged and use a model parallelism configuration to split model weights among the CPU preprocessors.
choices.explanation: The model fits the GPU resources already; redistributing its weights does not offload the separate preprocessing bottleneck.

choices.text: Configure the training job with a CPU instance group and a GPU instance group.
choices.explanation: Separate groups let the team add lower-cost CPU capacity independently of accelerator capacity.

choices.text: Use group membership in the training script to run the CPU preprocessing tasks and feed their results to the GPU training workers.
choices.explanation: The entry point otherwise executes on all hosts without assigning the contrasting workloads to their intended groups.

learning.reason: A heterogeneous cluster can provision CPU and GPU instance groups. The entry point must branch by group membership so CPU hosts prepare data and GPU hosts perform accelerator work.
learning.concept: Use separate instance groups and assign distinct execution roles in the training script.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Reduce variance from unstable trees without a second-level model
prompt: Several deep regression trees make highly variable predictions when trained on slightly different samples of the same dataset. Their errors are not completely correlated. The team wants to use these trees as the only model type, train them independently in parallel, and combine numerical predictions without a trained meta-model. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Fit the next tree to the previous ensemble's residuals until training loss stops improving.
choices.explanation: Residual correction is a sequential boosting procedure and does not meet the independent training constraint.

choices.text: Fit a linear meta-model on out-of-fold predictions from the trees and use its output at inference.
choices.explanation: Stacking trains a second-level model, which the team ruled out.

choices.text: Train each tree on an independent bootstrap sample and average the predicted values.
choices.explanation: The resampling creates model diversity. Averaging reduces the effect of individual tree fluctuations.

choices.text: Train every tree on the exact same examples with the same seed and deterministic settings, then average them.
choices.explanation: Identical fitted trees give identical predictions. Averaging them does not reduce variability.

learning.reason: Bagging fits independent estimators on resampled examples and averages their predictions to reduce variance when their errors are not perfectly correlated.
learning.concept: Choose parallel bootstrap aggregation instead of sequential error correction or training a stacking combiner.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Require the model to request a specific current lookup
prompt: A Bedrock Converse application provides several client-side tools. Before answering an order-status request, the assistant must request the order lookup tool on its first turn. The model supports explicit named tool choice, and the application executes tools. Which actions implement the flow? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Include the named order lookup in the tool configuration and set the tool choice to that specific tool for the first turn.
choices.explanation: The supported model is required to request the designated lookup instead of responding directly or choosing a different tool.

choices.text: Validate and execute the returned tool request in the application, then send its result with the matching toolUseId.
choices.explanation: The model asks for a tool. The application supplies the actual data from execution for the final answer.

choices.text: Set tool choice to auto and ask for the order lookup in the system prompt only.
choices.explanation: Automatic mode allows the model to skip tools or select a different tool.

choices.text: Set tool choice to any and leave several tools available without identifying the lookup.
choices.explanation: Any requires a tool request, but does not require the particular named tool.

choices.text: Return the arguments of the tool request to the customer as the order status.
choices.explanation: The arguments describe what to look up. They are not the result of the external lookup.

learning.reason: A named tool choice requires the supported model to request the declared lookup. Client-side tool execution then runs in the application, which sends the tool result back under the same request ID.
learning.concept: Enforce the named tool for the first model turn and complete the application-owned tool result exchange.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Repeat model evaluation on the same external responses
prompt: An ML team will compare evaluator configurations for an externally hosted text model. It has saved the model's responses to a fixed test set and cannot invoke that endpoint from the evaluation environment. Each evaluation must score the exact captured responses so generator sampling does not affect the comparison. Which Bedrock approach fits?

choices.text: Put only the prompts into a new model evaluation and select a similar Bedrock model as the generator.
choices.explanation: Its sampled responses are different inputs and cannot reproduce scoring on the captured external outputs.

choices.text: Use the external responses as the reference answers and configure the judge model as the generator to evaluate.
choices.explanation: That scores newly generated text against the captured responses, reversing which text is being evaluated.

choices.text: Use the evaluation job's overall prior score as the input for both evaluator configurations.
choices.explanation: An aggregate score cannot replace the per-prompt output data needed to compare how the evaluators score each case.

choices.text: Create a versioned evaluation dataset containing the test prompts, recorded responses, and reference answers where needed. Use the option to provide your own inference response data.
choices.explanation: The evaluation job scores the recorded text and can rerun on the same dataset without sampling the external generator.

learning.reason: Providing your own inference responses lets a Bedrock evaluation job evaluate captured prompt-response data without invoking a generator again.
learning.concept: Freeze the generation outputs as evaluation inputs when repeatability and endpoint isolation are required.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Interpret low permutation scores for correlated predictors
prompt: A SageMaker-hosted regression model has strong held-out accuracy. Two different measurements are near copies of one physical quantity. Permuting either column by itself barely affects accuracy. A reviewer concludes the entire signal can be removed. What should the ML engineer do before accepting that conclusion?

choices.text: Apply the same row permutation to both related columns on representative held-out data and compare the score with the unperturbed data.
choices.explanation: Joint permutation breaks the group's association with the targets while retaining the relationship between the two proxies.

choices.text: Approve removing both columns because each individual permutation changes the score only slightly.
choices.explanation: Each test leaves a proxy intact; the two tests cannot establish the effect of removing the whole signal.

choices.text: Use the original training accuracy as evidence that both columns are redundant.
choices.explanation: Training accuracy does not isolate the contribution of the inputs and is less reliable for generalization.

choices.text: Conclude that the two columns have small causal effects because their permutation scores are low.
choices.explanation: Permutation importance describes predictive reliance under a perturbation; it cannot establish causal effects.

learning.reason: When inputs are strongly correlated, a remaining proxy can preserve similar information after one feature is permuted, so small individual scores do not demonstrate that the common signal is irrelevant.
learning.concept: Test whether the model relies on the correlated signal as a group before dropping all of its proxies.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Teach desired answers without training the model to imitate callers
prompt: A team fine-tunes a causal language model in SageMaker using conversational examples, a compatible chat template, and TRL. Each example contains system instructions, user questions, and approved assistant replies. The model should use the instructions and questions as context, but the supervised loss should reward only tokens in the assistant replies. Which training configuration achieves this?

choices.text: Remove all system and user messages before training and train only on the remaining reply text.
choices.explanation: This removes the context needed to learn what an answer should depend on.

choices.text: Use the full conversational dataset and enable assistant-only loss with a template that provides the assistant token mask.
choices.explanation: The model conditions on the instructions and questions while updating against the targeted reply tokens.

choices.text: Use the full conversation and compute token loss equally over all roles.
choices.explanation: This also trains the model to reproduce questions and system messages, contrary to the specified training target.

choices.text: Pair every assistant reply with its user question as a rejected response and run preference optimization.
choices.explanation: A user question is context, not a rejected candidate answer for the same context. This does not implement the desired supervised token masking.

learning.reason: Assistant-only loss keeps the complete conversation available for conditioning and limits supervised token loss to the assistant spans supplied by the compatible template.
learning.concept: Distinguish the tokens the model may attend to from the tokens that should contribute to supervised loss.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Regularize an adaptive optimizer without putting decay into its moments
prompt: A SageMaker PyTorch training job uses Adam and adds an L2 penalty to the objective. The team wants ordinary multiplicative decay on parameters separately from the gradient update, with adaptive moment estimates driven by the task loss. Which change does this?

choices.text: Keep Adam and increase the explicit L2 coefficient.
choices.explanation: The penalty still enters the gradient that Adam uses to update its moment estimates.

choices.text: Use Adam with a smaller beta2 and keep the same L2 penalty in the objective.
choices.explanation: Changing the moment time scale leaves the penalty coupled to the gradient.

choices.text: Use AdamW with the desired weight-decay coefficient and remove the explicit L2 penalty from the task loss.
choices.explanation: The optimizer applies the parameter decay separately; removing the extra penalty avoids feeding another regularization term into the loss gradient.

choices.text: Disable any weight decay and increase the dropout rate.
choices.explanation: Dropout may regularize training, but it does not apply the specified direct parameter decay.

learning.reason: AdamW decouples the weight decay update from the adaptive optimizer's loss-gradient computation, so the decay term is not passed through its moment estimates.
learning.concept: Select decoupled weight decay when the desired shrinkage must remain separate from adaptive gradient moments.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Fix a binary loss after adding a probability layer
prompt: A binary PyTorch classifier in SageMaker started learning poorly after a refactor. The loss remains BCEWithLogitsLoss, but the training script now applies sigmoid to the head output before passing it to the loss. Binary targets are unchanged. The application still needs probabilities at inference. Which correction preserves the stable loss and the inference contract?

choices.text: Keep the sigmoid before BCEWithLogitsLoss and lower the learning rate.
choices.explanation: The input is still treated as a logit by the loss, which applies the equivalent of a second sigmoid.

choices.text: Remove the head sigmoid and treat raw logits as probabilities in production.
choices.explanation: The training objective receives the right values, but logits are unbounded and violate the prediction contract.

choices.text: Round the head sigmoid output to 0 or 1 before computing BCEWithLogitsLoss.
choices.explanation: Rounding blocks useful gradient information and still supplies an inappropriate input to the fused loss.

choices.text: Pass the raw head logits to BCEWithLogitsLoss and apply sigmoid once when serving probabilities.
choices.explanation: This matches the training loss contract and produces valid probabilities for the application.

learning.reason: BCEWithLogitsLoss includes the sigmoid calculation and uses a stable combination with binary cross entropy. It expects raw logits, while the inference application can transform the logits into probabilities once.
learning.concept: Keep logits at the fused training objective and apply the probability transform once at the prediction boundary.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Score forecasts against asymmetric business costs
prompt: A staffing team pays four times as much for one unit of underprediction as for one unit of overprediction. It needs one demand forecast per interval and wants to compare candidates using a loss that penalizes the two error directions in that same ratio. Which evaluation should it use?

choices.text: Compare held-out forecasts by mean pinball loss with alpha set to 0.8.
choices.explanation: For equal-sized absolute errors, the underprediction costs four times as much as the overprediction in this loss.

choices.text: Compare by mean pinball loss with alpha set to 0.2.
choices.explanation: This reverses the asymmetry and penalizes overprediction four times more than underprediction.

choices.text: Compare by mean absolute error and increase the number of overprediction cases in the validation data.
choices.explanation: Mean absolute error weights directions equally for a given evaluation sample, and changing the test mix does not implement the intended per-unit cost.

choices.text: Compare by root mean squared error so every negative residual contributes four times as much.
choices.explanation: Squaring gives equal costs to equal-sized errors of opposite signs.

learning.reason: Pinball loss at alpha 0.8 weights underprediction by 0.8 and overprediction by 0.2, matching the four-to-one ratio and targeting the conditional 80th percentile.
learning.concept: Translate direction-specific absolute error costs into the alpha value of an appropriate quantile loss.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Make human ratings consistent before approving a model
prompt: Two review groups disagree on whether partially correct answers should pass a new assistant's human evaluation. Replacing reviewers is not feasible. The release team can run a small calibration round before the full study and wants a concrete interpretation of disagreement. Which actions help achieve that goal? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Write concrete rating anchors for complete, partially correct, and incorrect answers with examples for the reviewers.
choices.explanation: Shared anchors clarify the ambiguous decision boundary.

choices.text: Assign each pilot item to exactly one reviewer to maximize the number of distinct prompts scored.
choices.explanation: With no overlap, the team cannot measure reviewer agreement on the same answers.

choices.text: Have reviewers independently score overlapping pilot prompts and answers.
choices.explanation: Comparing ratings for the same items reveals which judgments are inconsistent without letting one reviewer influence another's first rating.

choices.text: Share the expected model ranking before the pilot so both review groups know which model should win.
choices.explanation: This may bias judgments and create agreement without resolving the rubric's ambiguity.

choices.text: Review recurring disagreement cases against the written anchors and clarify ambiguous instructions before the full study.
choices.explanation: This connects the agreement evidence to specific changes in how the full evaluation is conducted.

learning.reason: An anchored rubric sets shared expectations, overlap makes agreement observable, and reviewing causes of disagreement gives the team evidence for revising the instructions before scale.
learning.concept: Calibrate human evaluation with explicit rating anchors and independent overlap before using scores for release decisions.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Measure both evidence attachment and citation accuracy
prompt: A retrieval-augmented answer may cite some passages that do not support the sentences they accompany. Other answer sentences that call for a citation are left uncited. The team wants to diagnose these failures separately in an Amazon Bedrock retrieve-and-generate evaluation. Which built-in metrics should it report? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Report citation precision to quantify how often cited passages correctly support the associated response text.
choices.explanation: It addresses the citations the answer provides, including irrelevant citations.

choices.text: Report context relevance alone and interpret it as the correctness of individual citation links.
choices.explanation: Relevant context in the retrieval set does not establish that the response linked a claim to the correct passage.

choices.text: Report citation coverage to quantify how well the response supplies citations where needed.
choices.explanation: It addresses missing citations even when the citations that are present are correct.

choices.text: Report answer completeness alone and infer from a complete answer that all claims are cited.
choices.explanation: Completeness evaluates how well an answer covers the question. It does not ensure that evidence is cited.

choices.text: Report the total number of retrieved chunks as a direct count of correct citations.
choices.explanation: Retrieval volume does not identify which chunks were cited or whether they support any claim.

learning.reason: Citation precision evaluates whether the existing citations are justified. Citation coverage evaluates whether the answer statements that should be cited have citations.
learning.concept: Separate the quality of supplied citations from the presence of citations for claims that need them.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Compare rankings when retrieval evidence has graded value
prompt: A RAG evaluation labels passages 0 for irrelevant, 1 for partially useful, and 3 for decisive evidence. The generator sees only the top five. The team wants to reward moving highly useful evidence earlier while still crediting several useful passages per query. Which retrieval metric best fits?

choices.text: Compute mean reciprocal rank using the first passage with a nonzero label.
choices.explanation: This focuses on one first relevant position and loses information about grades and later useful passages.

choices.text: Compute nDCG@5 with the graded relevance labels.
choices.explanation: The metric rewards more useful results and earlier positions within the exact context window the generator uses.

choices.text: Compute binary recall@5 after mapping all nonzero judgments to relevant.
choices.explanation: Recall credits retrieval of relevant passages, but the ordering inside the top five and their grades are ignored.

choices.text: Compute pooled accuracy of the generator's final answers and report it as a retrieval ranking score.
choices.explanation: End-to-end accuracy also depends on generation behavior and does not measure the order or graded relevance of retrieved passages.

learning.reason: nDCG at a cutoff uses graded gains, discounts later positions, and normalizes by the ideal ranking for each query.
learning.concept: Use a normalized rank metric when both graded relevance and the order of several useful hits matter.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Choose a synchronous endpoint for irregular CPU inference
prompt: A lightweight CPU model must return a result in the same HTTP request. Traffic comes in occasional bursts with hours of inactivity. The team can tolerate cold starts and uses a compatible image and small payloads. It does not need GPUs, private VPC attachment, or dedicated capacity. Which hosting approach best avoids paying for a continuously running instance?

choices.text: Create a SageMaker asynchronous inference endpoint scaled to zero and have the caller read the result from S3.
choices.explanation: This can suit unpredictable traffic but returns results out of band and does not meet the synchronous response contract.

choices.text: Run a scheduled Batch Transform job and return the latest S3 result to each caller.
choices.explanation: Batch output is not the prediction for a new request at call time.

choices.text: Create a SageMaker on-demand serverless inference endpoint without provisioned concurrency.
choices.explanation: It allocates capacity on demand and returns predictions in the invocation response.

choices.text: Keep one dedicated SageMaker real-time inference instance running and add capacity only when a burst begins.
choices.explanation: The idle instance still accrues provisioned compute cost between bursts.

learning.reason: On-demand serverless inference handles sporadic synchronous requests without dedicated always-provisioned compute, if model and feature constraints fit.
learning.concept: Choose serverless hosting when sporadic synchronous CPU requests can tolerate cold-start overhead.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Route to one independent model container on a shared endpoint
prompt: A SageMaker deployment must host two predictors that use incompatible inference frameworks. Each has its own image. Requests should run exactly one chosen predictor and share the same endpoint infrastructure. What should the engineer configure?

choices.text: Deploy the containers as a serial inference pipeline and use the second model only when the client names it.
choices.explanation: A serial pipeline passes output through the containers in order. It does not route to only a requested independent container.

choices.text: Package both model artifacts for one multi-model serving container and select an artifact with TargetModel.
choices.explanation: TargetModel selects artifacts loaded by that serving container. It does not route between the two incompatible images.

choices.text: Provide the two containers as consecutive stages and call them by separate local ports from the client.
choices.explanation: SageMaker exposes the endpoint invocation interface to callers, not the individual containers' local ports.

choices.text: Deploy the two containers in direct-invocation mode and set TargetContainerHostname to the selected container in each request.
choices.explanation: This selects one predictor on the shared endpoint without running the other container.

learning.reason: A direct-invocation multi-container endpoint serves independent containers and lets the requester specify the container by name.
learning.concept: Differentiate selecting one independent container from running a serial pipeline or selecting artifacts inside one shared serving container.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Improve GPU throughput without converting online calls to offline jobs
prompt: An EKS deployment uses Triton to serve a stateless model on GPUs. Many clients send single examples concurrently. Each client must keep its existing synchronous API, and load tests show that adding a brief bounded queue delay stays within the latency objective. The GPU is inefficient with single-example calls. What should the engineer configure?

choices.text: Enable dynamic batching on the stateless model and tune allowed batch sizes and max_queue_delay_microseconds against the end-to-end target.
choices.explanation: Triton can group concurrent inputs and keep the additional batching wait bounded.

choices.text: Require callers to accumulate a full batch before sending a request.
choices.explanation: That changes the existing single-example calling interface and moves waiting to the client.

choices.text: Use the sequence batcher to give unrelated calls a shared sequence identifier.
choices.explanation: Sequence batching is for requests that share model state. The independent predictions should not be represented as one sequence.

choices.text: Collect inputs in S3 and run scheduled batch jobs every hour.
choices.explanation: Scheduled output does not preserve the required synchronous response.

learning.reason: Triton dynamic batching can group independent requests inside the serving process and send their individual results back. A queue-delay bound controls the intentional wait to form a batch.
learning.concept: Batch compatible stateless calls at the server while retaining individual online responses.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Host approved model weights trained outside AWS
prompt: A team trained a supported model on premises and has portable weights and a compatible custom inference container for SageMaker. It must deploy those exact weights behind a managed SageMaker endpoint without retraining or embedding model weights in the image. The team will use the ModelDataUrl artifact option. Which actions complete the packaging and loading path? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Package the inference model files as a tar.gz archive in S3 and reference it with ModelDataUrl.
choices.explanation: The service retrieves the referenced archive for the model deployment.

choices.text: Point ModelDataUrl to an uncompressed local checkpoint on the training computer.
choices.explanation: SageMaker expects the specified archive in S3 and cannot read the training computer's filesystem.

choices.text: Point the container at /opt/ml/output/data for the hosted weights.
choices.explanation: That is a training output location, not the path where this deployment mounts model artifacts.

choices.text: Configure the container to load the extracted model files from /opt/ml/model when it starts.
choices.explanation: This is where SageMaker makes the ModelDataUrl artifacts available for inference.

choices.text: Launch a new managed training job to convert all external weights into endpoint state.
choices.explanation: The approved compatible weights can be transferred directly. Retraining would change the artifact.

learning.reason: SageMaker can fetch a model.tar.gz from S3 for ModelDataUrl and extract it under /opt/ml/model. The inference process loads those artifacts from that directory.
learning.concept: Keep the trained weights in a versioned artifact and load them from the managed model directory at container startup.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Fix an MCP transport mismatch before publishing tools
prompt: An MCP server works locally over standard input and output, but clients must discover and call its tools directly through an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Runtime deployment. The runtime is configured for the MCP protocol with the default port. The team can change the server transport without changing its tool definitions. Which configuration should it deploy?

choices.text: Keep the standard I/O transport and have the remote clients call the container's standard input.
choices.explanation: Remote clients cannot send network requests to the process's standard input through this runtime protocol.

choices.text: Serve MCP using Streamable HTTP on the default runtime port 8000 at /mcp and bind to the container's accessible interface.
choices.explanation: The runtime can route MCP requests to the server that speaks the expected protocol at the expected endpoint.

choices.text: Serve MCP requests only under /invocations on port 8080, leaving the runtime protocol set to MCP.
choices.explanation: That is associated with the default HTTP invocation contract, not the MCP endpoint for this runtime configuration.

choices.text: Expose a health endpoint only and let AgentCore discover tools from the image metadata.
choices.explanation: A health response does not implement MCP discovery or tool execution.

learning.reason: The runtime's MCP protocol uses Streamable HTTP and a serving path under the configured port. A local standard I/O transport does not expose that contract.
learning.concept: Match the deployed server transport and endpoint to the Runtime protocol rather than substituting a local-only transport.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Preview infrastructure replacement before moving a model workload
prompt: A CloudFormation template update changes networking and storage properties for an ML deployment. A reviewer must identify any proposed replacement of a stateful resource before traffic or infrastructure changes. The team will approve and apply the exact reviewed update. Which workflow meets the requirement?

choices.text: Run template validation and deploy if the template is syntactically valid.
choices.explanation: Validation does not compare the proposed update with the specific running stack to identify replacement.

choices.text: Run drift detection against the current template and assume any matching resources can be changed in place.
choices.explanation: Drift detection looks for differences from existing definitions. It does not preview how the new template will be applied.

choices.text: Create an update change set, inspect changes and replacement indicators, and execute the approved change set after review.
choices.explanation: This previews how the proposed template affects the running stack and defers resource changes until execution.

choices.text: Run UpdateStack immediately and use automatic rollback to undo unwanted replacements.
choices.explanation: Rollback occurs after an update begins and does not meet the required pre-change review.

learning.reason: A change set describes proposed changes against the deployed stack, including potential replacements. Its creation and review do not apply those changes.
learning.concept: Use a deployment preview that inspects proposed replacements and executes only the approved change set.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Protect reviewed inference images from accidental tag replacement
prompt: A CI system publishes reviewed inference images to one ECR repository. Release tags must keep pointing to the same image after they are pushed. An integration test stream still needs to move the development tag to each new build. The repository supports tag mutability exclusions, and the team wants the repository to enforce the rule. Which setting meets both requirements?

choices.text: Use fully immutable tags with no exclusions.
choices.explanation: This protects release tags but also prevents the required development tag updates.

choices.text: Keep all tags mutable and run a vulnerability scan for every image push.
choices.explanation: Scanning evaluates image findings. It does not stop a mutable tag from being reassigned.

choices.text: Add a lifecycle rule to expire untagged images quickly and leave tag mutability unchanged.
choices.explanation: A lifecycle rule controls retention after pushes. It does not reject an overwrite of a release tag.

choices.text: Use immutable tags with an exclusion matching only the development tag.
choices.explanation: The repository rejects attempts to overwrite existing release tags and allows the explicitly exempted tag to be updated.

learning.reason: Immutable mode with a narrowly scoped exclusion allows the designated development tag to move while keeping other tags protected from overwrites.
learning.concept: Configure release artifact identity at the registry without preventing the existing development pointer from moving.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Correct endpoint placement after subnet capacity errors
prompt: A SageMaker hosted model must connect to a private feature service from its inference containers. A deployment selected two private subnets in the same Availability Zone, and both are almost out of free IP addresses. The model's security group already permits the necessary private service traffic. Which change addresses the endpoint placement problem?

choices.text: Provide private subnets in different Availability Zones with adequate free addresses in the model's VpcConfig.
choices.explanation: This satisfies the subnet placement requirement and provides address capacity for the service-managed network interfaces.

choices.text: Keep the same pair of subnets and add an interface endpoint for SageMaker Runtime in a third subnet.
choices.explanation: That interface endpoint handles caller-to-runtime connectivity. It does not change the subnet selection or free addresses for the model containers.

choices.text: Keep both subnets in the same Availability Zone and increase only the security group rule quota.
choices.explanation: The group quota does not increase subnet address capacity or add a second Availability Zone.

choices.text: Remove the model's VpcConfig and add a public endpoint for the feature service.
choices.explanation: This changes the required private architecture and does not satisfy the model-container VPC attachment requirement.

learning.reason: SageMaker hosting uses the model's VPC configuration for network interfaces in the selected subnets. Hosted VPC access requires subnets in different Availability Zones with available addresses.
learning.concept: Provide the model containers with workable VPC placement before tuning routing or security rules.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Update a real-time fleet when quota cannot support a full second fleet
prompt: A supported SageMaker endpoint has 20 GPU instances. GPU quota can accommodate a small temporary batch of new instances, but it cannot accommodate an entire green fleet. The rollout must keep serving traffic, observe a bake period at each step, and support rollback on CloudWatch alarms. Which deployment plan fits?

choices.text: Use blue/green canary with one instance receiving the first fraction of traffic.
choices.explanation: The canary controls traffic percentage. The blue/green strategy still prepares the replacement fleet.

choices.text: Use a SageMaker rolling deployment with a batch size that fits the available headroom, a wait period, and rollback alarms.
choices.explanation: Only part of the fleet is replaced at a time, limiting extra capacity while preserving incremental verification.

choices.text: Use blue/green linear shifting with low traffic increments.
choices.explanation: Reducing traffic increments does not remove the need for blue and green capacity at the same time.

choices.text: Delete the current endpoint before creating its replacement with the same name.
choices.explanation: This avoids overlapping capacity but interrupts production traffic and skips the staged guardrails.

learning.reason: SageMaker rolling deployments create and promote parts of the replacement fleet sequentially, freeing old capacity after each successful batch. Deployment alarms can trigger rollback.
learning.concept: Select a guarded rollout with incremental capacity when blue/green would duplicate the fleet.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Deliver a generated report to the next deployment stage
prompt: In CodePipeline, a passing CodeBuild step writes a model evaluation report to dist/reports/model.json, relative to the source root. The project already uses CodePipeline artifacts, but the deployment step cannot find reports/model.json at the root of the unpacked output artifact. The test report itself is correct. What should the team change in the buildspec?

choices.text: Set artifacts.base-directory to dist and include dist/reports/model.json in artifacts.files.
choices.explanation: CodeBuild would look for a second dist segment under the specified base directory.

choices.text: Set artifacts.files to dist/reports/model.json and discard all paths.
choices.explanation: Discarding paths produces a flat model.json entry, which the deployment stage does not expect.

choices.text: Set artifacts.base-directory to dist and include reports/model.json in artifacts.files with paths preserved.
choices.explanation: CodeBuild resolves the file inside dist and packages the nested reports path without the dist prefix.

choices.text: Configure only a CodeBuild reports entry and assume it creates the pipeline's deployment artifact.
choices.explanation: The reporting facility does not package the expected file path for the next stage's input artifact.

learning.reason: When artifacts.base-directory is set, artifact file patterns resolve relative to that directory. The output archive includes the matching children and does not include the base directory itself.
learning.concept: Package the evaluated output at the required relative path using CodeBuild's artifact settings.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Reduce startup latency on repeated managed training jobs
prompt: A team starts several compatible SageMaker training jobs within minutes of one another. The jobs use the same matching resource settings but deliberately fit different models. Repeated infrastructure provisioning dominates the run time. Quota permits keeping compute for a short gap. Which change reuses the provisioned infrastructure without reusing model weights?

choices.text: Set one model's checkpoint path as the next run's input and leave the compute settings unchanged.
choices.explanation: Loading earlier weights would affect model initialization and does not retain training instances.

choices.text: Configure SageMaker Serverless Inference provisioned concurrency with the same instance count.
choices.explanation: Inference concurrency does not reserve a managed cluster for training jobs.

choices.text: Export the completed training image to a different ECR repository after every run.
choices.explanation: Changing image location does not retain compute between training jobs.

choices.text: Specify a suitable KeepAlivePeriodInSeconds and submit each matching follow-up training job before the pool expires.
choices.explanation: SageMaker can reuse the retained infrastructure while the next job fits its own model.

learning.reason: A managed warm pool can retain resources after a job and transfer them to a matching subsequent job started within the keep-alive period. Each job still runs its own training code.
learning.concept: Distinguish reusing an already provisioned training cluster from initializing new jobs with old model weights.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Keep identical questions from revealing another user's documents
prompt: A managed Bedrock knowledge base indexes a supported connector whose documents have different read permissions. One service role queries on behalf of all employees. The application must restrict retrieved evidence to what each signed-in employee can access, even when two employees ask the same question. Which configuration and request behavior should it use? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Enable ACL awareness on the supported data source and ingest the source document permissions.
choices.explanation: Without the ACL metadata, retrieval cannot evaluate the employee's document access.

choices.text: Use the single backend role ARN as the user context for every request.
choices.explanation: This loses the identity differences that determine which documents each employee may read.

choices.text: Retrieve all relevant documents and tell the foundation model not to quote restricted text.
choices.explanation: Instructions do not enforce document authorization and the model would already have obtained restricted passages.

choices.text: Accept a user ID field from the question body without checking it against the session.
choices.explanation: An arbitrary caller-supplied ID does not prove which employee is making the request.

choices.text: Derive the user context from the authenticated session and pass it on each Retrieve request.
choices.explanation: The knowledge base uses the supplied verified identity context to filter results for that employee.

learning.reason: ACL-aware retrieval ingests source permissions and applies them using verified user context supplied on each request. The service role alone does not identify the end user.
learning.concept: Carry authenticated end-user identity to the ACL-aware retrieval stage so restricted passages never enter the model prompt.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Supply GPU capacity for pending model replicas
prompt: An EKS Auto Mode service increases the number of inference replicas under load. Existing GPU nodes are full, new replicas are pending, and general-purpose nodes cannot satisfy the accelerated workload. The team wants to provision GPU capacity when pods require it without keeping a permanently sized GPU fleet. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Define a GPU-capable NodePool and configure the inference pods to request the supported GPU resource and meet its scheduling constraints.
choices.explanation: Pending pods can drive provisioning of compatible GPU nodes rather than adding CPU-only nodes or leaving replicas unscheduled.

choices.text: Increase the maximum replica count and leave the cluster configured with only its existing CPU-oriented provisioning rules.
choices.explanation: The replica count can produce more pending pods without making suitable GPU capacity available.

choices.text: Remove GPU requests from the pod spec so replicas can schedule on general-purpose nodes.
choices.explanation: Those replicas would lack the accelerator that the model runtime requires.

choices.text: Increase the memory limit on all replicas without configuring a GPU-capable node pool.
choices.explanation: More memory capacity does not satisfy a distinct GPU hardware requirement.

learning.reason: EKS Auto Mode or Karpenter can provision nodes from an appropriate GPU-capable NodePool when pending pod resource requests are compatible with that pool.
learning.concept: Make both the workload's accelerator requirement and the provisioner's compatible node capacity explicit.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Resume document indexing without replaying successful batches
prompt: A Standard Step Functions workflow refreshes a retrieval index by running Standard child executions in a Distributed Map. Several child executions failed after a transient service outage. Successful children already indexed their batches, equivalent writes are safe to retry, and the failed execution is eligible for redrive. How should the operator resume using the same inputs while avoiding work already marked successful?

choices.text: Start a new parent workflow execution with the same manifest and the same concurrency value.
choices.explanation: A new execution treats the manifest as new input and can run all batches again.

choices.text: Redrive the failed Map Run from the existing parent workflow execution.
choices.explanation: This resumes unsuccessful child workflow executions and preserves completed batches from the previous attempt.

choices.text: Add a Retry block to the Distributed Map state, then start a new parent run with the complete original manifest.
choices.explanation: Starting over repeats successful work, and Map-level retries can apply to all children.

choices.text: Rerun only the last step of the parent workflow without handling the failed child executions.
choices.explanation: This skips the missing document batches and leaves the index refresh incomplete.

learning.reason: The Distributed Map redrive path reuses the original input and handles unsuccessful child executions without starting successful children over in the ordinary failure case.
learning.concept: Recover failed workflow items using the recorded run state rather than retrying an entire index refresh.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Accept OAuth access tokens only for the intended gateway
prompt: Two internal APIs use the same OpenID Connect issuer. The client of an AgentCore Gateway must present an access token issued for that gateway. Tokens issued for the other API have the same issuer and signing key. The gateway will authenticate requests before invoking any tools. Which configuration distinguishes the tokens?

choices.text: Validate the token signature and issuer, leaving the audience unrestricted.
choices.explanation: Both tokens can be valid under the same issuer and key. Signature validation alone cannot distinguish the intended resource.

choices.text: Validate only that the JWT has not expired and send its token to every outbound target.
choices.explanation: An unexpired token can be intended for another resource. Outbound target authentication does not protect the gateway entry point.

choices.text: Configure inbound JWT authorization with the issuer's discovery URL and require the gateway's resource identifier as an allowed audience.
choices.explanation: A token for another API fails the audience check even if it was signed by the same trusted issuer.

choices.text: Set the other API's identifier as the only allowed audience and identify gateway callers by user agent.
choices.explanation: That would trust the wrong resource audience. User-agent headers do not prove token intent.

learning.reason: A custom inbound JWT authorizer uses the issuer's discovery and keys and can enforce the token's intended resource through the allowed audience list.
learning.concept: Check the resource audience in addition to issuer and signature when the issuer serves multiple APIs.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Resume the intended delegated task after a clarification
prompt: A controller calls an A2A specialist hosted on AgentCore Runtime. The specialist starts two separate tasks in the same conversation context. One task pauses with INPUT_REQUIRED and requests a delivery option. The controller gets the user's answer and must send it to the correct pending task, keeping the other task independent. What should it do?

choices.text: Send the answer using only the shared conversation context and assume it uniquely identifies the waiting task.
choices.explanation: Both tasks have the same context, so the context does not say which task should consume the answer.

choices.text: Create a fresh task with the entire prior conversation and ignore the existing task IDs.
choices.explanation: A fresh task does not resume the original pending task and can duplicate work.

choices.text: Cancel both tasks and return the clarification as the original specialist's output.
choices.explanation: Cancelling interrupts the tasks. The user-supplied clarification is an input, not the finished output.

choices.text: Send the answer as a follow-up message associated with the interrupted task's task ID, using the matching context if one is supplied.
choices.explanation: The task reference connects the answer to the intended pending work. The shared context alone would not select between two tasks.

learning.reason: An A2A client message can identify the task it continues. The context groups related activity, while the task identifier disambiguates which interrupted task should receive input.
learning.concept: Use the protocol task identity to continue the specific interrupted operation within a broader context.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Wait for an existing external dataset acceptance check
prompt: A SageMaker retraining pipeline must wait for an external batch quality service to accept a labeled dataset. The check can take an hour and already pulls work from SQS. The pipeline must resume the correct waiting execution only after that work reports success or failure. Which actions implement this integration? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Define a Callback step in the pipeline and target the queue consumed by the quality service.
choices.explanation: The step sends its arguments and token while waiting for an external result.

choices.text: Mark the pipeline step successful as soon as SQS acknowledges message receipt.
choices.explanation: Queue acceptance means the work was enqueued. It does not prove the dataset passed inspection.

choices.text: Start a second pipeline execution on completion and let the waiting execution expire.
choices.explanation: This does not resume the waiting execution and can duplicate downstream work.

choices.text: Keep the callback token from the queue message associated with the corresponding quality check.
choices.explanation: The token correlates the eventual result with the specific waiting pipeline step.

choices.text: When the check finishes, call the pipeline step success or failure callback with the original token.
choices.explanation: The result resolves the correct waiting step and its downstream path.

learning.reason: A Callback step sends a pipeline-generated token in an SQS message, and external processing must preserve that token to signal success or failure to the waiting pipeline step.
learning.concept: Retain the callback token across the external integration and finish the exact waiting step based on its real outcome.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Send multiple complete records per offline inference request
prompt: An offline SageMaker Batch Transform job processes large CSV files with one record per line. The container supports multiple complete line records per inference request but rejects inputs over a fixed payload size. Sending one record per call wastes time. Which settings should the engineer use?

choices.text: Set SplitType to Line, BatchStrategy to MultiRecord, and MaxPayloadInMB within the container's supported limit.
choices.explanation: SageMaker can send several whole records per invocation, up to the configured payload cap.

choices.text: Use SplitType Line and SingleRecord with a larger payload cap.
choices.explanation: Increasing the cap does not change the one-record-per-request batching policy.

choices.text: Set SplitType to None and assume that MultiRecord will split the CSV on line boundaries.
choices.explanation: Without line splitting the service does not use the lines as individual units for these mini-batches.

choices.text: Raise MaxConcurrentTransforms and remove the request size limit assumptions from the container.
choices.explanation: Parallelism changes the number of calls in flight. It does not make oversized payloads valid or group line records.

learning.reason: Line splitting identifies complete records, MultiRecord lets SageMaker group them, and MaxPayloadInMB limits the resulting payload size.
learning.concept: Choose per-request grouping without losing input record boundaries or exceeding the model's request limit.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Interpret capacity decisions with two target tracking signals
prompt: A SageMaker production variant uses Application Auto Scaling with target tracking on two different valid utilization metrics: per-instance traffic and a custom per-instance worker-occupancy metric. Both policies allow scale-in and have complete data. At a peak, traffic indicates scale-out but occupancy does not. Later, traffic alone indicates scale-in. What behavior should the team expect, assuming capacity limits and cooldowns do not prevent scaling?

choices.text: The variant waits for both policies before either adding or removing capacity.
choices.explanation: Requiring agreement for scale-out is stricter than the documented behavior.

choices.text: The variant can scale out at the peak but will wait to scale in until both policies are ready.
choices.explanation: One policy can justify additional capacity, while both scale-in-enabled policies must agree capacity can be removed.

choices.text: The variant can scale out and scale in whenever either policy is ready.
choices.explanation: Scale-in requires agreement from the scale-in-enabled policies, not just one signal.

choices.text: The last policy created overrides the earlier policy for both events.
choices.explanation: Independent target tracking policies are evaluated together rather than ordered by creation time.

learning.reason: Application Auto Scaling favors availability when combining target tracking policies. One ready policy can trigger an increase, and decreasing capacity requires agreement from all policies that enable scale-in.
learning.concept: Apply the different arbitration rules for adding and removing capacity when target tracking signals disagree.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Verify a new on-demand model deployment before sending live traffic
prompt: A scripted rollout creates a new on-demand deployment for an approved Bedrock fine-tuned model. It must preserve the existing production path until the new deployment is ready and has passed a smoke test. The create call returned a deployment ARN. Which actions should the rollout take next? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Update production routing as soon as CreateCustomModelDeployment returns an ARN.
choices.explanation: Allocation can still be in progress, so real requests can fail before readiness.

choices.text: Poll deployment status and continue to validation only once it is Active.
choices.explanation: The create response confirms the deployment was requested, while Active indicates it is available for inference.

choices.text: Invoke the new deployment ARN with a controlled test case, then change the production target only after the check passes.
choices.explanation: A smoke invocation validates the exact deployment before live traffic moves to it.

choices.text: Run the smoke test against the base foundation model and infer the fine-tuned variant is ready.
choices.explanation: That exercises a different target and cannot establish deployment readiness or fine-tuned behavior.

choices.text: Delete the existing production deployment before polling the new one.
choices.explanation: This removes the healthy serving path while the replacement is still uncertain.

learning.reason: Creating a deployment returns its identity before it is necessarily ready. A rollout can poll for Active, invoke the deployment ARN for validation, and switch only on success.
learning.concept: Gate production changes on both the deployment lifecycle and a real invocation of that deployment.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Avoid changing a tail-latency alarm on too little traffic
prompt: An ML endpoint's p99 latency alarm becomes noisy overnight when a period contains only a handful of requests. Operations wants to keep the p99 objective and the alarm's current state during statistically insufficient periods. The alarm must evaluate p99 once enough data arrives. Which change fits?

choices.text: Set missing data to not breaching without changing the percentile low-sample behavior.
choices.explanation: A period can contain some points and still be statistically insufficient. The missing-data setting does not address that case.

choices.text: Change from p99 to average latency and keep the same threshold.
choices.explanation: The alarm would no longer represent the tail-latency objective.

choices.text: Set the percentile alarm to ignore periods with low sample counts.
choices.explanation: CloudWatch keeps the alarm's state when the sample count is insufficient and evaluates the percentile in adequately sampled periods.

choices.text: Record no metrics outside business hours and reset the alarm to OK every night.
choices.explanation: This discards usable overnight measurements and does not preserve the existing state.

learning.reason: The low-sample policy can preserve a percentile alarm's state until enough observations exist to evaluate the percentile.
learning.concept: Use the percentile-specific sparse-sample behavior while retaining the original service objective.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Escalate only when two separate inference symptoms coincide
prompt: Two CloudWatch metric alarms monitor end-to-end inference failures and tail latency. The operators need both underlying alarm states for diagnosis, but they should page only when both alarms are in ALARM at the same time. Which configuration meets the requirement?

choices.text: Attach the same paging action to both underlying alarms and leave them independent.
choices.explanation: Either alarm can page before the second one enters ALARM.

choices.text: Create a composite alarm with an OR expression over the two ALARM states.
choices.explanation: An OR expression triggers as soon as either alarm enters ALARM.

choices.text: Replace both alarms with a single alarm on average endpoint latency.
choices.explanation: This loses the failures alarm and does not represent the desired combination.

choices.text: Create a composite alarm with an AND expression over the two ALARM states and attach the paging action only to the composite.
choices.explanation: Each underlying alarm remains visible, and the paging action is controlled by their simultaneous state.

learning.reason: A composite alarm can evaluate the states of existing alarms with a Boolean expression and serve as the sole source of the paging action.
learning.concept: Use a composite state rule to control escalation while retaining lower-level alarm signals.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Correlate a caller operation with an AgentCore execution trace
prompt: A service and its AgentCore runtime are both instrumented. The operations team observes spans from the service and the agent in X-Ray, but each call appears as two unrelated traces. The team must see caller and agent operations in one distributed trace without logging request bodies. What should it do?

choices.text: Propagate the caller's current X-Ray context in the X-Amzn-Trace-Id header on the AgentCore request.
choices.explanation: The downstream trace can retain the existing trace identity and causal relationship to the caller.

choices.text: Generate a new unrelated trace ID at the start of every AgentCore invocation.
choices.explanation: A new root records another trace, leaving the caller and agent operations separated.

choices.text: Reuse the same AgentCore session identifier as the trace ID of every request in a long conversation.
choices.explanation: A session groups requests across turns; it does not supply each call's distributed parent trace context.

choices.text: Log the same question text on both sides and match events using string equality.
choices.explanation: Repeated questions are ambiguous, and logging prompt contents violates the observability requirement.

learning.reason: With observability enabled, supplying the caller's active X-Ray trace context on the AgentCore request connects the runtime operation to the existing distributed trace.
learning.concept: Propagate distributed trace context across the invocation boundary instead of creating a new root at each service.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Improve multi-model latency when the model working set cannot stay resident
prompt: A CPU-backed SageMaker multi-model endpoint alternates between a stable set of popular models. Memory usage is high, ModelCacheHit has fallen, and model loading waits account for the latency increase. CPU and actual model execution time remain within their previous ranges. The complete popular set would fit in a tested larger-memory instance. What should the engineer try first?

choices.text: Use a higher-CPU instance with unchanged memory and assume the additional CPU will keep the whole working set cached.
choices.explanation: More compute does not provide more space to keep the model files resident.

choices.text: Benchmark an instance type with enough memory for the hot model set and confirm recovery of cache hits and latency.
choices.explanation: Larger resident capacity can avoid repeatedly loading popular models. The benchmark confirms the improvement under real traffic.

choices.text: Disable model caching and load artifacts from storage for every invocation.
choices.explanation: A stable, frequently reused working set is exactly where caching avoids repeat loading.

choices.text: Increase request timeouts and leave the cache working-set capacity unchanged.
choices.explanation: A longer timeout can hide failures but does not remove the load wait or restore latency.

learning.reason: When model-cache churn comes from insufficient memory, an instance with more memory can hold more hot models and reduce loading delays.
learning.concept: Size serving memory for cache residency when latency is dominated by loading instead of execution.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Diagnose request-limit failures separately from service capacity
prompt: An Amazon Bedrock application records two intermittent error groups: ThrottlingException during spikes from its own high-volume workload and ServiceUnavailableException even when its traffic is below the configured limits. The team wants the correct diagnosis before changing capacity settings. How should it interpret the errors?

choices.text: Treat both errors as proof the account exhausted its token quota and request the same increase for each.
choices.explanation: Service unavailability can occur below the caller's quota.

choices.text: Treat both errors as model input validation failures and shorten every prompt before retrying.
choices.explanation: Neither error code establishes that a request has invalid content.

choices.text: Check quota and rate usage for ThrottlingException, and investigate temporary service availability for ServiceUnavailableException.
choices.explanation: The two types point to different constraints. A quota change may help the first after verification and does not by itself resolve the second.

choices.text: Treat the numeric HTTP status alone as sufficient and ignore the service-specific error returned by the SDK.
choices.explanation: In particular, HTTP 429 can represent other errors on some operations. The service-specific exception helps distinguish cases.

learning.reason: ThrottlingException concerns a quota or request rate limit, while ServiceUnavailableException can result from temporary service capacity or high demand independent of the caller's measured quota.
learning.concept: Inspect the API error code and workload rate before deciding whether an account quota action addresses the observed failures.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Continuously evaluate a sample of live agent sessions
prompt: An AgentCore team already uses one-off evaluations on saved examples before release. It now needs ongoing quality scores from production interactions within a fixed evaluation budget. Observability is enabled, and the team can evaluate a fraction of live sessions with selected evaluators. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Increase the number of prompts in the same offline test set and rerun it after each deployment.
choices.explanation: This tests a larger fixed dataset but does not sample actual production behavior continuously.

choices.text: Measure invocation count and infer quality from higher overall usage.
choices.explanation: Volume is not a quality score and does not evaluate whether the agent fulfilled tasks.

choices.text: Make a model-as-judge call synchronously for every user request before returning the response.
choices.explanation: This evaluates all calls and imposes additional work and latency despite the goal of sampled monitoring.

choices.text: Create an online evaluation for the production agent's supported trace source with an explicit sampling rate and selected evaluators.
choices.explanation: The evaluation runs on sampled live interactions, providing ongoing quality signals while bounding evaluation volume.

learning.reason: An online evaluation configuration samples production sessions from a supported source and runs the chosen evaluators, so quality is measured continuously without scoring every interaction.
learning.concept: Configure continuous sampled assessment of actual agent behavior in production rather than reusing the fixed pre-release dataset.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Attribute shared GPU fleet costs to model teams
prompt: Several teams deploy models into separate namespaces on one EKS cluster. Their pods share accelerated EC2 capacity. Finance needs a billing export that can allocate the underlying accelerator, CPU, and memory costs per pod and then aggregate by namespace. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Enable split cost allocation data for the EKS billing export and aggregate accelerator, CPU, and memory cost records by namespace.
choices.explanation: The additional records expose the per-pod cost contributions behind shared instances.

choices.text: Tag each EC2 node with the team of the first pod scheduled there and assign all node charges to that tag.
choices.explanation: A node can serve several teams, so this cannot allocate its charges among the pods.

choices.text: Divide the cluster's monthly bill evenly across all pods.
choices.explanation: This ignores how different pods consume CPU, memory, and accelerators.

choices.text: Track only GPU kernel utilization in application logs and report its percentage as the billed cost.
choices.explanation: Utilization alone is not a billing export and leaves other resource costs unallocated.

learning.reason: AWS split cost allocation data adds pod-level records for the consumed compute resources, including accelerators on supported EKS configurations, that can be aggregated by Kubernetes metadata.
learning.concept: Use resource-level cost allocation for shared accelerated nodes instead of assigning the entire instance bill to one tag.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Restrict a shared artifact key to one tenant's encrypted manifests
prompt: An application encrypts small artifact manifests directly with the same symmetric AWS KMS key for several tenants. Each encryption includes a nonsecret Tenant context value. Tenant A's role must decrypt only ciphertext bound to Tenant=A, even if it accidentally receives another tenant's ciphertext blob. What should the key authorization require?

choices.text: Grant unrestricted kms:Decrypt on the shared key and rely on the tenant value in the application's log message.
choices.explanation: Logging the tenant neither restricts the permission nor cryptographically binds the request to its allowed context.
