choices.text: Limit the role's kms:Decrypt permission to requests with kms:EncryptionContext:Tenant equal to A and require matching context in the decrypt request.
choices.explanation: Another tenant's ciphertext cannot be decrypted with A's context, and a request for that other context is outside the role's permission.

choices.text: Tag the shared KMS key with Tenant=A while still using it for every tenant and grant decrypt based on the key tag.
choices.explanation: The common key tag is the same for all ciphertexts under that key. It cannot distinguish which tenant was bound to a particular artifact.

choices.text: Let the role supply a replacement context when decrypting any ciphertext obtained from another tenant.
choices.explanation: The caller cannot select a new context for ciphertext already authenticated with a different context at encryption.

learning.reason: The policy can allow Decrypt for the role only with its assigned encryption context. KMS also authenticates the context against the ciphertext, so changing a supplied value cannot make another tenant's blob decryptable.
learning.concept: Bind use of a common key to the artifact's authenticated nonsecret context for least privilege.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Verify that the audit record has not changed since delivery
prompt: A team keeps CloudTrail records for ML deployment changes in an audit bucket. It needs to show that the logs for a future release window were not modified or removed after delivery. CloudTrail integrity validation is currently disabled. Which actions establish and check the integrity evidence? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Enable S3 default encryption on the bucket and treat successful decryption as the audit result.
choices.explanation: At-rest encryption does not prove these are the original CloudTrail logs or that all files are present.

choices.text: Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation on the trail before the release window.
choices.explanation: CloudTrail supplies signed digest files containing hashes for delivered logs.

choices.text: Rely on enabling digest delivery to produce a completed validation report automatically.
choices.explanation: Delivering digests and validating them are separate operations.

choices.text: Run CloudTrail log validation over the relevant time range and retain the results with the audit.
choices.explanation: Validation verifies the digest chain and checks referenced log files against the delivered hashes.

choices.text: Enable S3 versioning and compare the latest log object timestamps alone.
choices.explanation: Versioning can retain revisions, but timestamps do not verify the delivered bytes or identify all missing logs.

learning.reason: Enabling integrity validation creates signed digest records for subsequent delivery. An auditor must run validation over those digests and the referenced logs to check integrity.
learning.concept: Generate integrity evidence when logs are delivered, then actually verify the evidence for the release window.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep unscanned objects out of a feature pipeline
prompt: External partners upload archives of training inputs to S3. The processing role may read only objects that complete a malware scan with a clean result. Uploaders must not be able to set the scan-result tag themselves, and failures or unsupported objects must stay blocked. Which changes enforce this workflow? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Start processing at ObjectCreated and remove the intermediate outputs later if a scan detects a threat.
choices.explanation: This allows the processing role to consume data before the required clean scan.

choices.text: Enable GuardDuty Malware Protection for the ingress bucket or prefix with scan-result tagging enabled.
choices.explanation: A completed scan can provide the documented result tag for the object.

choices.text: Deny only when the tag equals THREATS_FOUND and allow any object with no tag.
choices.explanation: Pending, failed, or unsupported scans can lack a clean result, so this policy fails open.

choices.text: Let uploaders attach the clean result tag as part of their upload, to avoid scanning delays.
choices.explanation: The tag would no longer be trustworthy evidence that the scan completed.

choices.text: Gate processing reads on a NO_THREATS_FOUND scan-result tag and reserve control of that tag for the trusted scan workflow.
choices.explanation: Objects without a clean result stay blocked, and an uploader cannot mark its own object clean.

learning.reason: Malware Protection for S3 can tag scan outcomes. A deny-by-default gate can allow processing only after the authorized scanner sets the clean status, with tag modification restricted.
learning.concept: Use a service-generated scan result as an authorization gate and preserve its integrity.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Use a rotated third-party credential without redeploying a worker
prompt: A Lambda inference worker calls an approved external model API that requires a vendor-issued credential. The credential is rotated through AWS Secrets Manager. The worker uses warm containers and should pick up the current value within the supported rotation interval without requiring a deployment each time. Which design fits?

choices.text: Set the vendor credential value directly in an environment variable and update Secrets Manager only.
choices.explanation: Rotating the secret does not rewrite a deployment environment variable that contains the old value.

choices.text: Retrieve the secret once at process initialization and keep that value for the entire life of the warm container.
choices.explanation: A warm container can outlive the rotation interval and continue using the retired credential.

choices.text: Store the secret identifier in the worker settings, restrict the role to that secret, and read AWSCURRENT through a cache with a suitable expiration interval.
choices.explanation: The secret identifier stays stable, while the worker refreshes the actual version as Secrets Manager rotates it.

choices.text: Use the AWS role's session token as the bearer credential on the vendor's API.
choices.explanation: An AWS session token is not the credential issued for that external API.

learning.reason: The worker can use its execution role to read the secret's current version. A bounded cache lifetime aligned to the rotation requirement avoids keeping the old value for the lifetime of a warm environment.
learning.concept: Resolve the third-party credential at runtime and control its cache behavior across rotation.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Evaluate an answer against approved evidence before showing it
prompt: An application generates short factual answers from retrieved manuals. Before displaying a candidate answer, it must assess whether the answer is supported by those passages and relevant to the user's question. It will use a configured contextual grounding check through ApplyGuardrail. Which inputs should it send with their respective roles? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Supply the assistant's unsupported explanation as the grounding source instead of the retrieved manual passages.
choices.explanation: Assessing an answer using its own unsupported output would not test grounding against the approved evidence.

choices.text: Supply the retrieved manual passages as the grounding source.
choices.explanation: The check can compare claims in the answer with the approved supporting text.

choices.text: Supply the original user question as the query.
choices.explanation: The query provides the relevance criterion for the candidate answer.

choices.text: Supply the generated candidate answer as the content to guard.
choices.explanation: The candidate is the text evaluated for support and question relevance before it is shown.

choices.text: Supply a list of denied words as the query instead of the user's question.
choices.explanation: A denied word list does not express what the user asked and cannot serve as the relevance target.

learning.reason: Contextual grounding evaluates guard content for support against a grounding source and relevance to a query. These three roles make the intended check explicit.
learning.concept: Keep evidence, user question, and generated answer separately identified for a contextual grounding evaluation.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Reduce an ML maintenance role's permissions with evidence
prompt: A maintenance role for a training platform has a broad IAM policy. Engineers have CloudTrail management-event history for a representative period, but a rare disaster-recovery action might not appear in the logs. They want a starting policy grounded in observed use without silently losing required permissions. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Install the generated policy unchanged and assume it covers every required action.
choices.explanation: Logs cover a period and feature scope, so required but unobserved actions can be absent.

choices.text: Use an external access analyzer's lack of findings as proof all permissions on the role are needed.
choices.explanation: External access findings concern resource sharing outside a zone of trust. They do not tell which identity actions this role needs.

choices.text: Keep every broad action and add a session tag describing the maintenance job.
choices.explanation: A tag by itself does not reduce permitted actions or resources without authorization conditions.

choices.text: Generate a candidate policy with IAM Access Analyzer from the role's CloudTrail activity, then review and test necessary actions including the recovery procedure.
choices.explanation: The template provides evidence of use, while review and tests preserve legitimate operations that were not observed.

learning.reason: Access Analyzer can produce a policy template from recorded role activity. The team must review action and resource scope, supported service details, and required operations absent from the chosen history.
learning.concept: Use observed activity to propose least privilege and validate duties that may be missing from the observation window.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep an internal model dependency from resolving to a public package
prompt: A model build restores approved private and public packages through a CodeArtifact repository. One internal package must accept new releases from the company's publisher only. Its name must never resolve to a version ingested from upstream, but unrelated public packages should remain available through the same repository. What should the team configure?

choices.text: Keep Publish allowed and set Upstream to Block for the internal package, with publishing granted only to the approved role.
choices.explanation: The registry accepts authorized internal releases and refuses upstream versions of that package.

choices.text: Set the internal package to allow upstream ingress and forbid direct publishing.
choices.explanation: This would block the approved publishing path and retain the unapproved source path.

choices.text: Remove every upstream and external connection from the repository.
choices.explanation: This prevents upstream resolution but also removes the unrelated public dependencies the build requires.

choices.text: Keep origin controls unchanged and scan the final inference image for vulnerabilities.
choices.explanation: Scanning may detect known vulnerabilities later. It does not enforce the dependency's required provenance during restore.

learning.reason: CodeArtifact package origin controls can continue to allow direct publishing while blocking ingestion from upstream for the selected private package.
learning.concept: Apply origin restrictions to the internal package without removing upstream access for independent dependencies.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Investigate unequal experiment exposure before interpreting uplift
prompt: An A/B experiment is configured to assign eligible users 50/50 to two model variants for each release. At a planned review with many users, 64% of unique recorded exposures are to one variant. The imbalance is larger than the prespecified tolerance. A headline conversion metric favors the smaller group. What should the team do first?

choices.text: Promote the variant with the higher conversion rate because its smaller group makes the gain conservative.
choices.explanation: The imbalance can result from selective loss of exposures and does not tell which direction a rate is biased.

choices.text: Pause the decision and compare eligible assignments, actual exposures, and missing logs by variant and segment.
choices.explanation: This checks where the ratio diverged instead of assuming both recorded groups represent the experiment as designed.

choices.text: Drop exposures randomly from the larger group until both recorded groups have the same size.
choices.explanation: Equalizing the reported counts does not correct selective inclusion or a broken assignment mechanism.

choices.text: Replace the conclusion metric with raw conversions and apply the originally expected ratio to the totals.
choices.explanation: Expected proportions cannot repair records that were assigned, served, or measured differently.

learning.reason: An unexpected exposure ratio can signal assignment, eligibility, or delivery and telemetry problems. Outcome interpretation should wait while the team tests which users reached assignment and exposure logging.
learning.concept: Investigate sample ratio mismatch before interpreting a potentially biased treatment effect.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Enforce an exact paid-request allowance per tenant
prompt: A managed model proxy uses an API Gateway REST API. Each accepted model invocation has the same charge to a tenant's plan. The team must prevent any caller from initiating model invocations above a fixed monthly allowance, including when requests arrive concurrently. Usage plans already provide ordinary traffic shaping. What should the team add?

choices.text: Set the API Gateway usage-plan quota to the allowance and assume it prevents all excess requests.
choices.explanation: Usage plans apply quotas on a best-effort basis and can allow requests above the target.

choices.text: Check a local in-memory counter in each backend worker and reset it at the start of the month.
choices.explanation: Parallel workers can keep different counts and can admit excess requests when scaling.

choices.text: Atomically check and consume one allowance in shared tenant state before starting the paid invocation, rejecting new requests when none remains.
choices.explanation: Concurrent requests cannot independently admit using the same remaining allowance.

choices.text: Count invocation metrics at the end of the day and block tenants on the next day if they were over.
choices.explanation: The paid requests would already have been initiated before the enforcement occurs.

learning.reason: API Gateway usage-plan quotas are best-effort. Exact admission can be implemented in the controlled backend by atomically checking and consuming one remaining invocation before calling the model.
learning.concept: Use an authoritative per-tenant admission counter when usage-plan throttling alone cannot guarantee a hard allowance.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Publish auditable intended-use limits for a released model
prompt: An approval board reviews a deployed model version every quarter. It needs a single governed record of intended use, excluded scenarios, risk level, validation evidence, and metrics that relate to that model version. Endpoint health graphs and the package approval state already exist. Which artifact should the team maintain?

choices.text: Use the endpoint's CloudWatch dashboard as the only record.
choices.explanation: Health and performance telemetry do not describe the approved application scope or validation rationale.

choices.text: Keep the model package's Approved status as the only evidence for the quarterly review.
choices.explanation: The status indicates a decision. It does not by itself explain intended use, the assessed risks, or the supporting tests.

choices.text: Write allowed use cases only into the endpoint name and retrieve data from server logs when requested.
choices.explanation: A name cannot store structured decision context and the supporting evaluation evidence.

choices.text: Maintain a SageMaker Model Card linked to the reviewed model version and update it with the approved context and evaluation evidence.
choices.explanation: It puts the intended use and associated evidence into one auditable model record.

learning.reason: A SageMaker Model Card can record model details, intended use and risk, background, and evaluation results. It supplies governance context beyond runtime health metrics or approval state.
learning.concept: Maintain evidence that connects a released model to its allowed use and the validation behind its risk decision.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Protect a private model from too many simultaneous invocations
prompt: A Lambda model router makes one blocking request to a private model service for each function execution. The model service supports at most 20 concurrent calls from this router. Traffic bursts may be throttled, and no other code path uses the router function. Which Lambda setting caps concurrently running router invocations?

choices.text: Set the router's reserved concurrency to 20.
choices.explanation: This is a maximum for concurrent executions of the function, as well as a reservation from the account pool.

choices.text: Set its provisioned concurrency to 20 and leave reserved concurrency unset.
choices.explanation: Provisioned concurrency preinitializes capacity, but the function can scale beyond it using available concurrency.

choices.text: Allocate twice as much memory per router invocation.
choices.explanation: Memory can change execution performance but does not define how many invocations Lambda may run concurrently.

choices.text: Set the function timeout lower and leave its concurrency unbounded.
choices.explanation: A shorter timeout limits how long a call may run, not the count of calls that may run at the same time.

learning.reason: Function-level reserved concurrency caps simultaneous executions, so a one-in-flight-request-per-execution router cannot exceed the downstream limit through this function.
learning.concept: Apply a function concurrency ceiling to protect downstream concurrent capacity.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Keep task continuity without replaying an entire growing transcript
prompt: An AgentCore application repeats all prior turns for every request. Analysis shows that input tokens per turn grow with session length, although the user needs only the current objective, earlier decisions, and recent context. Exact older wording can be fetched on demand and need not be included every time. Which change targets the main cost driver?

choices.text: Lower the response token limit and continue sending the complete transcript.
choices.explanation: This may reduce output tokens, but it leaves the measured growth in input tokens unchanged.

choices.text: Maintain the session summary, include it with relevant recent turns, and fetch particular older details when the task needs them.
choices.explanation: The model receives continuity information without processing every old turn again on each request.

choices.text: Fetch and append all long-term memory for every actor on every turn.
choices.explanation: This increases unrelated input and loses the intended session-level scope.

choices.text: Keep only the most recent question and discard all previous decisions and task state.
choices.explanation: This reduces input size at the expense of the continuity the user still requires.

learning.reason: A rolling session summary can carry condensed context. Supplying the summary plus relevant recent turns bounds routine model inputs while allowing older exact information to be retrieved when needed.
learning.concept: Decouple retained conversation history from the portion routinely submitted to the model.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Make repeated exact-key log investigations scan less data
prompt: An operations team investigates inference incidents by querying new structured JSON records in Standard-class CloudWatch log groups. Each query looks up one exact value of a custom predictionRunKey field across many records. The dashboard should preserve direct key lookup while reducing the scanned volume. Which change meets the requirement?

choices.text: Create the same field index but keep looking up each value with a regular expression using filter like.
choices.explanation: The regular-expression matching form does not use the field index to skip scan candidates.

choices.text: Create one custom CloudWatch metric dimension for every predictionRunKey.
choices.explanation: Metrics can count events by key but do not retrieve the matching log records. High-cardinality dimensions can also generate many time series.

choices.text: Create a field index on predictionRunKey and query the exact value with an equality filter in Logs Insights.
choices.explanation: An equality condition on the indexed field can reduce scan volume for matching records ingested under the index.

choices.text: Add the key to the JSON records without a field index and assume automatic discovery guarantees scan pruning.
choices.explanation: Discovery makes the key queryable. It is separate from building an index for efficient exact checks.

learning.reason: Field indexes can accelerate Logs Insights equality and IN conditions by letting the query skip records that cannot match an indexed field.
learning.concept: Select a field index and an index-eligible predicate for repeated exact high-cardinality lookups.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Build near-real-time warehouse features directly from a stream
prompt: A feature team needs to query Kinesis Data Streams records and join them with reference tables already in Amazon Redshift. The current hourly S3 export does not meet its freshness target. It wants a refreshable SQL relation and does not want to maintain a separate stream consumer. Which approach should it use?

choices.text: Create a normal materialized view on the existing hourly S3 export and increase its SQL refresh frequency.
choices.explanation: The view still can see only the files already delivered on the hourly schedule.

choices.text: Increase the retention of the Kinesis stream and keep the warehouse ingest schedule unchanged.
choices.explanation: Longer retention increases the replay window but does not shorten the path into Redshift.

choices.text: Run more Athena queries over the current export and load their results into Redshift hourly.
choices.explanation: This adds query work while retaining the freshness bottleneck at the export step.

choices.text: Create a Redshift external schema for the stream and a streaming materialized view with automatic refresh enabled.
choices.explanation: The view consumes the stream on refresh and provides a relation the warehouse feature queries can join.

learning.reason: Redshift streaming ingestion can read a Kinesis stream directly into a refreshable materialized view. SQL consumers can use the resulting view without first materializing an S3 copy.
learning.concept: Choose a warehouse-native incremental stream reader when the data must be queryable with SQL without file staging.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Retain model-training events without keeping all history on broker disks
prompt: An Amazon MSK topic on supported Standard brokers carries telemetry for features. Online consumers usually read the recent tail, but periodic retraining must replay up to 90 days of events through Kafka. Broker disks should retain only the most recent seven days of closed segments. The team cannot introduce a second retrieval interface. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: Enable tiered storage for the topic, set total retention to 90 days, and set local retention to seven days.
choices.explanation: Consumers still use Kafka for old segments, while primary storage keeps only the configured recent local range.

choices.text: Set the topic's overall retention to seven days and increase broker disk size.
choices.explanation: Capacity does not override the retention rule that removes history older than its allowed age.

choices.text: Export 90 days of records into S3 Glacier Deep Archive and remove them from the Kafka topic.
choices.explanation: The files require a separate restore and consumption flow, so Kafka clients cannot replay them as required.

choices.text: Increase the partition count but leave all 90 days in local storage.
choices.explanation: More partitions distribute traffic and data but do not establish different retention periods.

learning.reason: MSK tiered storage can retain closed Kafka segments beyond the desired local retention duration. Topic retention and local retention serve different purposes for the same consumer interface.
learning.concept: Set separate fast local and total replay retention periods while keeping the established streaming protocol.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Publish only one training manifest when writers retry concurrently
prompt: Two retried jobs can race to publish a manifest under the same stable S3 key. A successful first publication must remain the only published value. The bucket has no versioning or deletes for this prefix. Both jobs have permission to put the object. What should they use to prevent an overwrite atomically?

choices.text: Run HeadObject, then use an unconditional PutObject if HeadObject did not find the key.
choices.explanation: Both calls can observe absence before either write finishes, so the later write can overwrite the first.

choices.text: Use PutObject with If-None-Match set to * and treat the precondition failure as an existing publication.
choices.explanation: S3 evaluates absence when accepting the write, including when attempts race.

choices.text: Call PutObject with CopySourceIfMatch set to the checksum of the manifest.
choices.explanation: A conditional copy source check does not enforce absence at the destination of this PutObject operation.

choices.text: Calculate a unique checksum in each writer and put it in user-defined metadata on an unconditional write.
choices.explanation: The metadata records a property of the upload; it does not impose a destination precondition.

learning.reason: The If-None-Match wildcard on a conditional write makes S3 check for a current object as part of the write. A second writer cannot overwrite the winner by replaying a successful existence check.
learning.concept: Protect create-only publication at the storage operation rather than with a separate read followed by a write.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Evolve a stream reader that must replay old training data
prompt: A fleet of upgraded feature consumers must replay events written with any prior schema version retained on a stream. Producers and consumers can be coordinated so the old readers do not need to process events written with newer versions. The registry should reject schema changes that break the required replay compatibility. Which policy should the team select?

choices.text: Set it to BACKWARD so the check covers every historic version automatically.
choices.explanation: The non-transitive backward mode checks against the preceding version. It does not ensure the stated scope.

choices.text: Set it to FORWARD_ALL because the new consumers read the old data.
choices.explanation: Forward modes concern older readers handling new writes, reversing the compatibility direction.

choices.text: Set the registry to BACKWARD_ALL.
choices.explanation: The upgraded consumer can read data written using any retained prior version covered by the compatibility check.

choices.text: Disable compatibility checking and rely on a schema ID attached to every record to guarantee decoding.
choices.explanation: An ID identifies the writer schema. It does not ensure the upgraded reader supports incompatible records.

learning.reason: BACKWARD_ALL checks that consumers using the newest schema can read current records and records from all prior registered versions, not just the preceding version.
learning.concept: Choose compatibility direction and scope from which reader version must accept which writer versions.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Discover input changes without overwriting an approved training schema
prompt: An AWS Glue crawler runs against the raw prefix of a curated feature external table. The team must allow the crawler to report surprising inferred types, but the approved Data Catalog table types must remain unchanged until a human releases a schema update. The latest crawl tried to change a feature from numeric to string. Which crawler setting addresses this?

choices.text: Keep UPDATE_IN_DATABASE and add an Athena view that casts only the current training query inputs.
choices.explanation: The existing catalog table can still be changed even if one consumer works around it.

choices.text: Schedule the same crawler less often and keep UPDATE_IN_DATABASE.
choices.explanation: The update would occur less often, but it can still apply an incompatible type when the crawler runs.

choices.text: Drop the table before each crawl so it is rebuilt from the latest raw sample.
choices.explanation: Rebuilding from the sample can reproduce the undesired types and removes the approved contract.

choices.text: Set the crawler's schema change UpdateBehavior to LOG for the existing table.
choices.explanation: The crawler records detected changes without replacing the accepted types in the catalog.

learning.reason: Setting the crawler's schema update behavior to LOG reports differences instead of applying them to the existing table schema.
learning.concept: Keep schema discovery separate from acceptance of modifications to an existing featured data contract.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Handle removal from real-time features and historical storage separately
prompt: A feature group has both SageMaker Feature Store stores enabled. An engineer hard-deletes a customer record with a newer event time than the online value. The online GetRecord result no longer includes it, but the prior values are still present in the offline table. A separate approved purge must remove the history too. Which interpretation is correct?

choices.text: The online hard delete and offline history behavior are expected. Apply a separate approved deletion procedure to the offline records.
choices.explanation: The online serving state is removed. The offline store retains earlier versions and receives a deletion marker rather than erasing the prior history.

choices.text: Repeat DeleteRecord with HardDelete until old offline Parquet data is no longer visible.
choices.explanation: Repeating the online operation does not turn its offline marker into a physical history purge.

choices.text: Replace HardDelete with SoftDelete so the service erases all previous offline records for the key.
choices.explanation: SoftDelete is an online deletion mode and also does not erase offline history.

choices.text: Ignore the old offline data because GetRecord proves it has been physically purged everywhere.
choices.explanation: An online lookup is not evidence that historical offline artifacts were removed.

learning.reason: Feature Store can remove the online record and write an offline deletion marker, but a DeleteRecord call does not physically erase earlier offline records.
learning.concept: Separate online state removal from purging historical storage and treat the offline marker as a state transition.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Preserve microphone channel roles in conversation features
prompt: A service records a support representative and a customer on two separate channels with a known channel-to-role mapping. Some speech overlaps. A downstream model needs text and timing for each recorded channel without inferring which established channel belongs to whom. How should the team transcribe the recording?

choices.text: Mix both channels into mono and infer roles from the order returned by speaker diarization.
choices.explanation: Diarization can separate speakers in mixed speech, but speaker numbering does not preserve the original channel mapping.

choices.text: Enable Transcribe channel identification and map the returned channel labels to the known roles.
choices.explanation: The output preserves which channel each transcription item came from, including the role mapping defined at recording.

choices.text: Enable automatic language identification and use language labels to infer each speaker's role.
choices.explanation: The roles are independent of detected language and need channel attribution.

choices.text: Transcribe the original file without channel identification and split the merged response on pauses.
choices.explanation: Pauses cannot reliably attribute overlapping speech to the original channels.

learning.reason: Channel identification can transcribe the two input channels separately and labels the corresponding items. The fixed input mapping identifies the business role.
learning.concept: Use known channel separation for attribution when identity should follow the recording channels rather than inferred speakers.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Separate deliberately ignored telemetry from records that need repair
prompt: A Firehose transformation must exclude a known heartbeat record type from a feature pipeline. When a business event fails to parse, its original data must be routed automatically for repair and replay. Which per-record status choices should the Lambda transformer use? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Return Dropped for a parse failure that must remain available for replay.
choices.explanation: A deliberate drop is not the transformation failure path needed for replay.

choices.text: Return Ok with placeholder content when a business event fails to parse.
choices.explanation: The placeholder may enter the primary dataset and does not preserve the affected record in the proper failure path.

choices.text: Return Dropped for a known heartbeat that should not feed the feature dataset.
choices.explanation: This records an intentional exclusion rather than a processing error.

choices.text: Return ProcessingFailed for a business record that cannot be transformed.
choices.explanation: The service treats the record as failed and delivers relevant failure data to the S3 error path.

choices.text: Throw an error for the entire batch whenever it contains a heartbeat.
choices.explanation: This misclassifies expected ignored records and can unnecessarily fail valid records in the same batch.

learning.reason: Firehose distinguishes deliberate drops from failed transformations. Processing failures are retained in the configured S3 error handling location.
learning.concept: Return statuses that represent the input outcome so discarded and reparable records follow different paths.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Encode rare categories without leaking their outcomes
prompt: A training dataset contains many rare merchant categories. The team will use scikit-learn TargetEncoder for a binary task. A training row must not acquire a value calculated directly from its own target, and held-out rows must be encoded without looking at their targets. Which workflow meets both requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Fit one encoder on the full labeled dataset, then split the encoded rows into training and validation.
choices.explanation: Held-out targets would influence the learned mappings before the split.

choices.text: Call fit followed by transform on the same training rows and assume that this reproduces fit_transform cross-fitting.
choices.explanation: That path applies the fitted mapping to its own training examples instead of computing fold-separated training values.

choices.text: Apply TargetEncoder.fit_transform to the training predictors and their training targets.
choices.explanation: Cross-fitting encodes each training fold with statistics learned without that fold's own targets.

choices.text: Fit a fresh encoder directly on the validation labels to handle categories that did not appear during training.
choices.explanation: This leaks validation targets into inputs and creates inconsistent serving behavior.

choices.text: Use the fitted encoder's transform method for held-out and serving inputs.
choices.explanation: The encoder applies the stored training mappings and does not fit on validation or serving targets.

learning.reason: TargetEncoder.fit_transform uses internal cross-fitting for training data. Later transform calls use statistics fitted on the training data without requiring held-out targets.
learning.concept: Use out-of-fold encodings when fitting the model and training-only category statistics for evaluation and serving.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Split mixed-topic documents at changes in meaning
prompt: A Bedrock knowledge base will ingest unstructured narrative reports with unreliable line breaks and headings. Different paragraphs cover related ideas for widely varying lengths. Ingestion can use additional computation. The team wants the managed chunker to identify meaning shifts between nearby sentences instead of cutting at a regular token interval. Which approach meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use fixed-size token chunks with a larger overlap between neighbors.
choices.explanation: Overlap reduces context loss at regular cuts but does not choose breaks based on topic changes.

choices.text: Use a fixed parent size and a fixed child size through hierarchical chunking.
choices.explanation: Parent and child levels control retrieval granularity, not the requested semantic breakpoint selection.

choices.text: Use semantic chunking and tune the sentence buffer and breakpoint percentile against representative reports.
choices.explanation: The configured method uses semantic proximity to decide when to create a boundary.

choices.text: Turn off chunking and submit each entire report as one document unit.
choices.explanation: This produces no within-report topic separation and may exceed the intended retrieval input size.

learning.reason: Semantic chunking evaluates adjacent sentence context and uses a breakpoint configuration to detect meaningful shifts within a maximum chunk size.
learning.concept: Choose a content-dependent segmentation method when the boundary follows topic changes rather than formatting.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reject duplicate composite keys before model training
prompt: A Glue Data Quality check validates a feature snapshot. Tenant IDs repeat across events, and event IDs are unique only within a tenant. Both fields must be present, and the same tenant-and-event pair must never appear twice. Which validation expresses this contract?

choices.text: Apply an IsPrimaryKey rule to event_id alone.
choices.explanation: Event IDs that legitimately recur in different tenants would fail, and the tenant ID is not checked.

choices.text: Apply an IsPrimaryKey rule to each column separately.
choices.explanation: This requires individual uniqueness and rejects legitimate repeated tenant or event values.

choices.text: Apply only completeness rules to tenant_id and event_id.
choices.explanation: Values can all be present while the same pair occurs more than once.

choices.text: Apply one IsPrimaryKey rule with tenant_id and event_id as the composite key.
choices.explanation: It checks uniqueness of their combinations and requires complete key values.

learning.reason: A composite primary-key rule tests the combined values and rejects missing key fields and duplicate combinations, while allowing either component to repeat individually.
learning.concept: Validate uniqueness and presence at the compound key granularity required by the business.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Create training labels for objects in LiDAR data
prompt: A team with existing SageMaker Ground Truth access is labeling a collection of independent LiDAR point clouds. The model will predict a class and a 3D position, size, and orientation per object. Synchronized camera images can help a human recognize those objects. No persistent trajectory IDs are required. Which labeling setup fits?

choices.text: Use 3D point cloud object detection and include synchronized camera information for sensor fusion.
choices.explanation: Annotators can draw oriented cuboids in point clouds and use projected camera views for context.

choices.text: Use 2D image object detection and record only the pixel coordinates of each bounding box.
choices.explanation: A 2D box does not provide the required depth, 3D bounds, and orientation.

choices.text: Use semantic segmentation and assign only a class to every point.
choices.explanation: Per-point class labels do not directly provide a cuboid and orientation for each distinct instance.

choices.text: Use an image classification task and give each frame one label for the visible object class.
choices.explanation: Frame labels supply neither individual objects nor the geometry the model must learn.

learning.reason: A 3D point cloud object-detection task produces cuboids around object instances and can show their projections on associated camera images when sensor fusion is configured.
learning.concept: Match annotations to 3D object-instance geometry instead of substituting 2D boxes, per-point classes, or trajectory identities.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Measure unequal observed outcomes before fitting a model
prompt: An existing SageMaker Clarify customer audits labels from a legacy process. Facet A has 100 records with 60 positive labels, and facet B has 60 records with 30 positive labels. The reviewer needs the difference in positive label rates, calculated as A minus B, before there are model predictions. Which report fits?

choices.text: Report DPL of 0.30 by dividing the difference of 30 positives by 100.
choices.explanation: Using one facet's denominator for both counts does not compare the two within-facet proportions.

choices.text: Report DPL of 0.10 calculated from the observed labels.
choices.explanation: The observed positive share for facet A exceeds facet B's share by ten percentage points.

choices.text: Report only the difference in the number of records from each facet.
choices.explanation: Group representation differs, but record totals do not express the proportion of positive outcomes.

choices.text: Report a difference in the model's positive prediction rates.
choices.explanation: There are no predictions yet, and the requested measure concerns observed training labels.

learning.reason: The Difference in Proportions of Labels compares positive shares within each facet. Here the difference is 60/100 minus 30/60, or 0.10.
learning.concept: Compare within-facet observed outcome rates rather than raw positive counts or representation.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Retrieve the true closest authorized vectors for an audit
prompt: An OpenSearch-based review tool must return the exact top five vectors among a pre-authorized set of at most 30 documents for each request. The overall index has millions of vectors. Ordinary search may use approximate recall, but this audit cannot miss an eligible nearest neighbor. What should the team configure for the audit query?

choices.text: Find five approximate matches across the full index, then discard unauthorized results.
choices.explanation: The resulting list can omit all legitimate nearest neighbors when global candidates are unauthorized.

choices.text: Use an approximate search with a higher search-width setting and claim it guarantees exact recall for every query.
choices.explanation: Higher search breadth may improve recall but does not establish an exact result guarantee.

choices.text: Apply the eligible-document filter within a scoring script query and calculate exact vector distances across the filtered set.
choices.explanation: Only the authorized candidates enter the exact calculation, ensuring their actual nearest neighbors are considered.

choices.text: Run a keyword-only search over the eligible documents and rank them by lexical score.
choices.explanation: Lexical order is not the requested order by vector distance.

learning.reason: The scoring script approach applies a filter first and scores every remaining vector exactly. The explicit upper bound keeps exact work small.
learning.concept: Apply exact distance scoring only to a bounded eligible set when approximate recall cannot satisfy the contract.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Remove abandoned upload parts while retaining completed artifacts
prompt: A training uploader sometimes crashes after transferring only some parts of a large S3 dataset. Storage charges grow even though the completed-object listing has not increased. All successful uploads finish within a day, and completed objects must follow their existing long-term retention. Which rule addresses abandoned parts?

choices.text: Expire all completed objects after a day under the same prefix.
choices.explanation: This would remove required artifacts and does not specifically abort incomplete uploads.

choices.text: Transition completed objects to a colder storage class as soon as they arrive.
choices.explanation: Changing the storage class of completed objects does not reclaim parts associated with uncompleted uploads.

choices.text: Disable object versioning and rely on the completed-object listing to represent all billable data.
choices.explanation: The listing does not contain unfinished parts, and changing versioning does not clean up their upload state.

choices.text: Configure AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload after a suitable number of days for that prefix.
choices.explanation: It removes orphaned upload parts after the safe window and leaves already completed objects in place.

learning.reason: S3 stores uploaded multipart parts until completion or abort. A lifecycle abort action applies to incomplete uploads without expiring completed objects.
learning.concept: Target the lifecycle action to unfinished multipart state without changing the retention of published datasets.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Preserve evidence that a measurement was absent
prompt: A quality predictor must accept numeric inputs. For one sensor, missing readings are themselves informative and valid observed zeros are common. The team must fill null entries with zero for a downstream interface, but predictions must still be able to distinguish the two cases. Which preprocessing approach fits?

choices.text: Derive a missingness indicator from the original column and pass it with the zero-filled numeric feature.
choices.explanation: A model can distinguish a measured zero from a zero used to represent a missing reading.

choices.text: Fill with zero and derive the indicator by marking every zero as missing.
choices.explanation: After filling, this flags actual sensor zeros as if those observations were absent.

choices.text: Replace all zeros and missing values with the same training-set median.
choices.explanation: This merges both cases and fails to preserve observed zeros.

choices.text: Exclude all rows with missing measurements from training and leave inference preprocessing unchanged.
choices.explanation: This removes examples containing the learned missingness signal and does not define how inference handles nulls.

learning.reason: A missingness indicator computed before imputation distinguishes filled zeros from actual zeros while the numeric feature satisfies the downstream data type requirement.
learning.concept: Represent missingness independently when replacing nulls would otherwise merge different meanings.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prevent consumers from seeing reprocessed feature outputs twice
prompt: A Managed Service for Apache Flink job restores a replayable input and its operator state from checkpoints after a failure. It emits computed features to Kafka on Amazon MSK. Duplicates became visible because the existing output path committed records before a checkpoint completed. Which changes configure the supported Flink Kafka connector for exactly-once visibility? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Disable checkpointing after enabling producer retries so recovery starts as soon as a worker restarts.
choices.explanation: Producer retries alone do not coordinate application recovery state with publication of outputs.

choices.text: Keep periodic checkpointing enabled for the Flink application.
choices.explanation: The checkpoints supply the coordinated commit and recovery boundary.

choices.text: Set the Kafka sink delivery guarantee to EXACTLY_ONCE and configure a transactional ID prefix unique to this sink.
choices.explanation: The connector associates output transactions with successful checkpoints instead of exposing output from an abandoned attempt.

choices.text: Leave sink delivery at AT_LEAST_ONCE and rely on Kafka message keys to remove duplicate records immediately.
choices.explanation: Equal keys do not make Kafka immediately suppress records that were published twice.

choices.text: Configure downstream Kafka consumers with read_committed isolation.
choices.explanation: Consumers then see committed output rather than records from unfinished or aborted transactions.

learning.reason: A transactional Kafka sink commits output with a completed checkpoint. Consumers that read only committed transactions do not observe writes from aborted attempts.
learning.concept: Align checkpoint recovery, sink transaction commits, and consumer isolation for the final observable result.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Reduce a numeric representation while keeping all splits comparable
prompt: A model consumes dense numeric embeddings of an industrial process. The team wants a smaller linear representation that preserves as much variance as possible and uses the same coordinate system for training, validation, and future inference. It may fit an unsupervised linear transform on training rows. Which workflow fits?

choices.text: Fit a separate PCA transform independently on each split and serving batch.
choices.explanation: Axes can rotate or change order across fitted datasets, making the same component index inconsistent.

choices.text: Fit PCA on the training vectors, choose the retained component count, and reuse the fitted centering and projection for all other vectors.
choices.explanation: A single learned basis makes coordinates and transformations consistent while retaining the leading variation.

choices.text: Select the first few raw coordinates of every vector and assume these explain the greatest variance.
choices.explanation: The original embedding order does not establish an ordering of variance-preserving components.

choices.text: Fit PCA on the validation set and refit it whenever evaluation scores fall.
choices.explanation: This uses evaluation data to define the representation and makes validation-dependent decisions harder to interpret.

learning.reason: PCA finds leading variance directions in the training data. Shared centering and projection keep each split and future input in the same lower-dimensional coordinate system.
learning.concept: Learn a reusable lower-dimensional projection on the training data and apply it to every split.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Route text segments to the correct language preprocessing
prompt: A multilingual incident report alternates between English and Spanish sections. A document-level DetectDominantLanguage call returns two confidence scores. The team needs to choose preprocessing separately for each sufficiently long section, rather than estimate document composition from the scores. What should it do?

choices.text: Multiply the document-wide English confidence by the total word count and route that many leading words as English.
choices.explanation: The score is not a percentage of words or a location boundary.

choices.text: Choose one tokenizer for every section based solely on the highest report-level score.
choices.explanation: A report-level majority does not identify the language of each section.

choices.text: Send each sufficiently long section for language detection and use its supported high-confidence result for routing.
choices.explanation: Detection runs on the unit being routed and does not treat a whole-document score as a ratio of words.

choices.text: Interleave words from the entire document in several samples, then assign each original section the average confidence across samples.
choices.explanation: Mixed samples lose the section boundaries needed for reliable routing.

learning.reason: The confidence score expresses certainty about a detected language for the supplied text, not the share of the document written in that language. Running detection on coherent pieces supplies section-level evidence.
learning.concept: Align language detection input boundaries with the text units that will receive separate processing.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Retain a monthly feature without releasing exact event dates
prompt: A Spark preparation job receives exact dates for service visits. The approved feature contract allows analysts to compare visits by calendar month including year. They must not receive the original day, and they do not need to correlate individual visits. The raw source remains available only to the preprocessing role. What should the export do?

choices.text: Use only the number of the month and discard its year.
choices.explanation: This would mix the same month from different years, losing a required analytic distinction.

choices.text: Encrypt each exact date and give analysts the key so they can extract the month themselves.
choices.explanation: Readers with the key can recover the unapproved day detail.

choices.text: Derive the month and keep the original date in a supplemental column in the same export.
choices.explanation: The extra column would still include data outside the approved feature contract.

choices.text: Derive a year-and-month feature by truncating each date to its month and omit the original date from the output.
choices.explanation: The output preserves calendar month and year while withholding the actual day.

learning.reason: Truncating a date to month level preserves the calendar year and month while removing day detail from the derived feature. Excluding the raw date from the output enforces the feature contract.
learning.concept: Release the minimum time granularity needed for analysis and keep the detailed source out of the derived export.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Prepare valid demonstrations of tool-using conversations
prompt: A team is formatting Amazon Nova 2 supervised fine-tuning data. Synthetic examples teach a model to request a shipping quote and then explain the returned result. Every tool-use ID already matches its corresponding result. A validation pass finds that the exporter placed the tool request in a user turn, the result in an assistant turn, and omitted the tool declaration. Which changes repair the examples? (Choose three.)

choices.text: Replace the structured tool result with an unrelated assistant message and rely on the existing tool-use ID alone.
choices.explanation: An ID cannot supply the output fields the model needs for the demonstrated response.

choices.text: Declare the shipping quote tool with its name and input schema in the example's toolConfig.
choices.explanation: The tool use must name a tool declared for the conversation, with its expected input structure.

choices.text: Remove the tool declaration because a tool name inside toolUse is sufficient.
choices.explanation: The training format calls for the invocation to reference a tool named in the supplied configuration.

choices.text: Put the toolUse block in an assistant turn.
choices.explanation: The documented format permits the model's invocation in an assistant turn.

choices.text: Put the matching toolResult block in a user turn followed by the desired assistant response.
choices.explanation: The tool result supplies external context; the following assistant turn can demonstrate how to use it.

learning.reason: Nova tool-calling examples include tool definitions alongside the conversation. The assistant turn requests a tool and the result is carried in the user-side tool result turn.
learning.concept: Prepare the training conversation's tool schema and role-correct blocks so the examples teach the model's action and subsequent answer.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Augment rare component images without changing their meaning
prompt: A vision dataset contains far fewer left-handed parts than right-handed parts. A horizontal flip turns a left-handed part into an apparent right-handed one. Production images vary in lighting and framing. The team wants more valid minority training examples while preserving the class labels and bounding boxes. Which plan is suitable?

choices.text: Use class-preserving illumination and framing transforms on minority training examples, updating boxes for geometric transforms and leaving the holdout unchanged.
choices.explanation: These variations alter nuisance conditions without reversing the part's handedness or invalidating its geometry labels.

choices.text: Horizontally flip left-handed parts and keep their original left-handed labels.
choices.explanation: The flip changes the visual property the classifier is supposed to identify.

choices.text: Crop minority training images while keeping boxes at their original coordinates.
choices.explanation: The boxes no longer align with the cropped images and provide incorrect localization targets.

choices.text: Generate variants before splitting so that variants of the same image occur in both training and validation.
choices.explanation: Near copies in the holdout can make the measured generalization performance misleading.

learning.reason: Augmentations must preserve the assigned class and maintain geometry consistently for detection targets. Training-only label-preserving changes can expand the rare distribution without contaminating held-out data.
learning.concept: Select minority augmentations consistent with the physical label and transform spatial annotations with the image.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Quarantine rows that fail a cross-field training-data rule
prompt: An AWS Glue ETL quality gate checks generated training examples. A row is valid only when its expected action agrees with its independently reviewed outcome and its identifier is complete. The team needs each rejected row so it can repair the examples. A CustomSQL count alone reported the number of errors but did not identify rows. Which change helps?

choices.text: Return only the count of failing rows and treat each unit of that count as an input key.
choices.explanation: A scalar count does not carry the identity of failed examples.

choices.text: Configure a row-level CustomSQL query that returns the stable input keys of rows satisfying the rule, and use the row-level outcomes to quarantine unmatched rows.
choices.explanation: Glue considers returned input records successful and can identify the missing input records as failures.

choices.text: Return the primary keys of records that fail the check as the passing result set.
choices.explanation: Glue's returned rows are marked successful, so this would invert the intended classification.

choices.text: Return only a constant value for every valid row, regardless of its input key.
choices.explanation: Without an input key, the service cannot associate results with the individual source rows that need action.

learning.reason: In Glue row-level CustomSQL, the query should return primary dataset keys for records that pass. Glue matches those keys against input to identify the other rows as failures.
learning.concept: Return valid input row keys for row-level quality outcomes instead of supplying only an aggregate or the failing rows.

category: Data Preparation for ML and AI
examDomain: Data Preparation for ML and AI
title: Validate the newly written version of a feature configuration
prompt: A training launcher updates one item in a single-Region DynamoDB table and immediately verifies the new value. It has the complete primary key. A global secondary index sometimes returns an earlier value. The verification must observe successful writes without retrying until an index catches up. Which read should it use?

choices.text: Keep querying the global secondary index and set ConsistentRead to true on that query.
choices.explanation: GSIs do not support a strongly consistent query.

choices.text: Read from the DynamoDB stream and assume the next available record always corresponds to this verification.
choices.explanation: The stream is a change feed, not an immediate strongly consistent lookup by the known key.

choices.text: Use GetItem against the base table with ConsistentRead set to true.
choices.explanation: The strongly consistent base-table read reflects successful writes completed before the read.

choices.text: Read through a cache using its normal expiration policy.
choices.explanation: The cache may retain the old value after the update and cannot guarantee this read-after-write requirement.

learning.reason: Base table reads can request strong consistency, whereas global secondary indexes support only eventual consistency. Using the primary key avoids relying on asynchronous indexing.
learning.concept: Choose a read path that can guarantee freshness for the known base-table key.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Accelerate generation while retaining the target model's role
prompt: A production assistant needs the decoding behavior of its validated target model. Generation is slow because it does many sequential decoding steps. A compatible much smaller model proposes highly accurate short continuations on the same workload. The team wants to optimize serving without using that smaller model as a standalone replacement. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Send all requests to the smaller model and compare outputs with the target only during periodic audit.
choices.explanation: This removes the target's verification from live inference and changes what may be emitted.

choices.text: Let the draft return tokens immediately and mark them as verified when the target accepts them later.
choices.explanation: Unaccepted content could reach the user before the target has checked it.

choices.text: Generate a full response with both models independently, then return whichever finishes first.
choices.explanation: This does not use target verification of draft tokens and can prefer an unvalidated output path.

choices.text: Evaluate speculative decoding with the compatible draft and let the target verify its proposed tokens before accepting them.
choices.explanation: Verification retains the target's decoding role while high draft acceptance can improve latency.

learning.reason: Speculative decoding proposes tokens with a draft and verifies candidates using the target. A high acceptance rate can reduce target-model decoding steps without trusting unverified output.
learning.concept: Use a draft to propose likely next tokens and keep correctness of acceptance with the target model.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Reuse visual features when labels are scarce
prompt: A team has a small labeled dataset for four new categories of industrial parts. It has a pretrained vision encoder whose features already separate similar shapes, but the original classification head predicts unrelated categories. The initial training budget can update only a small task-specific component. Which starting approach meets those constraints?

choices.text: Freeze the pretrained encoder, replace its classification head, and train the new head on the four target labels.
choices.explanation: The approach retains useful visual features and updates only the small component that maps them to the new classes.

choices.text: Keep the pretrained head unchanged and assign its first four output indices to the four new labels.
choices.explanation: The original outputs have learned meanings independent of their index and do not correspond to the new labels.

choices.text: Initialize a new encoder randomly and freeze it while training a new head.
choices.explanation: Freezing random features discards the useful representation supplied by the existing encoder.

choices.text: Train a complete high-capacity encoder and head from scratch on the small dataset.
choices.explanation: This updates the whole model, exceeding the specified initial budget and losing available transfer knowledge.

learning.reason: Transfer learning reuses representations learned from a pretrained model. A new small classifier trained on the target categories can take advantage of those features without retraining the encoder.
learning.concept: Reuse the existing visual representation while learning the new label mapping from the limited labeled examples.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Choose a likelihood that matches discrete event counts
prompt: An operations model forecasts hourly fault ticket counts with SageMaker DeepAR. Observations are nonnegative integers, including many zeros, and the model must provide uncertainty estimates in the same count domain. The team wants the model likelihood to fit the data rather than correcting invalid samples afterward. Which setting should it choose?

choices.text: Use the Gaussian likelihood and clip negative values only when displaying predictions.
choices.explanation: Display-time clipping does not make the fitted uncertainty distribution a discrete count distribution.

choices.text: Use the negative-binomial likelihood for the target series.
choices.explanation: It is designed for nonnegative integer counts and naturally includes zero.

choices.text: Use the Student-t likelihood because it creates integer forecasts when all observations are integers.
choices.explanation: The distribution is continuous, and its support is not restricted to nonnegative integer counts.

choices.text: Treat each distinct count as an unrelated class and train a separate classifier for every observed hour.
choices.explanation: This removes the time-series likelihood and does not meet the requested probabilistic count forecasting approach.

learning.reason: DeepAR's negative-binomial likelihood is intended for nonnegative counts. It models zeros and discrete variability directly.
learning.concept: Select a forecasting likelihood from the support and interpretation of the observed target.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Fit the required training configuration by reducing activation memory
prompt: A PyTorch training job on SageMaker runs out of accelerator memory during large layers. Profiling shows that saved activations dominate, while model weights and optimizer state fit. The objective, precision, and microbatch size must remain the same. The team can afford additional computation per update. Which technique directly targets the problem?

choices.text: Write training recovery checkpoints to S3 more frequently.
choices.explanation: Recovery checkpoints preserve training state for restarts. They do not reduce the forward activations saved on the accelerator.

choices.text: Reduce the microbatch and increase gradient accumulation to compensate.
choices.explanation: That could reduce activation memory, but it changes the explicitly required microbatch size.

choices.text: Enable activation checkpointing for suitable blocks of the model and recompute their intermediates during backward passes.
choices.explanation: The method retains fewer activations simultaneously while preserving the configured batch and precision.

choices.text: Quantize all forward activations to a lower precision during training.
choices.explanation: This changes a precision constraint rather than trading additional computation for fewer stored activations.

learning.reason: Activation checkpointing drops selected forward intermediates and recomputes them during backpropagation, trading computation for a smaller peak activation footprint.
learning.concept: Use recomputation when activation memory is scarce and reducing the microbatch or precision is outside the constraints.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Shuffle across epochs without making distributed workers repeat one another
prompt: A SageMaker PyTorch script uses DistributedSampler and one data-loading process per rank. Each rank gets its own subset, yet every epoch repeats the same order. The team needs coordinated reshuffling across epochs and wants to avoid independently sampling overlapping subsets. What should it change?

choices.text: Give each rank a different random global shuffle seed and replace DistributedSampler with a normal random sampler.
choices.explanation: Independent ordering and sampling do not preserve the coordinated rank partitions.

choices.text: Enable DataLoader shuffle while keeping an explicit DistributedSampler and never updating its epoch.
choices.explanation: Shuffling must be coordinated by the distributed sampler. Merely adding loader-level shuffle does not update its epoch.

choices.text: Recreate the sampler each epoch using the same fixed seed and its default epoch value.
choices.explanation: The sampler repeats the same starting state and can produce the same ordering.

choices.text: Call sampler.set_epoch with the same epoch number on each rank before creating that epoch's data iterator.
choices.explanation: This lets the ranks use a new shared shuffled order and select their corresponding partitions.

learning.reason: DistributedSampler coordinates rank-specific partitions using its seed and current epoch. Calling set_epoch before the iterator is created changes the shared shuffled order across epochs.
learning.concept: Reshuffle distributed data through the sampler's epoch state while preserving coordination between ranks.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Lower the learning rate when validation has stopped improving
prompt: A PyTorch model is still far from its target error. Training and validation loss improved early, then validation loss stopped setting better values for several epochs. The team wants to continue optimization at a smaller learning rate only after the plateau persists for an agreed number of validations. Which schedule fits the request?

choices.text: Use ReduceLROnPlateau in min mode with suitable patience and call it with validation loss after each validation epoch.
choices.explanation: A sustained lack of better validation loss causes the rate to drop while training continues.

choices.text: Use early stopping to terminate immediately after the first unchanged validation loss.
choices.explanation: This ends training rather than attempting further optimization at a lower rate.

choices.text: Use a fixed-step scheduler and drop the rate every training batch regardless of validation loss.
choices.explanation: This schedule is independent of the requested validation-based trigger.

choices.text: Use ReduceLROnPlateau in max mode and supply validation loss.
choices.explanation: Max mode treats a larger value as improvement, reversing the meaning of this metric.

learning.reason: ReduceLROnPlateau monitors a supplied metric and reduces the learning rate when no improvement meets its configured threshold and patience. Min mode is appropriate for validation loss.
learning.concept: Choose a metric-driven learning-rate change when the training run should continue after a validation plateau.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Make model input requirements reproducible across experiments
prompt: An MLflow-tracked SageMaker team publishes candidate models from different training runs. A recent candidate began expecting a different input type, but release tests discovered it only after integration. The team wants each model artifact to carry its declared named input types and a reproducible serving example. Which change fits?

choices.text: Use run tags to describe feature names in prose and skip logging a model signature.
choices.explanation: Tags support tracking but do not define the artifact's machine-readable schema.

choices.text: Log each candidate with an explicit model signature and a representative input example, then test the candidate against that contract.
choices.explanation: The artifact carries both a machine-readable schema and a concrete request that can be reused in release verification.

choices.text: Log only aggregate accuracy and infer that similar metric values mean the model request shape also stayed the same.
choices.explanation: A similar evaluation score does not tell the serving layer what types and fields to send.

choices.text: Keep the input example in a mutable shared notebook and choose the latest notebook whenever an old model is deployed.
choices.explanation: The example may have changed since the model was logged, losing the reproducibility requirement.

learning.reason: MLflow model signatures describe the model input and output schema. A saved input example travels with the logged model and supplies a known request for validation.
learning.concept: Version the input contract with the model artifact and exercise it with reproducible serving data.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Choose a multiclass objective that gives rare classes equal weight
prompt: SageMaker Autopilot ranks candidates for classifying service incidents. Routine cases dominate the data, but each category should contribute equally to selection. For every category, reviewers want one score that accounts for both false alerts and missed cases. Which candidate metric fits?

choices.text: Rank by ordinary accuracy on the validation set.
choices.explanation: Accuracy weights individual examples and can reward the dominant classes while rare labels are misclassified.

choices.text: Rank by macro recall only.
choices.explanation: Each class has equal weight, but recall alone does not measure false alerts against that class.

choices.text: Rank the candidates by macro F1 on the agreed validation set.
choices.explanation: Per-class F1 incorporates both error directions, and the macro average gives each class equal influence.

choices.text: Rank by weighted F1 using class prevalence as the weight.
choices.explanation: More common labels would carry more weight than rare categories, which contradicts the selection requirement.

learning.reason: Macro F1 takes the average of the per-class harmonic means of precision and recall. Minority classes have the same weight in the macro average as large classes.
learning.concept: Use a per-class average when the objective values precision and recall for every category equally.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Recover more ANN candidates without changing returned context size
prompt: An OpenSearch index stores full-precision vectors and uses a Faiss HNSW method that supports query-time ef_search overrides. Offline judgments show that approximate search misses some true neighbors, but the retrieval API must still return ten matches and the team cannot rebuild the index this week. Some latency headroom is available. Which change should it evaluate?

choices.text: Increase only k and let the consuming service ignore every result beyond ten.
choices.explanation: This changes the search and response count contract, and exposes more data than the caller asked to receive.

choices.text: Increase the HNSW construction parameter ef_construction without rebuilding the existing graph.
choices.explanation: That setting affects graph construction and will not improve traversal of the graph that already exists.

choices.text: Decrease the search width to make room for more calls per second and assume this necessarily increases recall.
choices.explanation: Smaller search breadth can omit more relevant candidates even if the service handles more requests.

choices.text: Increase query-time ef_search while keeping k at ten, and measure recall and latency on representative searches.
