choices.explanation: The traversal can consider more candidates while returning the configured number; the check measures the tradeoff.

learning.reason: A larger HNSW search breadth can consider more candidates at query time and improve recall. It is separate from the requested number of returned neighbors.
learning.concept: Tune search effort without changing the index construction or the size of the returned result list.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Recover accuracy at the required integer inference precision
prompt: An image model must run on an inference target that accepts the supported 8-bit format. Post-training conversion meets size and latency targets but misses the required validation accuracy. The team still has labeled training data and can run another training pass. Which approach tries to recover accuracy without abandoning the deployment constraint?

choices.text: Apply quantization-aware training and validate the converted 8-bit model on the held-out data and target runtime.
choices.explanation: Emulating quantization during learning lets the model adapt before it is exported in the supported format.

choices.text: Deploy the original 32-bit model because its validation accuracy is higher.
choices.explanation: The float model does not meet the target's supported deployment format.

choices.text: Repeat exactly the same post-training conversion with the same configuration and assume the accuracy loss will disappear.
choices.explanation: Nothing in the unchanged conversion gives the model new information about the effects that caused the measured accuracy drop.

choices.text: Validate only the 32-bit training artifact after conversion, then deploy the 8-bit artifact without testing it.
choices.explanation: Float validation does not establish accuracy in the required low-precision path.

learning.reason: Quantization-aware training incorporates effects of inference-time quantization while learning weights. The resulting model can be converted and evaluated in the required low-precision format.
learning.concept: Train with the intended quantization behavior, then validate the actual deployed precision rather than the float checkpoint alone.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Evaluate every approved hyperparameter combination
prompt: An audit requires a SageMaker tuning run to train every combination of three approved optimizers and four approved batch sizes. The search space must include no additional numeric values, and no combination can be skipped based on earlier outcomes. Which configuration satisfies the audit?

choices.text: Use Bayesian search with continuous batch size bounds and stop once the best score stops improving.
choices.explanation: Continuous bounds allow values outside the approved list, and the stopping behavior can skip required pairs.

choices.text: Use Grid with the optimizers and the four batch sizes represented as categorical values, allowing all 12 trials.
choices.explanation: A grid enumerates the specified pairs and does not need to sample unapproved batch sizes.

choices.text: Use Random and assume that a budget equal to the number of possible combinations guarantees coverage of every pair.
choices.explanation: Random sampling is not the stated exhaustive evaluation strategy. It does not provide the required enumeration guarantee.

choices.text: Use a warm start and include only combinations already evaluated by a related tuning job.
choices.explanation: This can omit approved combinations absent from the earlier tuning results.

learning.reason: The grid strategy evaluates combinations of listed categorical choices. It is suitable when the combinations themselves, not just an estimated optimum, must all be measured.
learning.concept: Express a finite approved search space as enumerated values and use an exhaustive tuner.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Measure whether detections localize the correct region
prompt: Two model candidates usually predict the right class when a target appears. One often draws boxes wide enough to cover nearly the entire image. The release team needs a localization criterion that penalizes excess predicted area as well as missed target area. Which evaluation meets the requirement?

choices.text: Use only classification accuracy for images containing a target.
choices.explanation: A correct object class can coexist with a poorly placed or oversized box.

choices.text: Divide intersection area only by ground-truth area and ignore predicted area outside it.
choices.explanation: A full-image prediction can score perfectly on this ratio whenever it covers the true box.

choices.text: Use intersection over union against the labeled box for each matched detection.
choices.explanation: The denominator includes both boxes, so a very large predicted box cannot score well just by enclosing a small true target.

choices.text: Score whether the predicted center lies somewhere in the image.
choices.explanation: An image-wide check does not evaluate location, size, or overlap with the labeled object.

learning.reason: Intersection over union divides shared area by the union of predicted and labeled areas. Too much surrounding area or insufficient overlap reduces the score.
learning.concept: Measure overlap relative to total covered area instead of counting a correct class or a covered target alone.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Make a fair cross-model language evaluation
prompt: A report ranks two language models by raw token-level perplexity. The models tokenize text differently, and their scores were also calculated on different held-out corpora. The business wants to choose the model that answers the same support tasks better. What should the evaluator do?

choices.text: Choose the model with the lower perplexity because the exponentiation removes tokenizer and corpus effects.
choices.explanation: The exponent does not eliminate differences in tokenization or held-out text difficulty.

choices.text: Divide each model's perplexity by its vocabulary size and compare the quotients as task success scores.
choices.explanation: Vocabulary size alone does not correct the difference in tokenization or measure response success.

choices.text: Use a separate support benchmark for each model selected to match its strengths, then compare the resulting percentages directly.
choices.explanation: Different test sets change task difficulty and do not support a like-for-like comparison.

choices.text: Evaluate both models on the same held-out support tasks with the same response criteria and treat their original perplexities as incomparable evidence for the decision.
choices.explanation: Shared inputs and scoring align the result with the business objective, without comparing incompatible token units.

learning.reason: Tokenization changes the units in a token-level perplexity calculation, and corpus difficulty changes the results. A common task-level benchmark compares observable performance on the same inputs and scoring protocol.
learning.concept: Recognize when token-level perplexity is insufficient for a cross-tokenizer business comparison and use aligned task evidence.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Improve known product names in speech transcripts
prompt: An existing Amazon Transcribe workflow handles normal sentences correctly, but repeatedly misrenders a short list of equipment brand names in a supported language. The company has the spellings and can evaluate changes using sample recordings. It does not have enough domain text to train a language model. Which first change fits?

choices.text: Create and apply a custom vocabulary with the known names and supported display spellings, then test it on representative recordings.
choices.explanation: It supplies focused hints for the recurring terms without a custom language-model training corpus.

choices.text: Add the product names to a vocabulary filter configured to remove matching terms.
choices.explanation: Filtering would suppress terms once detected rather than improving their intended rendering.

choices.text: Switch to speaker partitioning and use the speaker labels as possible product spellings.
choices.explanation: Speaker labels identify speakers, not brand terms in their speech.

choices.text: Train a custom language model from a list containing only the desired brand names and no representative passages.
choices.explanation: A language model is suited to learning broader contextual patterns. The available list and symptoms fit a custom vocabulary.

learning.reason: A custom vocabulary targets recognition and display of specific domain terms. It does not require training a language model on broad in-domain text.
learning.concept: Use a vocabulary-level adaptation when known words are the issue and surrounding domain language is already handled well.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Check whether the model misses more true cases in one facet
prompt: A team with access to SageMaker Clarify compares a single screening classifier at one fixed threshold. Positive-label prevalence differs between two facets. The reviewer specifically wants to compare how often examples that truly belong to the positive class are found in each facet. Which metric fits?

choices.text: Use the difference in overall positive prediction rates between facets.
choices.explanation: That compares all predictions without conditioning on the actual positive labels.

choices.text: Use Recall Difference between the two facets.
choices.explanation: It directly compares how many actual positives are found in each facet, relative to the number of actual positives there.

choices.text: Use the difference in positive rates in the true labels before fitting.
choices.explanation: That measures dataset outcome prevalence, not how the trained model finds positive cases.

choices.text: Compare only overall model accuracy between facets.
choices.explanation: Accuracy mixes positive and negative decisions and can hide differences specifically among positive cases.

learning.reason: Recall difference compares true positives divided by all actual positives in each facet. It measures detection rates conditional on the true label rather than overall positive output rates.
learning.concept: Condition on the actual positive population when evaluating disparity in missed true cases.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Diagnose whether a generator overlooks available evidence
prompt: A RAG pipeline retrieves the passage needed for an answer and includes it in the prompt. Answers fail more often when that passage appears in the middle of a long context, but passage content and query difficulty vary across production examples. The team wants to isolate position as a cause without changing retrieval. Which test should it run?

choices.text: Increase k and rerun retrieval to compare the answer from the new set of passages.
choices.explanation: Adding passages changes the candidate content and length as well as positions, so it does not isolate the cause.

choices.text: Add another source that duplicates the answer and count any improvement as proof of position effects.
choices.explanation: Duplication changes evidence availability and frequency, so it cannot isolate the original passage's position.

choices.text: For each test question, run paired prompts with the same passages and move the answer-bearing passage among early, middle, and late positions while keeping the model and scoring fixed.
choices.explanation: The paired comparison controls evidence availability and tests the effect of context position.

choices.text: Compare model accuracy on unrelated short and long questions without tracking where evidence appears.
choices.explanation: This changes difficulty and context length without actually testing the hypotheses about position.

learning.reason: A paired experiment can move the same relevant passage within the same retrieved context while keeping the prompt content, model, and scoring fixed. This isolates sensitivity to evidence position.
learning.concept: Change only where already retrieved evidence appears to distinguish ordering sensitivity from retrieval misses.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Measure performance under the decoder's actual serving behavior
prompt: A sequence-to-sequence model predicts repair instructions. Its held-out token metric is high when each step receives the previous correct token. In production the decoder receives its previous generated token, and small mistakes can compound. Which change gives a release metric that reflects the observed failure?

choices.text: Continue feeding the previous correct token in validation and simply increase the number of tested sequences.
choices.explanation: More teacher-forced evaluations still omit the serving behavior implicated by the production failures.

choices.text: Replace the user's initial request in validation with the final reference response.
choices.explanation: Providing the target in the input would give away the solution and misrepresent the serving task.

choices.text: Score only the first generated token from each example because it is unaffected by earlier model errors.
choices.explanation: That deliberately omits the downstream effects the team needs to measure.

choices.text: Generate complete held-out responses from the initial inputs using the same decoding setup as production, and score the resulting sequences against references.
choices.explanation: This exposes cascading errors when the model conditions on its own predictions.

learning.reason: Teacher forcing can be useful during training but conditions on correct prefixes. Free-running validation can reveal errors when predictions condition on previously generated tokens, as in serving.
learning.concept: Evaluate complete autoregressive sequences with the same conditioning assumptions used at inference.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Explain a prediction relative to a meaningful operating state
prompt: An engineer uses Integrated Gradients on a PyTorch fault model. The explanation should describe why this example differs from prediction at a known normal operating state. For several sensors, an all-zero vector is an impossible physical state. Which configuration best matches the explanation question?

choices.text: Use the known representative normal-operation input as the attribution baseline and state that interpretation in the report.
choices.explanation: The attributions describe the change in model output relative to that specific physically meaningful baseline.

choices.text: Use the default zero baseline and report that the result explains change from the normal operating values.
choices.explanation: That baseline may be far from a valid normal input, so the interpretation does not match the computation.

choices.text: Use the same input as both the example and the baseline, then interpret zero attribution as proof no feature mattered.
choices.explanation: With no difference between the input and its baseline, the method cannot answer the requested comparison.

choices.text: Train a separate model on the baseline values and use its global input importance as the local explanation.
choices.explanation: That explains a different model across inputs, not the current model's prediction relative to the specified reference.

learning.reason: Integrated Gradients attributes a difference from the chosen baseline. A representative normal input supplies the intended reference instead of making the explanation relative to an unrelated zero state.
learning.concept: Choose a feasible explanation baseline that matches the reference state named by the reviewer.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Retrieve evidence when the second search key is unknown initially
prompt: A support assistant answers questions about remedy instructions using two sets of unlinked documents in a managed Bedrock knowledge base. Each answer requires looking up the product's firmware identifier, then searching remedy documents with that identifier. The user normally knows only the product name. Which retrieval design best fits?

choices.text: Split the request into two independent queries and always run both in parallel before processing any results.
choices.explanation: The remedy query would still lack the firmware identifier needed to disambiguate the correct instructions.

choices.text: Use agentic retrieval that can identify the firmware in an initial lookup and use that result to formulate the next search.
choices.explanation: The second search becomes specific to the product using the intermediate evidence.

choices.text: Send a single broad query for the product name and choose the longest passage in the response.
choices.explanation: Passage length does not establish the link between the actual firmware and the appropriate remedy.

choices.text: Skip the first lookup and ask the model to invent the firmware identifier it should retrieve.
choices.explanation: An unverified identifier can send retrieval to the wrong instructions.

learning.reason: An agentic retrieval flow can run multiple retrieval steps and use findings from an earlier lookup to form a later query. The firmware identifier cannot reliably be included in the second search before it has been found.
learning.concept: Choose sequential evidence-dependent retrieval when one lookup produces another lookup's required input.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Audit rare tasks without distorting the measured overall pass rate
prompt: A human evaluation deliberately gives half its review slots to rare but important requests. In production those requests account for 5% of eligible interactions. The reviewers need separate results for rare cases as well as an overall estimate for production. Requests were randomly selected within each evaluation group. Which reporting actions meet both goals? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Unweight the report and average all reviewed requests as if their case mix were the production mix.
choices.explanation: The heavily oversampled group would supply half the weight instead of its actual share.

choices.text: Drop all rare requests from the overall calculation and use only the routine group.
choices.explanation: Routine-only performance does not estimate the overall rate across eligible interactions.

choices.text: Assign extra weight to whichever group currently has a higher observed pass rate.
choices.explanation: Weights chosen from the outcome would bias the estimate and do not represent production prevalence.

choices.text: Report each group's pass rate separately so the rare group stays visible in the decision.
choices.explanation: Group results let stakeholders assess quality on the rare cases without losing it in an aggregate.

choices.text: Compute the overall estimate with the production shares of 5% and 95% for the two group rates.
choices.explanation: Weighting the rates by real traffic proportions estimates the requested production result.

source.label: National Center for Health Statistics sampling methodology

learning.reason: Disproportionate stratification supports precision in small groups. To estimate an overall population rate, weight group estimates by their actual population shares rather than their shares of the review sample.
learning.concept: Keep deliberately enriched groups visible and apply population weights when estimating overall traffic performance.

category: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
examDomain: ML Model and Foundation Model (FM) Development
title: Verify a revised prompt on examples that did not guide its design
prompt: A team iterates on a Bedrock prompt template for case summaries. It edits instructions and examples repeatedly after reading the outputs. Release reviewers need a credible estimate of how the final template handles unseen cases. Which practices should the team adopt? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use one development set for comparing drafts and adjusting the instructions and demonstrations.
choices.explanation: The team can iterate without learning the answers to the separate final test cases.

choices.text: Evaluate the frozen prompt on a separate unseen holdout with the agreed scoring criteria before approving it.
choices.explanation: The holdout measures the selected candidate on cases that did not influence the edits.

choices.text: Add every failed final test case to the prompt examples and immediately report the score on the same test set.
choices.explanation: That adapts the prompt to the test cases, so the new score is no longer unseen performance.

choices.text: Choose the final holdout after viewing each candidate's strongest outputs.
choices.explanation: Outcome selection can inflate reported performance.

choices.text: Use the same cases for editing and final evaluation because temperature is fixed.
choices.explanation: Deterministic sampling does not remove leakage from repeatedly using the same cases during development.

learning.reason: A development set supplies feedback while choosing the prompt. A separate unseen set can then measure performance of the frozen candidate without leaking per-example test feedback into its design.
learning.concept: Separate prompt selection feedback from final generalization evidence.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Set independent limits for queued and executing predictions
prompt: A SageMaker asynchronous endpoint handles documents that become too old to use if they sit in the queue for more than five minutes. Once an accepted request starts, its supported handler may need up to 20 minutes to finish. The caller can choose limits per request. Which configuration keeps both requirements?

choices.text: Set RequestTTLSeconds to 1200 and InvocationTimeoutSeconds to 300.
choices.explanation: This would allow stale queue entries and time out jobs that legitimately take longer to process.

choices.text: Set both limits to 300 so the endpoint enforces one common deadline.
choices.explanation: Jobs that start in time could still be terminated after five minutes of execution, missing the processing requirement.

choices.text: Set RequestTTLSeconds to 300 and InvocationTimeoutSeconds to 1200.
choices.explanation: The queue age is capped independently from the model's allowed execution time.

choices.text: Use only the client HTTP response timeout to enforce both limits.
choices.explanation: The enqueue response does not remain open while the model processes the document.

learning.reason: RequestTTLSeconds limits the time a request may remain queued. InvocationTimeoutSeconds controls its allowed processing time after it is picked up.
learning.concept: Set separate admission age and execution duration limits on the asynchronous request.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Preserve a previous resource during an approved stack replacement
prompt: A CloudFormation update will replace a stateful resource holding model experiment metadata. The change is intentional. The team must have CloudFormation create the replacement but leave the old physical resource available for separate audit and cleanup. The stack is not being deleted. Which template setting fits?

choices.text: Set only DeletionPolicy to Retain and assume it always controls replaced old resources.
choices.explanation: DeletionPolicy does not govern this replacement of a physical resource during an update.

choices.text: Use a stack policy denying replacement of the resource.
choices.explanation: This prevents the planned replacement rather than preserving the predecessor during it.

choices.text: Enable termination protection for the stack.
choices.explanation: Termination protection concerns deleting the stack. It does not select what happens to a physical resource replaced by an update.

choices.text: Set UpdateReplacePolicy to Retain on the resource before applying the replacement update.
choices.explanation: The stack can create the new resource while preserving the old physical instance outside its current management.

learning.reason: UpdateReplacePolicy applies to the physical resource CloudFormation replaces during a stack update. Retain keeps the old resource even after CloudFormation switches to managing its replacement.
learning.concept: Choose the lifecycle policy that governs the previous physical instance when a logical resource is replaced.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Evaluate every candidate revision through the release stages
prompt: A V2 CodePipeline can receive several approved model artifact revisions while its validation stage is locked by a long-running execution. Every candidate is required to pass or fail the same stages in arrival order and must never be displaced by a newer candidate. The deployment environment cannot validate candidates in parallel. Which execution mode meets that policy?

choices.text: Use the QUEUED execution mode.
choices.explanation: Waiting executions line up, so an older candidate does not disappear when a newer one arrives.

choices.text: Use SUPERSEDED mode and attach a manual approval within the validation stage.
choices.explanation: The approval can lengthen a wait, but does not remove superseding behavior for executions waiting at locked stages.

choices.text: Use PARALLEL mode and assume the unique artifact filenames force serial validation.
choices.explanation: Filenames do not serialize execution access to the shared environment.

choices.text: Increase source polling frequency and leave the default execution mode unchanged.
choices.explanation: Polling frequency does not change how executions are allowed to pass locked stages.

learning.reason: Queued execution waits at occupied stages and continues each queued revision. Superseded can skip an earlier waiting revision, and Parallel does not provide the required isolation.
learning.concept: Choose ordered pipeline execution that preserves queued candidate revisions under stage contention.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Route each element through a model flow and return one array
prompt: A Bedrock Flow accepts an array of short descriptions. The same validation and generation nodes must process each description separately. The caller requires one array of processed results from the flow, rather than one separate output event per description. Which node pattern satisfies this? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Use an Iterator to pass each input element through the validation and generation path.
choices.explanation: The downstream nodes are invoked for individual elements in the array.

choices.text: Connect the array directly to a Condition node so it runs each configured branch once per description.
choices.explanation: A condition chooses a path based on its input. It does not iterate over the array.

choices.text: Connect the per-item processing output to a Collector, then return the collected array from the flow.
choices.explanation: The Collector gathers the outputs and passes the combined array onward.

choices.text: Connect the output node directly after per-item processing and assume it implicitly waits to build an array.
choices.explanation: Without collection, flow iterations can produce separate output responses.

choices.text: Discard the original array length and use an output expression that takes only the first processed item.
choices.explanation: The first result cannot represent all input descriptions.

learning.reason: An Iterator emits each item for its sub-flow. A downstream Collector gathers the connected per-item results so a flow output can return a single array.
learning.concept: Pair item-wise orchestration with explicit collection when callers need one grouped response.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Replace one indexed document without rescanning a corpus
prompt: An application manages a custom Bedrock knowledge base data source through its document API. An approved policy has a stable custom document ID. The team needs to replace that policy's contents while leaving all other documents in place. Search should not retain the previous text under a second ID. Which operation fits?

choices.text: Ingest the edited policy under a new random ID and rely on retrieval to automatically suppress the old one.
choices.explanation: Both entries can remain eligible until the old one is deliberately updated or removed.

choices.text: Send IngestKnowledgeBaseDocuments for the existing data source and the same custom document ID with the approved replacement content.
choices.explanation: The existing identifier is updated rather than creating another document key for the previous and new content.

choices.text: Delete the entire knowledge base and recreate its contents with the new policy first.
choices.explanation: That removes and rebuilds unrelated indexed content, which the update does not require.

choices.text: Change the number of retrieval results on the query and leave both versions untouched.
choices.explanation: A query setting cannot replace stale document content in the index.

learning.reason: IngestKnowledgeBaseDocuments can add or replace a directly managed document using its existing identifier. Status can be checked while indexing completes.
learning.concept: Upsert existing directly managed content by stable document identity instead of creating a parallel document.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Share a supported GPU while maintaining hard workload partitions
prompt: Several small model servers need to run on the same supported NVIDIA GPU in Amazon EKS. Each pod needs a fixed accelerator memory allocation and hardware partitioning so a second pod cannot exhaust its share. The team can configure a supported slice profile. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Enable GPU time-slicing and use the pod's CPU memory limit to partition GPU memory.
choices.explanation: Time-slicing does not provide dedicated GPU memory, and normal pod memory limits do not establish MIG partitions.

choices.text: Request one whole GPU for each pod and schedule every pod simultaneously onto the same single GPU.
choices.explanation: Whole-device allocation cannot give the same one device exclusively to multiple pods at the same time.

choices.text: Enable MIG on supported nodes and have each pod request an appropriate MIG slice.
choices.explanation: A slice gives the pod dedicated accelerator resources within the shared physical device.

choices.text: Use a smaller model image and assume that image size acts as a hardware accelerator limit.
choices.explanation: Container storage size does not determine how much GPU memory a running model can allocate.

learning.reason: NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU partitions supported accelerators into hardware-backed instances with dedicated compute and memory. Time-slicing alone shares the same device memory.
learning.concept: Choose a hardware-backed GPU partition when sharing must preserve independent accelerator memory budgets.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Stop a model release before it enters an unhealthy environment
prompt: A deployment stage must make no changes while a named production alarm is in ALARM. The pipeline should check the live alarm when it is about to enter the deployment stage, even if every prior model test already passed. Which integration should the engineer use?

choices.text: Configure only an On Success condition on the deployment stage.
choices.explanation: An On Success check runs after its stage actions have occurred.

choices.text: Depend on the smoke test at the start of the previous build stage without rechecking before deployment.
choices.explanation: The environment may become unhealthy after that earlier check.

choices.text: Use only a model endpoint rollback alarm that can operate once traffic has already shifted.
choices.explanation: Rollback does not prevent entry into the deployment stage before any change occurs.

choices.text: Configure a deployment-stage Entry condition with the production CloudWatch alarm and a blocking result when it is not healthy.
choices.explanation: The check runs before the deployment actions start, which prevents changes while the alarm blocks entry.

learning.reason: A stage Entry condition can use a CloudWatch alarm rule to check environment health before the stage runs, separate from post-deployment verification or rollback.
learning.concept: Place the production health check at the stage entry boundary so an unhealthy target is not changed.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Promote the artifact produced by the right training execution
prompt: A SageMaker pipeline runs two training candidates concurrently for different input versions. A model creation step currently reads a shared S3 key named latest and can use the other execution's artifact. The step needs the artifact from the training step in its own run and should wait for that upstream result. Which change meets both requirements?

choices.text: Set the model input from step_train.properties.ModelArtifacts.S3ModelArtifacts in the pipeline definition.
choices.explanation: The pipeline resolves the dependency and passes the S3 URI created by the training step in this execution.

choices.text: Keep the shared latest key and add only an explicit training-before-model dependency.
choices.explanation: The local ordering constraint does not stop another execution from overwriting the shared key.

choices.text: Hard-code the output path from the most recent successful training job when defining the pipeline.
choices.explanation: That can pin a historical artifact independently of the current execution's training output.

choices.text: Have the model step list all model artifacts and choose the latest by modification time.
choices.explanation: Timestamps cannot identify which concurrently generated artifact belongs to this pipeline execution.

learning.reason: Referencing the training step's S3ModelArtifacts property passes its actual output to the model step and establishes a dependency in the same pipeline run.
learning.concept: Use a runtime property reference instead of guessing a shared storage location or relying only on execution order.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Expose a large tool catalog without sending every tool to the model
prompt: An internal agent already connects to AgentCore Gateway over MCP. The gateway has hundreds of tools and good tool descriptions. Passing the entire catalog to the model every turn exceeds context targets. The team wants to discover a narrow set of relevant tools from a natural-language task description. Which integration should it use?

choices.text: Use tools/list, truncate the first page to a fixed number of alphabetically ordered tools, and ignore the task description.
choices.explanation: Alphabetical truncation does not select tools by relevance and can hide the needed capability.

choices.text: Enable gateway semantic search and call the built-in search tool with the task description before selecting a returned tool.
choices.explanation: The gateway returns relevant tool candidates without requiring the model to receive every available declaration.

choices.text: Send the natural-language task as arguments to every available tool and retain the first successful answer.
choices.explanation: Executing all tools incurs unnecessary work and can trigger actions that the agent did not intend.

choices.text: Add all tool declarations to an unchanging prompt and shorten only the final model response.
choices.explanation: This still spends input context on the entire catalog, leaving the stated input problem unsolved.

learning.reason: When enabled, AgentCore Gateway exposes a built-in semantic search tool that finds relevant gateway tools for a natural-language query. The client can then select and invoke the appropriate returned tool.
learning.concept: Search tool capabilities first when a full manifest would overwhelm the caller's context.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Scope agent metadata to the turn or session that needs it
prompt: A Bedrock agent's action group needs a region value on later turns of the same session. One invocation also needs a temporary short-answer hint, which must be available to the orchestration prompt for that turn without automatically applying to later turns. The agent uses an advanced orchestration template. Which actions meet the requirements? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Set the region as a session attribute for the existing session.
choices.explanation: The action group can receive the value during later invocations in that session.

choices.text: Put both values in prompt session attributes and assume that the next invocation will automatically reuse them.
choices.explanation: The region would not persist to later turns through that field.

choices.text: Put both values in session attributes and instruct the model to forget the hint later.
choices.explanation: The application would still carry the hint across turns until it is removed from persistent session state.

choices.text: Set the hint as a prompt session attribute and include the prompt-session-attributes placeholder in the orchestration template.
choices.explanation: The template receives the turn-scoped hint without treating it as persistent session metadata.

choices.text: Put both values into the deployed agent alias description for every individual request.
choices.explanation: An alias description is not dedicated per-session or per-turn request context.

learning.reason: Session attributes persist across invocations within one session. Prompt session attributes apply to the turn and can appear through the orchestration template's prompt-session-attributes placeholder.
learning.concept: Use persistent session state for stable metadata and turn-scoped prompt state for invocation-specific instructions.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Size scratch storage for an image-based prediction task
prompt: An ECS Fargate inference task on a supported platform version unpacks a large container image and writes temporary feature files. Peak local disk use by the image and files together exceeds the default capacity but fits within 70 GiB. The output is persisted elsewhere, and scratch data should disappear with the task. What should the team configure?

choices.text: Increase the task memory allocation while leaving its ephemeral storage default unchanged.
choices.explanation: Memory allocation does not expand this filesystem capacity.

choices.text: Set an S3 object lifecycle transition on the final output bucket and leave the task storage unchanged.
choices.explanation: The job still needs enough local space before it can publish the final output.

choices.text: Set the task definition's ephemeralStorage size to accommodate the combined peak demand.
choices.explanation: The larger task-scoped storage covers image and scratch growth while retaining the intended lifetime.

choices.text: Configure two containers with additional bind mounts backed by the same unchanged ephemeral storage.
choices.explanation: Adding mount paths does not create additional physical capacity within the task.

learning.reason: Fargate task ephemeral storage includes space for container images and temporary local artifacts. It can be increased on supported platforms without creating a permanent filesystem.
learning.concept: Account for both image storage and workload scratch space in the task-local storage setting.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Support voice conversations where the user can interrupt
prompt: A voice assistant must accept audio continuously while it plays generated speech. When the user starts speaking during a reply, the client must respond to the model's interruption signal and stop playback of pending speech. The team wants a Bedrock model and transport designed for overlapping input and output. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Collect every utterance to a file, call a non-streaming text API after transcription, and finish playing each reply before accepting microphone input.
choices.explanation: Serial whole-turn processing cannot handle an interruption during outgoing audio.

choices.text: Replace the text response with unidirectional response streaming while leaving input closed until playback completes.
choices.explanation: Streaming the response alone does not carry live incoming audio during playback.

choices.text: Create a batch inference job for each dialogue turn and poll its completed output before reopening the microphone.
choices.explanation: Batch request and polling do not support an interactive duplex conversation.

choices.text: Use a supported Nova Sonic model through InvokeModelWithBidirectionalStream, keep the input stream open, and stop buffered playback when an interruption is reported.
choices.explanation: The duplex transport and event handling let the user speak before the generated audio has finished.

learning.reason: Nova Sonic bidirectional audio lets incoming speech reach the model while it is sending audio. The client can act on the documented interruption event to stop playing buffered audio.
learning.concept: Use a duplex speech session and handle interruption instead of serializing whole input and output turns.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Return a stable invocation correlation value without changing model input JSON
prompt: A custom SageMaker real-time serving container already receives a fixed input schema that cannot be extended. Callers need to attach a short support correlation value to an invocation and receive the value back in supported response metadata. The container can explicitly propagate it. Which mechanism should the team use?

choices.text: Pass the correlation value using CustomAttributes and have the container set that value in the supported response custom attributes.
choices.explanation: The request and response use a supported metadata channel while leaving the model's payload schema unchanged.

choices.text: Attach an arbitrary X-Case-ID header and rely on the managed runtime to forward and echo every header automatically.
choices.explanation: SageMaker forwards its supported headers rather than arbitrary request or response headers.

choices.text: Add a new required caseId field to the prediction request body.
choices.explanation: This alters the input schema, which callers cannot change.

choices.text: Record the value only as a deployment tag on the SageMaker endpoint.
choices.explanation: An endpoint tag is shared by invocations and cannot transport a caller's request-specific value back in the response.

learning.reason: InvokeEndpoint forwards its supported CustomAttributes header to the container, which can set the response custom attributes. This keeps the value outside the prediction body.
learning.concept: Choose the supported request and response metadata path and let the inference implementation return the correlation value explicitly.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Resolve the private runtime name from a connected data center
prompt: On-premises clients reach a SageMaker Runtime interface endpoint over a private network connection. Private DNS is enabled and works from inside the endpoint's VPC. The same regional runtime name resolves publicly through the data center resolver. The network path to the VPC's private addresses already works. Which DNS change lets clients use the same regional hostname privately?

choices.text: Create an outbound Resolver endpoint and forward only VPC-originated requests to the on-premises resolver.
choices.explanation: This solves the opposite lookup direction and does not route on-premises lookups to the VPC.

choices.text: Create a Route 53 Resolver inbound endpoint in the endpoint VPC and configure the on-premises resolver to forward the necessary runtime hostname or DNS zone to it.
choices.explanation: The VPC Resolver can then answer with the private address associated with the service endpoint.

choices.text: Keep on-premises DNS unchanged and alter only the inference model's VPC security group.
choices.explanation: A security group can change allowed network traffic but cannot change the DNS answer returned by the on-premises resolver.

choices.text: Replace the regional hostname with one hard-coded endpoint network interface IP address in all clients.
choices.explanation: This abandons the hostname requirement and binds clients to an address that can change.

learning.reason: An inbound Route 53 Resolver endpoint accepts DNS queries forwarded into a VPC. Conditional forwarding for the required AWS service name uses the endpoint VPC's private resolution.
learning.concept: Forward hybrid DNS queries toward the endpoint VPC's resolver in the correct direction.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Keep large batch outputs out of workflow state
prompt: A Step Functions Distributed Map starts document enrichment jobs. Every child succeeds, but combining their returned records exceeds the workflow payload limit. The downstream indexer can read S3 and needs access to every result, while the parent should carry only a small reference. What should the team configure?

choices.text: Raise Distributed Map concurrency so the aggregate result is assembled sooner.
choices.explanation: Parallelism changes runtime, not the size of the returned state.

choices.text: Set the Map result to null and expect the downstream indexer to reconstruct discarded child outputs from its input.
choices.explanation: The parent would no longer pass the data needed and no durable result export is configured.

choices.text: Configure ResultWriter to write child execution results to S3 and have downstream work read the exported result locations.
choices.explanation: The child artifacts are preserved externally and no large combined inline payload is needed.

choices.text: Switch to an Inline Map and keep concatenating every result into one state object.
choices.explanation: Changing the map type does not remove the state payload limit.

learning.reason: Distributed Map ResultWriter can export child execution results to S3. A compact result location can be passed without embedding all child records in the parent.
learning.concept: Offload large aggregated results to durable storage while passing a reference to the next step.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Catch rule boundary regressions before publishing a new policy
prompt: A team changes an Automated Reasoning policy used by an assistant to verify benefit eligibility. An edited rule alters an age boundary. The team must show that expected decisions at and around the boundary still produce the intended validation results before deploying the new policy. Which testing approach fits?

choices.text: Compare only the length of the updated policy text with its previous version.
choices.explanation: Document length cannot validate how the policy interprets specific cases.

choices.text: Run a generative helpfulness benchmark and use its average as proof the rule's decisions are unchanged.
choices.explanation: A helpfulness score does not assert the validation decisions around that boundary.

choices.text: Set every expected result from whatever the new policy produces on its first run.
choices.explanation: This removes the independent expectations that would reveal an unintended change.

choices.text: Create policy test cases just below, at, and above the boundary with the approved expected validation results, then run them against the candidate.
choices.explanation: The cases exercise the changed condition and make a difference from approved decisions visible before deployment.

learning.reason: Automated Reasoning policy tests can define inputs and expected validation results. Running targeted cases against the candidate policy can surface translation or rule regressions before release.
learning.concept: Test explicit examples around a changed rule boundary with approved expected outcomes, before selecting the policy version for production.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Move a compatible model to serverless without downtime
prompt: A team decides to move a compatible SageMaker model from an existing dedicated real-time endpoint to on-demand serverless. Its application can switch a stable internal routing setting after testing. The current endpoint must keep serving until equivalent behavior is demonstrated. Which migration is supported?

choices.text: Create a separate serverless endpoint, verify the candidate under expected traffic, then switch callers and retire the old endpoint after the cutover.
choices.explanation: A separate endpoint avoids the unsupported update direction and lets the team preserve service while checking the new path.

choices.text: Call UpdateEndpoint on the current endpoint and change the production variant directly to an on-demand serverless configuration.
choices.explanation: The service does not support converting a real-time endpoint to serverless through that operation.

choices.text: Set the existing real-time endpoint's production variant weight to zero and use that same endpoint as a serverless endpoint.
choices.explanation: Production variant weights change routing, not the endpoint's hosting type.

choices.text: Delete the serving endpoint first and reuse its name immediately for the serverless endpoint.
choices.explanation: This removes the healthy path before the candidate can be verified.

learning.reason: SageMaker does not support updating an existing real-time endpoint into serverless. Deploy a new serverless endpoint, verify it, and then shift callers before retiring the earlier path.
learning.concept: Choose a migration procedure that respects a non-convertible endpoint type and preserves the serving path during validation.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Treat model approval and live routing as separate states
prompt: A bad model version is running on a SageMaker production endpoint. The team maintains Model Registry approval state, but this project has no automation listening for approval events. Future releases must not select this version, and the current endpoint must return to a known-good version. Which actions are needed? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Set the bad model package version's approval status to Rejected.
choices.explanation: Future workflows that enforce approval can exclude that version.

choices.text: Change the package status only and wait for the endpoint to modify itself without a registered deployment integration.
choices.explanation: The endpoint keeps its existing deployment unless a deployment operation or configured workflow changes it.

choices.text: Mark the previous version Approved and assume it immediately takes production traffic without deploying it.
choices.explanation: Approval makes a model eligible. It does not directly assign any endpoint traffic in this setup.

choices.text: Overwrite the original model package's S3 artifact while keeping the currently loaded endpoint and its records unchanged.
choices.explanation: That undermines the traceable version and does not reliably replace the already deployed model.

choices.text: Redeploy the known-good approved model using the endpoint rollback or deployment procedure and verify the active model.
choices.explanation: This changes the actual serving configuration rather than relying on an unused approval event.

learning.reason: Registry approval communicates eligibility. Without integrated deployment automation, changing the approval alone does not update a live endpoint, so the team also needs a controlled rollback.
learning.concept: Revoke eligibility for future promotion and explicitly replace what the live endpoint serves.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Correct an incompatible request when releasing a managed prompt
prompt: A production service passes a reviewed Bedrock Prompt Management version ARN as the modelId in Converse. A release requires a new fixed system instruction and a different temperature shared across the app. The current change adds system and inferenceConfig fields directly to the Converse payload, causing an error. The service must continue pinning a reviewed managed prompt version. What should the team change?

choices.text: Keep sending system and inferenceConfig and move the version ARN into requestMetadata.
choices.explanation: Request metadata does not select the managed prompt version or legalize conflicting fields.

choices.text: Add the system instruction and inference setting to the prompt configuration, publish and review a new version, and call that ARN without the conflicting request fields.
choices.explanation: The new version carries both fixed settings and remains explicitly selected by its ARN.

choices.text: Set the temperature as a text prompt variable and leave the model's old inference configuration unchanged.
choices.explanation: A variable can substitute text in the prompt but does not set the model's generation temperature.

choices.text: Copy the prompt into client source, call the base model directly, and stop referencing versions.
choices.explanation: This can permit direct fields but removes the versioned managed prompt required by the service.

learning.reason: Converse requests using a managed prompt version cannot also supply system or inferenceConfig directly. Those settings belong in the managed prompt before the new version is published.
learning.concept: Define shared inference settings in the same versioned resource as the managed prompt rather than overriding prohibited fields per request.

category: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
examDomain: Deployment and Orchestration of ML and AI Workflows
title: Scale active asynchronous workers as their queue grows
prompt: An asynchronous SageMaker endpoint must always keep at least one working instance, so waking from zero is outside this design. When traffic rises, the goal is to keep approximately the same number of pending requests per instance. Requests vary in duration and the metric setup should represent queued work per available instance. Which target-tracking signal fits?

choices.text: Use only HasBacklogWithoutCapacity and leave the minimum instance count at one.
choices.explanation: The signal is for the special case of queued requests with no capacity and cannot track queue load on an active fleet.

choices.text: Track the lifetime count of completed outputs and increase capacity whenever it grows.
choices.explanation: A cumulative completion total does not represent the pending load each instance currently faces.

choices.text: Target ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance for the asynchronous endpoint variant.
choices.explanation: It represents pending work per worker and can guide scaling around the desired queue load.

choices.text: Track total queue size without normalizing and require that same total at all fleet sizes as a per-instance measure.
choices.explanation: The same queue total represents different amounts of pending work per instance when capacity varies.

learning.reason: ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance normalizes pending work by current workers. Unlike a wake-up signal, it supports tracking a queue workload target at a nonzero fleet size.
learning.concept: Use queue load relative to active capacity for ongoing asynchronous scaling.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Detect abnormal latency across normal weekly traffic cycles
prompt: A deployed model's latency follows a stable hour-of-week pattern. A single static threshold either alerts every busy weekday or misses unusual weekend degradation. The team has enough representative history and knows the timestamps of abnormal load tests that should never define normal behavior. What should it configure? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Set the permanent static threshold to the highest observed load-test value.
choices.explanation: This can miss lower but unusual production degradations.

choices.text: Enable CloudWatch anomaly detection for the latency metric and alarm on a sustained upper-band breach.
choices.explanation: The alarm can account for expected variation across the week instead of using one static value.

choices.text: Exclude the known load-test intervals from the anomaly detector's training data.
choices.explanation: Intentional test spikes do not need to become part of the expected production behavior.

choices.text: Disable all monitoring every weekend and retain the weekday alarm threshold.
choices.explanation: Weekend anomalies would become invisible even though the service still receives traffic.

choices.text: Add load-test windows as the model's only training samples.
choices.explanation: That teaches the unusual test workload as normal and discards representative production patterns.

learning.reason: CloudWatch metric anomaly detection can learn time-dependent expected behavior. Excluding known unusual windows keeps controlled load tests out of the baseline training data.
learning.concept: Use a seasonal expected band and exclude characterized test windows from baseline fitting.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Restore structured prediction data for a monitoring job
prompt: A SageMaker endpoint's prediction payload is valid JSON. Data Capture is enabled, but a monitor that expects raw JSON sees Base64-encoded entries. The capture configuration did not specify content type headers. The model and monitoring job must retain their JSON format. Which change fits?

choices.text: Increase the percentage of requests captured without specifying content types.
choices.explanation: This may produce more records, but it leaves their default encoding unchanged.

choices.text: Configure CsvContentTypes for the JSON MIME type and keep the JSON monitor unchanged.
choices.explanation: The capture settings would describe the payload inconsistently with the required JSON contract.

choices.text: Change the endpoint's response content type to an unrelated binary type without updating the capture configuration.
choices.explanation: That does not supply an expected JSON content type and can preserve the default Base64 encoding.

choices.text: Set Data Capture's JsonContentTypes to match the endpoint's JSON Content-Type header and verify newly captured records.
choices.explanation: The byte encoding can be selected based on the matching content type rather than falling back to Base64.

learning.reason: SageMaker defaults to Base64 encoding the captured payload when no capture content-type header is supplied. Registering the actual JSON media type allows matching data to be captured as JSON.
learning.concept: Configure the data capture format to match how the endpoint labels its JSON payload.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Analyze repeated inference activity at the experiment's randomization unit
prompt: An A/B study assigns each user once to a model variant. A user can generate many inference requests. The release metric is the percentage of eligible users who complete a task in the fixed follow-up period. A reviewer proposes treating every request as an independent observation to construct confidence intervals. What should the analyst do instead?

choices.text: Assign one success indicator to each eligible randomized user and compare the user-level rates and uncertainty between variants.
choices.explanation: The observation used for the metric now matches the randomized user and its follow-up period.

choices.text: Treat every inference request as an independent user and report the resulting confidence interval.
choices.explanation: That overweights frequent requesters and ignores correlation among requests from the same user.

choices.text: Randomly reassign each recorded request to a group after the test to create independence.
choices.explanation: Post hoc reassignment breaks the observed exposure and outcome relationship.

choices.text: Restrict the analysis to users with exactly one request and report it as the overall eligible user result.
choices.explanation: This discards users based on observed behavior and changes the population the metric covers.

learning.reason: The experiment randomizes users, and the target is a user-level outcome. A user-level summary avoids weighting frequent requesters as though they were independent randomized units.
learning.concept: Analyze a user-level outcome at the randomization unit when repeated requests share the same assignment.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Add accelerator telemetry to a serving dashboard
prompt: An EKS inference dashboard shows CPU, pod status, and request latency. A latency incident may come from NVIDIA GPU memory or utilization pressure. The platform has supported nodes and the NVIDIA prerequisites. The team wants managed CloudWatch collection and dashboards for GPU metrics without adding telemetry to every model container. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use only each pod's CPU memory utilization and treat it as GPU memory utilization.
choices.explanation: CPU memory and accelerator memory are different resources and can saturate independently.

choices.text: Enable supported CloudWatch Container Insights accelerated compute monitoring and add NVIDIA utilization and memory metrics to the dashboard.
choices.explanation: The cluster integration collects hardware-level evidence without requiring application metrics in each serving container.

choices.text: Collect additional request logs and infer GPU utilization from the count of successful predictions.
choices.explanation: Request count does not measure resource saturation or accelerator memory usage.

choices.text: Plot only the number of nodes with a GPU without collecting hardware telemetry.
choices.explanation: Inventory shows capacity exists but not whether it is busy or running out of memory.

learning.reason: Container Insights with enhanced observability on a supported EKS configuration can collect accelerator hardware metrics. CPU and pod state alone cannot measure accelerator memory or utilization.
learning.concept: Enable infrastructure accelerator telemetry at the cluster observability layer to complement prediction latency.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Block untrusted deployment packages for a model router
prompt: A model router runs as a Lambda ZIP function. The release team must prevent deploying packages that are unsigned or signed by an unapproved publisher. It already runs dependency vulnerability scans and will retain them. Which additional controls enforce package provenance? (Choose two.)

choices.text: Attach the same configuration but leave the untrusted artifact policy as Warn.
choices.explanation: Warn records a problem without blocking that deployment.

choices.text: Sign release ZIPs with AWS Signer using an approved signing profile.
choices.explanation: Lambda can verify the artifact against the trusted publisher configured for this function.

choices.text: Rely on a vulnerability scan alone as evidence of the publisher's cryptographic identity.
choices.explanation: Vulnerability scanning and signature verification establish different properties.

choices.text: Attach a code signing configuration allowing the approved profile and set the untrusted artifact policy to Enforce.
choices.explanation: Enforce rejects deployment attempts with an unsupported or missing signature.

choices.text: Attach the function's execution role as the signer and skip signing the ZIP.
choices.explanation: The execution role controls runtime permissions. It does not make the package signed with the required profile.

learning.reason: Lambda ZIP code signing verifies the package against an allowed signing profile. Enforce blocks untrusted deployments instead of allowing them with a warning.
learning.concept: Sign release ZIP archives with an approved publisher and make the runtime deployment gate enforce that signature.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Authenticate a certificate-based workload outside AWS
prompt: An on-premises batch program calls Bedrock using an AWS SDK that signs requests. It has an approved X.509 workload certificate from the organization's certificate authority. Security forbids long-lived AWS access keys. The workload needs time-limited permissions scoped to inference. Which credential flow meets the requirements?

choices.text: Create an IAM user, store its permanent access key in the batch program, and rotate it every year.
choices.explanation: This still leaves a long-lived access key and fails the stated credential requirement.

choices.text: Send the certificate text directly as a Bedrock bearer API key without obtaining any AWS credentials.
choices.explanation: An X.509 certificate is not a Bedrock bearer key and does not supply the credentials the SDK uses to sign.

choices.text: Configure IAM Roles Anywhere to trust the approved certificate authority and use its credential provider to obtain temporary credentials for a scoped inference role.
choices.explanation: The SDK signs its requests with role session credentials without storing permanent AWS keys.

choices.text: Attach an EC2 instance profile to the on-premises host and read credentials from the EC2 metadata service.
choices.explanation: The host is not running as an EC2 instance and cannot receive that instance profile through the EC2 metadata service.

learning.reason: IAM Roles Anywhere authenticates an external workload using a certificate from a configured trust anchor and obtains temporary credentials for an IAM role that the SDK can use.
learning.concept: Use certificate-based workload identity to obtain role sessions for signed SDK requests.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Block new discretionary training after the budget action runs
prompt: A team wants an automatic response after AWS Budgets detects actual training spend above a threshold. From that point, a dedicated experiment role must be unable to create new training jobs, while currently running work and approved production roles should remain unaffected. A delay in billing detection is acceptable. Which action fits?

choices.text: Publish only an email alert when the budget exceeds the threshold.
choices.explanation: Notification does not change whether the experiment role can start more jobs.

choices.text: Attach a broad account-wide deny covering all SageMaker operations.
choices.explanation: That can disrupt approved production activities and exceeds the requested scope.

choices.text: Use the forecast alert threshold as a real-time per-request admission check and make no authorization change.
choices.explanation: A forecast alert is not a real-time enforcement mechanism and does not revoke this role's ability to start work.

choices.text: Configure an automated AWS Budgets action that attaches a narrow deny on creating training jobs to the experiment role after the actual-spend threshold is detected.
choices.explanation: The action blocks later starts from that role once applied without requiring a policy that stops running jobs or affects other roles.

learning.reason: An automated budget action can apply a specified IAM policy to the targeted role. Restricting that policy to creating new training jobs limits the response to the requested access path.
learning.concept: Choose an authorization action for future training starts once budget detection has occurred, with explicitly scoped effects.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Cap permissions on roles created for short-lived ML experiments
prompt: A platform team delegates creation of experiment execution roles. Project owners may attach identity-based policies for each role, but those policies must never exceed a centrally approved maximum. Delegation already requires an approved boundary and prevents removing it. No resource policy grants permissions directly to the resulting sessions. What should the central team specify?

choices.text: Attach a central managed policy as the permissions boundary and let project owners grant required actions through identity policies within that limit.
choices.explanation: Effective identity permissions must satisfy both the delegated policy and the boundary.

choices.text: Put the full list of intended permissions in the role's trust policy and allow unrestricted identity policies.
choices.explanation: A trust policy controls who can assume the role. It does not cap the actions granted by the role's identity policy.

choices.text: Use the boundary as the only policy and assume it grants all the allowed actions.
choices.explanation: A boundary is a maximum, not an independent grant of those actions.

choices.text: Use only a tagging convention for project-owned roles and rely on reviewers to remove broad grants.
choices.explanation: A convention without policy enforcement cannot guarantee the maximum permissions.

learning.reason: An IAM permissions boundary defines the maximum identity-based permissions available to a role. Actual permissions require a matching grant and remain subject to the boundary and applicable denies.
learning.concept: Use a permissions ceiling for delegated role policy management without treating the ceiling as a grant.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Make artifact ownership consistent across writing accounts
prompt: Several experiment accounts upload artifacts to an older central S3 bucket. Some existing objects are owned by their uploading accounts because ACLs are still enabled. The platform must own all objects in the bucket and control artifact access through policies. Writer permissions can be migrated first. Which setting and access model meet the requirement?

choices.text: Leave the bucket in Object writer mode and rely on the platform to maintain its own independent bucket permissions.
choices.explanation: Object writer mode can retain uploader ownership of cross-account uploads rather than giving ownership to the bucket owner.

choices.text: Move approved writer permissions into policies and enable Bucket owner enforced for S3 Object Ownership.
choices.explanation: The bucket owner owns the objects and policy authorization replaces ACL-based access.

choices.text: Use different object tags to name the platform as owner while leaving ACLs enabled.
choices.explanation: Tags can describe data or support policy decisions, but they do not change object ownership.

choices.text: Require every writer to grant public-read ACL access so the platform can always retrieve objects.
choices.explanation: This exposes artifacts unnecessarily and does not give the platform ownership or replace ACLs.

learning.reason: Bucket owner enforced disables ACLs and gives the bucket owner ownership of objects. Approved writers and readers continue through policies that grant the necessary actions.
learning.concept: Choose policy-based S3 ownership for cross-account uploads after migrating any required ACL-derived grants.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Review model-resource compliance across accounts and Regions
prompt: Each account in an AWS organization already records supported inference and storage resources with AWS Config and evaluates the required rules. A central audit account needs one read-only view of recorded configuration and compliance across the enabled Regions. It must not own or remediate the member resources. Which setup meets the requirement?

choices.text: Disable Config in the member Regions and assume a new central aggregator records remote resources directly.
choices.explanation: The aggregator collects records made in source accounts and Regions. It does not replace their recorders.

choices.text: Store a CloudTrail organization trail and treat the API history alone as the current rule compliance dashboard.
choices.explanation: Event history does not directly expose the member Config rules' current compliance results.

choices.text: Set up an AWS Config organization aggregator with authorization for the required accounts and Regions.
choices.explanation: The central account can see existing configuration and compliance data without modifying the original resources.

choices.text: Move every evaluated inference endpoint into the central account.
choices.explanation: That changes ownership and operation despite the requirement for a read-only view.

learning.reason: An organization Config aggregator collects recorded inventory and compliance results across source accounts and Regions. Its aggregated view is read-only.
learning.concept: Aggregate existing evaluations centrally without moving source resource control.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Resolve a model deployment's private image authorization failure
prompt: A model version is shared from a registry account to a SageMaker deployment account. The deployment can read the model package and its S3 artifact. The endpoint fails only when SageMaker pulls a private inference image in the registry account. The deployment role already has the necessary identity-side ECR actions and can get an authorization token. The registry repository grants no access to that role. What should change?

choices.text: Add another read grant to the model artifact's S3 bucket and leave the ECR policy unchanged.
choices.explanation: S3 permission does not authorize private image pulls.

choices.text: Give the training job role write access to ECR instead and leave the deployment principal unauthorized.
choices.explanation: The deployment uses its configured role and needs read access, rather than a different principal receiving push capabilities.

choices.text: Enable image tag immutability and assume it grants read access to the deployment account.
choices.explanation: Image tag immutability protects tag updates. It does not grant cross-account access.

choices.text: Add a scoped ECR repository policy granting the deployment role the image pull actions on the relevant repository.
choices.explanation: The image owner authorizes that cross-account role to fetch the image manifest and layers.

learning.reason: Cross-account deployment also needs authorization on the private image repository. Granting the deployment role the required pull actions in that resource policy addresses the missing resource-side permission.
learning.concept: Inspect the missing ECR resource authorization independently from the model package and artifact permissions.

category: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
examDomain: Operating, Monitoring, and Securing ML and AI Solutions
title: Allow reply traffic through a restrictive endpoint subnet ACL
prompt: An internal application connects over HTTPS to a private interface endpoint. The endpoint subnet's network ACL permits inbound port 443 from the application's subnet, but its outbound rules block reply packets. The endpoint security group already permits the connection, the client subnet allows replies, and the client's ephemeral port range is known. Which scoped change solves the observed problem?

choices.text: Allow outbound TCP traffic on the client's ephemeral port range to its subnet in the endpoint subnet ACL.
choices.explanation: HTTPS replies use the client source port from the original connection as their destination.

choices.text: Allow outbound TCP port 443 only, since the initial request went to port 443.
choices.explanation: The return packet's source port is 443. The outbound ACL's destination port needs to match the client port.

choices.text: Increase the security group's inbound port range and leave the outbound ACL block in place.
choices.explanation: The ACL still independently evaluates the outbound response.

choices.text: Add a route to an internet gateway for reply traffic even though both participants are private.
choices.explanation: Changing the internet route does not remove the subnet ACL's missing return permission.

learning.reason: Network ACLs are stateless, so the return packet needs its own outbound allowance to the client's destination ephemeral port. A stateful security group does not override the subnet ACL.
